{color:#bf2600}*Important note:* {color}For testing, do not do merge until you have confirmed the pre-deploy steps from the “Automatic tagging of existing collections” section have been completed.

h1. *Coding tasks*

h2. *Create Elasticsearch index for collections*

This milestone consists of several key tasks:

# Index collection information in Elasticsearch.
# Ensure index is updated as collections and related data change.
# Use Elasticsearch for collection index pages.
# Use Elasticsearch when filtering collection index pages.
# Update the [+collection blurbs+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/views/collections/_collection_blurb.html.erb] to get their descriptions and counts from Elasticsearch.

A new {{collections}} index should be created in Elasticsearch. Each document in the index should have the following fields:

* From {{collections}}:
** {{name}} is currently a filter option on the collections index ("Filter by title or name"). We would like to change the filter option to just "Filter by title", at the same time still include {{name}} in each document, as it may be useful in the future.
** {{title}} is both a filter and sorting option on the collections index. It is also used to order collections on both users' collections pages and collections' subcollection pages.
** {{description}} will be used in blurbs. It is not currently used for filtering, but may be useful in the future.
** {{created_at}} is the default sorting option on the collections index.
** {{challenge_type}} is a filter option on the collections index, and it is used to determine which open challenges pages a collection should be on.
** {{parent_id}} is necessary so collections' subcollection pages can come from Elasticsearch.
* From {{collection_preferences}}:
** {{closed}} is a filter option on the collections index.
** {{moderated}} is a filter option on the collections index.
** {{unrevealed}} is not currently used for filtering, but may be useful in the future.
** {{anonymous}} is not currently used for filtering, but may be useful in the future.
* From {{gift_exchanges}} and {{prompt_memes}}:
** {{signup_open}} is necessary to determine which collections to include on the open challenges pages.
** {{signups_open_at}} is not currently used for filtering, but may be useful in the future.
** {{signups_close_at}} is used to order collections on the open challenges pages.
** {{assignments_due_at}} is not currently used for filtering, but may be useful in the future.
** {{works_reveal_at}} is not currently used for filtering, but may be useful in the future.
** {{authors_reveal_at}} is not currently used for filtering, but may be useful in the future.
* From other sources:
** {{owner_ids}} is necessary to determine which collections to include on users' collection pages. If the user is an owner of the collection, they should have at least one {{pseud_id}} in this array, and the collection should be on the user's collection page.
** {{moderator_ids}} is necessary to determine which collections to include on users' collection pages. If the user is a moderator of the collection, they should have at least one {{pseud_id}} in this array, and the collection should be on the user's collection page.
** {{general_fandom_ids}} are the ids of canonical fandom tags used on all public and restricted [+approved works+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e0f7ce52129a09f5483199a71802d5f30b9c433e/app/models/collection.rb#L59] in the collection or any of its subcollections. It should draw from both direct and indirect {{filter_taggings}}. This field will allow logged-in users to filter collections by fandom.
** {{public_fandom_ids}} are the ids of canonical fandom tags used on all public approved works in the collection or any of its subcollections. It should draw from both direct and indirect {{filter_taggings}}. This field will allow logged-out users to filter collections by fandom while ensuring the results do not include collections whose only works in the specified fandom(s) are restricted.
** {{general_fandoms_count}} is the total number of fandoms on all public and restricted works approved for inclusion in the collection or any of its subcollections. Unlike the {{general_fandom_ids}}, this field counts only direct {{filter_taggings}}. It will be used in blurbs to display the fandom count to logged-in users.
** {{public_fandoms_count}} is the total number of fandoms on all public and restricted works approved for inclusion in the collection or any of its subcollections. Like {{general_fandoms_count}}, this field counts only direct {{filter_taggings}}. It will be used in blurbs to display the fandom count to logged-out users.
** {{general_works_count}} is the total number of restricted and public works approved for inclusion in the collection or any of its subcollections. It will be used in blurbs.
** {{public_works_count}} is the total number of public works in the collection, to be used for blurbs.
** {{general_bookmarked_items_count}} is the total number of public bookmarks of public and restricted bookmarkables ({{Work}}, {{Series}}, and {{ExternalWork}}) approved for inclusion in the collection or any of its subcollections, to be used for blurbs.
** {{public_bookmarked_items_count}} is the total number of approved public bookmarks of public bookmarkables approved for inclusion in the collection or any of its subcollections, to be used for blurbs.

The documents should be reindexed when any of the following actions occur:

* A {{Collection}} record is created, updated, or destroyed
* The {{CollectionPreference}} belonging to the collection has its {{closed}}, {{moderated}}, {{unrevealed}}, or {{anonymous}} column updated
* A {{GiftExchange}} or {{PromptMeme}} belonging to the collection
** is created or destroyed
** has its {{signup_open}}, {{signups_open_at}}, {{signups_close_at}}, {{assignments_due_at}}, {{works_reveal_at}}, or {{authors_reveal_at}} column updated
* A {{CollectionParticipant}} associated with the collection
** is created or destroyed and has the {{participant_role}} of {{"Owner"}} or {{"Moderator"}}
** has its {{participant_role}} updated to or from {{"Owner"}} or {{"Moderator"}}
* A {{CollectionItem}} associated with the collection
** is created or destroyed
** has its {{user_approval_status}} or {{collection_approval_status}} column updated
* A {{Work}} in the collection has {{Fandom}} tags added or removed (+direct+ {{filter_taggings}} only)
* A {{Fandom}} tag used on a work in the collection
** has its {{canonical}} or {{merger_id}} column updated

Reindexing should be synchronous for changes to the {{Collection}} or its {{GiftExchange}} or {{PromptMeme}}. Otherwise, reindexing should be asynchronous.

Once indexing has been set up, all collection indexes should be drawn from Elasticsearch rather than MySQL. This includes:

* The main collections page, i.e. [+https://archiveofourown.org/collections+|https://archiveofourown.org/collections]
* The open challenges page, i.e. [+https://archiveofourown.org/collections/list_challenges+|https://archiveofourown.org/collections/list_challenges]
* The open gift exchanges page, i.e. [+https://archiveofourown.org/collections/list_ge_challenges+|https://archiveofourown.org/collections/list_ge_challenges]
* The open prompt memes page, i.e. [+https://archiveofourown.org/collections/list_pm_challenges+|https://archiveofourown.org/collections/list_pm_challenges]
* Users' collection pages, e.g. [+https://archiveofourown.org/users/testy/collections+|https://archiveofourown.org/users/testy/collections]
* Collections' subcollections pages, e.g. [+https://archiveofourown.org/collections/yuletide/collections+|https://archiveofourown.org/collections/yuletide/collections]

The filters on the main collections page should be reworked to use Elasticsearch. No new filter options should be added; however, the "Filter by fandom" option should be updated to filter using the {{general_fandom_ids}} field for logged-in users or admins and the {{public_fandom_ids}} field for everyone else.

And finally, the collection blurbs displayed on collection indexes should be updated to draw their descriptions and their counts of fandoms, works, and bookmarked items from the corresponding Elasticsearch fields:

* {{general_fandoms_count}}, {{general_works_count}}, and {{general_bookmarked_items_count}} should be used for logged-in users or admins
* {{public_fandoms_count}}, {{public_works_count}}, and {{public_bookmarked_items_count}} should be used for everyone else.

This should be handled using a decorator, similar to the way {{pseud_decorator.rb}} is used for blurbs in [+the results of a People Search+|https://archiveofourown.org/people/search?utf8=%E2%9C%93&people_search%5Bquery%5D=&people_search%5Bname%5D=testy&people_search%5Bfandom%5D=&commit=Search+People].

h2. *Update Collections to have their own tags*

It was decided as the original implementation of this issue progressed that searching (and therefore updating indexes) on collection sub-items was prohibitively difficult. Instead, we’re going to give collections their own tags (should already be done behind the scenes) and backfill the bookmarks'/works' fandoms with a Rake task.

h1. Post-merge tasks

* Update [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Development-Data#resque---elasticsearch-indexes-reading-history-and-more|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Development-Data#resque---elasticsearch-indexes-reading-history-and-more|smart-link] to add the new command for indexing pipelines.

h1. Deploy tasks

# Go into maintenance
# Run {{rails db:migrate:up VERSION=20250906065547}} (departure migration)
# Run {{rake After:add_collection_tags}} 
# Make sure the workers are running the new code, restart them if necessary
# Run {{rake search:index_collections}}
# Make sure all servers are running the new code
# Go back out of maintenance

Also needs a skin recache.

h1. Testing tasks

There is a lot to test here, so the instructions have been split into sections that can be divided among several volunteers, even if that means some redundancy between sections and the groupings seem odd. 

Please note that reindexing takes a few minutes, so you'll need to wait any time you're testing whether listings or search/filter results update as the result of a change. We also cache pages for logged out users, so logged out listings will take even longer to update (e.g., when testing the counts).

h3. Creating/deleting collections and changing owners and moderators

For this section, you'll need to check that some HTML classes have been added. You can do that with either your browser developer tools or a site skin that has separate styles for the selectors a.mod and a.owner, such as {{a.mod { background: pink !important; } a.owner { background: yellow !important }}}

To change the owners or moderators of a collection, you'll need to follow the Membership link in the subnavigation located on your collection's Dashboard or Profile page. From there, you can add a user to the collection, update their role, and/or remove their membership.

h3. Collection blurb Works count

The Works count refers to the number of works an individual can expect to find in the collection. This number will be different depending on whether the person looking at the count is logged out or logged in as a user or an admin.

In addition to waiting a few minutes for reindexing to occur, due to caching, you'll need to wait 10-15 minutes between each step to verify the logged-out count.

# Create an unmoderated collection with two public works (we'll need them both later). The logged-in and logged-out Works counts should both be 2.
# Add a restricted work. The logged-in Works count should increase to 3, but the logged-out count should stay at 2.
# Log in as an admin with the superadmin or policy_and_abuse admin role and 
## make sure you see the logged-in Works count (3) in the collection blurb.
## hide one of the public works. Both Works counts should decrease.
## unhide the work. Both Works counts should increase.
# Log back in as the user from Step 1 and remove the restricted work. The logged-in Works count should decrease but the logged-out count should not change.
# Add a restricted work you are willing to delete (it can be the same one from the previous step). Wait for the Works counts to update to include it and then delete the work. The logged-in Works count should decrease but the logged-out count should not change.
# Remove the public work. Both work counts should decrease.
# Change the collection settings to moderated and invite another user's restricted work to the collection. (Make sure you're not logged in as an archivist and the other user is an account you can log into, but is not an owner, moderator, or member of the collection, since these will skip the invitation process.) The Works count should not update.
# Log in as the user whose work was invited to the collection, go to your Collection Items page, and approve the work's inclusion in the collection. The logged-in Works count should update, but the logged-out count should not.
# As the same user, add another restricted work to the collection. Neither Works count should update.
# Log back in as the owner of the collection from Step 1, go to the collection's Manage Items page, and approve the work from Step 9. The logged-in Works count should increase but not the logged-out count.

h3. Collection blurb Bookmarked Items count

The Bookmarked Items count refers to how many distinct works, series, or external works are bookmarked in the collection, not how many bookmarks are in the collection. For example, if two users have both added bookmarks of the work Sliding Doors to a collection, that counts as one Bookmarked Item. 

Unless otherwise instructed, make sure the item you are bookmarking has not already been bookmarked in the collection.

In addition to waiting a few minutes for reindexing to occur, due to caching, you'll need to wait 10-15 minutes between each step to verify the logged-out count.

h3. Manually marking collections multifandom

It’s not yet possible to filter on the Multifandom field, but we want to allow users to set that information now in order to encourage accurate tagging.

h3. Automatic tagging of existing collections

Existing collections will be automatically tagged with up to 10 fandoms. These fandoms will be based on approved, public collection items in the collection and its subcollections. 

If the collection has more than 10 fandoms, no tags will be applied.

Collections will be marked Multifandom if none of the fandom tags in the collection share a metatag. Fandoms sharing a metatag are for example “Smosh” and “Game Grumps”, which share the “Video Blogging & Youtube RPF“ metatag.

Note that for the following steps, it's okay to reuse fandom tags as long as they're in different collections.

column1: Automatically email inactive tag wranglers and alert wrangling supervisors of wrangler inactivity
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

h1. Email inactive tag wranglers Each day, we should check the wrangling activity table created in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6013#icft=AO3-6013|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6013#icft=AO3-6013|smart-link] to find any wranglers who have not wrangled in the last 3 weeks. This number should be configurable. Setting it to 0 should disable the emails. Each of those wranglers should be sent an email with the subject "[AO3] Wrangling activity reminder". The email should go to the address listed on the wrangler's AO3 account. The reply-to address on the email should be tagwranglers-personnel@transformativeworks.org. This address should be configurable and will be used in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6493|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6493|smart-link] and [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6494|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6494|smart-link] as well. The wrangler should not be sent an additional email each day they fail to wrangle. Wranglers who have not wrangled since they received the tag wrangling role should only be emailed after 3 weeks have passed. To achieve this, giving wrangling permissions should update the last wrangling activity. The email should not be sent to certain accounts that are used for either administrative or other internal purposes. This list should be configurable. The accounts that should be excluded initially are: AO3_Wrangling_Project, Qem_Chibati, AO3_Support, AO3_Tag_Wranglers, testy_wrangler, TWSupervisor_Fandom_Hold. The emails should be coded as translatable, although we may never actually translate them. The emails should reference config variables where appropriate (e.g. the app short name in the subject, the full app name in the first sentence, the 3 week period). The HTML email should be approximately as follows: {noformat}

Hi <%= style_bold("USERNAME GOES HERE") %>,

This is an automated message from Archive of Our Own on behalf of Tag Wrangling Supervisors. We'd like to gently check in since no wrangling activity has been logged on your account in the past 3 weeks (21 days).

No worries! You're not in trouble; we just want to make sure everything's okay and see if there's anything you need. We know life can get busy, and this message is simply here to help if something's come up.

This message is only sent to you - Supervisors won't see it. We hope it gives you a chance to reflect on your own needs such as how you are feeling about wrangling and your availability on your own time.

As a reminder, wrangling policies ask everyone to wrangle at least once every two weeks. If there's still no sign of wrangling activity on your account a week from today (7 days), a note will go out to the wrangling Supervisors to follow up and check-in with you.

Feel free to reply to this email if:

  • You're having technical issues accessing the Archive.
  • You're still in training and need some help with getting started.
  • You need more tags in order to wrangle regularly.
  • You'd like a mentor, a cheerleading buddy, or you have any questions Supervisors can help with.
  • You believe this email was sent in error and you have been wrangling in the last 3 weeks.
  • Anything else is going on and you'd like to talk about it.

If you've already told wrangling Supervisors you're on a break, you can ignore this message. Supervisors have your date of return on the vacation board and will check-in to see how things are going once you’re back, so no further action is needed on your part.

If you're in need of an extended break or you need to take a formal hiatus, you can reply to this email or use the <%= style_link("Wrangler Hiatus & Retirement Form", "https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/PLACEHOLDER") %>.

If you would like to see the last wrangled date that's been logged for your account, you can find this located at the top of your wrangling page between the Assigned fandoms text and the fandoms you have assigned to yourself. This information is only visible to yourself and wrangling admin accounts.

Thanks so much for all the work you do. We really appreciate it! Please let us know if there's anything we can do to support you.

Best,
AO3

column1: Works removed from a subcollection by their creator remain attached to the subcollection as an approved work
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
If a work is added to a subcollection and the creator subsequently edits the work and removes the collection, it isn't fully purged from the subcollection. The work blurb no longer lists the collection, and the collection's work index no longer contains the work; however, it remains on the "Approved" list under "Manage Items" and continues to be counted in the Works (#) menu item.

*Steps to reproduce:*
# Create a parent collection
# Create a subcollection
# Post a work adding it to the subcollection
# Edit the work and remove the subcollection, select Update

*What happens:*
* The Works (#) menu item for both the parent and subcollection has not decreased
* The work is no longer listed in the Works index for either collection
* The collection is no longer listed on the blurb
* The work remains attached to the collection and can be found by the collection moderator by going to Manage Items -> Approved

*What should happen:*
* The work's association with the collection should be fully removed
* The works count for the subcollection and parent collection should be updated

09/Sep/20 8:46 PM;557058:1f736697-06a8-4e0f-8399-e9cf7c29b7ce;Okay, so replying to a comment requires updating the parent comment's `threaded_left` and `threaded_right` values. And Comment's [check_for_spam|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/08bda2c87f64cbe36d74b01f0616299ea3e161f9/app/models/comment.rb#L381] validation will run right before the updated parent comment is saved to the database. In this validation method, the `approved` value is overwritten with {{Rails.env.test? || !self.pseud_id.nil? || !Akismetor.spam?(akismet_attributes)}}.

If the parent comment was manually marked as spam, that means Akismetor most likely didn't mark that comment as spam when it was first posted. And so `approved` would most likely be overwritten with `true` when this validation runs.

The `mark_as_spam!` and `mark_as_ham!` methods use `update_attribute`, which skips validation, so that's why the unexpected `approved` overwriting doesn't happen when someone presses "Spam" or "Not Spam" on a guest comment.

This miiiight be related to AO3-5972? Comment's [destroy_or_mark_deleted|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/08bda2c87f64cbe36d74b01f0616299ea3e161f9/lib/plugins/acts_as_commentable/comment_methods.rb#L33] method uses `self.save`, which would run validations before saving. Maybe Akismetor flags "deleted comment" as spam?

So to prevent being able to reply to a spam comment, I was thinking about maybe adding a validation that checks that the parent is not spam. But I think this validation would need to be scoped (only for creation? is that possible?), otherwise there would be a validation error when trying to edit or possibly even delete a comment that's replying to a parent comment that was marked as spam sometime after the fact.

I'm not sure what to do about the check_for_spam validation. Is it desirable behaviour, rerunning a spam check on a guest comment every time someone replies to it?

column1: Gateway timeout, broken pipe, or connection reset error when updating spam status of works on either the admin spam page or individual work pages
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
*URLs:* 

* The admin spam page, i.e. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/spam|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/spam,] 
* individual work pages, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/123|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/123]

*Note:* This is probably related to submission to the spam checker, which only happens in production mode.

Occasionally, when attempting to bulk update moderated works on the admin spam page, e.g. by selecting the "Mark As Not Spam" checkbox for all works on a given page, you get a site-styled 500 error or a plain white 504 error. In New Relic, the 500 error appears as {{Errno::EPIPE: Broken pipe}} or {{Errno::ECONNRESET: Connection reset by peer}}.

Often, it is possible to work around this by selecting fewer works, or fewer lengthy works. However, PAC notes that Russian and to a lesser extent Chinese works are far more likely to 500, regardless of word count, and that the word count threshold for erroring is lower for these two languages.

This error also sometimes happens when attempting to mark a single work as spam or not spam from the work page itself. The work this happens to is usually long: I've seen it on a work of 30,000 words and another of 715,000. In both cases, refreshing several moments later revealed the works had been correctly marked as not spam.

Experimentation suggests {{Errno::EPIPE: Broken pipe}} results in the works (or work) not getting updated, while the works do get updated despite 504 errors or {{Errno::ECONNRESET: Connection reset by peer}}. In about 40 minutes of experimentation, I encountered (1) 504 error, (4) broken pipe errors, and about (15) connection reset errors. 

The 504 and broken pipes only happened on {{Admin::SpamController#bulk_update}}, whereas the connection reset happened for {{Admin::SpamController#bulk_update}} and {{Admin::UserCreationsController#set_spam}}.

It might help to queue the submission of the works to the spam checker. 

It would probably also be useful to include the works' word counts on [https://archiveofourown.org/admin/spam,|https://archiveofourown.org/admin/spam,] so PAC can more easily determine which works are likely to give them trouble.

column30:
In order to prevent users from creating misleading usernames, or usernames that cause technical difficulties, we need to be able to prevent them from creating accounts with certain names. These restrictions will also apply when renaming accounts.

* For now, we only need to prevent the use of exact usernames, e.g. we might want to prevent someone from using "admin," but it should not prevent them from using "my_exchange_admin." (We might do partial names later.)
* The list of banned usernames should be in the config file. Please do not use "blacklist" in the setting name.
* The ban should apply to guest commenter names as well as usernames.

h1. Testing

h2. Phase 1 (Done!)

The list of banned usernames is empty, as it will initially be on production (see Notes). 

Make sure you can:

* create an account.
* rename an account.
* comment while logged in.
* comment while logged out.

h2. Phase 2 (Done!)

The list of banned usernames will be updated to include {{ao3user}}, which is not currently in use on staging, and {{testy8}}, {{testy9}}, and {{testy10}}, which are currently in use.

Make sure you cannot:

* create an account with the banned username “ao3user”.
* rename an account to use the banned username “ao3user”.
* comment as a guest using one of the banned usernames.

But that you can:

* use the banned username as part of a username, e.g. if "ao3user" is banned, you can create an account named "ao3username."
* comment using a name that contains the banned username, e.g., if "ao3user" is banned, you can comment as "ao3username."
* log in as one of the banned testy names.
* comment while logged in to an account with one of the banned testy names.
** if you’d like to test other actions, e.g., posting a work, requesting and using a password reset, and/or changing your password, please do it here before renaming the testy account! 
* change your username from one of the banned testy names to a name that isn’t banned. (Please note what the new name is so we can set it back in the next phase!)

h2. Phase 3 (Ready to test!)

The banned usernames list will be emptied.

* rename the testy accounts to their previous names.
* make an account named “ao3user.”
* comment as a guest using one of the previously banned names.

h1. Notes

Before banned usernames can be fully implemented, it will be necessary to determine which of the names we want to ban are currently in use. These usernames will likely need to be changed, or the user may have difficulty accessing or updating their account, similar to the way issues with pseud icons or descriptions block password resets ([https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3589#icft=AO3-3589|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3589#icft=AO3-3589|smart-link]).

However, this need not prevent us from writing, testing, and deploying the code. Any names currently in use can be excluded from the banned username list until existing accounts are dealt with.

column1: Rails BOT: Mailer jobs stop eager loading HtmlCleaner in Resque 2.0
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
*How to reproduce*

Submit either the Support form (https://test.archiveofourown.org/support) or the Policy & Abuse form (https://test.archiveofourown.org/abuse_reports/new). You should receive an email copy of your submission, and the proper Zoho tickets will be created. However, the email copy of your submission will not be sent to the admin mailing lists. There are errors like this in Resque:
{code}
Worker
    test-app15:83486 on mailer at about 5 hours ago 
Class
    ActionMailer::DeliveryJob (via ActiveJob) 
Arguments

    ---
    job_class: ActionMailer::DeliveryJob
    job_id: 622c9b63-9cf9-42be-8b01-e461adb92388
    provider_job_id: 
    queue_name: mailer
    priority: 
    arguments:
    - AdminMailer
    - feedback
    - deliver_now
    - 15005
    executions: 0
    locale: en

Exception
    NoMethodError
Error
    undefined method `strip_html_breaks_simple' for #<AdminMailer:0x0000555e476c7820>
{code}

*Notes*: thanks to [~tickinginstant] for finding the root cause in AO3-5991.
{quote}
The {{app/models/skin.rb}} file calls {{include HtmlCleaner}}, but it calls it outside of the {{Skin}} class, which means that if the {{Skin}} class is loaded, all methods in {{HtmlCleaner}} will be available to all objects (including {{AdminMailer}}). But if the {{Skin}} class isn’t loaded, those methods won’t be available.

In testing and development, the factories are loaded, including {{factories/skins.rb}}, which accesses the constant {{Skin}} in its definition (instead of passing {{"Skin"}} as an argument to avoid loading it). In staging and production, however, {{FactoryBot}} isn’t included, and so the skin factory isn’t guaranteed to be loaded, and neither is {{app/models/skin.rb}}. This means that {{lib/html_cleaner.rb}} isn’t guaranteed to be included. That explains why it can’t be replicated in development (at least not without changing the skin factory definition).

This appears to caused by the 5.2 upgrade rather than the ActiveJob switch, because it looks like the Resque workers don’t load {{Skin}} both in {{master}} and {{master~}} (the version before this PR was merged), but do load {{Skin}} in {{master~3}} (the version before the 5.2 PR was merged).

More specifically, I think this may have been caused by upgrading Resque to 2.0. The new version was changed to respect the {{eager_load}} config setting, but apparently there’s an issue with rake and {{eager_load}} that can cause issues with Resque 2.0: [https://github.com/resque/resque/issues/1680|https://github.com/resque/resque/issues/1680|smart-link]. Unfortunately, {{rake_eager_load}} isn’t available in 5.2. Maybe instead it’d be better to manually add {{include HtmlCleaner}} to the {{AdminMailer}} file, and possibly modify the includes in {{app/models/skin.rb}} so that we don’t run into loading issues again in the future.
{quote}

To fix the issue, we should do all of the following:

- Explicitly include {{HtmlCleaner}} in {{AdminMailer}}.
- Fix {{factories/skins.rb}} to avoid directly referencing {{Skin}} and loading it; instead use {{factory :skin}} like other factories, and have {{:private_work_skin}} as a child factory.
- Move the {{include}} statements in {{app/models/skin.rb}} inside the class to avoid similar loading issues in the future: https://docs.rubocop.org/rubocop/0.86/cops_style.html#stylemixinusage.

column1: Wrangle tags page for a character cannot sort relationships by created date or taggings count
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
*How to reproduce*

# Log in as a wrangler, e.g. testy.
# Visit the page to wrangle relationships for any character tag, for example: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Bruce%20Wayne/wrangle?show=relationships|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Bruce%20Wayne/wrangle?show=relationships].
# Sort by "Created" or "Taggings".

*What happens*

The relationships are sorted by name (ascending), then by our selection as a secondary sort. This is somewhat hard to tell on the first page, because the primary sort uses "sortable_name", which a number of tags on the test site lack (e.g. "bruce wayne/tamara (supernatural)").

*What should happen*

The relationships should be sorted by our selection across pagination. In the case of "Taggings", the relationships should have a secondary sort by name (ascending) as a tie-breaker.

*Note*

For a character, {{.relationships}} has [an implicit order|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/54c7496ea8f717b0434ce4e550a5c0211649c985/app/models/character.rb#L18]. When applying our sort selection [in the controller|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/54c7496ea8f717b0434ce4e550a5c0211649c985/app/controllers/tags_controller.rb#L288-L297], we should use {{.reorder}}.

column1: Replace ActiveSupport::Cache::DalliStore with ActiveSupport::Cache::MemCacheStore
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
We are currently using ActiveSupport::Cache::DalliStore, provided by Dalli. This cache store implementation:

- [does not support the race_condition_ttl option|https://github.com/petergoldstein/dalli/pull/560],
- [does not fully support cache versioning and recyclable cache keys|https://github.com/petergoldstein/dalli/issues/710] (we are currently not using this feature, but we'd like to when we eventually get to Rails 6),
- [will eventually be deprecated in Dalli 3|https://github.com/petergoldstein/dalli/issues/573].

We should switch to [ActiveSupport::Cache::MemCacheStore|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/v5.2/caching_with_rails.html#activesupport-cache-memcachestore], which is provided by Rails and also uses Dalli underneath.

*Before deploying*:
Update the parents of the default skin:
{code:ruby}
Skin.default.update(role: "site", skin_parents_attributes: [{ position: 1, parent_skin_title: "Archive 2.0" }])
{code}
In case we need to undo that:
{code:ruby}
Skin.transaction do
  skin = Skin.default
  skin.parent_skins = []
  skin.update(role: "user")
end
{code}

*After deploying*: we need to flush the cache.
{code:ruby}
Rails.cache.clear
{code}

*How to test*: Rails 5.2 regression testing should cover this (e.g. "Is it later already?" works on the home page).

Some skin-specific test cases:

- As a user, make a custom skin that overrides the site skin, and start using it. Make sure that the skin is included in subsequent page loads. Then try editing the skin, and make sure that the changes are immediately reflected on the next page you visit.
- As a user, make a custom skin that adds onto the site skin, and start using it. Make sure that the skin is included in subsequent page loads. Then try editing the skin, and make sure that the changes are immediately reflected on the next page you visit.
- As an admin, go to Skins > Approved Skins, check "Chooser" for one of the listed skins, and press "Update." Then check the footer to make sure that the skin you selected is listed under "Choose Skin."
- As an admin, go back to the Approved Skins page, check "Not In Chooser" for the same skin, and press "Update." Then check the footer to make sure that the skin is no longer listed under "Choose Skin."

*Steps to reproduce:*

# Log in as User A
# Create an unrevealed collection
# Post a work to the unrevealed collection
# Make note of the work's URL
# Log out as User A
# Log in as User B
# Post a work that cites User A's unrevealed work as inspiration

*What happens:*

The note on user B's work includes the title and creator of the unrevealed work. This is also true of the downloads.

*What should happen:*

It should say, “Inspired by a work in an unrevealed collection.” 

(We tell logged out users that a work is “Inspired by [Restricted Work] by User A” when the parent is restricted, so saying something even though you can’t _see_ the work is consistent.)

*Testing notes:*

column1: Fix indexing error that sometimes occurs when deleting works
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When a work is deleted around the time that it's being reindexed, the indexing code will sometimes load the work, but not be able to find its stat counter. (They're both deleted in the same transaction, but the indexing code loads the work first, and then tries to find its stat counter later.) This results in a {{NoMethodError}} when calling {{comments_count}}, {{kudos_count}}, and {{bookmarks_count}}, all of which expect the {{stat_counter}} to exist, and all of which are included in the work's JSON document.

This error causes all other works in the same batch to fail to be indexed, which may contribute to AO3-5290.

*Testing Instructions:* This is an intermittent bug, so I'm not sure it can be consistently replicated. Probably the best policy with this is to deploy it, and check Resque a few days later to see if the error is still happening.

column1: Avoid BadRequest errors when indexing empty batches
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When one of the indexing classes generates an empty batch (either because the list of items it's indexing is empty, or because it doesn't need to make any changes to the index), it will submit an empty list to {{$elasticsearch.bulk(body: batch)}}. This causes a {{Elasticsearch::Transport::Transport::Errors::BadRequest}} error.

Because this error only occurs when the indexing classes are trying to submit zero changes to Elasticsearch, this doesn't affect functionality in any way, but it'd be nice to reduce the number of errors in Resque.

*Testing Instructions:* I think it would be best to check this in production by waiting a few days and checking whether the error shows up in Resque.

(I think this occurs when deleting bookmarks, because multiple people viewing a page with a deleted bookmark during the same second could cause the {{IndexSweeper}} to create two jobs with identical Redis keys. That results in the second job running with an empty batch. But that's probably pretty difficult to replicate on demand, so I think it's better to check production, where it happens on average 10+ times per day.)

{quote}Published: 2020-11-22 Words: 4 Chapters: 1/1 Hits: 0{quote}

{quote}Published: 2020-11-22 Words: 4{quote}

{quote}Published: 2020-11-22 Chapters: 2/2 Words: 6{quote}

h1. What should happen

The chapter count in the download should be *after* the word count, just like it is on the work show page. 

Additionally, it should say Chapters: 1/1 (as opposed to the current blankness) if the work only has one chapter.

column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Post > New Work
# Fill in required information
# Check "This work is part of a series" 
# Fill in "Or create a new one" with the title for a new series, e.g. "My New Series"
# Post

h1. What happens

The fact that the work is in a series is mentioned in a variety of places, and the phrasing isn't entirely consistent across locations:

*Work blurb displayed on work listings:* Part 1 of My New Series
*Meta on work show page:* Part 1 of the My New Series series
*Series section at bottom of work show page:* Part 1 of the My New Series series
*Meta on work download file:* Part 1 of My New Series
*Creator subscription email:* Part 1 of My New Series 

h1. What should happen instead

We'd like to update the phrasing on the work show page. Both the meta and series section should just say "Part 1 of My New Series," not "Part 1 of the My New Series series." 

This means there’s less awkwardness when your series includes “The” at the start or “Series” at the end, plus it gives you the ability to just… not refer to your series as a series, e.g. if you’re just looking for a way to link all of the works you’ve created around a fandom/theme.

column1: Save last read location on chapters or works in browsers
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
This is a bare-bones issue and requirements are subject to change:

- Last read location should be stored using localStorage.
- When a user visits a work or chapter, ask them "Do you want to have your read position saved locally on your device? Your location will not be stored centrally, this preference can be change by accessing local preferences in the page footer" if we've never asked them before. Their preference will apply to all works/chapters visited from the same browser.
-- If they have agreed to have the read location saved, jump to the read location. 
- Works in single page mode and in chapter-by-chapter mode should have separate read locations.
- When a user finishes reading a work or chapter, the last read location should be removed.
- As a user scrolls on a work/chapter, the last read location should be re-saved.
- There should be a local preferences page, linked in the Archive's footer.
-- This page should detect and warn if localStorage is not supported by the browser.
-- This page should allow users to enable or disable saving last read location.
- There should be a page listing which works/chapters currently have last read locations saved locally. Users will have options to resume reading works/chapters, delete last read locations for works/chapters, and as a stretch goal, export/import last read locations.

column1: Use data-* attributes for autocomplete
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
*What happens*

The autocomplete HTML currently uses attributes like {{autocomplete_no_results_text}} and {{autocomplete_hint_text}}. They _work_ fine, but if you run a page with an autocomplete field through an [HTML validator|https://validator.w3.org], it complains because those aren't actual HTML attributes.

*What should happen*

We want to use HTML5 {{data-*}} attributes (e.g. {{data-autocomplete-no-results-text}} or {{data-autocomplete-hint-text}}) for the autocomplete's custom attributes. This means we won't get as many validation errors on our HTML.

*Testing*

The behavior should not change. 

If you want to run the new version through a validator while it's on staging, you'll probably need to copy the page source and paste it in on the Validate by Direct Input tab, since the password protection on staging will probably prevent the validator from accessing the page.

*Notes*

This was pulled out of AO3-3306.

Groundwork for the user-facing aspects of collection tags.

* The {{Filterable}} module should be included in the {{Collection}} model.
* The unused [+*fandoms*+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b5bf2e7a5cd362d1e350f2be087e8049721a2484/app/models/collection.rb#L64-L65][ +and+ |https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b5bf2e7a5cd362d1e350f2be087e8049721a2484/app/models/collection.rb#L64-L65][+*filters*+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b5bf2e7a5cd362d1e350f2be087e8049721a2484/app/models/collection.rb#L64-L65][ +associations+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b5bf2e7a5cd362d1e350f2be087e8049721a2484/app/models/collection.rb#L64-L65] should be removed from the {{Collection}} model.
* To reduce code duplication while enabling the use of brand new (i.e. unsorted) tags on collections, the {{Bookmark}} model's {{tag_string}} and {{tag_string= }}methods should be moved into the {{Taggable}} concern. The {{Bookmark}} model should then be updated to include {{Taggable}}, which will also be included in the {{Collection}} model via {{Filterable}}.
* The number of tags that can be applied to a collection should initially be limited to 10, and the number should be configurable.
* There should be a migration adding two boolean columns, which will not yet be exposed in the interface, to the {{collections}} table:
** {{multifandom}} will allow a collection's owners to specify the collection is not meant to be fandom-specific (e.g. the [+/r/FanFiction Saddest Fanfic Recs collection+|https://archiveofourown.org/collections/FanFiction_Reddit_Saddest]). This will be necessary because the limit on the number of collection tags means they cannot tag every fandom featured in the collection.
** {{open_doors}} will indicate a collection corresponds with an archive rescued by the OTW's Open Doors project.

*Testing*

* Creating a collection should work normally
* A collection's Fandoms page should work normally
* Bookmark tags should work as normal, particularly creating a never-before-used tag
* Migration should run successfully, up and down

column1: Sinhala characters with extensions separated into two characters when posting from HTML (non-RTE) text field
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
*From Translation:*

{quote}Sinhala has extensions to combine two tones together, and that allows them to spell out these two tones by using just the one letter. And apparently, all of these extensions get separated on AO3. So one character becomes two.

Example, in Sinhala, it's possible to write the sound 'gri' with just the one letter, and on AO3, 'gri' appears as two letters, ie 'g' and 'ri', which is incorrect.{quote}

*Note:* For the test case, we are pasting from Google Docs. This probably isn't relevant, but could be.

If you paste the Sinhala word {{ප්‍රදානය}} into a text field that does not have the Rich Text editor active (e.g. comment form, news post form in HTML mode, work form in HTML mode) and press post, it separates the first character into two characters. The word becomes {{ප්රදානය}}.

If, however, you either:

* paste into the RTE
* paste into the HTML editor and then toggle to the RTE

then the work remains in the correct 5-character form: {{ප්‍රදානය}}.

Toggling _back_ to the HTML editor _after_ doing one of the above – but _before_ pressing post – will show you that, at some point in the process, it has been converted to {{ප්‍රදානය}}, which allows it to display correctly when posted. 

(Note that _after_ posting, you won't see it as {{ප්‍රදානය}} in the HTML editor, much like you wouldn't see {{ }} – you'd see a space as described in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3554|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3554|smart-link].)

The desired behavior, of course, is that after posting, the word should continue to be the 5-character form {{ප්‍රදානය}}.

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Post a work (but this mainly happens on news posts)
# Leave a comment on the work
# Log out
# Leave 25 more comments on the work (top level, not threaded)
# Log in as the work creator
# Go to the comment section with all the spam
# Mark all but the first and last comments as spam

h1. What happens

There are still two pages of comments, but each page only displays one comment.

h1. What should happen

There should be one page with two comments, because the spam comments should not count toward pagination. 

Note: a comment can be marked as spam, but have non-spam replies that we should show.

column1: Automatically apply tags to news post translations
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Currently, it's necessary to enter the tags for each translation of a news post. This creates extra work for Translation. It also increases the odds of us ending up with unwanted tags due to typos.

To prevent this, we'd like to make it so translations of news posts automatically acquire the tags of the non-translated news post.

* When you use the "Translation of" field on a news post and press "Post," any tags you have entered in the "Tags" field should be ignored, and instead the tags of the original post should be applied.
** There should be a note under the "Translation of" field that says, "Tags from the selected post will replace any tags entered on this page."
* When editing a translation, the note under the “Translation of” field should not be displayed, nor should the text input for the "Tags" section. Instead, the tags should be listed as simple, uneditable text.
* When the tags on a news post are updated, any translations of that post should also have their tags updated.

h1. Deleted user

*Note:* If you don’t have an account with unused invitations, you'll need to log in as an admin and go to {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/invitations}} to grant some.  

# Log in to an account with unused invitations _and_ which you don't mind deleting

# Choose and invitation and enter an email to send it to
# Make note of the invitation token (the keysmash)
# Press "Send Invitation"
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Profile > Delete My Account
# Confirm that you want to delete the account
# Log out
# Log in as an admin
# Invitations > Invite New Users
# In the "Track invitations" section of the form, fill in the "Invitation token" field with the token of the invitation you sent
# Press "Go"

h2. Deleted admin

# Ask a database admin to create a throwaway admin account for you (ideally using the Gmail {{+}} trick with your usual admin email address)
# Log in
# Invitations > Invite New Users
# Under “Send to email,” enter an email address (ideally one you own)
# Submit
# Log out of your throwaway admin account
# Ask a database admin to delete your throwaway admin account
# Log in to your usual admin account
# Invitations > Invite New Users
# Under “Track invitations,” enter the email address you sent the invitation to in Step 4

Under "Sender," it says queue, which we know is a lie.

It should say {{Deleted user}} or {{Deleted admin}} as appropriate.

Looking at {{updated_at}} is also misleading, because in those cases the chapter will still be updated (we set the {{content_sanitizer_version}} column to -1 to force a sanitizer rerun, which will set it back to 1, bumping the timestamp twice in the process).

*Follow-up to* [*AO3-5615*|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5615]*.*

# Log in as a tag wrangler
# Hi, username\! > Tag Wrangling
# In the "Fandoms" column of the table, follow the link to one of your fandoms.
# In the sidebar, there is a list of tag types (Characters, Relationships, Freeforms). Follow the link for one of those that has a count greater than 0 to access the fandom's "bin" for that type of tag, e.g. the character bin.
# Follow the "Edit" link for one of the non-canonical, non-synonimized tags listed in the table.
# Check the "Unwrangleable" checkbox and press "Save changes" to mark the tag unwrangleable.
# Repeat steps 2-4 to access the same "bin" once again.
# Follow the "Unwrangleable" link to access a table of just the tags you've marked unwrangleable (of that tag type and in that fandom, of course).
# In the "Manage" column, check the "Remove" box for a tag and press "Wrangle."

*What happens*

The tag is removed from the fandom and remains unwrangleable. This makes it impossible to find.

column1: Standardize email greetings and closings for i18n
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Our emails have several different greetings and closings + signature, most of which are used in multiple emails. As it stands, Translation has to translate the current greeting and closing + signature multiple times, which is unnecessary and tedious.

What we're going to do is make it so they're reusable across emails. That way, Translation can just translate each one once and be done with it.

List subject to tweaking.

*EXISTING GREETINGS*

* {{Hi !}} for
** feedback - copy of support ticket if you haven't provided a name
* {{Hi %name!}} for
** invite_increase_notification - here are some new invitations to hand out
** feedback - copy of support ticket, if you provided a name
* {{Hello from the Archive of Our Own!}} for
** invitation - here's the invitation you requested/someone sent you
** invitation_to_claim - claim some works we imported on your behalf
** claim_notification - we imported some works and the email we used matched your account, so we automatically added them to your account
* {{Dear %name,}} for
** delete_work_notification - you or a co-creator deleted your work
**  invite_request_declined - your request for invitations to share was declined
** anonymous_or_unrevealed_notification - your work's anonymous or unrevealed status changed
** invited_to_collection_notification - your work has been invited to collection
** added_to_collection_notification - your work has been added to collection
** admin_spam_work_notification - your work has been marked as spam and hidden automatically
**  admin_hidden_work_notification - your work has been hidden by an admin
** admin_deleted_work_notification - your work was deleted by an admin
* {{Hello, %name!}}
**  recipient_notification - someone gave you a gift work
* {{Dear Collection Maintainers!}} for
** potential_match_generation_notification - exchange matching has been completed
**  invalid_signup_notification - exchange matching can't be run
** collection_notification - you have received a message about your collection (unused notification, afaik)

*CHANGES TO GREETINGS*

* {{Hi %name!}} + {{Hello, %name!}} will be {{Hi, %name!}}
* {{Dear Collection Maintainers!}} will be removed.
* {{Hi !}} will no longer have an extra space.
* {{%name}} will always be bold in HTML emails. (This was inconsistent before.)
* {{%name}} will always be username for users. (This was inconsistent before.)

*EXISTING CLOSINGS & SIGNATURES*

* {{Regards,}} for
** invite_request_declined - "AO3"
** feedback - "the AO3 Support team"
* {{Best,}} for
** invitation_to_claim - "The Open Doors team \\n Organization for Transformative Works"
** claim_notification - "The Open Doors team \\n Organization for Transformative Works"
* {{Thanks!}} for
** invited_to_collection_notification - no signature
** added_to_collection_notification - no signature
* {{Sincerely,}} for
** admin_spam_work_notification - "AO3 Abuse"
** admin_hidden_work_notification - "AO3 Abuse"
* {{Cheers,}} for
** invite_increase_notification - "AO3"

*CHANGES TO CLOSINGS & SIGNATURES*

* {{Regards,}} + {{Sincerely,}} will be {{Sincerely,}}
* {{Best,}} + {{Cheers,}} will be {{Best,}}
* {{Thanks!}} will be removed.
* Abuse’s signature will be removed from admin_spam_work_notification, admin_hidden_work_notification,
* Support’s signature will be updated to {{The AO3 Support team}}, with a capital “T.” If other team names are added, they should use the format {{The [Committee Name] team}}. (Open Doors will keep the org name.)
* Signatures will now be bold in HTML emails. (This was inconsistent before.)

*BONUS CHANGES*

* Email subjects will now be consistently sentence case.
*  {{Abuse Team}} will be {{Policy & Abuse team}} in the:
** subject of admin_hidden_work_notification
** text of admin_spam_work_notification, admin_hidden_work_notification, and admin_deleted_work_notification

column1: Configure Phrase 3: Locale Eater
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Working with Translation to get Phrase ready for them to start on translating the emails. In our current setup after [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5806|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5806|smart-link], Phrase will push and pull from the same set of files. This will cause conflicts with changes from coders, as well as changes from the original source of our locale files (rails-i18n) when we need to update them.

Requirements: inside config/locales,

* "en" files are only edited by coders (custom order, code comments that should not be overwritten by Phrase);
* files imported from rails-i18n are also only edited by coders;
* all other locale files are generated by Phrase, should not be edited by coders, should not include the default locale "en", and should not re-export the translations from rails-i18n.

The application will use everything in config/locales - so coders can edit "en" files and immediately see changes without waiting for a push-pull round trip with Phrase.

*Testing*:

Let’s do a smoke test to make sure the locale files are getting loaded.

* Log in, post a work, and then delete the work. You should get an email about the work being deleted and it should look normal, i.e. not say “translation missing.”
* Make an unsuccessful attempt to log in as an admin, e.g. by entering the wrong username. You should get a blue flash error message and not, say, a 500 page or some text saying “translation missing.”

When this is merged, we'll want to export from Phrase via GitHub Sync to get all of the existing translations. 

Once _that_ is merged, we'll want to import to Phrase to make sure all of the English is correct -- search for "part12" and make sure it doesn't include the term "whitelist" to verify.

10/May/21 4:22 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;Another issue: when we change text, we don’t always change the translation key. This means that using GitHub Sync with our current settings does not update the text Translation has to work with:

{quote}By default Phrase will only extract new content and thus not delete or update any existing keys in your localization project. Phrase will scan your file and only import new keys or translations that are not already stored inside Phrase. *No data will be lost* by uploading files. However, if you want to overwrite existing data, respectively replace your Phrase project resources with the content from your localization file, we do offer the *Update translations* option. This option is available within the Translation Center upload interface and via the [API|https://developers.phrase.com/api/#uploads]. Your existing translations will be overwritten with the content of the uploaded localization file.{quote}

(That’s from the [Uploading localization files help page|https://help.phrase.com/help/uploading-localization-files].)

That means we need to add {{update_translations: true}} to our push config, as described on the [Setting up the Phrase Client help page|https://help.phrase.com/help/configuration]:

{noformat}push:
    sources:
    - file: ./locales/en.json
       params:
        update_translations: true {noformat}

(Scroll down to the “Parameters” section; they don’t seem to have skip links.)

I’m not 100% sure we want to include this change in this issue, however – it might be better to do it separately, once we’re sure the new push/pull set up is working, so we don’t accidentally override anything.

Until we do this, Translation should use the Upload Files function and the “Update translations” checkbox.

Currently, the {{#kudos}} element at the bottom of works contains a list of all users who have ever given kudos to the work. column1: Autocomplete menu remains open after selecting an item
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Sometimes, if you enter text in an autocomplete field, the list of suggestions does not close after you've made your selection. It remains open, covering other items on the page you might want to access.

!open_autocomplete (a98918a7-e946-43bd-bf5c-30fbb07dca91).png|width=1280,height=1078!

This is most likely to happen on fields that disappear once you've reached the maximum number of items you can enter (e.g. the "Synonym of" field on tags' edit pages, which only allows you to enter one tag; tag fields on various challenge sign-up forms, which limit you to a number specified in the challenge settings; tag set nomination forms, which limit you to one tag per field), but there is also a report of it happening on the new work form, which doesn't have any fields like that.

For *testing*, refer to the comments below the issue. The easiest way to reproduce it on demand seems to be as follows. We'll use a tag edit page's "Synonym of" field for this example, which you need to be a tag wrangler to access:

# Quickly type the name of a tag in the "Synonym of" field, e.g. Sherlock Holmes
# While the blue "Searching..." indicator is displayed, quickly press tab, Enter/Return, or the comma key, which will finalize your input, make the text input area disappear, and move keyboard focus to the ×
# When the search completes, the autocomplete menu will open even though you've moved on

If you experience this and you want to close the menu, you can use the × to remove the selection from the broken field and then make your selection more slowly (i.e. don't press the comma, Enter/Return, or Tab until the list of suggestions is visible).

column1: Make it Impossible to Assign Non-Canonical Fandoms to Wranglers
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Currently wranglers can assign themselves to any and all fandom tags, including those which are not yet wrangled and those which have been wrangled, but have been synned to another fandom tag rather than canonized. 

Once assigned to a wrangler, non-canonical fandom tags are challenging to remove and the assigning of these tags sometimes leads to disputes and personnel issues for a variety of reasons. Basically it's a big ol' hassle for everyone involved and since the update which caused canonical tags to display the tags in their syns, there is no longer any reason for this to be something wranglers can do as there is no benefit to it. Consequently, we'd like it to be made impossible to assign a wrangler or for a wrangler to assign themselves to any fandom tag that has not already been made canonical. 

If there is a way to make it so fandom tags are not a valid target to assign to wranglers until they have been marked canonical, that would probably be best, but we will gladly take any solution that keeps fandom tags that are non-canonical from being assigned to wranglers going forward. Thank you! <3

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

The counts for Works, Bookmarked Items, and Fandoms in the collection sidebar, as well as the counts on collection fandoms pages, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/yuletide/fandoms|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/yuletide/fandoms], are hell on the database.

We'd like to cache the Works, Bookmarked Items, and Fandoms counts in the sidebar for 5 minutes. We’d also like to cache the list of fandoms and their individual counts for 5 minutes (long term, we’d like to also start getting these counts via the Elasticsearch works index). This will help without creating too substantial a delay in new fandoms/changes in fandom counts appearing.

*Notes:*

It may be necessary to resolve [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5285|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5285|smart-link] while working on this.

## the fandom should appear on the collection's fandoms page
## the Fandoms count in the sidebar should increase
## the Works count in the sidebar should increase.
# While logged in, go to a collection’s Fandoms page (this will ensure the page and the sidebar are in the cache). Post a work to that collection. The work should be in a canonical fandom that has previously been in the collection. After about 5 minutes:

column1: Require users to opt in to having their works invited to collections
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
*On users' Preferences pages:*

* remove "Automatically agree to your work being collected by others in the Archive."
* add "Allow others to invite my works to collections." This should be unchecked by default.

This will require a migration, which should use [pt-online-schema-change|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Migrations#Using_ptonlineschemachange].

The migration should only add the new column. We'll remove the old one in a follow-up deploy.

The description of the old preference should be removed from the help pop-up ({{help/collection-preferences.html}}).

Docs may provide a description for the new preference.

*When "Allow others to invite my works to collections." is unchecked:*

When none of the creators of a work has checked "Allow others to invite my works to collections.", the "Add To Collections" button should be removed from the work. (Creators can always edit the work itself to add it to a collection.) 

Removing the button itself is not sufficient, however; there should also be a back end check to prevent inviting works whose creators do not allow invitations from collections.

*When "Allow others to invite my works to collections." is checked:*

The behavior when "Allow others to invite my works to collections." is checked should be the same as the existing behavior when "Automatically agree to your work being collected by others in the Archive." is unchecked.

That is, if one of a work's creators has enabled the preference, the "Add To Collections" option should be available on the work. 

When a collection moderator fills in the name of their collection, each creator of the work should receive a copy of the {{invited_to_collection_notification}} email. The work should not be added to the collection until one of its creators has approved its inclusion.

The text and HTML versions of the {{invited_to_collection_notification}} email should be updated to remove the paragraph mentioning how to enable automatic approval.

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a tag wrangler

# In the "Name" field, enter a tag name that's never been used on the site before. For this example, I'll use "6102 Variation Whoo," but you'll need to make your own.
# Select the "Additional Tag" category
# Press "Create Tag" to be taken to the edit page for the new tag
# Check the "Unwrangleable" checkbox
# In the "Fandoms" section, enter "Testing" in the "Add Fandoms" field
# Press "Save changes," which will update the tag and take you back to the edit page
# In the "Fandoms" section, check the checkbox next to the "Testing" tag to remove it
# Press "Save changes"

h1. What happens

The page will reload with an error:

Sorry\! We couldn't save this additional tag because:

* Unwrangleable can't be set on a tag with no fandoms.

However, if you shrug your shoulders and give up here, the tag will be saved, and it will be unwrangleable and have no fandoms. To see this, copy the URL for the tag's edit page and paste it into a new tab. You'll discover the tag has no fandoms and the "Unwrangleable" checkbox is indeed checked.

h1. What should happen

The tag should keep its fandom and its unwrangleable status.

h1. Notes

The “ignore the error” method also works on existing tags, not just new ones.

column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

First, we'll need a work with a tag that is unwrangleable and that doesn't have a fandom. There are two ways to do this:

* [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6102#icft=AO3-6102|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6102#icft=AO3-6102|smart-link]
* [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6121#icft=AO3-6121|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6121#icft=AO3-6121|smart-link]

We're going to do this using AO3-6102.

# Log in as testy, who wrangles the "Testing" fandom
# Post > New Work
# Fill in required fields, including filling in "Fandoms" with "Testing"
# Fill in "Additional Tags" with a tag that's never been used on the site before. For this example, I'll use "testing new [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5615#icft=AO3-5615|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5615#icft=AO3-5615|smart-link] bug," but you'll need to make your own.
# Go to the unwrangled freeform page for the Testing fandom: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/wrangle?show=freeforms&status=unwrangled|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/wrangle?show=freeforms&status=unwrangled]
# Locate the tag you made
# Check the checkbox to the left of the tag name
# Enter "Testing" in the "Wrangle to Fandom(s)" field above the table
# Press the "Wrangle" button that's in the same fieldset
# Now follow the "Freeforms (X)" link in the sidebar to see all the freeform tags wrangled to the "Testing" fandom
# Locate the tag again
# Follow the corresponding "Edit" link
# Check the "Unwrangleable" checkbox
# Press "Save changes"
# Now go to the page listing all of the unwrangleable freeform tags wrangled to the "Testing" fandom. (There's not a good way to get there from a tag's Edit page, so you can just go to this URL: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/wrangle?show=freeforms&status=unwrangleable)|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/wrangle?show=freeforms&status=unwrangleable)]
# Locate the tag again
# Check the checkbox for the corresponding "Remove" option
# Press one of the "Wrangle" buttons that's directly above or below the table

Now you have an unwrangleable tag without a fandom, yay\! Time to either try to edit the work or create a new work using the tag. We'll edit the work we created.

# Log in as testy, if you're not already
# Hi, testy\! > My Works
# Follow the "Edit" link for the work you used the tag on
# Make a change to the work, e.g. edit the summary
# Press "Post"

h1. What happens

The edit page reloads with an error that says:

Sorry\! We couldn't save this work because:

* The following tags are invalid: testing new AO3-5615 bug. Please make sure that your tags are less than 100 characters long and do not contain any invalid characters.
* Unwrangleable can't be set on a tag with no fandoms.

Additionally, the offending tag no longer appears in the "Additional Tags" field. Because of that, if you press "Post" again, the work will post with the tag removed.

h1. What should happen

I should be able to save the work on the first attempt. The tag should not be removed.

h1. Notes

* The same behavior happens if you try to use the tag when posting a brand new work.
* You can add or edit chapters on a work with an unwrangleable, fandom-less tag.
* Admins also get the same error when trying to edit a work with an unwrangle, fandom-less tag.
* As both an admin and a user, you *can* update the work if you're removing the tag.
* You can delete the work.
* This is the really fun one: if you get the error message and then use the "Cancel" button, back button, or just simply stop editing the work, the tag will still appear on the work blurb and meta, *but* if you go to the tag's show page, the work will not be listed. This is probably a caching issue, since going to the work's edit page will not show the tag in the "Additional Tags" field. Possibly related to [AO3-4932|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4932]?

h1. Testing

The fix rolls back the changes in AO3-5615, so you’ll want to make sure:

* you can mark a tag as unwrangleable if it’s not in a fandom
* you can remove a fandom from an unwrangleable tag via the tag’s edit page
* you can use an unwrangleable tag with no fandom on a work without getting an error

h1. *What happens:* 

on the first admin post, the "Translations:" section lists Suomi (fi) before Arabic (ar).

We sort by languages by "Name for alphabetical sorting" ({{sortable_name}}), but if it's blank, we fall back on the short code. If [the sort is done in SQL|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/526f31cc84d4de809fa17030dc255c626f8f2a82/app/models/language.rb#L13] (e.g. on the /languages list), it's case-insensitive (because of the MySQL collation utf8mb4_unicode_ci), and "ar" goes before "Suomi" as expected.

However, if [the sort is done in Ruby|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/526f31cc84d4de809fa17030dc255c626f8f2a82/app/helpers/admin_post_helper.rb#L2-L7] (e.g. for the list of translations on an admin post), it's case sensitive, so "Suomi" comes before "ar".

h1. *What should happen:* 

several things.

* Sorting the languages of admin post translations should be case-insensitive. A good way to fix it is to replace the Ruby sort in the admin post helper with a SQL sort.
* The field "Name for alphabetical sorting" should be required. The field should be marked as such in the language form, and there should be a corresponding validation on the language model.
* There should be a rake task to automatically set {{sortable_name}} to {{name}} for languages where {{sortable_name}} is empty.
* There should be a note under the field "Name for alphabetical sorting" that explains what it is for. We can reuse instructions provided by the Translation committee: “This should be the language name or (if applicable) its name transliterated into the Latin alphabet. If the language's first character has diacritics, remove the diacritics.”

h1. Deploy notes

h2. Before deploy

Run the Before task: {{bundle exec rake Before:backfill_language_sortable_name}}

h2. After deploy

Notify the Translation committee to update [their language creation/update instructions|https://wiki.transformativeworks.org/mediawiki/Translation_Workflow_for_Support_and_Policy_%26_Abuse].

column1: Expose option for admins to hide comments
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h2. Current behavior True story: the comments table has a {{hidden_by_admin}} column, and setting that column to true from the console does indeed hide the comment\! The comment is replaced with a placeholder: {{

(This comment is under review by an admin and is currently unavailable.)

}} If you are logged in as an admin, the comment remains visible for review. Attempting to access a hidden comment via direct link while logged in redirects to your dash with an error message. Attempting to access it while logged out redirects to the user log in page. (This is a bit odd, but it's how hidden works work, too.) However, there's no button for this, so it's a pain to use. h2. Stuff you can test Ergo, we'd like to add a "Hide Comment" button to all comments. Access to this feature should match the access granted to the Freeze Thread feature: * *Works:* the feature should be available only to policy_and_abuse and superadmin admins * *News posts:* the feature should be available to all AO3 admins * *Tags:* the feature should only be available to tag_wrangling and superadmin admins Comments that are hidden should have an "Make Comment Visible" button that makes the comment visible. When the comment content is visible (i.e., when logged in as the user who left the hidden comment or as an admin who has permission to hide/unhide the comment), hidden comments should also have a blue notice banner like spam comments: {{

<%= ts("This comment has been hidden by an admin.") %>

}} (I.e., if you’re a tag_wrangling admin accessing a work with hidden comments, you should not see a regular-looking comment with a blue notice banner, but rather a placeholder saying the comment is under review. For hidden comments on tags, though, you’d see a notice banner, the comment text, and the comment actions.) The hide and unhide actions should apply to individual comments, not threads. Neither the "Hide Comment" nor "Make Comment Visible" button needs a confirmation message like the "Delete" button has, although they do need standard success and error messages. Hiding or unhiding a comment should be logged on the admin activities page. The placeholder should be given margins as described in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6034|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6034|smart-link]. The class {{unavailable}} should be added to the {{li}} containing the placeholder ({{hidden}} is more intuitive, but it’s kind of being used for actually hiding stuff). h2. Code stuff It looks like the original plan was to deal with comment hiding in the user creations controller (where we handle works, series, etc), but because all other actions admins can perform on comments (delete, spam/not spam, and freeze/unfreeze) are handled in the comments controller and model, let's handle it there to avoid muddying the waters when it comes to what constitutes a user creation. Any references to comments should be removed from the user creations controller. Like freezing and unfreezing, hiding and unhiding should be separate controller actions. h1. Deploy notes Has CSS changes.

column1: Add user and work IDs to work blurbs to allow muting or highlighting
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
In order to allow users to create skins that hide or highlight specific works or works by specific users, we'd like to:

* add a user's ID to the user's profile
* add the IDs of all of a work's approved creators to the work blurb's classes in the format {{user-123}} (using IDs rather than names will prevent your styling from vanishing if the user changes their name)
* add the ID of the work itself to the work blurb's classes in the format {{work-123 }}(although a work blurb's ID attribute contains the work ID already, if we add it as a class, and *later* – i.e. not in this issue -- add the same class to any bookmarks of that work, you will be able to use the selector {{.work-123}} to hide or highlight the work in both work and bookmark listing)

Additionally:

* add the ID of a series to its blurb's classes in the format {{series-123}} (this will only apply to user dashboards and series pages, not to bookmark listings)
* update the ID attribute of series blurbs to match the format used by works ({{series_123}} rather than {{series_123_blurb}})
* add the ID of an external work to its blurb's classes in the format {{external-work-123}} (this will only apply to the external work show page, which you see upon following the linked title from a bookmark, not to the blurbs shown on bookmark listings) 
* update the ID attribute of external work blurbs to match the format used by works ({{external_work_123}} rather than {{external_work_123_blurb}})

*How to test:*

* check that user profiles now contain the user ID, and note the ID of a user
* create and use a skin that highlights (it's easier for testing than hiding) 
** a work, e.g.{{ .work-123 { background: LightCyan; }}}
** a series, e.g. {{.series-123 { background: Lavender; }}}
** an external work, e.g. {{.external-work-123 { background: LemonChiffon; }}}
** works by a user, e.g. {{.user-123 { background: LightGray; }}}

Things to pay attention to while testing:

* does the style targeting works by a user actually apply to the user you intended (i.e. is the profile actually showing the correct user ID)
* does the style targeting works by a user update if a work is edited to add or remove the user as a co-creator (i.e. when the user is added, the style should be applied within a few moments; when they are removed, it should be removed within a few moments) 
* does the style targeting works by a user update if the work's anonymous status changes (i.e. the style should not be applied when the work is anonymous, but should be applied when the work is de-anoned)
* does the style targeting works by a user update if the work's revealed status changes (i.e. the style should not be applied when the work is unrevealed, but should be applied when the work is revealed)
* does the style apply on other (non-bookmark) pages where the work blurb is shown (e.g. history, the marked for later section of the homepage, gifts, etc – but please note that because {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/items}} and {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/NAME/collection_items}} are weird in general and can contain both works and bookmarks, we're skipping those for now)
