column1: Add user IDs to series blurbs
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Following [AO3-6131|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6131], we want to add series creator IDs to series blurbs. This still does not include bookmark listings – we're doing one thing at a time here – but only the series blurbs on:

* user dashboards, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/testy|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/testy]
* user series pages, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/testy/series|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/testy/series]
* a series' bookmark page, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/series/63758/bookmarks,|https://test.archiveofourown.org/series/63758/bookmarks,] which can be accessed by following the linked number in "Bookmarks: 1" from the series' blurb

Because of that last one, we'll have to make sure that a series is touched when it becomes anonymous or is de-anonymized. (Anonymous series blurbs are not displayed in the other two locations.) Touching the series will update its classes to add or remove the series creator IDs as appropriate.

*Testing*

# Log in
# Post a work in a new series
# Bookmark the series
# Go to your user profile and note down your user ID
# Create and use a site skin that applies styling to anything with your user ID, e.g. {{.user-123 { background: LightGreen !important; }}}
# Check that your series blurb is now light green (or whatever) on the pages described above
# Edit the work in your series to add it to an anonymous collection
# Check that your series blurb is no longer light green on its bookmarks page (it will have disappeared from the other two places it was light green)
# Edit the work in your series to remove it from the anonymous collection
# Check that your series blurb is light green again in all three places (it will have returned to your dash and series page)
# Edit the work in your series to add it to an unrevealed collection
# Check that your series blurb is still light green on its bookmarks page, since its creator is still visible (it will have disappeared from the other two places it was light green)
# Edit the work in your series to remove it from the unrevealed collection
# Check that your series blurb is still light green on all three pages (it will have returned to your dash and series page)

The deploy step should use [appleboy/ssh-action|https://github.com/appleboy/ssh-action] to SSH into the staging server and run the Capistrano script there. * GitHub Actions doesn't automatically cancel duplicate jobs, which means we may want to make the deploy action a completely manual step.

column1: Remove gem Delorean from test dependencies
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
[Delorean|https://github.com/bebanjo/delorean], a gem for mocking {{Time.now}}, has been discontinued. Its functionality can be fully replaced by Rails' [TimeHelpers|https://api.rubyonrails.org/v5.2/classes/ActiveSupport/Testing/TimeHelpers.html], so there's no reason for it to stick around.

Note that we also use [timecop|https://github.com/travisjeffery/timecop], another gem for testing time-dependent code, which is not as straightforward to replace. Specifically, we use {{Timecop.travel}}, which [jumps to a arbitrary point in time AND lets time continue to flow instead of freezing it|https://github.com/travisjeffery/timecop#the-difference-between-timecopfreeze-and-timecoptravel], to force cache expiration in a few places. Rails' TimeHelpers has no equivalent functionality. We'll leave timecop uses alone for now.

*How to test*: none, automated.

column1: Move list of target servers out of Capistrano deploy scripts
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Capistrano scripts for each stage ([staging, production|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/tree/c2f27c95463958b1fd184670616364ba9592029c/config/deploy]) maintain a list of servers ([at minimum, hosts and their roles|https://capistranorb.com/documentation/advanced-features/properties/]) to deploy to. These scripts need to be updated any time we need to add/remove/move servers (e.g. AO3-6098).

column1: Protected users should not be able to receive gifts
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
In AO3-5525, we added a new "Protected User" role.

Until we can add a preference to allow all users to turn off gifts, which is a bit more involved in terms of both process and code, we'd like to make it so protected users cannot receive gifts unless the gift work fulfills a gift exchange assignment or a claim of a non-anonymous prompt. 

Attempting to give a gift you can't give should give an error: "You can't give a gift to \[name]."

This can probably be done with a validation. Bonus: It will most likely be possible to update the code for this and reuse it for the preference when the time comes. 

Testing

Set up:

# Log in as User A, who will be our protected user.
# Create a gift exchange collection with open sign-ups and random matching and sign up for it.
# Create a prompt meme collection with open-sign-ups that allows anonymous prompts and sign up for it, creating one anonymous prompt and one non-anonymous prompt.
# Log in as User B.
# Sign up for the gift exchange from Step 2.
# Claim the prompts from Step 3.
# Log back in as User A.
# Close sign-ups for your gift exchange, run matching, make sure User B is assigned to write for you, and send assignments.
# Log in as a Policy & Abuse admin and give User A the "Protected user" role.

And now the actual testing\!

# User B should be able to fulfill their gift exchange assignment for User A with User A listed as the gift recipient. 
# User B should be able to fulfill their prompt meme claim for User A's non-anonymous prompt and successfully list User A as the gift recipient. Note that unlike with gift exchanges, you must enter User A in the "Gift this work to" field.
# User B should be able to fulfill their prompt meme claim for User A's anonymous prompt, but they should not be able to list User A as the gift recipient. Note that unlike with gift exchanges, you must enter User A in the "Gift this work to" field.
# User B should not be able to post or update a work unaffiliated with the assignment/claim from Steps 1 or 2 and list User A as the gift recipient.
# If User B edits the work from Steps 1 or 2 and disconnects the work from the assignment/claim, they should not be able to continuing listing User A as the gift recipient. (The error message will be a little weird with an extraneous "Gifts" in front of it, but that's the same Rails-related cause as AO3-5635.)

We'd like to make it so protected users' works cannot be cited as related works or translations. This will tide us over while we look into adding a preference to provide all users with this option in preferences.

# Create a work
# Log in as User B
# Create a work that cites User A's work as a parent work
# Create another work without citations
# Log in as a Policy & Abuse admin and give User A the "Protected user" role.

And now the actual testing\!

* User B should be able to edit the work they created and the citation should remain intact
* User A should be able to approve or remove existing citations
* User B should not be able to post a new work that cite User A's work
* User B should not be able to edit an existing work to add a citation of User A's work

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
[https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/change_username|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/change_username] We'd like to make it so users can only change their name 1 time every 7 days. Both of these values should be configurable. To accomplish this, we'd like to record the date of the last rename in a {{renamed_at}} column on the {{users}} table and, if the date is more than 7 days ago, you can change your name again. There should be a rake task that fills in the {{renamed_at}} column with the date of the last rename (if any), which can be found in the {{log_items}} table. It’s [action 7|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/7e583009b59acb17e805cb228c545aec6893627c/config/config.yml#L419]. The message at the top of the change username page should be updated to: {noformat}

Please use this feature with caution. You can change your user name 1 time every 7 days. You last changed your user name on [renamed_at].

For information on how changing your user name will affect your account, please check out the Account FAQ. Note that changes to your username may take several days or longer to appear. If you are still seeing your old user name on your works, bookmarks, series, or collections after a week, please contact Support.

{noformat} “You can change your user name 1 time every 7 days” should be internationalized so it handles pluralization of time/days depending on the number (e.g. “1 time,” “5 times”), and “You last changed your user name on \[renamed_at]“ should be left off if there is no {{renamed_at}} data. If you have already changed your username, you should get an error message that says, "Sorry, you can only change your user name 1 time every 7 days. You last changed your user name on \[renamed_at]." (We're aware it should be "username," but we don't want to introduce inconsistency with all the other instances of "user name," nor do we want to expand the scope of this issue to cover changing all of those.)

13/Mar/21 12:03 AM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;Something like this will probably work for the rake:

{code:ruby}  task(add_renamed_at_to_user: :environment) do
    total_users = User.all.size
    total_batches = (total_users + 999) / 1000
    puts "Updating #{total_users} users in #{total_batches} batches"

    User.find_in_batches.with_index do |batch, index|
      batch_number = index + 1
      progress_msg = "Batch #{batch_number} of #{total_batches} complete"
      batch.each do |user|
        renamed_at_from_log = user.log_items.where(action: ArchiveConfig.ACTION_RENAME).last&.created_at
        next unless renamed_at_from_log
        
        user.update_column(:renamed_at, renamed_at_from_log)
      end
      puts(progress_msg) && STDOUT.flush
    end
    puts && STDOUT.flush
  end{code}

column1: Allow admins with specific roles to view IP address and guest email on comments
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Currently, any admin can view the IP address of a comment or work. We'd like to restrict this ability to only admins with the policy_and_abuse and superadmin roles.

At the same time, we also want to allow admins with the policy_and_abuse, support, and superadmin roles to view the email of a comment, if available (only on guest comments).

*How to test*:

* While logged out, leave a guest comment A. You should not be able to see the guest email or IP address at the bottom of the comment.
* While logged in as a user, leave a comment B. You should not be able to see the IP address at the bottom of the comment.
* While logged in as a user, post a work. You should not be able to see the IP address at the top of the work.
* While logged in as an admin with policy_and_abuse or superadmin role, you should see:
** at the bottom of comment A, "Email: (A's email)", then on the next line, "IP Address: (IP address of A's guest)";
** at the bottom of comment B, "IP Address: (IP address of A's guest)";
** at the top of the work, "IP Address: (IP address of user)."
* While logged in as an admin with the support role, you should see:
** at the bottom of comment A, "Email: (A's email)", but not the IP address;
** at the bottom of comment B, neither the email nor the IP address;
** at the top of the work, no IP address.
* While logged in as an admin with other roles, view comment A and B and the work. In both cases, you should not be able to see the guest email or IP address at the bottom of the comment, or the IP address at the top of the work.

*Notes*: the comment view templates are:

* [_single_comment.html.erb|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/40fb60907f998e86424c097b4a4edfca1ca3e0f5/app/views/comments/_single_comment.html.erb#L65-L67]

column1: Limit the number of tags that can be used on works
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
It should not be possible to use more than 75 total [user-defined tags|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/f6e1b98aa472c0777cf2140064218c1d5a8c87c5/app/models/tag.rb#L23] (fandom, character, relationship, or additional tags) on a work. Category, rating, and warning tags should not count toward this total.

The limit should be configurable.

*Work form changes*

The limit should be explained on the top of the tag section, which currently says, "Tags are comma separated, 100 characters per tag." 

The new text should be: "Tags are comma separated, 100 characters per tag. Fandom, relationship, character, and additional tags must not add up to more than 75. Archive warning, category, and rating tags do not count toward this limit."

*Error message*

If your work has more than the total number of tags permitted, previewing, saving, or posting should fail until the excess tags are removed. 

This should be done with backend validation, and the error message should say, "Fandom, relationship, character, and additional tags must not add up to more than 75. Your work has \[x] of these tags, so you must remove \[y] of them."

*Existing works*

Existing works with over 75 tags will continue to exist, but the creator must remove tags if they wish to edit the work or add chapters to it. 

It should be possible to delete works that have over 75 tags without needing to remove any tags. 

It should be possible to bookmark works that have over 75 tags. (We currently use [@bookmarkable.save when creating a bookmark|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b63fce67a3975ec0614bb535c75d76c8dafbda71/app/controllers/bookmarks_controller.rb#L196], which prevents creating bookmarks of invalid works.)

If a work with over 75 tags is in an unrevealed or anonymous collection, it should be possible to reveal or deanonymize the work.

If someone have gifted you a work with over 75 tags, it should possible to accept or reject that gift.

If a series contains a work with over 75 tags, it should be possible to add other works to the series or edit the series.

*Admin*

When you are logged in as an admin, the [work meta|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/views/works/_meta.html.erb] should indicate "Over Tag Limit: Yes" or "Over Tag Limit: No". This should be in the {{<dl>}}, beneath "Akismet Reported As Spam:"

*External works*

On the Bookmark External Work page ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/external_works/new}}), the limit should be explained on the top of the tag section, which currently says, "Creator's Tags (comma separated, 100 characters per tag). Only a fandom is required." 

The new text should be: "Creator's Tags (comma separated, 100 characters per tag). Only a fandom is required. Fandom, relationship, and character tags must not add up to more than 75. Category and rating tags do not count toward this limit."

Attempting to save a bookmark of an external work with over 75 tags should fail. This should be done with backend validation, and the error message should say, "Fandom, relationship, and character tags must not add up to more than 75. You have entered \[x] of these tags, so you must remove \[y] of them."

When posting a work, it should still be possible to cite a work not on the Archive using the “This work is a remix, a translation, a podfic, or was inspired by another work.” (Citing a work creates an external work, hence including this in this section.) 

*Stats*

To get data on the frequency of tag counts on works:

{{results = ActiveRecord::Base.connection.exec_query "SELECT tag_count, COUNT(*) AS frequency FROM (SELECT taggable_id, COUNT(*) AS tag_count FROM taggings WHERE taggable_type = 'Work' GROUP BY taggable_id) tc GROUP BY tag_count"}}

{{puts "Tag count,\tfrequency"; results.rows.each { |r| puts "#{r[0]},\t#{r[1]}" }; nil}}

Note: This needs to be updated to only look at user defined tags.

*Blocking*

This needs an announcement first.

We also have a number of linked issues whose fixes will require us to update tags on works. These should be resolved first, since this change will make it more difficult to update a work’s tags.

Note: This issue can only be handled by AD&T staff as it requires access to some Zoho API info that cannot be shared outside the org.

If you're logged in as an admin with the role policy_and_abuse or superadmin and you go to a user's profile page, you should

* be able to see the "Edit My Profile" link
* follow said link to the edit page

On the edit page, there should be an "Ticket ID (required)" field at the bottom of the form. This field should only be present for admins. It should have a footnote specifying only numbers should be entered.

!Screen Shot 2021-04-10 at 10.31.50 PM.png|width=799,height=629!

We should use Zoho's API to validate that a ticket with the given number exists. 

If no number is provided, it should not save the change and should give the admin an error saying the field cannot be blank.

If a ticket with the number does not exist, the admin should not be able to save changes and should get an error message saying "Ticket ID must exist."

If a ticket with the number does exist, the change should be saved and a new admin activity log item should be created and displayed on the Activities admin page:

* the target should say "User \[login]" and should link to the user's profile
* the summary should say "Ticket #000", and it should link to the relevant ticket on Zoho (we don't want to record a summary of the text before the change because profiles include personal information subject to privacy laws)
* the time of the change and the name of the admin who made the change should also be recorded

column1: Series blurbs display wrong rating icon when a work in the series is not rated, and a bookmarked series appears in search results and filters for all ratings used on its works
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
*Steps to reproduce wrong rating icon*

# Log in 
# Post > New Work
# For "Rating," select "Not Rated"
# Fill in other required fields
# Check "This work is part of a series"
# In the "Or create an use a new one" field, fill in a title for your series
# Press "Post"
# Post > New Work
# For "Rating," select "General Audiences"
# Fill in other required fields
# Check "This work is part of a series"
# Use the "Select one of your existing series" option to select the series you created when posting the previous work
# Press "Post"
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard

*What happens* 
The rating icon displayed on the series blurb is for the General Audiences rating, but it should be the icon for the Not Rated rating. 

*What should happen*
The rating icon that displays on the blurb is meant to be that of the series' highest-rated work. After consulting with Content Policy, we have determined the ratings are, from lowest to highest:

General Audiences
Teen And Up Audiences
Mature
Explicit 
Not Rated

The rating icon should not change based on whether or not the highest-rated work is restricted, hidden, or unrevealed. That is, if a series has 3 public General Audiences works and 1 restricted, hidden, or unrevealed work that is rated Explicit, the series icon should still be Explicit for everyone.

*Steps to reproduce bookmarked series appearing in search results and filters for all ratings used on its works*

# Complete all the steps for reproducing the wrong rating icon
# Follow the link in the blurb to access the series
# Press "Bookmark Series"
# Press "Create"
# Wait a moment or two
# Hi, username! > My Bookmarks
# In the "Include" section of the filters, expand the "Ratings" section
# Choose "General Audiences"

*What happens*
The series you just bookmarked appears. The "Ratings" section of the filter also contains "Not Rated"

*What should happen*
The series should only appear in the results for the highest rating (the one that is used for the icon). In the case of our example case, this is "Not Rated."

Again, the rating should not change based on whether or not the highest-rated work is restricted, hidden, or unrevealed. That is, if a series has 3 public General Audiences works and 1 restricted, hidden, or unrevealed work that is rated Explicit, the series should still filter as Explicit for everyone.

column30:
Steps to reproduce

# Log in as admin
# Go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/faq/new?language_id=fake|https://test.archiveofourown.org/faqs/new?language_id=fake] or [https://test.archiveofourown.org/faq/EXISITING-CATEGORY/edit?language_id=fake|https://test.archiveofourown.org/faqs/EXISITING-CATEGORY/edit?language_id=fake] 
# Fill in the form or make changes
# Press the submit or save button

*What happens*

The FAQ is published and this causes any non-admin attempting to access the FAQs to get a 500 error

*What should happen*

-When you try to submit or save, it should fail with an error that says the language isn't valid.-

When you try to access one of those URLs, you should be redirected and receive an error message, so you cannot create an invalid FAQ.

*Notes*

If this happens in the meantime, you can delete the incorrect category.

First, look up the category by title:

{{faq = ArchiveFaq.where(title: "The Title").first}}

Then find the incorrect locale:

{{category_translation = faq.translations.where(locale: "incorrect_locale").first}}

Then destroy it:

{{category_translation.destroy}}

You’ll also need to destroy any questions for that locale. (Even if the locale’s category page is blank, they’ve been created.) Find them:

{{questions = Question::Translation.where(locale: "incorrect_locale")}}

Yeet them into a black hole:

{{questions.each(&:destroy)}}

Don’t freak out if you follow the FAQ link in the main navigation and find no FAQ categories: you probably accessed the borked category at some point, so the cookie is taking you to the category list for that locale. Switch to English and everything will still be there.

column150:
03/Apr/23 8:41 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;I’m not sure creating tags in the initializer is a good idea. The code referencing {{AdminSetting}}, {{Locale}}, and {{Language}} is wrapped with 2-3 different rescue blocks to avoid errors when running commands like {{rake db:drop}} and {{rake db:create}}, and [referencing models in initializers breaks entirely on Rails 7|https://stackoverflow.com/questions/73422545/rails-model-no-longer-available-in-initializer-after-upgrade-to-rails-7-0].

The issue is fixable by moving all of the code referencing those classes into callbacks, but it might be cleaner to create a {{db/seeds.rb}} file to construct everything, and call that whenever necessary (in development or tests).

(Also worth noting: initializers will not be rerun at the start of each test, so whenever truncation is used for database cleaning there will need to be some way to recreate the tags. So moving the tag creation code into an initializer will still require some duplicate setup code for tests.)

column1: User can't delete account if they have chapters that don't have works

column30:
{code:ruby}> Chapter.where(work_id: nil).size
=> 42066 
> chapter_ids = Chapter.where(work_id: nil).pluck(:id) ; nil
=> nil 
> Creatorship.where(creation_id: chapter_ids, creation_type: "Chapter").size
=> 34139 {code}

There are roughly 42k chapters in the database without works, probably due to work deletion choking. (We want to make work deletion asynchronous so it doesn't happen as much: AO3-5517.)

There are about 34k creatorships for these chapters.

If one of those chapters belongs to you and you try to delete your account, nothing happens. No error page, it just does nothing when you press the button to delete your account.

We should make it so any work-less chapters you own are deleted and account deletion proceeds as expected. 

If there are co-creators on your work-less chapter, it shouldn't delete the chapter outright, but it should delete your creatorship. As long as the chapter has a creator, we'll just let the chapter hang out for now.

*Testing*

A database admin will need to:

# Create an account you're cool with deleting
# Post a work
# Add another chapter to the work 
# Add a co-created chapter to the work
# Set the {{work_id}} columns of the chapters from steps 3 & 4 to {{nil}}, probably using {{update_column}} to avoid callbacks and validations
# Attempt to delete the account

This is fixed if:

* the account is deleted
* the chapter from step 3 no longer exists in the database
* the chapter from step 4 does exist in the database

column1: Live validation errors not read by screen readers
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

*Using a screen reader...*

# Log in
# Post > New Work
# Tab to the "Work title" field
# Do not enter anything in this field
# Tab away from the field

h1. What happens

An error message ("We need a title\! (At least 1 character long, please.)") appears on the screen, but it is not read.

h1. What should happen

Your screen reader should alert you to the new error message so you can go back and fix the problem.

h1. Notes

[How to make inline error messages accessible|https://hiddedevries.nl/en/blog/2017-04-04-how-to-make-inline-error-messages-accessible]
[ARIA19: Using ARIA role=alert or Live Regions to Identify Errors|https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG20-TECHS/ARIA19.html]

We'll need to make sure the span that holds the error message is included in the DOM on load and has role="alert" set. (Currently, the span does not appear until the validation runs.)

[Using Aria-Invalid to Indicate An Error Field|https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Techniques/aria/ARIA21]

If you can also use aria-invalid and aria-describedby to associate the invalid field with the error span, that would be a fantastic bonus.

column1: Remove unused actions in CommentsController
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
There are two unused/unreachable actions in the {{CommentsController}}: {{add_comment}} and {{cancel_comment}}. They both count as covered, but only as a result of RSpec tests designed to check them. They're not linked anywhere in the code.

(Technically, {{cancel_comment_button}} can produce a link to the {{cancel_comment}} action, but [only if it's called on a comment that's (a) a new record, and (b) not a reply comment|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c7a78bc277e676cbbc39ee152dedfe07b00c349e/app/helpers/comments_helper.rb#L239-L252]. But {{cancel_comment_button}} is only called in [one place|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c7a78bc277e676cbbc39ee152dedfe07b00c349e/app/views/comments/_comment_form.html.erb#L107-L108], and the conditions under which it's called are exactly the conditions that prevent it from linking to the {{cancel_comment}} action.)

The two methods should be deleted from the {{CommentsController}} class, the routes should be removed, the view {{add_comment.js.erb}} should be deleted (there is no view for {{cancel_comment}}), and any code involving the {{add_comment}} param should be deleted. In addition, the {{cancel_comment_button}} method should be refactored so that it no longer refers to the {{cancel_comment}} action.

*Testing Instructions:* Try clicking the "Reply" button on a comment, then the "Cancel" button to make sure that it's still working. Similarly, try clicking the "Edit" button on one of your own comments, and then use the "Cancel" button to make sure it's still working.

column1: Non-admins can rename tags with Asian characters
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
As noted by @tickinginstant in this PR comment:
[https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4009#issuecomment-865097461|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4009#issuecomment-865097461]

The regex in [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b63fce67a3975ec0614bb535c75d76c8dafbda71/app/models/tag.rb#L193|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b63fce67a3975ec0614bb535c75d76c8dafbda71/app/models/tag.rb#L193] will strip any characters that aren't ASCII for comparison.  The intent is to allow tag wranglers to change accents or casing, but this has the unintended side-effect of treating all non-Latin characters as equivalent.  For example, that means a tag containing only Chinese characters will be considered equivalent to any other tag with only Chinese characters (or Japanese, or Korean, for that matter) and the tag can be changed completely by any tag wrangler.

That regex should be modified to something like {{/[\u0300-\u036F]/}} in order to allow only modification of diacritical marks as intended.

*Testing*

# A regular wrangler should still be able to update a tag’s name to replace a character with diacritics (e.g., ö or ø) with a similar character without diacritics (e.g., o) or vice versa.
# A regular wrangler should not be able to completely change the name of a tag with non-Latin characters, e.g., you should not be able to change 백일의 낭군님 to  残剑震江湖.
# An admin should be able to change the name of a tag to anything they want.

column1: Use Rails timezone for work/chapter date calculations
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The work/chapter date calculations use {{Time.now}} and {{Date.today}}, which return times/dates in the system's time zone (UTC, for production). That code also checks those times/dates against {{revised_at}} and {{revised_at.to_date}}, which are automatically converted to {{Time.zone}} (Rails's timezone – Eastern by default, but could be anything thanks to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6189#icft=AO3-6189|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6189#icft=AO3-6189|smart-link]). This results in some timezone-related bugs in the work/chapter dating calculations.

We'd like to switch from {{Time.now}} to {{Time.current}} and from {{Date.today}} to {{Date.current}}, so that all of the calculations take place in the Eastern time zone.

*Testing Instructions:*

# Create a new work and wait a few days, or pick an old work.
# Some time between midnight and 4:00 AM UTC time, try to redate the work to the current UTC date. Make sure you get an error telling you that your publication date is invalid.

column1: Story Parser copies story meta to imported chapter 2+
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When a multi-chapter work is imported, the StoryParser scrapes work meta from the HTML page and copies the work title, summary and notes to the chapters after chapter 1 if they don't already have values for these fields. This leads to repetition and may affect readability if the summary is long. 

See https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1073383 for a manually-imported example, whose chapter list looks like this:
 !Screenshot 2021-06-27 at 15.13.51.png|thumbnail! 
(Chapter 7 happened to have a title, so it only got the duplicate summary)

h2. Steps to reproduce
This behaviour is also visible when importing works manually:
1. Import multiple pages that contain work title and summary meta fields (ie separate lines starting with `Title:` and `Summary:` respectively) but no chapter titles (identified by `Chapter title:`). 
1. Note that once the work is imported, chapter 2 and subsequent have the title set to the title of the work, and a copy of the work summary is displayed at the top of the chapter.
Open Doors can make a temp site available with this type of data if needed for testing.

h2. Details
The problem is due to code in the [get_chapter_from_work_params method in the StoryParser|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/models/story_parser.rb#L435-L443] which copies meta scraped from the chapter page into the work as well as the chapter. Probably the only fields that need to be copied into chapters from the work are the date fields.

Note that this is low priority for Open Doors imports as they can work around the issue by synthesising missing chapter titles and removing the summary from chapter pages so that meta doesn't get scraped from the HTML, but it isn't desirable behaviour.

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a regular user
# Post > New Work
# Fill in the form with regrettable things
# Press "Post"
# Fill in the work's comment form with regrettable things
# Press "Comment"
# Follow the "Edit" link at the top of the work
# Follow the "Orphan Work" link at the top of the edit page
# Choose "Leave a copy of my pseud on" on the orphaning confirmation page
# Press "Yes, I'm Sure"
# Decide you were not sure and contact Support or Policy & Abuse to have your pseud removed from the work and your comments on it
# Be a Support or Policy & Abuse volunteer who contacts AD&T to remove the pseud from the work and your comments

h1. What should happen

When you are logged in as a {{superadmin}} or a {{support}} or  {{policy_and_abuse}} admin

*_and_* you go to a work that belongs to one of the orphan_account's non-default pseuds (i.e., any pseud other than orphan_account itself), 

*_then_* there should be a "Remove Pseud" button located in between "Mark As Spam" and "Delete Work." 

If JavaScript is enabled, then pressing that button should trigger a confirmation popup asking, "Are you sure you want to remove the creator's pseud from this work?"

If JavaScript is not enabled, then pressing that button should take you to a confirmation page along the lines of [one of our confirm_delete pages|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/views/bookmarks/confirm_delete.html.erb]. Refer to “Confirmation page” section below for a mock-up and copy of the text. (The structure should follow that of the linked page.)

Confirming your desire to remove the pseud should remove it, perhaps using a variation of this code from @redsummernight:

{noformat}pseud = User.orphan_account.pseuds.find_by(name: "name")
pseud.works.each { |w| pseud.change_ownership(w, User.orphan_account.default_pseud) }{noformat}

It should also record an admin activity for this action. The activity should *not* include the name of the pseud that was removed.

If there are multiple orphan account pseuds on the work, pressing the "Remove Pseud" button should not trigger a confirmation popup. Instead, it should take you to a page that instructs you to choose which pseuds you wish to remove from a list of checkboxes. (You do not need to go through a confirmation page after this.) The pseuds should be removed and the admin activity logged as above. Refer to “Selection page” section below for a copy of the text. (Again, the structure should follow that of the linked confirm_delete page as closely as possible.)

caution notice: Are you sure you want to remove the creator's pseud from this work?

button: Yes, Remove Pseud

h2. Selection page

h2: Remove Pseud

caution notice: Please choose which creators' pseuds you would like to remove from this work.

unordered list: one checkbox for each non-default orphan pseud in the standard byline format of “pseud (orphan_account)”

button: Remove Pseud

!pseud_select (54d9cf77-745c-4ee5-80ff-0d49197ba115).png|width=842,height=185!

The name should appear in the autocomplete suggestions.

It doesn't.

*Notes*

column30:
{{TagSetNominationsController#index}} takes 10 seconds, on average. We should add some indices to help with that.

All of the queries in that action depend on the {{owned_tag_set_id}} from the {{tag_set_nominations}} table, but (a) there are no indices on the {{tag_set_nominations}} table, and (b) the only index on the {{tag_nominations}} table that references {{tag_set_nominations_id}} (which is used by the join) is on {{(type, tag_set_nominations_id)}}, which only covers those queries that specify a type. This means that a line like {{if @tag_set.tag_nominations.unreviewed.empty?}} could require a full-table scan.

*Notes:* There are 1+ million rows in the {{tag_nominations}} table, so that part of the migration may need to use {{pt-online-schema-change}} in staging & production. The {{tag_set_nominations}} table is much smaller and can probably get away with a normal migration, though.

*Testing Instructions:* This adds some indices, so there shouldn't be any visible changes. Migrate up, migrate down, migrate up again.

*This will require updating mappings, restarting workers, and reindexing tags after it is deployed.*

{{TagWranglingsController#index}}, also known as the mass wrangle bin, takes an average of 8 seconds to load. We'd like to load the lists of unwrangled tags from Elasticsearch instead of SQL, to try to speed it up.

It would also be good to modify the cached unwrangled tags counts, shown in {{TagWranglingsController#index}}, {{TagWranglersController#show}}, and {{UnsortedTagsController#index}}, so that they are loaded from ES.

*Testing Instructions:*

* Go to your wrangling home page. Make sure the counts look reasonable
* Click on "Fandoms by media".
* Pick a medium and some fandoms, and press "Wrangle."
* Make sure that the fandoms you picked are no longer listed there.
* Click on "Characters by fandom".
* Pick some characters, fill in the name of a canonical fandom, and press "Wrangle."
* Make sure that the characters you picked are no longer listed there.
* Repeat for "Relationships by fandom" and "Freeforms by fandom."
* Wait an hour, and make sure that the counts in the sidebar change to reflect the wrangling you've done.
* Create a work with a brand new fandom, character, relationship, and freeform. Check each of the four pages, and make sure that all of your new tags are listed in the appropriate places. (They may take a minute or two to show up, but they should show up eventually.)
* Wait another hour, and make sure that the counts in the sidebar change to reflect the wrangling you've done.

31/Mar/22 5:23 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;The mass wrangle bins allow sorting by taggings count, so addressing this issue is going to require fixing the bug I mentioned [here|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4144#issuecomment-1068201039]:

{quote}The {{taggings_count_cache}} column in the database (which is used to set the {{uses}} field in ES) is only updated when {{Tag.write_redis_to_database}} is called. Unfortunately, {{Tag.write_redis_to_database}} avoids tag callbacks on write (presumably for speed reasons, since it's called once every 2 minutes and updates all tags that have had their count viewed recently, not just those that have had their count changed), which means that the {{uses}} field in ES is not kept up-to-date. That's going to have to change if you want to allow users to sort on the {{uses}} field.{quote}

column151:
04/Apr/22 2:28 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;The (mostly) up-to-date tag counts are already stored in Redis ([https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1f6acc7421f9a649d36386be525886409395bd94/app/models/tag.rb#L68-L72|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1f6acc7421f9a649d36386be525886409395bd94/app/models/tag.rb#L68-L72|smart-link]), but ES only has access to information that has been explicitly sent to it, typically through reindexing.

I think modifying the taggings count code to avoid the extra work is probably the most critical aspect. Once the {{taggings_count_cache}} updates are guaranteed to be updates, and not just a process caused by someone viewing the tag, I expect there ought to be more wiggle room for reindexing tags on update.

(It’s possible that this should be a separate issue blocking this one.)
column152:

The {{taggings_count}} getter calls the setter if there is no cached value, and the setter initiates the eventual write to the database through Redis. Please correct me if I got any of this wrong. 

I was wondering if the fix would be as simple as just comparing the {{tag_update_#{id}_value}} (if one exists) to the value passed to the method and only creating the {{tag_update}} if the counts differ.

Another option would be separating out the caching from writes to Redis for updating the database in calls that stem from the {{taggings_count}} getter since I believe it queries the database directly to get the count if it is not cached.

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a tag wrangler. We'll assume you're using testy, who is assigned the Testing fandom.
# Post > New Work
# Fill in required information, and make sure to enter "Testing" (or another fandom you are assigned) in the fandom field.
# In the fields for characters, relationships, and additional tags, enter tags that have never been used before. (Appending the issue number to a tag is a good way to accomplish that.)
# Preview
# Save As Draft
# Hi, testy\! > Tag Wrangling
# Look for the tags in the appropriate unwrangled bin for your fandom, e.g., the additional tag you created will be in Testing's unwrangled freeforms bin. You can access this bin by following the linked number located in the Testing fandom's row under the Unwrangled and Freeforms columns. The tags are listed in alphabetical order, so you may need to use the pagination.
# Hi, testy\! > Tag Wrangling
# Now also look for the tags in the appropriate mass bins, e.g., the character tag you created will be in the characters bin, which you can access by following the Characters by Fandom link in the sidebar. The tags are listed in creation order, so you will need to use the pagination.

h1. What happens

The tags are there.

h1. What should happen

If a tag does not have a posted work, it should not be there, nor should it be included in the count.

However, the tag should continue to be included in results for tag searches (Search > Tags).

h1. Notes

Tags are already [indexed in Elasticsearch with the field has_posted_works|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/63ed5aa8387b7593831811e66a2f2c2654bdea15/app/models/search/tag_indexer.rb#L70].

column1: Add an index to the tag_set_associations table
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The {{tag_set_associations}} table has no indices, so some queries involving it have to search through all 600,000+ rows. We should add an index starting with {{owned_tag_set_id}}, since most queries involving tag set IDs should specify the {{OwnedTagSet}}. (The {{Prompt#restricted_tags}} method is [one of the only places|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/63ed5aa8387b7593831811e66a2f2c2654bdea15/app/models/prompt.rb#L166] where the {{OwnedTagSet}} isn't specified, but that's because of [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5712|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5712|smart-link] .)

It might also be good to add an index starting with {{tag_id}} and another starting with {{parent_tag_id}}, particularly if this is addressed before [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5712|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5712|smart-link] . And a unique index on all three fields would be nice. But the index on {{owned_tag_set_id}} is probably the most important part.

*Notes:* The table is large enough that we probably want to use {{pt-online-schema-change}} on staging/production for this one.

*Testing Instructions:* Run the migration, revert it, and then run it again to make sure it works both ways.

column30:
For collections and challenges, admins with the support, policy_and_abuse, or superadmin role should be able to access all pages the challenge owners can access. 

They should not, however, be able to change any settings, sign-ups, prompts, etc. Attempting to do so should redirect them to one of the following with an error message:

*  the page they came from
*  the collection dashboard ([https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME),|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME),] or 
* the homepage 

The exact error message and behavior may vary based on current behavior. For example, attempting to access an individual sign-up's edit page at [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/signups/####/edit|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/signups/####/edit] will redirect an admin to the homepage and prompt them to log out of their admin account first. It's a little weird, but in the interest of not making things overly complex, keeping it is probably the sensible move.

Nothing should be hidden or visibly disabled, since Support will sometimes want to make screenshots.

*Collections:*

These pages should also be accessible on gift exchanges and prompt memes.

* Manage Items pages: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/items|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/items]
* Collection Settings page: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/edit|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/edit]
* Membership: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/participants|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/participants]

*Gift Exchanges*:

* Sign-ups: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/signups|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/signups]
** Ideally, "Search by Pseud" and "Download (CSV)" should also work.
* Individual sign-ups: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/signups/###|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/signups/###]
* Requests Summary: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/requests|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/requests]
** Sometimes, mods make this page public. Admins should have access to it even if it is not public.
* Matching: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/potential_matches|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/potential_matches]
* Assignments: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/assignments|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/assignments]
* Individual assignments: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/assignments/###|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/assignments/###]
* Challenge Settings: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/gift_exchange/edit|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/gift_exchange/edit]

*Prompt Memes:*

* Unposted Claims: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/claims|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/claims]
* Challenge Settings: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/prompt_meme/edit|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME/prompt_meme/edit]

h2. Testing

In addition to making sure you can access those pages while logged in as a support or superadmin admin, please try pressing some buttons you shouldn’t be allow to use, e.g. saving edits to the settings, modifying members, purging assignments, deleting sign-ups.

Please also confirm these pages are not accessible by admins with other roles.

column30:
If you set up a gift exchange’s matching settings in a certain way (i.e., you neither require nor allow any type of tags, but matching settings rely on at least one type), this causes matching to hang. 

We should have a process to check when Challenge Settings are saved that checks the values and throws an error.

*Steps to reproduce*

# Log in
# Create a new gift exchange:
## Browse > Collections > New Collection
## Fill in required fields
## For “Type of challenge, if any” choose “Gift Exchange”
## Press “Submit”
# On the “Setting Up the \[Collection Title] Gift Exchange” page
## In “Schedule,” check the “Sign-up open?” checkbox
## In the “Request Settings”, set all tag choices to 0 Required, 0 Allowed 
## In “Offer Settings,” set all tag choices to 0 Required, 0 Allowed
## In “Minimum Number to Match,” set Characters to 1
## Press “Submit”
# Create two sign-ups using the same fandom and no character tags
## Follow the “Sign-up Form” link in the sidebar
## Fill in the same Fandom for both Requests (1) and Offer (1), e.g. enter “Testing”
## Do not fill in Characters
## Press “Submit”
## Log out, then log back in as a different user
## Repeat Steps 4a-4d
# Log in as the challenge owner and return to you collection/challenge
# Run matching
## Follow the “Challenge Settings” link in the sidebar
## In Schedule, *un*check the “Sign-up open?” checkbox
## Press “Update”
## Follow the “Matching” link in the sidebar
## Press “Generate Potential Matches”

*What happens*

Matching hangs.

*What should happen:*

Matching should not hang.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The link to the Challenges and Collections FAQ in the 'anonymous or unrevealed notification' email needs to be updated now that that FAQ no longer exists.

*Steps to reproduce*

# Log into account #1 and create a work 
# Log into account #2 and create a collection  
# With account #1, add the work to the collection
# With account #2, change the collection status to 'unrevealed' or to 'anonymous' (or both)
# Follow the “Manage Items” link in the collection sidebar
# Follow the “Approved” link near the top of the page
# Check the “Anonymous” or “Unrevealed” (or both) boxes for the work you created
# Press “Submit”

*What happens?*

You receive an email containing the sentence "For more information, visit our Collections and Challenges FAQ" and a [link to the old FAQ page|https://archiveofourown.org/faq/collections-and-challenges?language_id=en#replacedfaq], which has now been replaced by new FAQs.

*What should happen?*

You should receive an email containing the sentence "For more information, visit our Collections FAQ" and the following link instead: [https://archiveofourown.org/faq/collections?language_id=en#collectionoptions|https://archiveofourown.org/faq/collections?language_id=en#collectionoptions]

*Additional testing notes*

The coder has also updated two outdated links in the Terms of Service and Terms of Service FAQ.

Please confirm that the hyperlink in this sentence of the TOS now to the correct location: Archive users may create Collections and encourage other users to submit fanworks to those Collections.

And the hyperlink in this portion of the TOS FAQ: Please consult the Archive FAQ. Please note that participants may provide information to the maintainer for purposes of participating in a collection or challenge.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Automatic reconnect and transactions don't play well together. Specifically, if a disconnect/reconnect occurs in the middle of a transaction, the first half of the transaction is rolled back (because it wasn't committed before the disconnect), and the second half of the transaction isn't wrapped in a transaction (because the transaction isn't reopened after the reconnect).

Let's get rid of automatic reconnect, to prevent these half-transactions.

*Note:* {{config/database.yml}} isn't under version control, so the PR part of this should just be the removal of the {{activerecord-mysql-reconnect}} gem.

column1: Include IP address, referrer URL, and title of public site skin in support tickets
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
We're going to do some fun site skin things! To make handling any skin issues (seriously, theme or style would've killed us?) easier, we want to make sure tickets sent to Support automatically include information about which skin a user is using.

* Support will need to set up a custom field in the ticket tracker. The name will probably be something like {{cf_site_skin}}, but you'll need to check in with them.
* This should not be user-facing, and it should ideally not even be a hidden field on the Support and Feedback page, since that would be editable. You can look at how we handle the Rollout version ({{cf_rollout}}) for inspiration.
* If the user is using a public site skin (including Default), the field should reference it by title. If the user is using a non-public site skin, the field should say "Custom skin."
** Note: If the user has set a skin using the skin chooser in the footer or the Set for Session option on the skin page, this will override the skin they have set in their preferences/by using the Use button on the skin page. Ergo, the field should list the skin set via the session cookie ({{session[:site_skin]}}) if present. If none is present, then it’s safe to use the preference skin.
* It does not need to be recorded in the database.

Additionally, Support sometimes needs to pass tickets to Policy & Abuse. Policy & Abuse sometimes needs IP address and often needs URLs so they can action the tickets. Therefore, Support would like the tickets they get to also include IP addresses and referrers.

* Support will need to set up custom fields for these as well; probably something like {{cf_ip}} and {{cf_referer}}, but you'll need to check with them.
* These should also be neither user-facing nor hidden fields.
* These do not need to be recorded in the database.
* If the referrer is not an AO3 URL (e.g., if the person is coming from the pinned tweet or the link in an email footer), it can be left blank. If it _is_ an AO3 URL, it should be presented as-is (i.e., without any of the URL clean-up used by the abuse form) and should not have any restrictions applied.
* The “Our spam filter does collect IP addresses, but we never see them” message should be removed from the form.

*Testing*

To test the skin field, you'll want to submit a support ticket while using 

* the Default skin,
* a public skin from the chooser in the footer
* a public skin from the skins page, and 
* a custom skin.

To test the referrer, you will also need to submit a support ticket from

* the link in an email
* a page on the site

You should also make sure the message about IP addresses is no longer on the support form.

Someone from support will need to confirm the ticket contains the right info.

NB: We’re not changing the admin feedback mailer because it’s being removed in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6443|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6443|smart-link].

column1: Random Items button on a collection doesn't work from the collection homepage
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Go to any collection.
# From the collection home page, follow the "Random Items" link on the left sidebar.

h1. What happens

If "Random Items" is clicked on the collection home page, the user remains on the same page.

h1. What should happen

The collection homepage should reload with a new set of random works.

h1. Notes

The way this feature actually works is super subtle. If you’re on a collection that shows _recent_ works on its homepage by default, e.g., [https://archiveofourown.org/collections/queercharactersgen|https://archiveofourown.org/collections/queercharactersgen] on production, it’s easier to see. 

* Go to the page linked above, observe that it lists “Recent works”
* Follow the “Profile” link
* Follow “Random Items”

At first glance, it looks like “Random Items” just takes you to the collection homepage.

If you look more closely, you’ll see that it takes you to the homepage but now the homepage displays “Random works” rather than “Recent works.”

That’s it; that’s the feature: it [appends ?show_random to the collection URL|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/da11290f5ae6c3328d164cac6b7f5d2742c72f29/app/views/collections/_sidebar.html.erb#L34-L38], which [loads a  list of 5 random works and 5 random bookmarks on the collection homepage|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/da11290f5ae6c3328d164cac6b7f5d2742c72f29/app/controllers/collections_controller.rb#L68-L74].

21/Sep/21 10:18 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;The reason the link on the collection homepage doesn’t work is because the link is marked as {{remote: true}} in that case:

{noformat}  <% if controller.controller_name == 'collections' && controller.action_name == 'show' %>
  <%= link_to 'Random Items', 
    :url => collection_path(@collection, :show_random => true), :method => :get, :remote => true %>  
  <% else %>  
  <%= link_to 'Random Items', collection_path(@collection, :show_random => true) %>
  <% end %>{noformat}

[(source)|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6b99402ac54eba0b220e85163408c777322c2251/app/views/collections/_sidebar.html.erb#L34-L39]

But the link shouldn’t be marked as {{remote: true}}, because the collection homepage doesn’t have any JS-specific responses. So {{rails-ujs}} will try (and fail) to treat the HTML of the collection homepage as JS, instead of reloading it.

(Note: Thanks to full-page caching, logged-out users will see the same set of randomized works for about an hour, even if they repeatedly reload to try to re-randomize. If that’s a problem, someone needs to play around with the nginx configuration. Otherwise, I think this issue could be marked Easy.)

column1: Non-admin wranglers can syn a canonical tag to another canonical
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

tl;dr if you're logged in as a non-admin wrangler, you can syn Canonical A to Canonical B *if* you still have a tab open to Canonical A's pre-canonization edit page. This sometimes happens accidentally because wranglers often have multiple tabs open.

# Log in as a user with the tag wrangler role
# Create some new character and relationship tags\! The easiest way to do this en masse is by creating a new work:
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required information
## In "Characters" field, enter three new character tags, e.g. {{AO3-6239 Canonical Char 1}}, AO3-6239 Syn Char 1, {{AO3-6239 Char 1}}
## In relationships field, enter two new relationships, e.g. {{AO3-6239 & Ship 1}}, {{AO3-6239 / Ship}} 1 
## Press "Post"
# We're going to need to edit two of these tags, so 
## Find the link to {{AO3-6239 Canonical Char 1}} in the work meta, open it in a new tab/window, follow its "Edit" link
## Find the link to {{AO3-6239 Char 1}} in the work meta, open it in *two* new tabs/windows, and in each of these windows, follow its "Edit" link
# On the edit page for {{AO3-6239 Canonical Char 1}}, check "Canonical" and press "Save changes"
# On one of the edit pages for {{AO3-6239 Char 1}}, check "Canonical" and press "Save changes"
# Still in the same tab, add some associations to {{AO3-6239 Char 1}}
## Fill in the "Relationships" section with {{AO3-6239 & Ship 1}}, {{AO3-6239 / Ship 1}}
## Fill in the "Synonyms" section with {{AO3-6239 Syn Char 1}}
## Press "Save changes"
# Wait a minute or two
# Now switch to the other tab where you have {{AO3-6239 Char 1}}'s edit page open
# Fill in the "Synonym of" field with {{AO3-6239 Canonical Char 1}}
# Press "Save changes"

h1. What happens

{{AO3-6239 Char 1}} becomes a synonym of {{AO3-6239 Canonical Char 1}}. 

{{AO3-6239 Canonical Char 1}} now has all the associations that were attached to {{AO3-6239 Char 1}}. 

h1. What should happen

The changes should not be save and you should get an error message that says, "Only an admin can make a canonical tag into a synonym of another tag."

Once we have

*  set up the i18n-tasks gem ([AO3-6003|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6003])
*  run the initial i18n-tasks normalization task and merged the result (also AO3-6003)

and before we

* merge any other i18n work
* add any other translations to Phrase

we need to rename some keys we use in the mailers. They're currently named things like "part5" or "para1," which is not great if we want to add or remove paragraphs.

To do this, we’ll

* use [i18n-tasks mv|https://github.com/glebm/i18n-tasks#move--rename--merge-keys] to update the keys for all locales at once (commands below)
* update the view files to actually use those keys
* merge those changes
* import all of the locales – not just the English – back into Phrase

We use JavaScript to let users show/hide the form. When JavaScript is disabled, it’s always open to make sure people can create or update their bookmarks. The x can’t hide the form without JavaScript, so it’s just a link to the page’s #comments section.

column1: Changing fandom name while approving tag set nominations can split the fandom
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Steps to reproduce the bug:

1. Create a new tag set: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/new|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/new]
2. Select "Currently taking nominations?"
3. Enter some limits for Fandom and Character nominations (for instance, 2 and 5).
4. Select "Submit" so the tag set will be open for submissions.
5. Have at least 2 different accounts nominate tags for the tag set, as follows:
a.  Both accounts should select the same fandom (it can be anything, but for this purpose, let's say "Wrong Fandom".
b.  Both accounts should enter, under "Wrong Fandom", the character "Right Character".  They should also enter several other random characters of their choice.
6. As the tag set maintainer, go back to your tag set and select "Review Nominations".
7. See "Wrong Fandom" with the character "Right Character x2" (or however many multiple nominations this character has.)
7. Using the text box next to "Wrong Fandom," enter "Right Fandom" as if you want to manually change the fandom name when you approve it.    Do not approve or change the characters.
8.  Select "Submit".

What should happen: 

The fandom "Right Fandom" should appear at the top of the page under "Already Approved Fandoms", with the full list of nominated characters underneath it.  "Wrong Fandom" should not be approved or appear anywhere.

What actually happens:

Two fandoms appear at the top of the page under "Already Approved Fandoms" - Right Fandom, containing all characters who were nominated 1 time, and Wrong Fandom, containing any characters that were nominated 2 or more times.  The fandom is now "split", and various further problems/errors can occur from here as the confused mod tries to sort out the problem:

* If you try to change the multiple-nominated character name under the Wrong Fandom, such as to "Right Character (Books)", you receive an error: "Oh no\! We ran into a problem partway through saving your updates, changing Right Character to Right Character (Books) – please check over your tag set closely\!" Both "Right Character" and "Right Character (Books)" will now show in the fandom box.
* If you try to change the multiple-nominated character name to a name already approved (such as in the Right Fandom version of the nomination), you receive the same error as above, plus the additional error "Someone else has already nominated the tag \[TAGNAME] for this set but in fandom \[FANDOMNAME].  (All nominations have to be unique for the approval process to work.) Try making your nomination more specific, for instance tacking on FANDOMNAME2."
* You can reject the multiple-nominated character under the Wrong Fandom and then edit it manually back into the correct fandom using batch loading.
* You can approve the multiple-nominated character under the Wrong Fandom and it should go through, but this is nonintuitive.

See attached images of this happening in a real tag set under review.

column1: Possible to submit additional nominations beyond the maximum using multiple windows
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
There is an exploit which allows users to nominate one more than the fandom limit set by the tag set rules, which subsequently also prevents the user from editing their nomination.  

Steps to reproduce:

1. Create a tag set with a fandom limit (e.g. 2)
2. Create a nomination in the tagset but leave the last fandom slot unfilled
3. Open two windows editing the same nomination
4. Fill two different fandoms into each of the last slots and hit submit on both windows

The last edit screen to finish saving will show three nominations.  Note: this only appears to work to allow N+1 fandoms - attempting to do this in, for instance, 5 different windows still only accepts 1 additional fandom, not 5 additional fandoms.

If you attempt to edit the nomination and delete the third fandom to bring it back in line with the rules, the nomination can no longer be edited. The following flash error message appears:

Sorry\! We couldn't save this tag set nomination because:
You can only nominate 2 fandom tags

Example nomination and tag set:

[https://archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/8218/nominations/220972|https://archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/8218/nominations/220972] (I had them make AO3_ADT and Sarken (AO3_ADT) owners and mods).

A similar thing happens with character nominations (and presumably other fields such as relationships, additional tags, etc), making it possible to add additional characters beyond the maximum.

1. Create another nomination
2. Fill out both fandoms but nominate no characters. 
3. Open 2 edit nomination windows
4. Nominate 2 different characters in each window under the first fandom, for a total of 4 separate characters
5, Click submit in both windows.

Result: you have 4 characters nominated in that fandom.  

Example: [https://archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/8218/nominations/220978|https://archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/8218/nominations/220978]

What should happen:

You should not be able to nominate more tags in a given category (fandoms, characters, relationships, etc.) than specified by the challenge settings.  Attempting to add extras via a second window should result in an error such as "Sorry\! We couldn't save this tag set nomination because: You can only nominate 2 fandom tags"

column1: Incorrect pluralization in kudos emails
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. A brief language lesson.

In English, the number of people who've left kudos on your work does not change the verb we use in the email:

* Singular: username *left* kudos on Work Title.
* Plural: username1 and username2 *left* kudos on Work Title.

In French, for example, the verb must change based on the number of people:

* Singular: username *a félicité* votre œuvre Work Title.
* Plural: username1 et username2 *ont félicité* votre œuvre Work Title.

Other languages get even more complex, e.g., you might need a different verb if 5 people have left kudos than if 50 have left kudos.

h1. The bug

Note: It doesn't matter if the people leaving kudos are logged in users, guests, or a combination of both. 

If...

* 3 people leave kudos on Work A and Work C, and 
* 1 person leaves kudos on Work B, 

Then you might get an email that incorrectly uses the plural verb for Work B:

{quote}username1, username2 et username3 *ont félicité* votre œuvre Work A.

username *ont félicité* votre œuvre Work B.

username1, username2 et username3 *ont félicité* votre œuvre Work C.{quote}

Or that incorrectly uses the singular for Work A and Work C:

{quote}username1, username2 et username3 *a félicité* votre œuvre Work A.

username1, username2 et username3 *a félicité* votre œuvre Work C.

username *a félicité* votre œuvre Work B.{quote}

If...

* 1 person leaves kudos on Work A and Work C, and 
* 2 people leave kudos on Work B, 

Then you might get an email that incorrectly uses the singular verb for Work B: 

{quote}username *a félicité* votre œuvre Work A.

username1 et username2 *a félicité* votre œuvre Work B.

username *a félicité* votre œuvre Work C.{quote}

Or that incorrectly uses the plural for Work A and Work C:

{quote}username *ont félicité* votre œuvre Work A.

username *ont félicité* votre œuvre Work C.

username1 et username2 *ont félicité* votre œuvre Work B.{quote}

h1. Whyyyyy

If you read over the examples again, you might notice a pattern: when there are kudos for multiple works, the pluralization for every work is determined by the last work in the email.

The problem appears to be that the {{@kudos_count}} we use to determine pluralization ({{count: @kudos_count}}) is not set for each work ({{commentable}}):

[kudo_mailer.rb|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/4085de66e21dde41a9e6730b0f746e205b6da3a5/app/mailers/kudo_mailer.rb#L18-L40]:

{code:ruby}  kudos_hash.each_pair do |commentable_info, kudo_givers_hash|
    # Parse the key to extract the type and id of the commentable - skip if no commentable
    commentable_type, commentable_id = commentable_info.split('_')
    commentable = commentable_type.constantize.find_by(id: commentable_id)
    next unless commentable


    # If we have a commentable, extract names and process guest kudos text - skip if no kudos givers
    names = kudo_givers_hash['names']
    guest_count = kudo_givers_hash['guest_count']
    kudo_givers = []


    if !names.nil? && names.size > 0
      kudo_givers = names
      kudo_givers << guest_kudos(guest_count) unless guest_count == 0
      @kudos_count = names.size + guest_count
    else
      kudo_givers << guest_kudos(guest_count).capitalize unless guest_count == 0
      @kudos_count = guest_count
    end
    next if kudo_givers.empty?


    @commentables << commentable
    @kudo_givers[commentable_info] = kudo_givers{code}

[batch_kudo_notification.text.erb|https://github.com/sarken/otwarchive/blob/6b99402ac54eba0b220e85163408c777322c2251/app/views/kudo_mailer/batch_kudo_notification.text.erb#L2-L8]

{code:ruby}<% @commentables.each_with_index do |commentable, index| %>
    <% givers_list = @kudo_givers["#{commentable.class.name}_#{commentable.id}"].to_sentence
       commentable_link = "\"#{commentable.commentable_name.html_safe}\" (#{polymorphic_url(commentable)})".html_safe %>
    
    <%= t 'mailer.kudos.text.left_kudos', givers_list: givers_list, commentable_link: commentable_link, count: @kudos_count.to_i %>{code}


Additionally, if you check the count supplied by {{@kudos_count}}, it's off by one if there are any guests involved. 

That appears to be because {{names}} ultimately includes not just the usernames, but also the string that represents guests, e.g., {{"a guest"}} or {{"5 guests"}}. 

So {{kudos_count = names.size + guest_count}} is actually doing {{["username1", "username2", "a guest"].size + guest_count}}

The collection maintainers get an email with the subject line "\[AO3]\[Collection title] Assignments sent."

That is indeed what should happen, but the user_mailer.collection_notification.assignments_sent.subject key should match that (\[%\{app_name}]\[%\{collection_title}] ...).

column1: Kudos mailer handles capitalisation incorrectly
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The kudos mailer is set up to force "guest"/"guests" to be written in lowercase. That should not be the case, as there are languages where that word has to be capitalised.

1. Set your locale in 'Preferences' to German (Deutsch)
2. Create a work
3. Leave guest kudos on a work

*What happens*

You'll receive a kudos notification with "Ein gast hat Kudos für \[title] hinterlassen" or "# gäste haben Kudos für \[title] hinterlassen"

*What should happen*

"Gast" and "Gäste" should be capitalised. (They are capitalized in the locale file, but getting converted to lowercase because {{capitalize}} is being called on, e.g., {{"ein Gast"}}.)

h1. The preference We want to add a new preference to the preferences page: Allow others to give me gift works outside gift exchanges and prompt memes. * The database column should be called allow_gifts. * The preference should be on/true for all users that exist at the time of deploy. (This is necessary to minimize the effect it will have on ongoing challenges that do not use the Archive's assignments or claims feature, or that encourage users to create additional gifts for requests they aren't assigned to or haven't claimed.) * The preference should be off/false for all users created after deploy. * The preference should be located in the "Collections, Challenges and Gifts" section of the preferences page, directly beneath "Automatically agree to your work being collected by others in the Archive." It should be called, "Allow others to give me gift works outside gift exchanges and prompt memes." * The collection-preferences.html help file, accessed using the "?" link in the "Collections, Challenges and Gifts" heading, should be updated to include the following: {noformat}
Allow others to give me gift works outside gift exchanges and prompt memes
If this option is disabled, users are only able to give a gift work to another user if they're completing a gift exchange assignment or fulfilling a claimed prompt in a prompt meme. If you'd like to allow users to give you gift works outside of assignments and claimed prompts, enable this option. Note that you're always able to refuse gifts individually. Check out How do I refuse a gift? for instructions.
{noformat} Migrations do not need to be a separate pull request. *Testing:* * Log in as an existing user and go to your preferences page. Ensure the checkbox for "Allow others to give me gift works outside gift exchanges and prompt memes." is checked and in the correct location. * Create a new account and go to your preferences page. Ensure the checkbox for "Allow others to give me gift works outside gift exchanges and prompt memes." is unchecked and in the correct location. * Access the help file using the "?" link in the "Collections, Challenges and Gifts" heading. Ensure that the help text matches the text in this issue. h1. The functionality If a user turns the preference off, they should not be able to receive gifts unless the gift work fulfills a gift exchange assignment or a claim of a non-anonymous prompt. When accessing the sign-up form for a gift exchange or prompt meme, users who have the preference turned off should see a yellow caution notice at the top of the sign-up page, directly below the heading but above the notice about email addresses: "Signing up for this challenge will allow users to give you gift works in response to your requests. However, you can always refuse a gift." Attempting to give a gift to a user with the preference disabled should give a red error that says: "#\{byline of the pseud/user you tried to gift} does not accept gifts." *Testing set up:* # Log in as User A, who will be our challenge mod as well as our recipient. # Update your preferences so "Allow others to give me gift works outside gift exchanges and prompt memes." is off/unchecked. # Create a gift exchange collection with open sign-ups and random matching and sign up for it. # Create a prompt meme collection with open-sign-ups that allows anonymous prompts and sign up for it, creating one anonymous prompt and one non-anonymous prompt. # Log in as User B, who will be our gift-giver. # Sign up for the gift exchange from Step 2. # Claim the prompts from Step 3. # Log back in as User A. # Close sign-ups for your gift exchange, run matching, make sure User B is assigned to write for you, and send assignments. *Testing:* # User B should be able to fulfill their gift exchange assignment for User A with User A listed as the gift recipient. # User B should be able to fulfill their prompt meme claim for User A's non-anonymous prompt and successfully list User A as the gift recipient. Note that unlike with gift exchanges, you must manually enter User A in the "Gift this work to" field for prompt fills. # User B should be able to fulfill their prompt meme claim for User A's anonymous prompt, but if they list User A as the gift recipient, they should receive an error. # User A should be able to access their Gifts page and refuse the gift works from Steps 1 and 2. # User B should be able to edit the works from Steps 1 and 2 after User A refuses them. # User B should not be able to post or update a work unaffiliated with the assignment/claim from Steps 1 or 2 and list User A as the gift recipient. # If User B edits the work from Steps 1 or 2 and disconnects the work from the assignment/claim, User A should remain listed as the gift recipient. (Note: Originally said should not, oops, my bad.) # If User A updates their preferences so "Allow others to give me gift works outside gift exchanges and prompt memes." is turned on/checked, any user should be able to give them a gift. It wouldn't hurt to check Steps 1-3 again, this time ensuring User B can always give User A a gift. Please also make sure the caution notice is displayed on sign-up pages when logged in as a user who has "Allow others to give me gift works outside gift exchanges and prompt memes." turned off/unchecked.

column1: Allow SSL for SMTP to be configurable
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
On Debian 11, we get an error when sending mails:

{noformat}OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError (hostname "localhost" does not match the server certificate){noformat}

The easiest solution seems to be to disable SSL support for [SMTP in Rails|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/action_mailer_basics.html#action-mailer-configuration], specifically by setting {{enable_starttls_auto}} to {{false}} and {{openssl_verify_mode}} to {{none}}.

{quote}{{:enable_starttls_auto}} - Detects if STARTTLS is enabled in your SMTP server and starts to use it. Defaults to {{true}}.

{{:openssl_verify_mode}} - When using TLS, you can set how OpenSSL checks the certificate. This is really useful if you need to validate a self-signed and/or a wildcard certificate. You can use the name of an OpenSSL verify constant ('none' or 'peer') or directly the constant ({{OpenSSL::SSL::VERIFY_NONE}} or {{OpenSSL::SSL::VERIFY_PEER}}).{quote}

h2. Testing instructions

On our current Debian 10 systems, check that email notifications still work:

* One synchronous example, e.g. for work deletions.
* One asynchronous (via workers) example, e.g. for kudos and comments.

Get Systems to upgrade staging servers to Debian 11 and test again.

column30:
# Log in.

# Fill in valid fields.
# Put the text "‍" in the title.

[The work appears to have no title|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1074568] – there's a blank space where the title should be, and in the work blurb there's no title link to click on (which makes the work inaccessible if it has only one chapter, and doesn't have any comments or kudos). There may be similar issues with the HTML code for other invisible characters, like "​" (the zero-width space).
column149:
10/Nov/22 10:00 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;A similar trick works for tags ([notice the blank fandom|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1078326]). It probably works for most models with string attributes that aren’t supposed to be blank, because most strings passed as params are processed with these two steps:

# Strip non-printing characters like the zero-width joiner.
# Process with {{Sanitize.clean}}, which parses the string and converts most entities escaped with & into the unescaped version.

So by entering the character as {{‍}}, it avoids being stripped by step 1, but then step 2 converts it back into a character that would have been stripped.

(Note that [those characters probably shouldn’t be stripped|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6087], so re-stripping them after the call to {{Sanitize.clean}} is not the right answer here.)
