column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Currently all challenge moderators/owners get CCed in the {{collection_notification}} email that lets them know challenge assignments have been sent out. This email should instead be generated individually so that users' locale preferences can apply.

# On your Preferences page, select a locale other than English
# Create a collection
# Create a gift exchange challenge
# Sign up for this challenge with at least two different accounts
# Open the challenge's Membership page (/collections/NAME/participants) and mark a second account as challenge owner
# Close sign-ups and run matching
# Send out assignments

*What happens*

Both challenge owners are CCed on an “Assignments sent” email in English saying that assignments have been sent out.

*What should happen*

Each challenge owner should receive their own email, following their locale preferences. At least the footer should be translated, other text may remain in English, depending on availability of translations at the time of testing.

Note: [AO3-6255|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6255] is about the subject line of this same email.

*Testing*

In addition to the testing steps above, please also test:

# Default on one of the assignments
# Run matching in a collection with invalid signups and multiple owners, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/ge_invalid_signups|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/ge_invalid_signups]

Each owner should receive their own “Challenge default by …” email after step 8, with at least the footer translated according to their locale preferences.

Each owner should receiver their own “Invalid sign-ups found” email after step 9, with the footer translated according to their locale preferences.

Furthermore, each owner should receive their own “Potential assignment generation complete” email after step 6, with the footer translated according to their locale preferences.

column1: Ensure that any before_action filters that redirect with an error should instead render it for JS requests
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
We are still sometimes seeing the error {{ActionView::Template::Error: undefined method `downloads_enabled?' for nil:NilClass}} in our logs, so [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5598|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5598|smart-link]  doesn't eliminate it entirely.

If we submit a JS request (like loading the comments), and the server does a redirect to a page that doesn’t have a JS view (like the login page or the work page), it’ll skip the {{fetch_admin_settings}} callback, but will still try to render the rest of the page normally. This results in undefined method errors, because {{@admin_settings}} is still nil.

The {{fetch_admin_settings}} callback has been removed in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6558|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6558|smart-link], but we still need to make sure that any {{before_action}} filters that redirect with an error should, for JS requests, return some JS that displays the error instead, so that the user doesn’t just click and have nothing happen.

h2. Testing

Log in as an admin and change an admin setting. Make sure that setting actually changes and takes effect.
column149:
08/Jan/22 4:26 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;Are you certain this is a caching bug?

The {{downloads_enabled?}} function is only called in one place in views: the work header. But it’s called on the {{@admin_settings}} variable, not on {{AdminSetting.current}}, which means that  there are two ways for that error to occur: either {{fetch_admin_settings}} isn’t called (which happens for JS & JSON requests, as well as autocomplete), or {{AdminSetting.current}} returns {{nil}}.

Looking at the code, I’m not sure how either one could occur, but I’m particularly puzzled about how {{AdminSetting.current}} can return {{nil}}, because it's supposed to return an {{OpenStruct}} with some default settings if the call to {{Rails.cache.fetch}} returns {{nil}}. Is it possible that this is some weird issue with {{fetch_admin_settings}} getting skipped instead, maybe because of a link being accidentally marked as {{remote: true}} when it shouldn’t? Or some third party creating a badly-formed XHR request?

When I do this on my machine, I get this error: {noformat}ActionView::Template::Error (undefined method `invite_from_queue_enabled?' for nil:NilClass): 14:

15: <%= t(".restricted.commenting_unavailable") %> 16: <%= t(".restricted.account_exists") %> 17: <% if @admin_settings.invite_from_queue_enabled? && @admin_settings.creation_requires_invite? %> 18: <%= t(".restricted.no_account", request_invite_link: link_to(t(".restricted.request_invite"), invite_requests_path)).html_safe %> 19: <% elsif @admin_settings.account_creation_enabled? && !@admin_settings.creation_requires_invite? %> 20: <%= link_to t(".restricted.signup"), signup_path %>{noformat} Basically, if you submit a JS request (like loading the comments), and the server does a redirect to a page that doesn’t have a JS view (like the login page or the work page), it’ll skip the {{fetch_admin_settings}} callback, but will still try to render the rest of the page normally. This results in undefined method errors, because {{@admin_settings}} is still nil. (I’m not sure what the best approach to fix it is, though. Switching to {{AdminSetting.current}} everywhere would prevent the issues with {{@admin_settings}} being nil and thus prevent the error from occurring in NewRelic, but that doesn’t fix the real error, which is that when you’re doing a JS request, any {{before_action}} filters that redirect with an error should probably return some JS that displays the error instead, so that the user doesn’t just click and have nothing happen.)

column30:
Suspended users are able to leave kudos. They should not be able to do that.

*Steps to reproduce*

# Suspend a user
## Log in as an admin with the superadmin or policy_and_abuse role
## Manage Users > Find Users
## Fill in “Name” with the name of the user you want to suspend
## Press “Find”
## Follow the “Details” link for the associated user
## In “Warnings and Suspensions,” choose “Suspend: Enter whole number of days”
## Enter some number of days in the field
## Enter some text in the “Notes” section
## Press “Update”
## Log out
# Log in as the user you suspended
# Locate a work you didn’t create
# Press “Kudos”

*What happens*

You successfully leave kudos.

*What should happen*

If JavaScript is enabled, you should receive a red flash error without the page reloading. The error should say: “You cannot leave kudos while your account is suspended.”

If JavaScript is disabled, you should be redirected to your dashboard, where you will see the message, “Your account has been suspended until \[date]. You may not add or edit content until your suspension has been resolved. Please [contact Abuse|https://test.archiveofourown.org/abuse_reports/new] for more information.” (This is consistent with attempting to leave comments.)

*Notes*

This also applies to banned, aka permanently suspended, users. Please test that as well.

column1: "Chapter # of [title]" in co-creation emails is not translatable
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When a user is added as co-creator of a chapter, the email contains a linked "Chapter # of \[title]" that is not translated, unlike the rest of the email. This applies to all three co-creation emails that can apply to chapters ({{creatorship_notification}}, {{creatorship_request}} and {{creatorship_notification_archivist}}).

*Steps to reproduce*

1. In 'My Preferences,' choose a locale that has translations uploaded, e.g. French
2. Make sure your account has the 'Allow others to invite me to be a co-creator' preference enabled
3. Log in with a *different* account than the one you want to receive the email with. 
4. To generate {{creatorship_request}}, create a work. Add a new chapter, select the 'Add co-creators?' ticky and input the name of the account you wish to receive the email notification with.
5. To generate {{creatorship_notification_archivist}}, you'll need to log in with an account with archivist permissions, such as testy. While logged in as testy, create a work. Add a new chapter, select the 'Add co-creators?' ticky and input the name of the account you wish to receive the email notification with.
6. To generate {{creatorship_notification}}, you can use the work you already used for step #5, or: create a new work, add your account as co-creator, and accept the co-creation request from your account. Then, starting from a work that _already has_ a co-creator, add a new chapter and ticky the box under "Current co-creators" that corresponds to the user you want to receive the email with.

*What happens*

The line "Chapter # of __" (e.g. "Chapter 2 of 'Testing co-creation') is in English even if the entire email is translated. (It doesn't matter whether the chapter has a title. The chapter title does not appear in this email.)

*What should happen*

That line should not be in English.

column1: Same work appears on multiple pages of search results due to ties in Elasticsearch
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h2. Problem description

Our sorting recipes (for example [WorkQuery|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e60e8226f193eed1daf13f6ab2ea45b49b58e7a9/app/models/search/work_query.rb#L273] one) include only primary search criteria and don't tell ES what should happen if elements are equal. This may result in inconsistent sorting.

We want to unambiguously break ties and return predictable results.

h2. Background

It's possible that this change will in some degree solve the intermittent issue "work appears on multiple pages".

If works A and B are are considered equal as per sorting criteria, their order is not guaranteed to be persistent between searches. Actions such as updating works, adding comments, changing stats, wrangling tags should cause reindexing and thus change the default ES sorting order.

Lets say works A and B are suppose to end up as as last work on page 1/first work on page 2. It might happen that on navigation to page 1 works order is (A, B), so work A is shown on page 1, and on navigation to page 2 order would become (B, A), so again work A would be shown on page 2, instead of expected work B.

In production this behavior might be observed for a period of time (at least couple of minutes) and can be reproduced in different browser sessions. It's unclear what causes it/how much caching or elasticsearch internals are involved.



Note that the issue is valid not just for works, but for bookmarks (and possibly tags) as well.

h2. Testing instructions

Reproducing search instability is a bit difficult in real environments with many Elasticsearch shards as problem depends in which shard the work ends up in.

(After identifying the works in the same shard it should also be possible to reproduce "work appears on multiple pages" by changing setup such a way that these works appear on different pages. It would be possible to observe behavior at least once, but maybe not for a couple of minutes as in production.)

# Create at least 13 works by author Writer (there are currently 12 work shards by default, so with 13 works we assure there are at least two in the same shard)
# Navigate to works by Writer and sort works by Author.
# Notice works order (before the fix it would seem random).
# For the first work from the bottom:
## Update summary to "Updated 1"
## Assure/wait for reindexing to complete
## Refresh the page with works from step 2
# Check if the order changed (summary number is out of order).
# Keep repeating steps 4 and 5 for all other works updating summary to "Updated n".

Current behavior: 
At least two works switch places at least once.

Expected behavior:
Works order keeps being stable

column1: Try to reduce frequency of RecordNotFound errors when calling flush_work_cache
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
There are a lot of Resque errors along the lines of this one:
{code}
Tag
Arguments
--- perform_on_instance

--- 71249578

--- flush_work_cache
Exception
ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
Error
Couldn't find Tag with 'id'=71249578
{code}
When a brand new tag is created, the {{flush_work_cache}} job is enqueued after the tag is committed to the database. However, the Resque workers sometimes process jobs so quickly that when the worker tries to read the tag from one of the read-only database copies, that copy hasn't processed the commit that created the tag yet, causing the job to fail due to a {{RecordNotFound}} error.

We'd like to switch the {{queue_flush_work_cache}} callback so that it no longer runs when a tag is first created, since when a tag is first created there are no other works that need their cache flushed.

h1. Testing Instructions

To make sure that changing the callback from {{after_save}} to {{after_update}} didn't break anything, it would be good to make sure that the cache expiration still works when a tag is renamed:
# Pick a tag.
# Open a work that uses that tag.
# Rename the tag.
# Wait five minutes to make sure that the cache expiration runs.
# Reload the work.
# Make sure that the name shown in the work's tags has changed.

We also want to check whether this has reduced the number of errors like the one shown above, so this issue should be set to Pending Attention On Beta.

column1: Tag bookmark listings for logged-out users include series where the only works with that tag are restricted
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h2. Steps to Reproduce

# Log in
# Post a public work in a brand new series under a canonical fandom tag. Call it "Canonical Fandom A"
# Post a restricted work in the same series with a different canonical fandom tag. Call it "Canonical Fandom B"
# Bookmark your own series, and wait a minute or two it to be indexed
# Log out and look at the list of bookmarks for "Canonical Fandom B"

h3. What Should Happen

The bookmark shouldn't be listed, because the only work in the series tagged with "Canonical Fandom B" is restricted, and you are viewing the page logged-out.

h3. What Actually Happens

The bookmark is listed.

h3. Notes

This one's tricky, because we want logged-in users to be able to find series by their restricted tags. This will likely involve modifying the indexer to split certain tag-related fields into two (one for guests, one for registered users), and have all of the queries/aggregations on those fields switch between the variants. This will probably need to be done for {{tag}}, {{filter_ids}}, {{fandom_ids}}, {{character_ids}}, {{relationship_ids}}, {{freeform_ids}}, {{archive_warning_ids}}, {{category_ids}}, and {{rating_ids}} (but see [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6163#icft=AO3-6163|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6163#icft=AO3-6163|smart-link] for other issues with the rating field).

h2. Testing instructions

The steps listed in “steps to reproduce” and additionally:

# Log in again and change the work from Step 3 (Canonical Fandom B) to unrestricted
# Wait 5-15 minutes
# While still logged in, look at the list of bookmarks for "Canonical Fandom B." You should see the bookmark
# Log out and look at the list of bookmarks for "Canonical Fandom B." You should see the bookmark again
# Log in as an admin with the {{superadmin}}, {{legal}} or {{policy_and_abuse}} role
# Hide the work from Step 2 (Canonical Fandom A)
# View the series its in and make sure its tags are not listed on the series blurb
# Wait 5-15 minutes
# Still logged in as an admin, look at the list of bookmarks for "Canonical Fandom A." You should *not* see the bookmark
# Log out and look at the list of bookmarks for "Canonical Fandom A." You should *not* see the bookmark
# Log in as the user again and look at the list of bookmarks for "Canonical Fandom A." You should *not* see the bookmark

Change your locale in preferences to a language that has translations for emails and for the {{activerecord.models.work}} key uploaded (none as of this writing, the existing translation for the latter has been deleted, but it can be readded if necessary) 2. Make sure your "Allow others to invite me to be a co-creator." preference is enabled 3. Log in with a different account 4. column1: User suspension message provides incorrect time for the end of a user's suspension
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
# Log in as admin with the role superadmin or policy_and_abuse 
# Mange Users > Find Users
# In "Name" field, enter the login of a user whose account you have access to
# Press "Find"
# Follow the "Details" link in the correct row of the results table
# Under "Warnings and Suspensions," choose "Suspend: enter a whole number of days"
# Enter a number of days, e.g. 2
# In "Notes," supply some text explaining why you're suspending the user
# Press "Update"
# Log out as admin
# Log in as the suspended user
# Post > New Work

*What happens*

You are redirected to your user page with the flash error: "Your account has been suspended until Sun, 27 Feb 2022 23:55:39 +0000. You may not add or edit content until your suspension has been resolved. Please contact Abuse for more information."

The time in the error message is exactly 48 hours from the time the admin created the suspension, but that's not the time the suspension will be lifted – suspensions are lifted en masse once per day by the [unsuspend_users rake task|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b63fce67a3975ec0614bb535c75d76c8dafbda71/lib/tasks/admin_tasks.rake#L2-L6 ], which lifts the suspensions of any user whose {{suspended_until}} time is no more than 12 hours after the task is run.

{{User.where(["suspended_until <= ?", 12.hours.from_now]).update_all("suspended_until = NULL, suspended = false")}}

The [task is run at 06:51 UTC|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b63fce67a3975ec0614bb535c75d76c8dafbda71/config/schedule.rb#L37-L40] so the user above would not be unsuspended until Monday, February 28 2022, 06:51 UTC.

*What should happen*

The message should reflect the actual date the user will be unsuspended. Ideally, this information should be provided in the user's preferred timezone, but it should not include the time itself.

*Notes*

The draft work deletion message has similar issues.

column1: Numbers in Marathi/Hindi text should appear in Devanagari script
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
In text for languages using [Devanagari script|https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devanagari_numerals] (e.g. Marathi, Hindi), numbers should appear in the same script (०, १, २, ३, ४...) instead of Arabic numerals (0, 1, 2, 3, 4...).

Full list:

0 - ०
1 - १
2 - २
3 - ३
4 - ४
5 - ५
6 - ६
7 - ७
8 - ८
9 - ९
10 - १०
1,000 - १,०००
10,000 - १०,०००
100,000 - १,००,०००
1,000,000 - १०,००,०००
10,000,000 - १,००,००,०००

*Steps to reproduce*

1. Set your locale in Preferences to receive emails in Hindi or Marathi
2. Go to your Dashboard -> Invitations -> Request invitations
3. Request any number of invitations
4. Using an admin account with the PAC role (or a superadmin account), authorise or deny the request

*What happens*

You'll receive an email that mentions the number of invitations using an Arabic numeral (e.g. "4") amid the Marathi or Hindi text.

*What should happen*

The number of invitations should be mentioned only in Devanagari script, as per the list above.

This setting doesn't apply to comments on your own works; for more on controlling who can interact with you on your works check out the Posting and Editing FAQ.{quote} When a user enables the preference and comments on a news post or a work by another user, anyone who is logged out should not be able to reply to their comment. The "Reply" button should be removed from affected comments when the preference is enabled, but the caching we use for logged-out users means it may continue to appear for 45 minutes or an hour. We should also use a before_action to check the ability to reply, just like we do with frozen comments, works and news posts that restrict comments, etc. The wording of the error message should be consistent with the other errors: {quote}Sorry, this user doesn't allow non-Archive users to reply to their comments.{quote} Guests should still be allowed to reply to you on your works, including works you have co-created. h1. column1: Users with invalid pseud icons, icon alt text, or icon comment text can't request password resets or be suspended; also, changes to pseud icons on staging affect production
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
If you have a pseud with 

* an invalid icon (i.e., an icon that's not image/gif image/jpeg image/png),
* icon comment text over the max length (250 characters),
* or icon alt text over the max length (50 characters)

then

* when you are logged out, you cannot request a password reset
* and an admin cannot suspend your account

We plan to [email users about this|https://github.com/otwcode/otw-scripts/pull/18] to give them an opportunity to correct the issue, and then remove any invalid icons or text that remain after the deadline given in the email.

We need to commit the code for fixing the pseuds to the repo, since it does not belong in the otw-scripts repo, which deals solely with sending emails.

In order to test the code for fixing pseuds, we also need to fix the issue where changing a pseud icon on staging changes the pseud's icon on production. This happens because staging and production use the same S3 path; staging should be given its own that includes "staging" in the name, while production's should be unchanged to avoid wiping out any icons. 

-We will also need to temporarily stop validating icon type on staging so we can upload some invalid icons.- We can test the rake by uploading a valid icon and changing the {{icon_content_type}} column to something invalid.

*Post-deploy*:

* Update the [email templates|https://github.com/otwcode/otw-scripts/tree/master/config/email_templates/2022-03-invalid-pseuds] to use actual dates in the placeholders.
* Run the [Ruby script|https://github.com/otwcode/otw-scripts/blob/master/scripts/lookup_invalid_pseuds.rb] to collect the affected user email addresses, then run the resulting bash script ({{/tmp/runme.sh}}) to actually send the emails.
* Wait until the deadline mentioned in the emails, then run {{bundle exec rake After:fix_invalid_pseud_icon_data}}.

column1: Incomplete error message when including invalid tag with ^ symbol
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
There are certain restricted symbols that can’t be included in tags: , ^ * < > { } = ` \ %  When a user-generated tag includes one of these symbols, an error message appears when the user tries to preview or post the work, indicating that the tag cannot include any of the symbols in question.  For example, “Tag name 'Test*' cannot include the following restricted characters: , ^ * < > { } = ` \ %”

However, if a tag includes the caret symbol ^, this error message displays incorrectly.  Instead everything before the caret will not display.  For example, entering the tag Test^ will lead to the error message “' cannot include the following restricted characters: , ^ * < > { } = ` \ %”

Steps:

# Create a new work 
# Enter in one of the tag fields (Fandoms, Relationships, Characters, or Additional Tags) a tag including the ^ symbol.
# Attempt to post the work

What should happen:

* you should get an error message saying “Tag name 'TAGNAME^' cannot include the following restricted characters: , ^ * < > { } = ` ， 、 \ %”

What does happen:

* you get a confusing cut off error message that removes everything before the ^ symbol, including the words “Tag name” that are not even part of the user-generated tag.

What do I do once I've chosen someone? Both you and your fannish next-of-kin need to send a message to our [Abuse team|https://archiveofourown.org/abuse_reports/new], which handles next of kin requests, indicating that you want to have them as your fannish next-of-kin and that they agree. This doesn't open an Abuse case. *Changes*: "send a message to our Support team"; delete the sentence "This doesn't open an Abuse case." h5. What if my fannish next-of-kin decides they're tired of being my fannish next-of-kin? Either party can revoke a fannish next-of-kin agreement by [sending a message to our Abuse team|https://archiveofourown.org/abuse_reports/new] (this will not be an Abuse case, but our Abuse team handles the process). *Changes*: "sending a message to our Support team"; delete "(this will not be an Abuse case, but our Abuse team handles the process)”. h5. What if I decide I don't like my fannish next-of-kin agreement? Send an e-mail saying that you want to terminate the agreement. column30:
We have three kinds of bookmark blurbs:

* bookmark blurbs, which contain the bookmarkable and a single user's bookmark. These are used for
** the Recent Bookmarks page, i.e., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks|https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks]
** bookmark search results
** user and pseud dashboards, e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/NAME|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/NAME] and [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/NAME/pseuds/NAME|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/NAME/pseuds/NAME]
** user and pseud bookmark listings, e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/NAME/bookmarks|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/NAME/bookmarks] and [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/NAME/pseuds/NAME/bookmarks|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/NAME/pseuds/NAME/bookmarks]
** collection dashboards, e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME]
* bookmarkable blurbs, which contain the bookmarkable and multiple users' bookmarks. These are used for
** tag bookmark listings, e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/NAME/bookmarks|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/NAME/bookmarks]
** collection bookmark listings, e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collection/NAME/bookmarks|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collection/NAME/bookmarks]
* short bookmark blurbs, which contain a single user's bookmark. These are used for
** the bookmarkable blurb, to list the individual bookmarks
** a bookmarkable's bookmark page, e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/###/bookmarks|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/###/bookmarks]

Bookmark blurbs should have the user ID of both the bookmarker and the bookmarkable's creator(s). They should also have the bookmarkable’s ID (i.e., work-123, series-123, external-work-123).

Bookmarkable blurbs for series and works should have the user ID of only the bookmarkable's creator(s). They should also have the bookmarkable’s ID (i.e., work-123, series-123, external-work-123).

Short bookmark blurbs should have the user ID of the bookmarker.

column1: Allow users to block other users from commenting
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. What it should do

Blocking should apply to users and stick around if the user changes their name. (Only the blocked user's current name should be displayed.) 

Blocking a user should prevent them from:

* commenting on your works
* replying to comments on your works (i.e., they cannot reply to you, themselves, or a third person)
* directly replying to your comments on news posts, their works, or anyone else's works
* editing comments they have previously left on your works or comments 

It should not prevent them from:

* commenting on tags you wrangle
* replying to comments on tags you wrangle (i.e., they can reply to you, themselves, or a third person)
* replying to your comments on tags you do not wrangle
* deleting comments they have previously left on your works or comments

If you’ve co-created a work (or works) with them:

* they should be able to comment on the work or works you’ve co-created
* they should not be able to reply to  you on the work or works you’ve co-created

"Preventing" should involve back end checks in addition to hiding the relevant forms and buttons. 

"Your works" includes your anonymous works and works you have co-created.

h1. Who you can block

You should not be able to block:

* official accounts ([+AO3-5986+|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5986] should be implemented before comment blocking); you should receive an error.
** Text: Sorry, you can't block an official account.
* yourself. There shouldn’t even be a button for this.

h1. How you can block

* Wherever the button appears, it should say “Block” when the user is not currently blocked and “Unblock” when the user is currently blocked. (We’re calling it “the block button” below for simplicity.) 
* The block button should only be shown to logged in users.
* Checks for whether a particular user can be blocked (i.e., did the blocker co-create a work with the potential blockee) should occur after pressing the block button, not before displaying it.
* Blocking or unblocking a user should require confirmation, no matter where you are blocking them from (i.e., profile, dashboard, comments, Blocked Users page). 
** This should be a full page confirmation that provides information about what blocking does, similar to the confirm_delete.html.erb pages for deleting works, chapters, and so on.

!confirm_block (a196325a-4c43-4978-ab55-e5298ba4bb50).png|width=752,height=410,alt="Block username confirmation page with a big caution area for text about what blocking does."!

+Text for blocking confirmation page:+ 

Are you sure you want to *_block_* username? Blocking a user prevents them from:

* commenting on your works
* replying to your comments anywhere on the site

Blocking a user will not:

* delete or hide comments they previously left on your works; you can delete these individually
* hide their comments elsewhere on the site

!confirm_unblock (c36c916e-ff2f-47aa-8d2d-390c8862bbdd).png|width=50%,alt="Unblock username confirmation page with a big caution area for text about what unblocking does."!

+Text for unblocking confirmation page:+

Are you sure you want to *_unblock_* username? Unblocking a user allows them to resume:

* commenting on your works
* replying to your comments anywhere on the site



h2. From comments

* All comments from logged in users should have a block button located on the far right.
* Your own comments should not have a block button.

Example 1: When the currently logged-in user (current_user) has replied to another user (other_user) on some third party’s work (or a news post), and other_user then blocks them, current_user should not have a Reply option on other_user’s comments, nor should they have an Edit option on their existing reply to other_user. They should still have Reply and Edit options elsewhere, and they should have a block option for other_user and thread links for all comments.

!current_user_blocked_by_other_user (95f733bc-efdd-4062-a707-909354c84e5a).png|width=1389,height=495,alt="Comment section where current_user is blocked by other_user after having already replied to other_user. There is no option for current_user to add additional replies to other_user or edit their existing comment."!

Example 2: When current_user has commented on a work, and one of the work creators blocks them, current_user should not have a Reply option on any comments, nor an Edit option on their own comments. They should still have a block option for other commenters, as well as the thread links.

!current_user_blocked_by_work_creator (352a7ba3-6e10-46f2-9e8a-5326c80c303d).png|width=1398,height=568!

Example 3: The work creator is logged in. They have blocked a user (blocked_user) who previously left comments on their work. The work creator sees all options on the comments as usual; blocked_user’s comment contains an Unblock option.

!work_creator (723f654f-7632-47c2-ae18-b273a2f1612c).png|width=1380,height=497!

Notes:

* We should be able to check for blocked users in bulk, so avoid n+1 queries and make sure database indices exist. 
* We'll use the decorator pattern to add blocked info to all comments in one go.

h2. From dashboards and profiles

* User and pseud dashboards, as well as user profiles, should have a block button located to the left of the subscribe button.
* Your own dashboard or profile should not have a block button.

!profile_or_dash (0b76f8ef-3e00-4529-bf1c-d03afbdd4b07).png|width=1206,height=227,alt="A block button next to a subscribe button on a dashboard or profile."!

h2. From the Blocked Users page

* Your preferences page should have a "Blocked Users" link on top, between "Manage My Pseuds" and "Change My User Name." (Note: Admins cannot access a user’s preferences, so they will need to manually enter the URL.) 
* This link should point to the Blocked Users page, located at {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/blocked/users}}, where you should be able to manage your blocked users.
* The Blocked Users page should be accessible only by the user who owns the page as well as by admins with the {{policy_and_abuse}}, {{support}}, or {{superadmin}} roles. 
* Admins should be able to see all the buttons, but should receive an error if actually attempting to block or unblock users. (Similar to [AO3-6218|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6218].) 
* At the top of the page, there should be detailed information about what blocking does.
* It should be possible to block additional users from this page via a tiny form (with autocomplete) like the one for adding collection members. ([+AO3-4659+|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4659] indicates there are some issues with this sort of form, but we can fiddle with the two forms in a separate pull request.)
* The page should display the default pseud blurbs for users you've blocked, ranging from newest at the top to oldest at the bottom, with the sort explicit in the code. It should be paginated.
* The pseud blurbs should contain a block button in the lower right corner. (Functionally, this will only ever be the “Unblock” form of the button.)

+Text for top of Blocked Users page:+ 

Blocking a user prevents them from:

* commenting on your works
* replying to your comments anywhere on the site

Blocking a user will not:

* delete or hide comments they previously left on your works; you can delete these individually
* hide their comments elsewhere on the site

!preferences_page (99138764-472d-4fae-b1ad-aaefd2744dca).png|width=1024,height=240,alt="A preferences page with the new Blocked Users link between Manage My Pseuds and Change My User Name"!

!blocked_users_page (67aed1ec-df78-4583-aca0-3cf13e010190).png|width=50%,alt="Blocked Users page with a notice about what blocking does, a form to block users, and pseud blurbs for blocked users with the option to unblock."!

h1. Notes

* The migration can be a simple Rails migration; it does not need to be done with {{pt-online-schema-change}}.
* The new table should include [timestamps|https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveRecord/ConnectionAdapters/SchemaStatements.html#method-i-add_timestamps].

h1. Deploy notes

Migration must be run ahead of time: {{bundle exec rake db:migrate:up VERSION=20220519071139}}

column1: Allow tags to be sorted by number of uses
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
We’d like to modify the tag search form introduced in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5830|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5830|smart-link] to allow tags to be sorted by the number of uses.

h2. Implementation Notes

In Elasticsearch, the {{uses}} field for tags is based on the {{taggings_count_cache}} column. However, the {{taggings_count_cache}} is only updated in {{Tag.write_redis_to_database}} ([source|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/22394a36d4a93ac9f0e3d703871c42ca0483ee4e/app/models/tag.rb#L38-L51]), which uses {{update_all}} to skip callbacks. So Elasticsearch is only informed of the new {{taggings_count_cache}} value when the tag is manually edited by a wrangler. This means that sorting on {{uses}} produces very buggy-looking results.

The reason {{Tag.write_redis_to_database}} skips callbacks is because (a) it's a scheduled task that runs every 2 minutes, and (b) any tag with fewer than 1000 uses will be added to the list of tags processed by {{Tag.write_redis_to_database}} every time the tag’s taggings count is viewed. (i.e. When a tag is listed in tag search results, when a tag is listed in the wrangling bins, when a tag is edited.)

We’d like to add some kind of indexing (or partial indexing) whenever the taggings count changes to keep the {{uses}} field up-to-date. To avoid overwhelming Elasticsearch with updates, we'd also like to avoid doing extra work when the taggings count doesn't change. 

h2. Deploy Instructions

To account for older updates to the {{taggings_count_cache}} that didn’t make it into Elasticsearch, we need to reindex all tags with {{rake search:index_tags}}.

h2. Testing Instructions

*Note:* The {{uses}} field is the number shown beside the tag when searching, not the number of works shown on the fandom index page or the tag works page.

# To test updates of small tags:
## Create a work using two brand new tags with very similar names, similar enough that you can easily create a tag search that will return both of those tags and very few other tags.
## Remove Tag A from the work.
## Wait 5-10 minutes for the search to update.
## Perform a tag search that will return both tags, and sort by uses in descending order. Tag B should be listed first, and Tag A should be listed second.
## Change the order from descending to ascending. Now Tag A should be first, and Tag B should be second.
## Go back to the work and replace Tag B with Tag A.
## Wait 5-10 minutes for the search to update.
## Perform another tag search sorted by uses in descending order. Tag A should now be listed first.
# To test updates of larger tags:
## Find two tags with over 1000 uses that have very similar taggings counts. You should be able to do this by doing a tag search with no query, but sorted by number of uses.
## Perform a search sorted by uses, and figure out what page the two tags are on and what order they appear in.
## Add enough works to the smaller tag to make it slightly larger than the other tag.
## Wait somewhere between 3 minutes and 40 minutes, depending on how large the tags you’ve chosen are.
## Perform the search again, and return to the page that the two tags were on. Depending on how this issue was tackled, they may be in the same order that they were before – this isn’t a bug, it’s just the way that the code works.
## Wait 5-10 minutes for the search to update.
## Perform a search sorted by uses, and return to the page that the two tags were on. Verify that they have switched order.

05/May/22 1:35 PM;61f7429f9c1d520069211f56;I’ve figured out a basic approach and will go ahead and create a branch to test it on, but I wanted to post it here in case anyone had any insight.

There are 3 steps to this:

# Make sure writes from Redis to DB are from actual changed count values.
# Use callback function to reindex Elasticsearch document when writes to DB happen.
# Ensure that callback function is triggered when writes to DB happen.

Here’s what I’m planning to use for the three steps:

For the first step, it’s possible to approach this by ether checking to see if the counts have actually changed before adding to redis update or by preventing calls to {{write_taggings_to_redis}} unless the counts have changed. Since there's no way to determine this within {{taggings_count=(value)}}, I've decided to go with the first approach. If {{taggings_count=(value)}} is never called except from {{taggings_count}} or {{update_cache_count(id)}}, I could try the second approach, but I don't believe that is the case. It would also be feasible to make this change if, outside of the previous two methods, {{taggings_count=(value)}} is only called when there is an actual change to the count.

I will use the code ticking instant wrote out in a previous pull request that was trashed for other reasons.

{code:ruby}  def write_taggings_to_redis(value)
    # Atomically set the value while extracting the old value.
    old_redis_value = REDIS_GENERAL.getset("tag_update_#{id}_value", value)

    # If the value hasn't changed from the saved version or the REDIS version,
    # there's no need to write an update to the database, so let's just bail
    # out.
    return value if value == old_redis_value && value == taggings_count_cache

    # If we've reached here, then the value has changed, and we need to make
    # sure that the new value is written to the database.
    REDIS_GENERAL.sadd("tag_update", id)
    value
  end{code}

For the second step, I will add a statement to the {{after_update}} method:

{code:ruby}    # Reindex immediately to update the unwrangled bin.
    if tag.saved_change_to_unwrangleable? ||
      tag.saved_change_to_taggings_count_cache?
      tag.reindex_document
    end{code}

For the third step, I will change the code of {{Tag.write_redis_to_database}} using some code written by ticking instant from the previously mentioned pull request to make the method more readable and changing the method from {{update_all}} to {{update}} so the callback is triggered:

{code:ruby}  def self.write_redis_to_database
    batch_size = ArchiveConfig.TAG_UPDATE_BATCH_SIZE
    REDIS_GENERAL.smembers("tag_update").each_slice(batch_size) do |batch|
      Tag.transaction do
        batch.each do |id|
          value = REDIS_GENERAL.get("tag_update_#{id}_value")
          next if value.blank?
          Tag.where(id: id).update(taggings_count_cache: value.to_i)
        end
        REDIS_GENERAL.srem("tag_update", batch)
      end
    end
  end{code}
column150: 05/May/22 4:43 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;The tag is added to the reindex queue every time it’s saved, thanks to the [call|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/5168edd38ea72e644bfd0e85447c3c56ba1f7e20/lib/searchable.rb#L5] to {{after_save :enqueue_to_index}} in {{Searchable}}. The direct call to {{reindex_document}} when setting {{unwrangleable}} is used to try to get the tag to disappear from the bins as soon as it’s wrangled, instead of after a short delay, but I don’t think that kind of responsiveness is quite as critical for the number of uses. (Particularly since the cache of {{taggings_count}} already introduces a delay in the displayed value vs. the value used for sorting.) So you can probably get away with skipping step 2, if you’re going to switch to using {{update}} instead of {{update_all}}.

16/Oct/23 9:15 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;I also still see the ordering issue. I started with

{noformat}Freeform: First Kiss ‎(7943)
Freeform: Violence ‎(7852)
Character: Jack Harkness ‎(7845)
Fandom: Bandom ‎(7638){noformat}

And an hour and 20 minutes later, the count for Jack Harkness has updated, but not the order:

{noformat}Freeform: First Kiss ‎(7943)
Freeform: Violence ‎(7852)
Character: Jack Harkness ‎(7853)

Maybe the thing to do is remove the new cache deletion callback and instead update the following tagging callback:

{noformat}def update_taggings_count
  tagger.update_tag_cache unless tagger.blank? || tagger.destroyed?
end{noformat}

{noformat}def update_taggings_count
  return if tagger.blank? || tagger.destroyed?
  tagger.taggings_count = tagger.taggings.count
end{noformat}

The current version of the callback (top) calls {{update_tag_cache}} which stops the process of updating the count if it finds a valid number in the cache:

{noformat}  # If the cached count is nil or _should_ be nil (because it's less than ArchiveConfig.TAGGINGS_COUNT_MIN_CACHE_COUNT),
  # then we call taggings_count, which _also_ checks the cache, and if it's still nil,
  # then we _set_ taggings_count, which in turn prompts writing to Redis.
  def update_tag_cache
    taggings_count if cache_read.nil? || (cache_read < ArchiveConfig.TAGGINGS_COUNT_MIN_CACHE_COUNT)
  end{noformat}

Small tags don’t have anything in the cache, so {{taggings_count}} gets called:

{noformat}  def taggings_count
    cache_read = Rails.cache.read(taggings_count_cache_key)
    return cache_read unless cache_read.nil? || (cache_read < ArchiveConfig.TAGGINGS_COUNT_MIN_CACHE_COUNT)
    real_value = taggings.count
    self.taggings_count = real_value
    real_value
  end{noformat}

And again, there’s no cache read for a small tag, so we proceed to {{taggings_count=(value)}}, which is where we actually add the value to Redis:

{noformat}  def taggings_count=(value)
    expiry_time = Tag.taggings_count_expiry(value)
    # Only write to the cache if there are more than a number of uses.
    Rails.cache.write(taggings_count_cache_key, value, race_condition_ttl: 10, expires_in: expiry_time.minutes) if value >= ArchiveConfig.TAGGINGS_COUNT_MIN_CACHE_COUNT
    write_taggings_to_redis(value)
  end{noformat}

But for a big tag, we’re bailing out once {{update_tag_cache}} finds something in the cache, and {{taggings_count=(value)}} / {{write_taggings_to_redis(value)}} is indeed never being called for tags with cached counts. So it seems like the newly added tag callback isn’t fixing it because it only deletes the cached count if {{tag.saved_change_to_taggings_count_cache?}} , but the number in the database only changes if we successfully invoke {{write_taggings_to_redis(value)}}? 

A big downside to the tagging callback change I’m suggesting is it’s a _lot_ of counting, because we check the real tagging count for a tag every single time we create or destroy a tagging. :| For things like Ratings, Warnings, and Categories, which are huge tags that are on almost every work, that’s gonna be kind of ridiculous.

column1: Revision dates in work blurbs mix time zones with caching, resulting in ordering that looks inconsistent
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Go to your preferences and set your time zone to GMT+13.
# Post a new work, and view it on your dashboard.
# Go to your preferences and set your time zone to GMT-12.
# Post a new work in the same fandom, and view it on your dashboard.

*What Happens:* The work that you posted first appears to have been posted the day after the work you posted second. This is because the date is displayed in the current user’s time zone, and then cached. So the first work’s date is displayed in GMT+13, and the second work’s date is displayed in GMT-12 – apparently 1 day earlier, even though the work was actually posted later.

*What Should Happen:* When you change your time zone, the work’s date should be displayed in your new time zone.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Parent collections should contain the works that are in all their respective child collections.  But\! sometimes they don’t, when the collection was added to the parent collection after already containing works.

Steps to reproduce:

# Create a collection, Collection A.
# Add some works to Collection A.
# Create a new collection, Collection B.
# Edit Collection A and make Collection B a parent of it.

What should happen:

Works in Collection A should also appear under Collection B once Collection B is a parent of Collection A.

What actually happens:

They don’t.

column1: N+1 queries when displaying comments
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When displaying a collection of comments, the following queries are performed once per comment displayed:

# [The number of reviewed replies is counted.|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/59bb5ebc3ca4fa86056b410d922152905b8cc179/app/views/comments/_comment_thread.html.erb#L9]
# [The reviewed replies are loaded, if there are any.|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/59bb5ebc3ca4fa86056b410d922152905b8cc179/app/views/comments/_comment_thread.html.erb#L15]
# [The pseud is loaded to check whether the comment can be marked as spam.|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/59bb5ebc3ca4fa86056b410d922152905b8cc179/app/helpers/comments_helper.rb#L129]

The comment’s parent also must be loaded (along with the work and its pseuds, in the case of comments on chapters), though when displaying multiple comments they usually share a parent, so the N+1 queries often end up hitting the query cache instead of the database.

That makes for 2-3 queries per comment when cached. When uncached, the user is loaded alongside the pseud, for 3-4 queries per comment.

The issues [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5986|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5986|smart-link], [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6323|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6323|smart-link], and [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6327|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6327|smart-link] also involve loading the user even when cached, as well as contributing other queries.

We’d like to be able to display a single page of comments more efficiently, without performing database queries for each comment. Ideally, the number of database queries should be independent of the number of comments displayed.

h1. Testing Instructions

In staging and production, there’s not enough information in the logs to determine whether there are n+1 queries. (Bullet can catch some, but only those that involve loading associations.) So verifying that there aren’t n+1 queries is going to have to be a process that occurs in review/automated testing.

However, the pull request does touch a lot of pieces of comment-related code, so it would be good to test the following:

# View the comments on an admin post.
# View the comments on a tag (if you’re a tag wrangler; you can use testy for this).
# View the comments on a single chapter.
# View the comments on a one-shot.
# View all comments on a multi-chapter work.
# Find a work with at least two pages of comments, and make sure that the page buttons work.
# Click “Reply” on a comment, then click “Cancel.”
# Post a comment on a work, and then post two replies to that comment. Make sure that all three comments appear with the correct indentation, and in the correct order. Click on the “Thread” link for the first comment, and make sure that the indentation/order are still correct.
# On a moderated work, post an unreviewed comment. Make sure that it doesn’t show up when you view the work’s comments. Log in as the creator of the work, and make sure the comment does appear on the unreviewed comments page.

column1: Use different endpoints for requesting password resets and for resetting passwords
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
We use the [Devise controller for passwords|https://github.com/heartcombo/devise/blob/f8d1ea90bc328012f178b8a6616a89b73f2546a4/app/controllers/devise/passwords_controller.rb], where:

* POST /users/password (action {{users/passwords#create}}) is for requesting a password reset;
* PUT /users/password (action {{users/passwords#update}}) is for actually resetting the password.

In practice, [both types of requests end up as POST because|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/v6.0/form_helpers.html#how-do-forms-with-patch-put-or-delete-methods-work-questionmark]:

{quote}However, most browsers _don't support_ methods other than "GET" and "POST" when it comes to submitting forms.

Rails works around this issue by emulating other methods over POST with a hidden input named {{"_method"}}, which is set to reflect the desired method.{quote}

In order to apply different rate limits to the 2 request types (at nginx level), we need them to use different paths, by [setting up an alias for the second request type|https://github.com/heartcombo/devise/#configuring-routes].

*How to test*:

On staging, visit [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/password/new|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/password/new] and submit the form multiple times in quick succession. You should quickly get a “Retry later“ error.

Follow the “Change my password.“ in the password reset email. You should be able to successfully set a new password, without getting a “Retry later“ error.

column1: Fix comment cache expiration
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
[The cache on comments doesn’t expire after a week.|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4120?focusedCommentId=358622] This is because the {{cache}} function in views takes a single positional argument (the cache key), but in {{comments/single_comment}} the intended cache key argument is passed as a keyword argument, forcing all of the keyword arguments – including the intended expiration time – to be used as the cache key, instead of being used as keyword arguments.

Let’s fix that.

*Testing Instructions:*

# Log in.
# Find or create a pseud whose name doesn’t match your login.
# Post a comment with that pseud.
# View the comment to establish the cache.
# Change your username (but not to the name of the pseud you picked).
# View the comment again, and notice that the parenthesized username on the comment hasn’t changed.
# Wait 1 week for the cached comment to expire.
# View the comment again, and verify that the name on the comment has changed.

column1: Remove default_scope for bookmarks
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The bookmark model sets the {{default_scope}} to {{order("bookmarks.id DESC")}}. Additional calls to {{order}} won’t override the default, but instead add to it, causing unexpected and unwanted behavior, e.g., [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3869|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3869|smart-link] 

So we’re not surprised by this behavior again, we’d like to get rid of {{default_scope}} and update any queries that rely on bookmarks being ordered by descending ID.

*Testing*

# With several accounts, log in and bookmark the same work (it’s not a bad idea to use a work that already has several bookmarks). Then check the bookmarks page for the work ( {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/###/bookmarks}}, accessed by clicking the linked number where it says “Bookmarks: [Number]” in the blurb or meta for a given work) and ensure the bookmarks are listed in the correct order, with the most recent at the top.
# The bookmark you created should also appear on [https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks|https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks]. (Note: This page is cached. It may take 30-60 minutes for new bookmarks to show up.) Because there are multiple bookmarks for the work, this will cause a “Show Most Recent Bookmarks” button to appear on the bookmark. Pressing the button will list more bookmarks; they should also be in order from newest to oldest.
# Get a superadmin (AD&T) to disable the “Turn on caching (currently experimental)” admin setting. If the site stays upright, bookmark a few different works and ensure they are in the correct order on [https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks|https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks]. They’ll show up immediately because caching is off.

column1: Prevent N+1 queries when indexing works
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Currently, indexing N works produces a lot of queries:

* The {{WorkIndexer}} class produces roughly 24N+1 queries for a batch of size N.
* The {{WorkCreatorIndexer}} class produces 2N+1 queries for a batch of size N.
* The {{BookmarkedWorkIndexer}} class produces roughly 17N+1 queries for a batch of size N.

In order to improve performance, it’d be good to use {{includes()}} to reduce the number of queries produced by these indexers.

h1. Testing Instructions

Bullet doesn’t flag the number of queries produced during background jobs, so there’s no way to check the number of queries in QA. That said, it would be good to test that these three indexers are still working.

# Create a work in an anonymous collection.
# Create a non-private bookmark of your own work.
# Wait a few minutes for the work and bookmark to be reindexed.
# Check that the work appears on its fandom’s works page.
# Check that the work appears on its fandom’s bookmarks page.
# Check your “Works in Collections” page to make sure that the work appears there.

column1: Add a rake task to fix thread column for comments from 2009
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
In January 2010, the {{thread}} field of comments was overhauled to set each comment’s {{thread}} equal to the ID of the root comment. However, the [rake task|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/98ea563c50acd7bc9969df4b0757bb5343c50223/lib/tasks/migrate_tasks.rake#L123-L131] for correcting the {{thread}} of existing comments only fixed duplicate threads (threads that were shared by more than one top-level comment). This left many comments from 2009 with incorrect {{thread}} values.

Any replies to these comments will have “Parent Thread” links that point to the wrong comment (or no comment at all). Plus, with the changes introduced by [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6333|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6333|smart-link], these comments now trigger 500 errors when viewing the work with {{show_comments=true}}. We'd like to fix that.

The pull request for this issue should:

# Add a rake task to fix any top-level (i.e. depth 0) comments that have {{thread != id}}, and update all replies (and replies to replies, etc.) to match. Something like the following should work, though it might be good to add more progress messages:
{code:ruby}def fix_comment(comment)
  comment.with_lock do
    if comment.reply_comment?
      comment.update_column(:thread, comment.commentable.thread)
    else
      comment.update_column(:thread, comment.id)
    end
    comment.comments.each { |reply| fix_comment(reply) }
  end
end

Comment.top_level.where("thread != id").each { |comment| fix_comment(comment) }{code}
# Update [test/fixtures/comments.yml|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/test/fixtures/comments.yml] to make sure that the {{thread}} values are set properly when someone calls {{rake db:otwseed}}.

column1: Handle or prevent RecordNotUnique errors for tag wrangling operations
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
These three {{Tag}} functions can cause {{RecordNotUnique}} errors to appear in Resque:

* {{update_filters_for_filterables}}
* {{transfer_or_remove_associations}}
* {{update_inherited_meta_tags}}

We’d like to address these errors, either by modifying the code to use {{upsert}} to prevent errors when multiple processes are inserting duplicate records at around the same time, or by using the {{ActiveJob}} system to retry jobs that encounter {{RecordNotUnique}} errors.

h1. Testing Instructions

Because the {{RecordNotUnique}} errors are caused by having two similar tasks run at the same time, it’s difficult to reproduce the error on demand. For staging, it should be sufficient to check that the following still work:

* Testing {{update_filters_for_filterables}}:
** Pick two tags of the same type, A and B.
** Make A canonical.
** Make B a synonym of A.
** Wait 10+ minutes for the filters to update.
** Make sure that when you view the tag A, it also includes works tagged only with B.
** Remove the synonym relationship between A and B.
** Wait 10+ minutes for the filters to update.
** Make sure that when you view the tag A, it no longer includes works tagged only with B.
* Testing {{transfer_or_remove_associations}}:
** Pick two canonical fandoms A and B.
** Pick a character C and add A as its parent.
** As an admin, edit the tag A and syn A to B.
** Wait a few minutes for the job to run.
** Check the tag page for C to make sure that it has B listed as a parent tag.
* Testing {{update_inherited_meta_tags}}:
** Pick three canonical tags of the same type, A, B, and C.
** Subtag C to B, and B to A.
** Wait 10+ minutes for the filters to update.
** Make sure that when you view the tag A, it also includes works tagged only with C.
** Remove the metatag relationship between B and C, and between A and B.
** Wait 10+ minutes for the filters to update.
** Make sure that when you view the tag A, it no longer includes works tagged only with C.

h1. Deploy Steps

# Turn off wrangling in the admin settings.
# Run these lines in the console to restart all of the previous failed tag jobs. 
{code:ruby}Resque::Failure.each do |id, job|
  next unless job.dig("payload", "class") == "Tag"
  next unless job.dig("exception") == "ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique"
  next if %w[transfer_or_remove_associations transfer_or_remove_favorite_tags].include?(job.dig("payload", "args", 2))
  Resque::Failure.requeue(id)
  Resque::Failure.remove(id)
end{code}
(It might be good to run this twice, once during the deploy and one a day or two before the deploy, so that this step finishes quickly during the deploy.)
# Wait for all tag tasks to finish running. Go back to Step 2 if any of them fail.
# Do the deploy.
# Wait until all unicorns and resque workers have finished restarting.
# Re-enable wrangling in the admin settings.
# Start a {{screen}} session.
# Run {{rake Tag:destroy_invalid_common_taggings}}.
# Run {{rake Tag:destroy_invalid_meta_taggings}}.

Once this has been deployed, it should be marked as Pending Attention on Beta, and someone should check to see if it helps prevent new {{RecordNotUnique}} errors from appearing in the Resque failures queue.

[~accountid:629dc33e9b728c006a926594]:

{quote}At that point, I was getting a bunch of {{Mysql2::Error::ConnectionError: Access denied for user 'root'@'172.23.0.6' (using password: YES)}} errors when I tried to either rerun the {{init.sh}} script or just do {{docker-compose up -d web}}. It took me a while to realize that fixing the password in the two files mentioned in the wiki ({{config/docker/database.yml}} and {{docker-compose.yml}}) was insufficient, since {{config/docker/database.yml}} is only copied to {{config/database.yml}} if it doesn't exist yet.{quote}

The bash init script uses {{-n}} to avoid overwriting existing local config files:

{noformat}cp -n config/docker/database.yml config/database.yml
cp -n config/docker/redis.yml config/redis.yml
cp -n config/docker/local.yml config/local.yml{noformat}

This is inconvenient when you’re first setting up the dev environment and possibly rerunning the script multiple times.

Ideally we should move the {{MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD}} out of docker-compose.yml and switch to [an .env file that’s ignored by version control instead|https://docs.docker.com/compose/environment-variables/#the-env-file].

But a quick fix would be to remove the {{-n}} flag to overwrite the local files. This will make it more similar to [the init.cmd file behavior|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/742827a740dee71d3abcfd945822b1fe2fd60973/script/docker/init.cmd#L4-L6] as well.

Just in case, let’s add {{-b}} to the cp commands to keep a backup copy of the local config files ({{local.yml}} before init.sh runs will be kept as {{local.yml~}}), and update our {{.gitignore}} to exclude backup files.

# Delete the pseud from Step 2
## Hi, username\! > My Preferences > Manage My Pseuds
## Press “Delete” button that corresponds with the pseud from Step 2
## Press “OK” to confirm

h1. What happens

The pseud Issue6359Test is deleted. 

The pseud that matched your original account name is the only one that remains. You can change it freely.

Your account most likely does not turn up in autocompletes when your username is entered.

From [~accountid:557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6]:

{quote}Because there’s already a pseud whose (lowercase) name matches the (lowercase) name of the new account, [changing the username doesn’t modify either of the pseuds|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e0c66d738d69d20e59674506e991fc50e5783995/app/models/user.rb#L519-L520]. So after the rename, you have one pseud \[Issue6359Test] and one with your old username. But [the check to make sure that you don’t delete the pseud with your username|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e0c66d738d69d20e59674506e991fc50e5783995/app/controllers/pseuds_controller.rb#L133-L134] does a case-sensitive comparison, so it’s perfectly fine allowing the user \[issue6359test] to delete the pseud \[Issue6359Test].

(I think you can do a similar thing with accented characters, too.){quote}

h1. What should happen

When you change your username in Step 3d, the capitalization of the pseud ({{Issue6359Test}}) should be changed to match that of your username ({{issue6359test}}). Then it should not be possible to delete it in Step 4.

h1. Notes

This also applies to pseuds where the diacritics don’t match the username, e.g., if in Step 2b you created the pseud {{ïssue6359tést}} instead.

column30:
h1. What it should do For the time being, muting a user should consist of throwing a cached bit of CSS into the page {{}} after all stylesheets (including sandbox.css), e.g., {{.user-111, .user-222 { display: none !important; visibility: hidden !important; }}}. (The numbers are the muted users' IDs.) This will hide all of a user's works, series, and bookmarks from work and bookmark listings and search results, as well as any logged-in comments the user has left on works or news posts. The cache should be expired whenever a user mutes or unmutes a user. You should only be able to mute 1000 users. This number should be configurable. h1. Who you can mute You should not be able to mute: * official accounts; you should receive an error. ** Text: Sorry, you can't mute an official account. * yourself; there shouldn’t even be a button for this on dashboards or profiles, and you should receive an error if you attempt it from the Muted Users page. ** Text: Sorry, you can't mute yourself. h1. How you can mute * Wherever the button appears, it should say “Mute” when the user is not currently muted and “Unmute” when the user is currently muted. (We’re calling it “the mute button” below for simplicity.) * The mute button should only be shown to logged in users. * Checks for whether a particular user can be muted (e.g., is it an official account) should occur after pressing the mute button, not before displaying it. * Muting or unmuting a user should require confirmation, no matter where you are muting or unmuting them from. ** This should be a full page confirmation that provides information about what muting does, similar to the confirm_block.html.erb pages for confirming blocks. (It will eventually offer additional options.) ** The confirmation pages for blocking and unblocking will also need text changes. +Text for muting confirmation page:+ h3. Mute testy Are you sure you want to *mute* testy? Muting a user: * completely hides their works, series, bookmarks, and comments from you; there will be no empty space, placeholder text, or other indication something has been removed Muting a user will not: * prevent you from receiving comment or subscription emails from this user * hide their works, series, bookmarks, and comments from anyone else To prevent a user from commenting on your works or replying to your comments elsewhere on the site, visit your Blocked Users page. Please note that if you are not using the default site skin, muting may not work properly. The Skins and Archive Interface FAQ has instructions for reverting to the default site skin. +Text for unmuting confirmation page:+ h3. Unmute testy Are you sure you want to *unmute* testy? Unmuting a user allows you to: * see their works, series, bookmarks, and comments on the site +Updated text for blocking confirmation page:+ h3. Block testy Are you sure you want to *block* testy? Blocking a user prevents them from: * commenting on your works * replying to your comments anywhere on the site Blocking a user will not: * hide their works or bookmarks from you * delete comments they previously left on your works; you can delete these individually * hide their comments elsewhere on the site To hide a user's works, bookmarks, series, and comments from you, visit your Muted Users page. +Updated text for unblocking confirmation page:+ No changes. h2. From dashboards and profiles * User and pseud dashboards, as well as user profiles, should have a mute button located to the right of the block button. * Your own dashboard or profile should not have a mute button. h2. From the Muted Users page * Your preferences page should have a "Muted Users" link on top, to the right of "Blocked Users." (Note: Admins cannot access a user’s preferences, so they will need to manually enter the URL.) * This link should point to the Muted Users page, located at {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/muted/users}}, where you should be able to manage your muted users. * The Muted Users page should be accessible only by the user who owns the page as well as by admins with the {{policy_and_abuse}}, {{support}}, or {{superadmin}} roles. * Admins should be able to see all the buttons, but should receive an error if actually attempting to mute or unmute users. * Below the “Muted Users” {{

}}, there should be a navigation {{
    }} containing button-style “Blocked Users” and “Muted Users” links to allow for ease of switching between blocking and muting. (Like other navigation, the links should be created using {{span_if_current}}.) ** This navigation should also be added to the Blocked Users page. * At the top of the page, there should be detailed information about what muting does. ** The text on the Blocked Users page will also need to be updated. * It should be possible to mute additional users from this page via a tiny form (with autocomplete) like the one for blocking users. * The page should display the default pseud blurbs for users you've muted, ranging from newest at the top to oldest at the bottom, with the sort explicit in the code. It should be paginated. * The pseud blurbs should contain a mute button in the lower right corner. (Functionally, this will only ever be the “Unmute” form of the button.) !muted_users.png|width=58.33333333333333%,alt="The Muted Users page, as described above."! +Text for top of Muted Users page:+ h3. column1: Emoji entered in tags behave erratically
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Entering emoji in tags fields can turn certain emoji into other emoji, or make them disappear entirely, or generally behave unexpectedly.

Steps to reproduce:

# Create a new work or bookmark.
# Add an emoji like 💕 (two hearts) as a tag on the work/bookmarker’s tags.
# Save the work/bookmark.

What should happen: Your emoji should stay what you entered it as.

What actually happens: Your lovely two hearts emoji is now 💩 (poop emoji).  Ack, bad\!

This one is a consistent error so it’s good for testing, but not the only example of this problem.  This issue happens with various emoji, although some remain correct (smilies seem to be largely ok for instance).  If there’s a pattern to which ones work and which don’t, I don’t know it.

Further testing on this: entering a cat, a whale, and a train turned into three curling stones (???).  Any further emoji entered in that field on the same work ([https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1077202|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1077202]) simply vanished upon saving.  (The smile with hearts and the cat face remained the same when entered in the rel and character fields respectively.)

column149:
12/Jul/22 11:17 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;This is caused by the database collation. The {{utf8mb4_unicode_ci}} collation apparently [thinks of all 4-byte emoji as equal|https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41147829/how-can-i-search-by-emoji-in-mysql-using-utf8mb4]. So whichever of those single-emoji tags was created first will always be the one retrieved from the database on a lookup, and all of the other tags cannot be created (for emojis with 4 bytes, at least). In production, it looks like the single 4-byte emoji tag is 🤣. On staging, the single 4-byte emoji tag is 💩. There are similar issues with tags of any length – as long as a tag has a 4-byte emoji, it’ll be treated as a wildcard for all other 4-byte emojis.

The fix would be to switch collations. Apparently {{utf8mb4_unicode_ci}} is an old collation, and {{utf8mb4_unicode_520_ci}} is the newer version that correctly separates emoji and still allows for case-insensitive comparison. (There are apparently even newer collations, but they might require a newer version of MySQL, too. What version are you using currently?)

Unfortunately, [it appears that|http://mysql.rjweb.org/utf8mb4_collations.html] {{utf8mb4_unicode_520_ci}} also considers {{Æ}} equivalent to {{ae}}, while {{utf8mb4_unicode_ci}} considers them to be separate characters, so any migration to fix this is going to have to have extra code to avoid deleting tags, as happened during the original transition to {{utf8mb4}}. There also may be other characters with that issue that aren’t listed on the linked website, so the solution for detecting these tags needs to be fairly general.

(Another alternative might be to switch to a binary collation, but that’s a can of worms in a different way.)

EDIT: This applies to all 4-byte characters, not just emoji, which means that it affects pseuds as well. (Pseud names are required to match {{/\A[\p{Word} -]+\Z/u}}, so they can’t include emoji, but there are a number of {{\p{Word}}} characters among the set of 4-byte characters, all of which will be treated as interchangeable by the database.) So it might be good to change more than just the tag name collation.
column150:
13/Jul/22 4:44 PM;557058:f99670ac-6f0b-469b-bdfb-a9817a67932f;The sushi-beer problem: [https://dev.mysql.com/blog-archive/sushi-beer-an-introduction-of-utf8-support-in-mysql-8-0/|https://dev.mysql.com/blog-archive/sushi-beer-an-introduction-of-utf8-support-in-mysql-8-0/|smart-link].

Since we’re still on 5.7, we can only get to {{utf8mb4_unicode_520_ci}}. But MySQL will eventually use {{utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci}} as the default collation for utf8mb4, available from 8.0.

Systems also have plans to switch to MariaDB (we’re only using it in Docker/development right now), as another possible scheduling factor.

column1: Rewrite a section of the related works code to use accepts_nested_attributes_for
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
We’d like to rewrite some of the related works code to use {{accepts_nested_attributes_for}} instead of a custom {{parent_attributes=}} function. This should address the issue from [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6144|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6144|smart-link] where invalid related works are incorrectly saved when you press “Preview,” and should make it easier to add new validations to related works in the future.

h2. Testing Instructions

The goal here is to make sure that the related works code is working the same as it did before. There are a number of different related works bugs that this will not tackle, so if you happen to run into them, that’s to be expected:

[https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-1506|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-1506|smart-link]

[https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2373|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2373|smart-link] 

[https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-1784|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-1784|smart-link]

[https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-1726|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-1726|smart-link] 

[https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2151|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2151|smart-link] 

[https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6058|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6058|smart-link] 

Some steps to test:

# We want to test that the error messages look okay, since they’re now generated differently, so on the new work form or the edit work form, do the following:
## Try entering an invalid URL (keyboard smashes will work for this). Make sure that the error that you get when submitting the form looks reasonable.
## Try entering the URL of a work that doesn’t exist on staging. Make sure that the error that you get when submitting the form looks reasonable.
## Try entering a URL on staging that’s not related to a work. Make sure that the error that you get when submitting the form looks reasonable.
## Try leaving the URL blank, and filling in a Title and/or Author. Make sure that the error that you get when submitting the form looks reasonable.
## Try filling in a valid URL, and leave the Title and Author blank. Make sure that the error that you get is reasonable.
## Try filling in the URL of a work on staging that has at least one of its creators marked as a protected user. Make sure that the error that you get is reasonable.
# We want to make sure that related work notifications are still sent out for new works, so on the new work form, do the following:
## Try filling in the URL of a work on staging that you own.
## Press Preview, and wait a few minutes to make sure that you don’t get a notification.
## Post the work, and wait a few minutes to make sure that you do get notified.
# We want to make sure that related work notifications are still sent out when drafts are posted, so edit a draft and do the following:
## Try filling in the URL of a work on staging that you own.
## Press Preview, and wait a few minutes to make sure that you don’t get a notification.
## Post the work, and wait a few minutes to make sure that you do get notified.
# We want to check that preview still works, so edit a work (posted or not) and do the following:
## Try filling in the URL/Title/Author with valid values.
## Press Preview => Edit => Preview.
## Make sure that on both preview pages, the header lists “Inspired by Title by Author” (or “A translation of Title by Author”, if you checked the translation box).
## Press Cancel.
## Check the work’s header and make sure that it doesn’t list the new parent.
## Edit the work again and re-enter the URL/Title/Author from before.
## Press Post.
## Check the work’s header and make sure that the new parent is now listed.
