column1: Add confirmation page and email when a user changes the email on their account
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Currently, if a user changes the email address on their account, there is no method to confirm that they actually own the email address they're changing to. This can lead to situations where a user changes to an email address they do not own, and that person starts getting their emails from the site. We would like to add a separate confirmation page and email as part of the email change process. After submitting their new email, there should be a new page created (like the muting confirmation page) where they are presented with the email they entered and asked whether this is the correct email. Upon agreeing, an email is sent to the new address and they need to confirm it by clicking on a link in the email before their account's email is actually updated. If they do not confirm within a certain length of time, the email address should not be changed. We'll most likely want to use Devise's[ |https://www.rubydoc.info/github/heartcombo/devise/main/Devise/Models/Confirmable][+Confirmable module+|https://www.rubydoc.info/github/heartcombo/devise/main/Devise/Models/Confirmable] for this, which has the following option: {noformat}+reconfirmable+: requires any email changes to be confirmed (exactly the same way as initial account confirmation) to be applied. Requires additional unconfirmed_email db field to be set up (t.reconfirmable in migrations). Until confirmed, new email is stored in unconfirmed email column, and copied to email column on successful confirmation. Also, when used in conjunction with send_email_changed_notification, the notification is sent to the original email when the change is requested, not when the unconfirmed email is confirmed.{noformat} h2. The incorrect password error message and link are correct. (/) 

Entering things that aren’t emails gives me little popups under the field trying to get me to input something that looks like an email address. These messages don’t quite match “AO3 Style” but that’s not really a problem. 

Entering a password but no email into the form gives me “You must enter a new email address.” (/) 

Entering a new email B into the form and clicking Yes sends both emails to the right places.  (/) Though using the +alias trick, I notice that the request email lands in my inbox AFTER the confirmation email ❓  I’m sure a couple of milliseconds doesn’t make that much of a difference but it might be nice if the request email came first. 

The links in the emails are blue, I believe they should be red ❌  But they do all go to the right place and the email text is otherwise correct. (/) The date in the confirmation email is localized (though unlike in Chinese and English, in French it does not show the timezone); the subject line of the request notification email is translated but the translation is outdated (incorrect, but expected/no action needed). 

Entering my old email A into the form takes me to the confirmation page which tells me that clicking Yes will send an email, but clicking Yes does not send any email. (I knew this would happen, but it might be confusing to users.) Entering my old email A into the form and clicking Yes while there’s another email B request still pending … sends the “email change request” to the old email, telling me to check my old email, but no confirmation email is sent anywhere. (This is similar to what happens on production now, you get an email to yourself about having changed to your own email.) Given this, I don’t know if we wanted to interrupt this “enter email A into the form” behavior at the first step, since the second step doesn’t really achieve anything (either “no action” or “useless email”)? It’s probably not super important though. 

Entering the same email B into the form again (without confirming the first email B change) updates the date in the pending request banner. (/) 

Entering a different email C into the form updates both the date and the email in the banner. (/)

If I’m logged out, I get: “Sorry, you don't have permission to access the page you were trying to reach. column1: Editing a character or relationship that has been nominated in a tag set removes it from the "Review Associations" page of the tag set
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to Reproduce

# Find or create a character tag “Char X” that has been wrangled into a canonical fandom “Fandom 1.”
# Create a tag set with open nominations.
# Nominate “Char X” with a different fandom “Fandom 2.” (Make sure that “Char X” is not wrangled into “Fandom 2,” because otherwise it’ll never appear on the “Review Associations” tag, edited or not.)
# Review nominations for the tag set.
# Accept both nominations (the fandom and the character).
# Note that “Char X” is listed among the unassociated tags.
# Look at (but don’t modify) the “Review Associations” tab.
# Note that it suggests adding the “Char X → Fandom 2” association.
# Log in as a wrangler.
# Go to the Edit page for “Char X.”
# Press “Save changes” without making any changes.
# Log back in as the tag set owner.
# Note that “Char X” is still listed among the unassociated tags.
# Look at the “Review Associations” tab.

h1. What Should Happen

It should still contain the suggested “Char X → Fandom 2” association.

h1. What Actually Happens

The suggested association is gone.

h1. Notes

[https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3757|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3757|smart-link] is specifically related to wrangling & tag sets, but the “Review Associations” page isn’t cached, so this isn’t a caching issue.

Once [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6328|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6328|smart-link] is in, it won’t be necessary to have tag wrangler access to trigger this bug, because tags will be saved more frequently to keep the count up-to-date. So you’ll be able to trigger the bug by nominating a character, and then writing a work with that character tag.

The cause of this is the difference between [the code for setting the value of parented|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/26603cf9510587afa4ebd911a399de6a8b84a6c9/app/models/tagset_models/tag_nomination.rb#L74-L89] in the {{TagNomination}} class, and [the code for fixing parented when the tag is updated|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/26603cf9510587afa4ebd911a399de6a8b84a6c9/app/models/tag.rb#L1142-L1156]. The former sets {{parented}} to true only if the tag was nominated in one of its canonical fandoms; the latter sets {{parented}} to true for all tag nominations as long as the tag has any canonical fandoms at all. So whichever callback fired more recently will determine whether the tag appears on the “Review Associations” page.

(Practically speaking, the {{TagNomination}} callback will only fire when the tag is first being nominated, because [nominations are approved in bulk without callbacks|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/26603cf9510587afa4ebd911a399de6a8b84a6c9/app/models/tagset_models/owned_tag_set.rb#L77-L78]. So this bug occurs even if the tag is edited before the nomination is approved.)

column1: Editing a series that has works in different pseuds affects the pseuds on the works
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
If you have works in a series under different pseuds, and you edit the series (such as the summary), it messes up the pseuds on the works.

h2. Steps to reproduce

* Create a work that’s in a new series
* Create a second work in that same series with a different pseud
* Edit the whole series (like, edit the summary). Note that both pseuds are highlighted.
* Select Update. Note that both works now have both pseuds on them.
* Edit the whole series again. Select 1 pseud.
* Select Update. Note that both works now have that 1 pseud on them.

h2. What happens

* If you edit the series summary, and don't touch the pseuds (which default to having the ones used in the works highlighted), it changes the works to have all pseuds that are highlighted.
* If you edit the series summary, and select 1 pseud, it changes the works to have that 1 pseud.
* Additional testing ( [https://test.archiveofourown.org/series/64149|https://test.archiveofourown.org/series/64149] ) shows that it only affects pseuds within an account. It does not spill to separate accounts. (609145)

Reported by a user in zoho 547388

column1: Recipient with multiple givers order not stable in Assignments page
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
How to produce this issue:

# Set up a challenge and have over 20 participants sign up (the assignments page displays 20 results at a time, so over 20 is needed to observe this problem.)
# Close signups and run matching (recommended to set matching parameters so that anyone can match with anyone, for simplicity).
# Go to the the Assignments page ([https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/potential_matches|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/potential_matches]) 
# Make the last recipient on page 1 of the results the same as the first recipient on page 2 (e.g. If testy is signed up, make testy the recipient in both of those assignments).
# Page back and forth between page 1 and page 2.

What you would expect: the order of assignments should remain stable despite paging back and forth.

What actually happens: the order of those assignments with the same recipient can flip around unpredictably.  This causes confusion and problems for exchange mods.

I think what is currently determining the order of the list is the recipient’s username.  So in cases where this is identical, there should be a second ordering factor of some sort to make sure the order remains stable.  I would suggest using Assignment ID (the number in the left column) to determine which assignment out of several for the same recipient should come first, but I’d be happy with anything that keeps things in the same order from page to page.

02/Jan/23 2:53 PM;557058:f99670ac-6f0b-469b-bdfb-a9817a67932f;We found an issue with the update, where emails cannot be sent:

{noformat}SSL_connect returned=1 errno=0 state=error: certificate verify failed (self signed certificate){noformat}

Ruby 3.0.5 is bundled with net-http 0.2.1 which enables {{starttls}} by default ([https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/44698|https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/44698|smart-link]). But the mail gem does not explicitly disable {{starttls}} even if we [set it to false|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/db121b3137835668330ca0172d38320a95dd1431/config/config.yml#L42].

While the fix for mail is pending ([https://github.com/mikel/mail/pull/1435|https://github.com/mikel/mail/pull/1435|smart-link]), we’ll need to [monkey-patch it|https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/44698#issuecomment-1069675285] to get around the issue. ETA: looks like mail 2.8.0 has the fix ([https://github.com/mikel/mail/issues/1434|https://github.com/mikel/mail/issues/1434|smart-link]).

How to test on staging: try any action that results in an email notification (e.g. kudos, work deletion).

column1: Reorganize My Assignments page
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Currently, a user’s My Assignments page [lists all undefaulted assignments from oldest to newest, and then all undefaulted pinch hits from oldest to newest|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/de0fa361add04f0be7fed8a91d2651373eeb48d4/app/controllers/challenge_assignments_controller.rb#L80]. All are listed on a single page, without pagination.

To make it easier to find the most pressing information – assignments waiting to be filled – we would like to make some changes:

* Split assignments across two pages like we do with the My Claims page: the default URL ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/testy/assignments}}) should list unposted assignments, and {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/testy/assignments?posted=true }}should list complete assignments.
* Navigation links for “Unposted Assignments” and “Completed Assignments” should be added after the page heading. They should use {{span_if_current}} to indicate which you are accessing. (These are the terms in the Status info of the blurbs on the page, more or less – they use “Complete!” rather than “Completed”.)
* Each page should list all appropriate assignments from oldest to newest regardless of whether they're pinch hits or not.
** When there are multiple assignments that were sent at the same time (which can happen if the user has multiple assignments in one challenge), they should then be sorted by ascending ID to ensure stable pagination.
* When necessary, pages should be paginated at top and bottom, using the default number of items for pagination.
* The "Assignments (#)" count in dashboard sidebar should only include unposted assignments, like "Claims (#)" only includes unfulfilled.
* The note about checking for claims prompts should have the class {{notes}} instead of {{note}} – bonus points if you change the Claims page as well. (And maybe add a period to the “Try X” sentences.) 

!Screen Shot 2022-10-24 at 8.18.22 PM.png|width=100%,alt="Mock-up of My Assignments page, with navigation items for Unposted Assignments and Completed Assignments. The Unposted Assignments is styled to look pressed because it is currently selected."!

## Manage Items > Approved
## Locate the bookmark
## Check “Remove”

*What happens*

The bookmark remains on the Bookmarked Items page, even after waiting several minutes for it to be reindexed. The collection info is, however, removed from the bookmark.

*What should happen*

The bookmark should be removed.

*Notes*

This is an indexing issue. To fix it, an admin can Troubleshoot the bookmarker’s account to reindex the bookmarks by the bookmarker. The bookmarker can also edit the bookmark, e.g., change its notes or tags.

There might be a fix for this in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6026|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6026|smart-link], but there’s a better chance of it getting fixed sooner as a solo issue.

column1: HTML parser sometimes breaks title attributes containing single quotes
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to Reproduce # Open the “Post > New Work” form. # Fill out all required fields. # Enter the following HTML: {noformat}Cause I'm having a good time{noformat} # Press Preview or Post. h1. What Happens If you hover over the text of the work, the title attribute says “Don”, not “Don’t stop me now.” If you view the source of the work, the parser appears to have outputted the following: {noformat}

Cause I'm having a good time

{noformat} h1. Notes This doesn’t happen if the title attribute is set on a paragraph, or on a tag that’s already been placed inside a paragraph when the parser first runs. But it happens on {{
}}s, {{}}s, {{}}s, {{}}s, {{}}s, {{
}}s, etc. – any tag that isn’t in [the list of tags in dont_touch_content_tag?|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/d74d404f052b4e60e223c712fff619844695806d/lib/html_cleaner.rb#L224-L228] The reason this occurs is because when {{add_paragraphs_to_text}} is rewriting the document, it reformats most tags by calling {{open_tag}}, which [regenerates the list of tag attributes using single quotes to enclose all attributes|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/d74d404f052b4e60e223c712fff619844695806d/lib/html_cleaner.rb#L4-L19]. This, of course, breaks when the attribute contains a single quote. The only unaffected tags are those listed in {{dont_touch_content_tag?}}, or any tag contained inside one of the {{dont_touch_content_tag?}} tags, because those are reformatted by [calling Nokogiri’s native node.to_s|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/d74d404f052b4e60e223c712fff619844695806d/lib/html_cleaner.rb#L279-L290], which handles attributes containing {{'}} correctly. h1. Testing # Before deployment, find or create a work with complex HTML. # After deployment, check that the work from Step 1 displays the same. # Create a work with this text (or some other title attribute with a single quote) in its summary, notes, and work text: {noformat}Cause I'm having a good time{noformat} Make sure that it displays properly in all three places. # As any admin, go to [http://test.archiveofourown.org/faq,|http://test.archiveofourown.org/faq,] edit one of the existing categories, and add a new question with the same text as Step 3. Then make sure the title attribute is correct when viewing the question. h1. Deployment History # 0.9.327: the initial fix. We reworked the sanitizer, bumped the sanitizer version, but did not change how {{sanitize_field}} works ([https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4382|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4382|smart-link]). This added a lot of database writes, and we had to roll back. # 0.9.328: we considered undoing just the sanitizer version bump ([https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4384|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4384|smart-link]) before undoing the initial fix entirely ([https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4385|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4385|smart-link]). Then we added a temp fix to ensure all content gets sanitized as a last step before being displayed ([https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4389|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4389|smart-link]), without changing how the sanitizer works. This prevents the bug while we rework the sanitizer as originally planned. # 0.9.329: [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4391|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4391|smart-link] refactored the sanitizer, as well as {{sanitize_field}} to avoid the added database writes. Instead, we added a rake to do the database writes in the background. We had some issues with Resque ([https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6421?focusedCommentId=359472|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6421?focusedCommentId=359472|smart-link]), so we deployed the change without running the rake for now. # 0.9.330: LogItem were sanitized differently by the new rake, we restored the existing behavior and fixed staging data ([https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6421?focusedCommentId=359517|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6421?focusedCommentId=359517|smart-link]). The rake has not been run on production yet. # TODO: fix the remaining issues with the rake and run it on production. h1. Deployment Notes It wouldn’t hurt to send folks an email saying, heads up, you might want to fix your work, but we don’t need to leave Dewplayer hanging around until then, after [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6097?focusedCommentId=359935|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6097?focusedCommentId=359935|smart-link]. It might be good to hold off on running the rake task for a few days after deploying. If, after deploying, anyone complains about the text of their work being mangled, we can try to tweak the parser further in response to those complaints, and only run the rake task to process existing fields once we’re satisfied with the behavior of the parser. The rake task can be run with: {noformat}rake resanitize:all{noformat} It will put all jobs on the {{resanitize}} resque queue, so that they can be throttled separately from other jobs.

{quote}There's apparently an [issue with Resque|https://github.com/resque/resque/issues/1598] where jobs will exit using exit!, which doesn't properly close the connection to MySQL, resulting in "Aborted connection" errors on the MySQL end of things. On my machine, MySQL seems to discover that the connection has been closed almost instantaneously, but I'm not sure if adding a network + a load balancer(?) between the database servers and the Resque workers might result in more of a delay between the worker improperly closing the connection, and the server realizing that the connection should be counted as closed.{quote}

We tried to diagnose the issue by running {{Kernel.fork { ApplicationRecord.connection; pp Time.now; exit! }}} in a staging Rails console, but we couldn’t locate the corresponding “Aborted connection“ errors in /var/log/mysql/error.log (in our setup, Rails talked to a database proxy - MaxScale - which complicates debugging).

For the record, {{max_connections}} for each of the 3 staging database servers is 100. (On production, it’s 10000). Staging has 21 resque workers + 16 unicorn workers, so shouldn’t have gotten close to that limit. [~accountid:557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6]:

{quote}As I understand it, the [5 connection limit for the pool|https://api.rubyonrails.org/v6.0/classes/ActiveRecord/ConnectionAdapters/ConnectionPool.html#method-c-new] is just a limit -- it won't actually generate those connections until they're needed. And there's no threading anywhere, so I don't think any of the workers would ever check out more than one connection at a time. So the most you'd ever get is two per resque worker (one for the parent, one for the forked child), and you can't get to 100 with that unless they're not being closed properly when the forked child exits.{quote}

[~accountid:557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6]:

{quote}Looking at that error log, here's what seems to be happening from the sequence of errors shown:

1. Something sends a {{SIGTERM}} to the worker. (Not the child, which is running the job, but the parent.)

2. The worker tries to log this, but [encounters this NewRelic bug instead|https://github.com/newrelic/newrelic-ruby-agent/issues/1020].

3. Because the error means it's not a clean shutdown, it tries to record the fact that it's shutting down in Redis. But it blocks because someone else is using the connection.

4. While it's blocked, it receives a {{SIGCONT}} signal, which it tries to log using NewRelic. This triggers the NewRelic bug a second time.

Obviously the multiple NewRelic failures aren't helping, but ultimately the whole sequence was triggered by a {{SIGTERM}}, so the worker was going to die anyway. It's possible that this didn't happen before because the jobs were failing quickly as a result of the connection issue. Now they're running, and running long enough that something (the monitoring system?) can send signals to them, triggering the NewRelic issue.{quote}

To address the New Relic bug, we will update the gem: [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6449|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6449|smart-link].

Sometimes, users will supply chapter show URLs (e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/chapters/123|https://test.archiveofourown.org/chapters/123] or [https://test.archiveofourown.org/chapters/123?some_params=something|https://test.archiveofourown.org/chapters/123?some_params=something]) in the abuse form’s “Link to the page you are reporting” field. 

It’s annoying for Policy & Abuse not to have the work IDs handy.

So when a user does this, before we run {{before_validation :clean_url, on: :create}} and {{validate :url_is_not_over_reported}}, we'd like to:

* look up which work the chapter belongs to
* add the work information to the URL
* assuming the chapter and work can be found, run the usual before_validation and validation checks
* if the chapter or work cannot be found, don’t modify the URL and don’t error, just send the report on through with the URL as entered

*Testing*

*NB:* Unless [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6044|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6044|smart-link] is fixed first, you’ll need to remove the {{test}} subdomain from the URLs as well.

# Locate a multi-chapter work

# Follow the Policy Questions & Abuse Reports link in the site footer

## making sure to provide an email address you have access to, and
## pausing at the “Link to the page you are reporting” field to remove the work info from the URL, e.g., changing {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/123/chapters/789}} to {{https://archiveofourown.org/chapters/789}}

# Fill out the form,

This happens if you submit a URL without the scheme, e.g. having just {{archiveofourown.org/chapters/2165131/}} in the form field. This was never a problem before because we never tried prepending stuff to the URL until now.

Let’s fix this by parsing the URL in this order in one validation:

* Skip if it doesn’t match the regex for works, users, or chapters
* Parse it once, check if the scheme is nil; if so, prepend “http://“ to the string and parse again
* Remove query and fragment
* Parse the chapter ID and try to prepend the work ID to the path

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
We'd like to restrict which URLs can be submitted using the Policy Questions & Abuse Reports form.

When you submit a repot using a URL that is not allowed, you should get an error: 

{quote}The "Link to the page you are reporting" field should contain the correct URL for the specific work, comment, or other content you wish to report. If you are submitting a policy question, please report the homepage instead.{quote}

*Reportable user pages:*

Form should not error if URL contains additional parameters (e.g., {{/users/:id/works?fandom_id=id}} or {{/users/:id/pseuds/:id/edit}}). 

However, we do not want to allow pages PAC cannot access, such as {{/users/:id/readings}}.

{noformat}/users/:id
/users/:id/works
/users/:id/works/drafts
/users/:id/works/collected
/users/:id/bookmarks
/users/:id/series
/users/:id/profile
/users/:id/collections
/users/:id/gifts
/users/:id/blocked/users
/users/:id/muted/users
/users/:id/pseuds
/users/:id/inbox

/users/:id/pseuds/:id
/users/:id/pseuds/:id/works
/users/:id/pseuds/:id/bookmarks
/users/:id/pseuds/:id/series{noformat}

*Reportable collection pages:*

Any page within a specific collection or challenge should be reportable. 

However, [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6218|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6218|smart-link] must be done first to ensure PAC has access to the reported pages.

{{/collections/:id}}

*Reportable tag set pages:*

Only the show page should be reportable. Admins do not have access to other pages within tag sets, and the form should error for other tag set pages.

{{/tag_sets/:id}}

*Other reportable pages:*

Form should not error if the URL contains additional parameters (e.g., {{/admin_posts/:id?show_comments=true}}, {{/bookmarks/:id/edit}}, or {{/tags/:id/works}}). 

However, it should error if there is no ID (e.g., {{/works/search?work_search=query}} or {{/bookmarks}}).

{noformat}/admin_posts/:id
/works/:id
/bookmarks/:id
/series/:id
/chapters/:id
/tags/:id
/comments/:id{noformat}

*And a homepage in a pear tree:*

column1: Remove ARIA "complementary" role from work and chapter title, summary, notes
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
[Firefox's Reader View|https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/firefox-reader-view-clutter-free-web-pages] strips out HTML sections with the [“unlikely” ARIA role of "complementary"|https://github.com/mozilla/readability/blob/fde359445cc96888fd8fa9717d336558ace83a5d/Readability.js#L147], in addition to doing [a number of other calculations to determine if sections should be shown|https://github.com/mozilla/readability/blob/fde359445cc96888fd8fa9717d336558ace83a5d/Readability.js#L999-L1004] (e.g., [checking if there are more than 25 characters in a paragraph|https://github.com/mozilla/readability/blob/fde359445cc96888fd8fa9717d336558ace83a5d/Readability.js#L1010]).

Having the “complementary” role means that chapters in Reader View never contain their chapter titles as the titles. Currently the chapter in Reader View starts with the fixed string "Chapter Text". It should instead be the same as the normal text: "Chapter : ".

The role should be removed to make sure the following sometimes appears in Reader View:

* Work: title, summary, notes, endnotes
* Chapter: title, summary, notes, endnotes

*Testing*

On a multichapter work with end notes and a summary, and a final chapter with end notes, access the final chapter. View the page source and search for {{role="complementary"}}. It should not appear.

column1: Work in anonymous collection does not generate subscription notifications to someone also subscribed to the creator
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Users can subscribe to a work in an anonymous collection and should receive notifications when it updates.  However, if any of those users are also subscribed to the creator of the anonymous work, they won’t get a notification when that work updates.

To replicate:

# While logged in as User A, subscribe to User B’s entire profile (by going to their dashboard and selecting ‘Subscribe’ there)
# While logged in as User B, post a new work in an anonymous collection.  (User A should not receive a notification at this point, since that could de-anon your work.)
# While logged in as User A, subscribe to that anonymous work (by going to the work itself and selecting ‘Subscribe’ there).
# While logged in as User B, post a new chapter to your anonymous work.  

What should happen: User A should receive a subscription notification like anyone else subscribed to the anonymous work.  The subscription notification should inform them that Anonymous has posted a new chapter of Work Title (not de-anoning the author).

What actually happens: User A does not get a subscription notification, presumably because the mechanism that prevents them from receiving subscription updates on anonymous works when they are subscribed to the creator’s profile is also blocking them from receiving subscription updates on the individual work.

column1: Set User.current_user in an around_action hook, so that it's cleared more consistently in tests
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When a request by a logged-in user is processed, {{User.current_user}} is set at the beginning of the request, but never cleared afterwards. This is fine in most cases, because when the next request comes in, {{User.current_user}} will be set again, overwriting the previous value.

However, in features and in request specs, where requests are sometimes interleaved with e.g. calls to {{FactoryBot.create(:work)}}, this can cause errors, because all of the actions performed after the end of the request are treated as though they were being performed by the user who made the previous request. This can result in errors like, “x does not allow others to invite them to be a co-creator,” when trying to create a work with a single creator.

To prevent these errors from affecting the tests, most of the feature steps that call {{FactoryBot.create(:work)}} also include an {{I start a new session}} step to make sure that {{User.current_user}} is cleared, and the N+1 comments request spec explicitly calls {{User.current_user = nil}}.

Let’s set {{User.current_user}} in an {{around_action}} hook, setting it before the request and clearing it after the request is complete, so that calling {{User.current_user}} is more accurate in tests.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Current behavior To create a new admin, a database admin runs a script ([create_admin.rb|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e7c7da0a33a554cfde124ef1ad2e3df5ce005470/script/create_admin.rb]) that creates their account and assigns a password and roles. The script outputs some text for our wiki list of admins and text for creating password files, which the database admin then shares with the admin.  If an admin wants their password reset, a database admin is also responsible for that. If it is necessary to temporarily disable admin access, a database admin can reset an admin's password, preventing them from logging in. h1. Desired behavior h2. Resetting admin passwords We should use the [Devise Recoverable module|https://www.rubydoc.info/github/heartcombo/devise/main/Devise/Models/Recoverable] to allow admins to reset their own passwords without assistance from a database admin.  There should be a "Forgot admin password?" link on the admin login page. !2btUgKivY9T2roGA1zxUMX-ntctxMQUu8quHhrFN4sMld8amPT_fTfXXEgYRbmpGIAKD9Iz20aRc8C8W9xpBJCfLblntBw32vODrNL8qe9FrzvAQb5aX-TTRClZhKTHvGQ-5qPefSBTizVd6lOBm-GkJwBZv1Plsg9fpngwgkLpk_ahgXDaUF_wpfMEung|width=1600,height=633! {noformat}
Reset password

{noformat} The reset page at  {{/admin/password/new}} should resemble [the new password page for users|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e7c7da0a33a554cfde124ef1ad2e3df5ce005470/app/views/users/passwords/new.html.erb] with modified text: !gMEbwe35obvQmiTr1dDbw00luudRRe5RX-JY6kT6QGZjLm2B75AOpyCyiiKm4y365W6UBEQ9iUaMyAVH2m8yRhvGA6daut5a7BLXqpGe6z7PKLsJkZ-0yTLiwk0R-lrBO6mBuwTAltZ0CizyjRbpaR_PPcSf8bEBeveDXtw5Haz87anht_I0VpwKiwkPsg|width=1358,height=410! {quote}Forgotten your admin password? If you've forgotten or would like to change your admin password, we can send instructions that will allow you to reset it. Please tell us the username or email address for your admin account. Admin email address or username: ______ [Reset Admin Password]{quote} Submitting the form should redirect you to the admin login page with a blue flash notice saying, "Check your OTW email for instructions on how to reset your admin password." *EDIT:* The reset password page should just ask for username, not email. We don’t currently allow admins to log in by email, and it’s goofy to allow it one place but not the other. *Subject:* {quote}[AO3] Reset your admin password{quote} *HTML:* {quote}Dear <%= style_bold(@admin.login) %>, Someone has requested a password reset for your account. You can change your account password by following the link below and entering your new password. <%= style_link("Change my password.", devise password reset URL %> If you do not use this link to reset your password within a week, it will expire, and you will have to request a new one. If you did not request this password reset, you may ignore this email and your previous password will continue to work.{quote} *Text:* {quote}Dear <%= @admin.login %>, Someone has requested a password reset for your account. You can change your account password by following the link below and entering your new password. <%= devise reset URL %> If you do not use this link to reset your password within a week, it will expire, and you will have to request a new one. If you did not request this password reset, you may ignore this email and your previous password will continue to work.{quote} The edit password page at {{/admin/password/edit?reset_password_token=keysmash}} should resemble the [user edit password page|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e7c7da0a33a554cfde124ef1ad2e3df5ce005470/app/views/users/passwords/edit.html.erb], but the heading should say "Set My Admin Password" and the button should say "Set Admin Password." ("Set" works for both new admins and admins who need to reset or change their password.) !lhhaTSCXwE5BBCMu545TtyNGNTSB_zjqaMX1SqjPJeW8wE3OxZRqBPKxRgWffheRdgXLyjJjWMPB6zlUDc5vVQOb2bMuL-_RpYv8HZMUV6c0YHagfGhsdYyxakORFLxBTNwgGuEw8XyAJHLO1uRSWoHO1tIlqeBSYMfN5YUVgZUBN_3p3PFmjFGngJPmpQ|width=1408,height=560! Reset requests will be rate limited using the same nginx approach we use for rate limiting user password resets. (This is done by Systems.) The minimum length for the password should be set to 10 and the max should remain 40. These should be configurable separately from user password length requirements. h2. Setting passwords for new accounts Admins should be required to set their own password before signing in for the first time after account creation.  A database admin should still need to run script/create_admin.rb, and the script should continue to create the admin account, assign a password and roles, and output the wiki information, but it should no longer output the password information for the database admin to share. Additionally, the password should now be assigned using {{SecureRandom.alphanumeric(10)}}, not {{pwgen}}, which can be removed. Instead, the script should send a Devise password reset email to the email address provided for the admin. *Subject:* {quote}[AO3] Your AO3 admin account{quote} *HTML:* {quote}Hi, <%= style_bold(@admin.login) %>! Your AO3 admin account has been created.  <%= style_bold("Admin username:") %> <%= @admin.login %> <%= style_bold("Admin login URL:") %> <%= style_link(new_admin_session_url, new_admin_session_url) %> Please <%= style_link("follow this link to set your password", devise reset url) %> so you can log in.{quote} *Text:* {quote}Hi, <%= @admin.login %>! Your AO3 admin account has been created. Admin username: <%= @admin.login %> Admin login URL: <%= new_admin_session_url %> Please follow this link to set your password so you can log in: <%= devise reset url %>{quote} The link in the email will take them to the same edit password page described in the section on resetting admin passwords. h2. Disabling access -To ensure admin access can still be disabled, an allow_resets column should be added to the admin table. This column should be set to true by default.-  -When it is set to false, attempting to access the password recovery page should redirect the admin to the Archive homepage with a red flash error message saying, "Admin password resets are currently disabled."-  -This way, a database admin can still revoke access by changing an admin's password from the console and setting allow_resets to false.- Allow database admins to lock admins out of their accounts, _but_ use the Devise Lockable module to do it rather than rolling our own solution with an {{allow_resets}} column. Lockable comes with the wonderful bonus of actually signing the locked account out. A script should be added to handle this; it should prompt you to enter either a comma-separated list of admin logins to disable or {{ALL}} to disable all accounts.  Script for locking: {{bundle exec rails r script/lock_admin.rb}} Script for unlocking: {{bundle exec rails r script/unlock_admin.rb}} You can also do it from the Rails console using {{admin.lock_access!({ send_instructions: false })}} or {{admin.unlock_access!}} h1. h1. Support tickets

Support tickets should no longer be recorded in the database and the {{feedbacks}} table should be dropped. The associated class should no longer inherit from {{ApplicationRecord}}, but should still {{include ActiveModel::Validations}} (like we do in [WorkSearchForm|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ea6a25b610fc1b8cf3f11e537471edd2c7ed7149/app/models/search/work_search_form.rb#L1-L5]). 

[https://test.archiveofourown.org/support|https://test.archiveofourown.org/support]

If the ticket tracker is down and a user attempts to submit a support ticket, they should receive a sensible error message telling them to try again later. (Text TBD.)

If the ticket tracker is up, the ticket should be created in the tracker and [the feedback email|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ea6a25b610fc1b8cf3f11e537471edd2c7ed7149/app/mailers/user_mailer.rb#L405] should be sent to the address provided on the form.

To test, ensure that you receive the email containing the summary and content of your report, and ask a Support volunteer to check that all information in your ticket has arrived in the tracker.

h1. Abuse tickets

The {{abuse_reports}} table should have all columns dropped +except+ {{id}}, {{email}}, {{url}}, and {{created_at}}. These columns are needed for the {{url_is_not_over_reported}} and {{email_is_not_over_reporting}} validations.

A daily task should delete any rows older than that time period, since they will no longer be needed.

[https://test.archiveofourown.org/abuse_reports/new|https://test.archiveofourown.org/abuse_reports/new]

If the ticket tracker is down and a user attempts to submit a support ticket, they should receive a sensible error message telling them to try again later. (Text TBD.) Nothing should be recorded in the database.

If the ticket tracker is up, the ticket should be created in the tracker and [the abuse report email|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ea6a25b610fc1b8cf3f11e537471edd2c7ed7149/app/mailers/user_mailer.rb#L418] should be sent to the address provided on the form. A row should be added to the database containing the {{email}}, {{url}}, and submission date time ({{created_at}}) for the report.

To test, ensure that you receive the email containing the URL and comment portion of your report, and ask a Policy & Abuse volunteer to check that all information in your ticket has arrived in the tracker. 

It would also be a good idea to make sure the reports per day limit is applied to your email address, and the reports per month limit is applied to the URL.

* Do the same with a bookmark search

* Post a new work and make sure the work summary has all HTML stripped out of it in the subscription email (HTML version of the email)

column1: Try to fix deadlock issues with the readings:to_database task
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The rake task {{readings:to_database}} is currently broken. The original cause of the issue appears to be the {{ActiveRecord::Deadlocked}} error, which may have been caused either by (a) conflicts between two machines running the task at the same time, or (b) conflicts between a single copy of the task, and a user deleting their account (and thus all of the readings associated with that account).

As a result of this recurring error, the task was unable to finish processing the {{Reading:new}} Redis set, which ended up growing more and more until it became so large that calling {{smembers}} to retrieve the set and process its contents produces a timeout error. (This also means that while the {{smembers}} query is running, no other processes can access {{REDIS_GENERAL}}, leading to 500 errors from Redis timeouts.)

We’d like to do the following to try to address this:

# Use {{sscan}} instead of {{smembers}} to access the {{Reading:new}} set, so that we can actually process all 27+ million (and growing) readings currently stored on Redis.
# Move most of the code in {{readings:to_database}} into an {{ActiveJob}} with {{retry_on ActiveRecord::Deadlocked}}, so that it can automatically retry on deadlock.
# Try sorting the batches in the readings code so that they’re processed in a consistent order, avoiding deadlocks when the task is being run on multiple machines at once.
# Try to tweak the {{readings}} association on users so that it doesn’t conflict with the readings code. (Maybe {{dependent: :delete_all}} instead of {{dependent: :destroy}}, to try to make deletion faster and leave less time for conflicts? Or maybe a custom callback that changes the order they’re destroyed in?)

h1. Testing Instructions

These bugs only occur at _very_ large scales, so there’s no real way to replicate them on staging. It’s enough to make sure that the history code still works:

# Log in as a user with history enabled.
# View a work that you’ve never viewed before.
# Wait until it’s 55 minutes after the hour, then wait another few minutes to let the task run.
# Make sure that the work you viewed is listed in your history.

h1. Deploy

The cron job that runs {{rake readings:to_database}} is temporarily disabled on production to avoid timing out other processes relying on the same Redis instance handling readings. It should be re-enabled once the fix is deployed.

column1: Make StatCounter.stats_to_database scale better

column30:
Currently, {{StatCounter.stats_to_database}} is defined [like this|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/4a559c386d027cf55e69236076d2f1b9c5177d15/app/models/stat_counter.rb#L20-L27]:

{noformat}    work_ids = REDIS_GENERAL.smembers('works_to_update_stats').map{ |id| id.to_i }
    Work.where(id: work_ids).find_each do |work|
      work.update_stat_counter
      REDIS_GENERAL.srem('works_to_update_stats', work.id)
    end{noformat}

Using {{find_each}} here ensures that we’re never loading too many works from the database at once, but if the {{works_to_update_stats}} set is large (as might be the case if the stat counter job encounters a lot of errors over a period of time), the query itself may become too large for the database to handle:

{noformat}Class
    StatCounter 
Arguments

    --- stats_to_database

Exception
    ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid
Error
    Mysql2::Error::ConnectionError: Got a packet bigger than 'max_allowed_packet' bytes{noformat}

We’d like to make the job more scalable.

column1: Address LockWaitTimeouts in the readings code
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The readings code is experiencing occasional lock wait timeout errors (which is particularly a problem now that the readings are so backed up – the jobs tend to overlap a lot). We’d like to switch readings to use a similar system to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6457|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6457|smart-link] for the batch updates, so that they can be run in parallel, in their own queue so that they can be throttled as needed, and with a retry on {{ActiveRecord::LockWaitTimeout}} and {{ActiveRecord::Deadlocked}} so that if the parallelism becomes a problem they can (try to) recover.

(In the current system, we have a single job that’s trying to process 50+ million readings, to try to catch up to the present. We could retry on {{ActiveRecord::LockWaitTimeout}} in that job, but it’ll be running for days, and with that many transactions, we might run out of retries before the job finishes. If we split it into smaller jobs, we can finish faster, and the number of retries permitted will be proportional to the number of transactions.)

h1. Testing Instructions

As is the case with a lot of issues recently, we can’t really test this at scale, but we should make sure that we haven’t broken things worse.

# Log in as a user with history enabled.
# Visit a work that you’ve never viewed before.
# Wait until a little after :55 to let the readings job run.
# Make sure that the work now appears in your history.

h1. Deploy Notes

This needs a new {{readings}} Resque queue (and workers for said queue).

Since the existing rake will be removed, we need to remove the crontab entry:

{noformat}55 * * * * /bin/bash -l -c 'cd /home/ao3app/app/current && RAILS_ENV=production bundle exec rake readings:to_database  >> /home/ao3app/log/readings:to_database.log 2>&1' > /dev/null 2>&1{noformat}

Once we’re satisfied with the new code and want to catch up on the backlog of readings, we can run the following:

{code:ruby}(1..(REDIS_GENERAL.get("Reading:job_id").to_i + 1)).each do |i|
  RedisSetJobSpawner.perform_later("ReadingsJob", key: "Reading:new:#{i}")
end{code}

This should iterate through all of the various sets of readings that were split off by the previous code, and create a bunch of jobs for each of them.

{noformat}after_commit :recache_settings
def recache_settings
  Rails.cache.write("admin_settings", self)
end{noformat}

By writing to the cache, instead of just deleting it, you can ensure that even if one of the databases is lagging a little, the next person to try to fetch the admin settings is guaranteed to get the modified version, instead of fetching an old version from the database and writing it to the cache.

column30:
*Steps to reproduce*

# Log in as an admin with the policy_and_abuse, support, or superadmin role
# Manage Users > Find User
# Search for a user
# Follow the “Details” link for the user
# Enter another user’s username and email in the Fannish Next of Kin fields
# Save
# Change the username and email in the Fannish Next of Kin fields
# Save
# Remove the username and email in the Fannish Next of Kin fields
# Save
# Again in the FNOK fields, enter the username and email of another user, but this time make it one you have access to and don’t mind deleting
# Save
# Leave this tab/window open and in another browser or private window, log in as the user you just entered as the FNOK
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Profile > Delete My Account
# Confirm you want to delete your account
# In the tab where you’re logged in as admin, refresh the page and notice that the FNOK field is now blank

*What happens*

Nothing is recorded in the User History table for any of these changes, so we don’t have any records when things get confusing. Instead, we have to spend time puzzling things out.

*What should happen*

We want to log these changes in the User History table, not just for the user who is getting (or losing) a FNOK, but also for the user who is becoming (or ceasing to be) the FNOK. 

We’ll use user IDs so we don’t keep unnecessary records of deleted usernames, and so we don’t get confused in the event someone’s username changes.

Date - Fannish Next of Kin Added: [user ID] - Change made by [admin login]

Date - Added as Fannish Next of Kin for: [user ID] - Change made by [admin login]

Date - Fannish Next of Kin Removed: [user ID] - Change made by [admin login]

Date - Removed as Fannish Next of Kin for: [user ID] - Change made by [admin login]

Date - Fannish Next of Kin Removed: [user ID] - System Generated

If the form is submitted without making changes, nothing should be added to the activities log.

h1. Testing Instructions

# Check all of the autocomplete fields:
## Go to the new work form, and check that:
### Tags appear in each of the tag autocompletes (Fandom, Character, Relationship, and Additional Tags).
### Pseuds appear in the “Gift this work to” field.
### Collections appear in the “Post to Collections / Challenges” field.
## Go to the Collections page, and check that collections appear in the “Filter by title or name” field.
## Create a collection, and make sure that your other collections appear in the “Parent collection (that you maintain)” field.
## Go to a work listing, and check that tags appear in the “Other tags to include” field.
## Go to “My Bookmarks > Bookmark External Work” page, and check that URLs appear in the “URL” field when you start typing.
## Go to the new Site Skin form, and under “Advanced” select “Add parent skin.” Then make sure that some skins appear when you start typing in the field that appears.
## As an admin, go to the new admin post page, and check that:
### Some tags appear when you start typing in the “Tags” field.
### Some posts appear when you start typing in the “Translation of” field.
## Create a tag set with at least 21 fandoms, and several characters, each of which has been assigned to at least one fandom by editing the tag set and selecting “Add Association.” Then create a gift exchange, and go through the following steps:
### Under “Challenge Settings,” make sure the tag set appears under the “Tag Sets To Use” field. Select it.
### Check “Fandom only?” and “Tag set fandom only?” for characters.
### Open signups.
### When signing up, check that the fandoms appear in the autocomplete for the “Fandom” field.
### When signing up, pick a fandom with character(s) in the tag set, and check that the character(s) from that fandom appears in the autocomplete for the “Character” field.
### Sign up for the exchange as at least two users, preferably more.
### Close sign-ups and run matching.
### Try editing the matches, and make sure that the autocomplete works when you are trying to replace the recipient of a complete assignment.
### Try editing the matches, and make sure that the autocomplete works when you are trying to replace the giver of a complete assignment.
# Rails 6.1 changes the default value of the case sensitivity option for the uniqueness validator, so we should probably check the following:
## Create two skins of the same name up to capitalization. Make sure they can both be created without errors.
## Log in as a user, and leave a comment on a work, then leave another comment with the same pseud that’s almost identical except for the capitalization. Make sure that the second comment gives a nice error.
## Try to create a user account with email/login the same as an existing account, but with different capitalization for both. Make sure you get errors for both the email and the login.
## Try to create a tag set with the same title as an existing tag set, but with different capitalization. Make sure you get a nice error.
## Try to sign up on the invitations queue twice with the same email, with slightly different capitalization on the second one. Make sure that the second one yields *two* “Email is already part of our queue.” errors.
## Create two pseuds for the same user, then try to rename the second pseud so that it’s the same as the first pseud but with different capitalization. Make sure that you get a “Name has already been taken” error.
## Try to create a collection with the same name as an existing collection, but different capitalization. Make sure it fails.
## As an admin, try adding an email to the Banned Emails list, then try adding the same email but with slightly different capitalization. Make sure the second addition fails with a nice error.
## As an admin, create an API key with a specific name, then try to create another API key with the same name, but different capitalization. Make sure the second addition gives a nice error.
## As an admin, try to create a new locale with the same ISO code as an existing locale, but with different capitalization. Make sure you get a nice error.
# PhraseApp appears to have a bug when used with Rails 6.1 + Ruby 3.0, which occurs when calling {{translate}} from a view with a key that has no associated translation. It also affects any code using {{ts}}. So we should check some views:
## View the Site Map, and make sure that all of the text looks okay.
## View the Diversity statement, and make sure that all of the text looks okay.
## View the Donate or Volunteer page, and make sure that all of the text looks okay.
# 6.1 deprecates the {{errors[:base] << message}} syntax, which is used in a lot of validators, and in abuse reports. To avoid the spammy deprecation warnings, we’re probably going to want to change this syntax, which means we should check that the code still works:

column1: Allow tag wrangling admins to download CSV of wranglers' last wrangled tags
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
# Log in as an admin with the tag_wrangling or superadmin role
# Go to a user’s wrangling page (https://test.ao3.org/tag_wranglers/USERNAME/)

There should be a button-style “Tags Wrangled (CSV)” link under the “username’s Wrangling Page” heading that allows you to download a CSV of tags that were last wrangled by the user. (You can check the Profile, Subscribe, etc navigation on user show pages to see how the markup should be handled on pages with icons and underlined headings.)

The CSV should be tab-separated and include Tag Name, Date Updated, Tag Type, Merger, Fandoms, Canonical, Unwrangleable. (“Merger” is the tag it is synned to, if any, and “Canonical” and “Unwrangleable” have true or false values.)

You can adapt what we usually do from the console:

{code:ruby}user = User.find_by(login: "username")
wrangled_tags = Tag.where(last_wrangler: user) ; nil
wrangled_tags.each do |tag|
  merger = tag.merger_id? ? tag.merger.name : ''
  fandoms = tag.respond_to?(:fandoms) ? tag.fandoms.map(&:name).join(" + ") : ''
  puts "#{tag.name},#{tag.updated_at},#{tag.type},#{merger},#{fandoms},#{tag.unwrangleable}"
end ; nil{code}

The CSV should _not_ be treated liked downloads and cached on the front ends; it should be generated on demand and only available to authorized admins, like challenge CSVs are only available to the challenge moderators.

The “Tags Wrangled (CSV)” link should not be present if you are not logged in as an authorized admin.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Note: This information is already indexed for [works|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/fcb6a8e6eeec7f5001d31da07d72219d82ee5ded/app/models/work.rb#L1177] and [series|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/fcb6a8e6eeec7f5001d31da07d72219d82ee5ded/app/models/series.rb#L229].

The filters for bookmarks should allow searching, sorting, and filtering by word count:

* The Sort by select menu in the filters (found on pages like https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/TAG_NAME/bookmarks) should have a Word Count option under the two date options.
* The More Options section of the filters should have a Word Count section above the two search fields. It should be the same as the Word Count section on work filters.
* The Sort by select menu on the Bookmark Search page (https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search) should also have a Word Count option added under the two date options.
* Above the Work language field on the Bookmark Search page, a Word count field should be added. 

We will not be adding support for the {{words: 100}}, {{words:<1000}}, etc syntax in "Search within results" due to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5104|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5104|smart-link].

Because some but not all works in a series can be restricted, we need to index two separate word counts, one for logged in users (including restricted works) and one for guests (excluding restricted works), similar to how we would tackle [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6304|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6304|smart-link].

*Testing*

Note: External works do not have word counts; only works and series.

# On the Bookmark Search page, ensure you can search and get expected results using the new Word count field, including when you use >, <, or ranges like {{1000-5000}}.
# On the Bookmark Search page, ensure you can use the Sort by Word Count option to get the expected results.
# On a page with bookmark filters (e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/bookmarks|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/bookmarks]), ensure you can use the Word Count option to get the expected results.
# And again on a page with bookmark filters, ensure you can use the new Sort by option to get results sorted in the expected order.

Additionally:

# Create a series with 2 works, one of those works restricted to only logged-in users
# Bookmark the series
# Make sure you can find the bookmark on your bookmarks page when filtering by the combined word count of both works
# Log out
# Go back to your bookmarks page and make sure the bookmark shows up when filtering _only_ by the word count of the one visible work (not when looking for the combined word count)
# Log back in and make the restricted work visible to all users
# Wait 5-15 minutes
# Make sure you can find the bookmarks on your bookmarks page when filtering by the combined word count of both works
# Log out
# Go back to your bookmarks page and make sure the bookmark shows up when filtering by the word count of both works combined (not when looking for the word count of the unchanged work)
# Log back in
# Edit one of the works to modify the number of words
# Wait 5-15 minutes
# Make sure you can find the bookmark on your bookmarks page when filtering by the new combined word count of both works
# Log out
# Go back to your bookmarks page and make sure the bookmark shows up when filtering by the new combined word count of both works

column1: Remove ApplicationController#set_media, and load the media for the menu only when necessary
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The {{ApplicationController#set_media}} method performs three database queries, and assigns the results to the variable {{@menu_media}}. The only place the {{@menu_media}} variable is used is here: {code:ruby} <% cache "menu-fandoms-version3", skip_digest: true do %> <% for medium in @menu_media %> <% unless medium.id.nil? %>
  • <%= link_to ts("#{medium.name}", key: 'header.fandom'), medium_fandoms_path(medium) %>
    • <% end %> <% end %> <% end %>{code} [(Source)|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/2d92ec1e100d2db8d98c791258b8ea115044975d/app/views/menu/_menu_fandoms.html.erb#L3-L9] Because this cache block has no expiration time set, and is never expired with a call to {{expire_fragment}}, this will basically never be a cache miss. This means that in almost every single page load, the {{@menu_media}} variable will be computed, but never accessed. The queries performed to compute {{@menu_media}} are fairly quick to execute (probably just a few milliseconds), but it would be marginally faster to remove the {{ApplicationController#set_media}} function, and modify this code so that the media for the menu are loaded only when the cached media list needs regenerating. (For tidiness, it’d be nice to keep the code out of the view file, but placing it in a helper or in the media model would make sense.) h1. Testing Instructions Load the homepage, and check that the media listed in the menu still look correct.

column1: Add code to allow ES search results to load records with includes()
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The issues [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4394|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4394|smart-link] and [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4438|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4438|smart-link] are intended to decrease the number of database queries required to display work and bookmark listings. Both controllers call {{includes()}} in some cases, but they still perform n+1 queries in others, in part because the search code doesn’t have any easy way to call {{includes()}} on the records being returned by the search. We’d like to change that.

Because caching and calling {{includes()}} work at cross-purposes to some extent (if a fragment is cached there’s not much point in preloading the data used to generate it), we don’t want to start out by calling {{includes()}} on everything, and then have to roll it back if it slows things down instead of speeding things up. So we’ll be starting slow with this issue, without trying to immediately eliminate all n+1 queries.

column1: In a challenge where relationships are checkboxes, editing a prompt for A/B/C will automatically check the A/B and B/C checkboxes
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to Reproduce

# Create a tag set with three relationships: {{A/B/C}}, {{A/B}}, and {{B/C}}.
# Create a prompt meme or gift exchange using that tag set. Set the number of allowed relationships in requests to at least 1, but make sure you don’t check the “Fandom only?” or “Tag set fandom only?” box for relationships — you want them to show up as checkboxes.
# Sign up for the prompt meme/gift exchange requesting only {{A/B/C}}.
# Edit your sign-up.

[This gift exchange|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/ti_overlapping_tags] is already set up with the required settings, so if you want to see it in action on staging you can skip steps 1 and 2.

h1. What Should Happen

The edit form should have the {{A/B/C}} relationship checked, but not the {{A/B}} or {{B/C}} relationships.

h1. What Actually Happens

In addition to {{A/B/C}}, the {{A/B}} and {{B/C}} boxes are also checked.

h1. Notes

This occurs because the code for checkboxes in tag sets is a little imprecise — basically, to check whether a tag should be checked on the edit form, it looks at the comma-separated list of tags (in this case, just {{A/B/C}}), and checks whether the value of the checkbox is included in that string. Because {{A/B/C}} contains {{A/B/C}}, {{A/B}}, and {{B/C}}, all three checkboxes will be automatically checked whenever {{A/B/C}} is checked.

Note that it doesn’t actually add the tags {{A/B}} and {{B/C}} to the prompt unless you save the prompt without unchecking the checkboxes. But it does mean that every time you want to edit your prompt, you have to remember to uncheck the {{A/B}} and {{B/C}} tags.

You can reproduce this with other tags, as long as the tags are the same type, and at least one of the tags is a substring of the other. For obvious reasons, that’s easiest to do with relationships, but this would also work for fandoms, characters, and freeforms if you pick the right tag names.

column1: Merge the Bookmarkable module and the BookmarkCountCaching module
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
We have two different systems for caching the number of public bookmarks associated with a work.

The {{Bookmarkable}} module defines {{public_bookmark_count}} for all types of bookmarkable. This cache expires every 2 hours, and whenever the bookmarkable is touched. It’s used in bookmark blurbs (the number in the upper right corner). 

The {{BookmarkCountCaching}} module defines {{public_bookmarks_count}} (note the plural) for just works. This cache never automatically expires, but is manually deleted whenever a bookmark is created, edited, or deleted. It’s used in work blurbs and headers.

We don’t need two different methods of caching the same number. Let’s pick one of the two names, rename all references to the other, and merge the {{BookmarkCountCaching}} module into the {{Bookmarkable}} module. I’m not sure which expiration scheme we want to keep, but combining the two schemes seems doable.

column1: Update skins:cache_all_site_skins to target skins in the footer's chooser
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When we make CSS changes, we need to run this rake before they show up in the default skin:

[https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b36c43d281b8db77f410e0d014bdb1319a3fb3f4/lib/tasks/skin_tasks.rake#L160-L163|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b36c43d281b8db77f410e0d014bdb1319a3fb3f4/lib/tasks/skin_tasks.rake#L160-L163|smart-link] 

The rake looks for skins with {{cached: true}}. The {{cache!}} method [sets the field to false, does its job, then sets the field back to true again at the end for affected skins|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b36c43d281b8db77f410e0d014bdb1319a3fb3f4/app/models/skin.rb#L228-L267]. If {{cache!}} fails to complete for whatever reason, the not cached skin will not be picked up by the next run of the rake.

We can make the rake more consistent by selecting the specific skins that need to be cached:

* the default skin;
* the skins listed in the chooser in the site footer ({{Skin.in_chooser}}).

The rake should print out the names of the skins it caches.

h1. Testing

Run {{bundle exec rake skins:cache_all_site_skins}} on all app servers (Systems can do this via Ansible), after a deploy containing CSS changes.

column1: Try bypassing the cache for CSS classes when the pseuds are already loaded
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The code for generating the CSS classes for a work uses a cache, resulting in 20 separate memcached gets for all work index pages.

Once pseuds are loaded on all work indexes ([https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6475|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6475|smart-link]), it might be faster to rewrite the {{css_classes_for_creation_blurb}} function to use {{pseuds.pluck(:user_id).uniq}} instead of {{users.pluck(:id).uniq}}, and bypass the cache when the pseuds are loaded (or just skip the cache altogether). Let's try it, preferably in a release without any other performance changes, so that it’s easier to check if it’s an improvement.

h2. Notes

The first pull request for this only changed the database query, without touching the caching. We will decide whether to change the caching based on the performance on production.

h1. Testing Instructions

Mute a user who has some public works, and view their {{/users/NAME/works}} page to make sure that all the works are invisible.

column1: Character & Relationship Tags No Longer Register Properly in Works Autocomplete Post-Fandom Rename
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Generally all fandom renames are done via admin these days by synning the old fandom tag to the newly created fandom tag. 

When doing so, sometimes the character & relationship tags do not register properly with the new fandom tag which results in those tags which were moved to the new fandom tag via synning the old fandom tag to the new NOT showing up in the works autocomplete unless we either:

a.) Use the Troubleshooting Options to Fix the Tag Count associated with each individual tag.
b.) Remove and re-add the fandom tag to each tag.

Unfortunately, when this happens, it seems to be an all or nothing deal where if it happens, it happens to every tag in the fandom and it’s recently happened on several very large fandoms which results many Support tickets since big fandoms are often very visible and popular fandoms, it’s also a lot of work to put right from the Tag Wrangler side of things. 

With this bug, we’d be very content with either a fix so that this didn’t happen or a way to handle it reasonably quickly if it does. 

*STEPS TO REPRODUCE:*

* Create New Fandom Canonical Tag
* Syn Old Fandom Canonical Tag to New Fandom Canonical Tag
* Check Work Posting Form to see if Character and/or Relationship tags populate.

}} above the character counter, which usually comes right after the form field it applies to, so it's _possible_ that influences how a browser calculates the size when switching between modes if it doesn’t happen on every character counter. Was it an https URL? It looks like the [ExternalWorksController|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/81f6aefb22774f3da1a9e0fa0a7d41de0ff07b17/app/controllers/external_works_controller.rb#L14-L15] reformats the URL before looking it up in the database:

{code:ruby} url = ExternalWork.new.reformat_url(params[:external_work_url])
 @external_work = ExternalWork.where(url: url).first{code}

Reformatting includes [changing from https to http|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/81f6aefb22774f3da1a9e0fa0a7d41de0ff07b17/lib/url_helpers.rb#L6-L11]:

{code:ruby}  def reformat_url(url)
    url = url.gsub(/https/, "http")
    url = "http://" + url if url && url.length > 0 && /http/.match(url[0..3]).nil?
    url.chop if url.last == "/"
    url
  end{code}

The reformatting operation is also performed [before the external work is saved|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/81f6aefb22774f3da1a9e0fa0a7d41de0ff07b17/app/models/external_work.rb#L42-L46], but there do seem to be a few external works with https instead of http (presumably added before the callback was added). *Setup*

You’ll need an approved site skin with a name containing an exclamation point. You might already have one  like “The Screeny Exposure!” – if you do, you can skip right to steps to reproduce.

# Log in as a user
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins > Create Site Skin
# Fill in form, using an exclamation point in your skin title, and making sure to check “Apply to make public”
# Submit
# Log in as an admin with the superadmin role
# Skins > Approval Queue
# Locate the skin in the table
# Check the corresponding “Approve” checkbox
# Press “Update”

*Steps to reproduce*

# Log in as an admin with the superadmin role
# Skins > Approved Skins
# Locate the skin in the table
# For one of the actions, e.g., Unapprove, click the word rather than the checkbox

*What should happen*

The checkbox should be selected. (You can try on another skin like Reversi to see the desired behavior.

*What happens*

Nothing, because the label element’s {{for}} attribute (which doesn’t have the exclamation point) doesn't match the checkbox's {{id}} attribute (which does have it):

{noformat}<label class="action" for="make_uncached_the_screeny_exposure_">
Uncache  
  <input type="checkbox" name="make_uncached[]" id="make_uncached_the_screeny_exposure!" value="882">
</label>{noformat}

The exclamation point may not be valid in {{id}} attributes, so it’s probably best to remove it there rather than add it to the {{for}}.

column1: Store ID of user who creates collection item on the collection item, as well as the time the item's anonymous or unrevealed setting was updated
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Changes

h2. Store ID of user who creates collection item

When a collection item is created, e.g., by a creator adding a work or bookmark to a collection or a maintainer inviting a work, we should store the ID of the user who prompted the item’s creation on the collection item for our own edification.

It should stay as long as the collection item exists (i.e., don’t nil it out if the work creator removes themselves from the work, the collection moderator removes themselves from the collection, or the user deletes their account). 

We can call it {{collector_id}} or {{collection_item_creator_id}} or some such.

h2. Store datetime of the latest change to the collection item’s anonymous and unrevealed setting

Additionally, whenever a collection item’s unrevealed or anonymous setting is changed (e.g., by a mod revealing the entire collection or individual works), the date and time of the change should be recorded in a corresponding {{unrevealed_updated_at}} or {{anonymous_updated_at}} column.

h1. Testing

This information shouldn’t be displayed anywhere for now. Database admins will need to test.

h2. Store ID of user who creates collection item

You’ll need

* an account (User1) that
** you don’t mind deleting
** has a co-owned collection
* a second account (User2) with 
** at least one work and 
** the “Allow others to invite my works to collections” preference enabled

The {{collector_id}} or {{collection_item_creator_id}} on each collection item should list User1’s ID when User1

#  posts a work to their collection
#  edits an existing work to add it to their collection
#  adds a bookmark to their collection when creating the bookmark
#  edits an existing bookmark to add it to their collection
#  uses the “Invite to Collection” option on User2’s work to add it to their collection

The information should remain on those collection items when User1

# removes themselves as a co-owner of their collection
# deletes their account

h2. Store datetime of the latest change to the collection item’s anonymous and unrevealed setting

You’ll need 

* a collection that’s set to both anonymous and unrevealed
* at least one anonymous and unrevealed work in that collection. 

The{{unrevealed_updated_at}} or {{anonymous_updated_at}} column should change when

# the unrevealed box is unchecked on the Manage Items page
# the anonymous box is unchecked on the Manage Items page
# the unrevealed box is checked on the Manage Items page
# the unrevealed box is checked on the Manage Items page
# the “This collection is unrevealed” box is unchecked on the Collection Settings page
# the “This collection is anonymous” box is unchecked on the Collection Settings page

The columns should not change when

# the “This collection is unrevealed” box is checked on the Collection Settings page
# the “This collection is anonymous” box is checked on the Collection Settings page

(these actions do not change a collection item’s unrevealed or anonymous setting)

[~accountid:712020:517903ac-c419-4aa0-b773-3cb887f8dddb] Which account was serving as your User C for this case? 

I’m asking because if User C has the archivist role (like testy and testy10), they can add co-creators to works without going through the request process. That should definitely cause the work not to be gifted, and it’s probably why the [~accountid:640931c87655a3223a25987a] got the error even though you didn’t.

However, if User C isn’t an archivist and User B is just an _invited_ co-creator who hasn’t accepted the request… hm.

column1: Use parent aggregations for bookmarks instead of a separate query for aggregations
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Back when the {{BookmarkQuery}} class was created, there were no parent aggregations in Elasticsearch, so the parent aggregations are filled in by adding an [extra Elasticsearch query|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ccd24c3697144cc303f17c0e19cc65ff24915a5b/app/models/search/bookmark_query.rb#L24-L34]:

{noformat}# After the initial search, run an additional query to get work/series tag filters
# Elasticsearch doesn't support parent aggregations, and doing the main query on the parents
# limits searching and sorting on the bookmarks themselves
# Hopefully someday they'll fix this and we can get the data from a single query
def search_results
  response = search
  if response['aggregations']
    response['aggregations'].merge!(bookmarkable_query.aggregation_results)
  end
  QueryResult.new(klass, response, options.slice(:page, :per_page))
end{noformat}

But Elasticsearch now has [parent aggregations|https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/8.7/search-aggregations-bucket-parent-aggregation.html]. We should modify the {{BookmarkQuery}} class to use them, so that we can perform a single query instead of two to get the info we need. This may help reduce some of the load on Elasticsearch caused by bookmark queries (though definitely not all of it).

column1: Process hit counts using a modified version of the RedisSetJob system
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
There are deadlock errors happening fairly regularly with the {{RedisHitCounter.save_recent_counts}} job. They appear to be happening at :00 and :30, suggesting that the job may be conflicting with the {{StatCounterJob}} (which runs at :00 and :30). To help with this, we’d like to (a) allow multiple workers to work on the hit count updates at the same time, so that the job will hopefully be able to finish before the {{StatCounterJob}}s start running, and (b) allow the hit count job to be restarted when it encounters a deadlock, so that even if it does conflict briefly with the {{StatCounterJob}}, it has a good chance to recover.

We have already done this for several tasks using the {{RedisSetJob}} class and the {{RedisSetJobSpawner}} class, but the hit counter uses Redis hashes, not Redis sets. So we'd like to modify the {{RedisSetJob}} system to allow it to be adapted for use with Redis hashes.

h1. Testing Instructions

# Visit someone else’s work. Record the number of hits shown in the header.
# Wait until after the next :15 or :45.
# Check that the number of hits listed in the work header has increased by 1.

It might also be good to check that this hasn’t broken the existing set-based jobs, so you may also want to do the following:

# View a work.
# Wait until after the next :55.
# Make sure that the work appears in your reading history.

* {{rspec ./spec/helpers/works_helper_spec.rb:50}} # WorksHelper#sorted_languages returns all languages sorted alphabetically
* {{rspec ./spec/lib/tasks/work_tasks.rake_spec.rb:125}} # rake work:reset_word_counts when there are multiple languages updates only works in the specified language

*Testing*

Run the full RSpec test suite with {{bundle exec rspec spec}} or run {{bundle exec rspec spec/controllers/api/v2/api_works_spec.rb spec/lib/tasks/after_tasks.rake_spec.rb spec/helpers/works_helper_spec.rb spec/lib/tasks/work_tasks.rake_spec.rb}}. 

The CI does not reproduce/test this issue because the controller tests are run separately from the other tests.
