column1: Allow archivists to add works directly to collections without creator approval
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
*Steps to reproduce*

Users with the archivist role have the special power to immediately add anyone as a co-creator, regardless of their preferences, for Open Doors purposes. Collections need to work similarly.

# Log in as a user with the archivist role (on staging, you can use testy)
## To add this role to a user, log in as an admin with the superadmin or open_doors role
## Manage Users > Find Users
## Fill in “Name” with the username of the person you want to give the archivist role to
## Press “Find”
## Check the “Archivist” checkbox in the row for that user
## Press “Update” to save
# Create a collection
## Browse > Collections
## New Collection
## Fill in required fields
## Press “Submit” to save
# Go to a work, ideally one created by a user who does not have the “Allow others to invite my works to collections” preference enabled

*What happens*

There is no way to add the work to my collection.

*What should happen*

There should be an “Add To Collections” option on the bottom of _every_ work on the Archive, regardless of the creators' preferences. 

It should resemble the “Invite To Collections” option that appears on the works of users who allow collection invitations, but it should say “add” wherever “invite” appears.

Entering the name of one of your collections into the field and submitting the form should immediately add the work to the collection and notify the work creator(s).

The email subject should be: 

{quote}[AO3][COLLECTION TITLE] An Open Doors archivist has added your work to a collection{quote}

The HTML email should say:

{quote}Dear <%= style_bold(@user.login) %>,

The collection maintainers of <%= style_link(@collection.title, collection_url(@collection)) %> have added your work <%= style_creation_link(@work.title, work_url(@work)) %> to their collection!

Because the collection maintainers are acting in their official capacity as Open Doors archivists, they are allowed to add your work to this collection, even if you have collection invitations disabled. Archivists will only add a work to a collection if it was hosted on an imported archive.

If you would like to remove your work from this collection, please visit your <%= style_link("Approved Collection Items page", user_collection_items_url(@user, status: "approved")) %>.{quote}

The text email should say:

{quote}Dear <%= @user.login %>,

The collection maintainers of "<%= @collection.title %>" (<%= collection_url(@collection) %>) have added your work "<%= @work.title %>" (<%= work_url(@work)) %>) to their collection!

Because the collection maintainers are acting in their official capacity as Open Doors archivists, they are allowed to add your work to this collection, even if you have collection invitations disabled. Archivists will only add a work to a collection if it was hosted on an imported archive.

If you would like to remove your work from this collection, please visit your Approved Collection Items page: <%= user_collection_items_url(@user, status: "approved")) %>{quote}

column1: Use standard analyzer for creators and bookmarker on bookmark search
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
On work search, the {{creators}} field uses Elasticsearch's [standard analyzer|https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/analysis-standard-analyzer.html], while on bookmark search, we use the [simple analyzer|https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/analysis-simple-analyzer.html] for both the {{bookmarker}} and {{creators}} fields.

This means that in the bookmark search form, no matter if one

* searches "bookmarker: testy" in the "Any field on bookmark",
* or searches "testy" in the "Bookmarker" field

the results are essentially for {{*testy*}}, [returning also bookmarks from testy5, testy7, etc|https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search?bookmark_search%5Bbookmarkable_query%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bother_tag_names%5D=Testing&bookmark_search%5Bbookmarkable_type%5D=&bookmark_search%5Blanguage_id%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmarkable_date%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmark_query%5D=bookmarker%3Atesty&bookmark_search%5Bother_bookmark_tag_names%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmarker%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmark_notes%5D=&bookmark_search%5Brec%5D=0&bookmark_search%5Bwith_notes%5D=0&bookmark_search%5Bdate%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bsort_column%5D=&commit=Search+Bookmarks]. The same thing happens when [searching "creators: testy" on the Bookmark Search|https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search?bookmark_search%5Bbookmarkable_query%5D=creators%3Atesty&bookmark_search%5Bother_tag_names%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmarkable_type%5D=&bookmark_search%5Blanguage_id%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmarkable_date%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmark_query%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bother_bookmark_tag_names%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmarker%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmark_notes%5D=&bookmark_search%5Brec%5D=0&bookmark_search%5Bwith_notes%5D=0&bookmark_search%5Bdate%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bsort_column%5D=&commit=Search+Bookmarks] (but [not in the Work Search|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/search?commit=Search&work_search%5Bquery%5D=creators%3Atesty&work_search%5Btitle%5D=&work_search%5Bcreators%5D=&work_search%5Brevised_at%5D=&work_search%5Bcomplete%5D=&work_search%5Bcrossover%5D=&work_search%5Bsingle_chapter%5D=0&work_search%5Bword_count%5D=&work_search%5Blanguage_id%5D=&work_search%5Bfandom_names%5D=&work_search%5Brating_ids%5D=&work_search%5Bcharacter_names%5D=&work_search%5Brelationship_names%5D=&work_search%5Bfreeform_names%5D=&work_search%5Bhits%5D=&work_search%5Bkudos_count%5D=&work_search%5Bcomments_count%5D=&work_search%5Bbookmarks_count%5D=&work_search%5Bsort_column%5D=_score&work_search%5Bsort_direction%5D=desc]).

To make the behavior more consistent between the two forms, we’d like to use the standard analyzer for bookmark search’s {{bookmarker}} and {{creators}} fields.

We need to reindex before we move to Elasticsearch 8 (AO3-6259), so this should be done in the same release.

I started with two canonical fandoms (Veronica Mars (TV) and Dead Like Me) and two canonical characters in one of those fandoms (Logan Echolls and Duncan Kane), but it’s possible it doesn’t matter how the tags are wrangled or if they exist.

# Log in
# Create a tag set that allows character and fandom nominations
## Browse > Tags > Tag Sets > New Tag Set
## Enter a Title
## Check “Currently taking nominations?”
## For Nominations Limits, set fandoms to 4 and characters to 3 (so you can have some wiggle room if you mess up)
## Submit
# Nominate a character in a fandom
## Nominate
## For Fandom 1, enter Veronica Mars (TV)
## For the first character in Fandom 1, enter Logan Echolls
## Submit

## Edit
## Use the *×* to remove Logan Echolls from under Veronica Mars (TV)
## In Fandom 2, enter Dead Like Me
## For the first character in Fandom 2, enter Logan Echolls
## Submit
## You’ll get an error saying, “Someone else has already nominated the tag Logan Echolls for this set but in fandom Veronica Mars (TV). (All nominations have to be unique for the approval process to work.) Try making your nomination more specific, for instance tacking on (Dead Like Me).” 
## Frown a bit
## Use the *×* to remove Logan Echolls from under Dead Like Me
## Enter Duncan Kane in his place
## Submit

Both fandoms are still nominated (correct) and Duncan Kane is nominated as a character under Dead Like Me (also correct). However, under Veronica Mars (TV), there is a blank spot where a character should be (refer to image).

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Ban or suspend a user
## Log in as admin
## Manage Users > Find Users

## Find

h1. What happens

You get an error:

{quote}Invalid creator: testy_banned is currently banned and cannot be listed as a co-creator. {quote}

{quote}Invalid creator: testy_suspended does not allow others to invite them to be a co-creator.
Invalid creator: testy_suspended is currently banned and cannot be listed as a co-creator.{quote}

The message revealing the user’s banned or suspended status should instead say 

{quote}Invalid creator: name cannot be listed as a co-creator.{quote}

Ideally, if they had co-creator invitations turned off, it would only show

{quote}Invalid creator: name does not allow others to invite them to be a co-creator.{quote}

14/Apr/26 9:02 PM;712020:c6679159-6662-4054-9969-6e556eb0bd39;Hi Brian,

I've pushed a fix for the staging error. The issue was that some orphaned comments have {{nil}} values for{{threaded_left}}/{{threaded_right}}, which causes two problems:

# {{sort_by!}} crash — comparing {{nil}} with an integer raises {{ArgumentError: comparison of NilClass with 2 failed}} (the error you saw on staging).
# *Parent lookup failure* — the query using {{threaded_left < ? AND threaded_right > ?}} with {{nil}} values can't find a parent, hitting the {{raise}}.

The fix:

* Changed {{map}} to {{filter_map}} with {{next if orphan.nil?}} to skip {{missing_id}}s that no longer have child comments.
* Added {{|| 0}} fallback in {{sort_by!}} so {{nil}} {{threaded_left}} values don't crash the comparison.
* Replaced {{raise}} with {{puts}} + {{next}} when the parent can't be determined, so the task logs a message and continues instead of aborting.

I also added a spec that reproduces the scenario (two orphaned comment threads, one with{{nil}} {{threaded_left}}) to verify the task doesn't raise.

column161:
16/Apr/26 6:57 AM;557058:baa5f297-c116-4036-bbf1-109f8a7e50a7;[~accountid:712020:c6679159-6662-4054-9969-6e556eb0bd39] The decision what to do here isn’t up to me, but when fixing works that didn’t show comments due to this bug, the following was my experience:

I encountered two different groups of broken comments:

# The thread value is clearly bogus. The commentable and the parent (the chapter) is deleted. These were the most frequent case and the most obvious, because usually the comment text was something like “thanks for commenting”, so a reply by the author of the work. However, the thread value pointed towards a comment on a work not authored by that account. These are the comments that make it impossible to view comments on another unrelated work due to the bogus thread value (showing comments on works collects them by thread value, so it grabs the broken, unrelated comment and then errors on display).
## My conclusion for what happened there: The comments weren’t deleted when the work they were on was deleted. Likely because comment deletion happened in the wrong order (deleting parents before children) and if you try to delete the child then, it errors because the commentable is deleted. I suspect the thread value was bogus because the thread used to be stored differently (just a number that counts up instead of an id of another comment) and was possibly somehow missed by the migration that was meant to fix those values (maybe because the parent or commentable was already deleted).
## My fix for these comments: Delete them. The parent they were meant to be on is gone anyway, ergo they should be gone (deleting a parent deletes its comments). There would be no correct place to put them because the comment the thread value points to was always clearly the wrong place.
# The thread value is not clearly bogus (the comment it points to is deleted, so I don’t know enough to come to a conclusion). The commentable and the parent is deleted. These don’t cause issues with unrelated works, they only error on CommentsController#show.
## My conclusion for what happened there: The comments weren’t deleted when the work they were on was deleted. Likely because comment deletion happened in the wrong order (deleting parents before children) and if you try to delete the child then, it errors because the commentable is deleted.
## My fix for these comments: Do nothing. They could be deleted since there is no reason for them to exist when the parent is gone, but it didn’t seem worth my time to fix these when they only affect comments on works that are already gone, so you’re less likely to come across them naturally.
## The sentry events I linked are a comment from this group.

I never encountered comments broken in this way where the parent was still a valid parent. However, this may have been for lack of looking, not for lack of existing, since I only really cared about the first group of comments.

Tag Options

If you want to limit the tags that users can choose from when signing up, you can either use an existing tag set, make one of your own, or use a combination of the two. Once you have the tag sets you want to use ready, you can add them to your Prompt Meme.

Tag sets should only be used where you want users to have a choice. If you're running a Prompt Meme for a specific relationship or character, set that kind of tag to 0 tags required/allowed instead.

The same group of tag sets is used for both requests and offers, since otherwise offers and requests can't match against each other. People can choose different tags in their requests and offers, but they have to choose from the same set.

You don’t have to specify tags for every kind of tag you have allowed. For instance, if you only add fandom tags to your tag set, participants will be able to choose any canonical character or relationship within those fandoms while signing up.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. General

When Policy & Abuse bans a user for spam, they are shown an overview of the user's works and comments. They would like:

* to be able to see this same information without banning the user (and without risk of mass deleting)
* “Comment on [title]” to link to the comment, not the commentable

Additionally, for easier navigation between user administration pages and user pages, admins would like:

* the dashboard shown on user administration pages
* user dashboards, pseud dashboards, and user profiles to link to the user administration page
**  and as long as I’m doing that, the user’s Invitations page (because the link is already there for the user)

Note: Attached images show the PAC/super admin view of pages.

h1. Testing

h2. Terms/Example URLs

* User Administration page: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/users/USERNAME|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/users/USERNAME/]
* User Creations page: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/users/USERNAME/creations|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/users/USERNAME/creations]
* User dashboard: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME]
* Pseud dashboard: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/pseuds/PSEUDNAME|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/pseuds/PSEUDNAME]
* User profile: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/profile|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/profile]

h2. Admins with the {{open_doors}}, {{support}}, or {{tag_wrangling}} role

# should see a dashboard sidebar on User Administration pages 
# should not see a button-style “Profile” navigation link on User Administration pages (because the dashboard sidebar has it now)
# should not see a button-style “Creations” navigation link on User Administration pages
# should not be able to access User Creations pages by going directly to the URL
# should see button-style “Invitations” and “User Administration” links on user dashboards
# should see button-style “Invitations” and “User Administration” links on pseud dashboards
# should see button-style “Invitations” and “User Administration” links on user profiles

h2. Admins with the {{superadmin}} or {{policy_and_abuse}} role

# should see a dashboard sidebar on User Administration pages
# should not see a button-style “Profile” navigation link on User Administration pages (because the dashboard sidebar has it now)
# should see a button-style “Creations” navigation link on User Administration pages and be able to access User Creations pages by following it
# should see button-style “Invitations” and “User Administration” links on user dashboards
# should see button-style “Invitations” and “User Administration” links on pseud dashboards
# should see button-style “Invitations” and “User Administration” links on user profiles

When on the confirmation page for banning a user for spam, and on User Creation pages:

# should see a dashboard sidebar
# should see a paginated list of works, and following the pagination should return them to the top of the Works section
# should see a paginated list of comments, and following the pagination should return them to the top of the Comments section
# should see direct links to the comments in the format “Comment on the news post TITLE,” “Comment on the work TITLE,” “Comment on the tag NAME,” or “Comment on unknown item,” and following the links should lead to the correct comment. (Note: “Comment on unknown item” is for weird bugs like [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6531|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6531|smart-link].)

h2. Users and guests

# Logged out users should not see button-style “Invitations” and “User Administration” links on user dashboards, pseud dashboards, or user profiles
# Logged in users 
## should not see button-style “Invitations” and “User Administration” links on user dashboards, pseud dashboards, or user profiles they do not own
## should see button-style “Invitations” links on their own user dashboard, pseud dashboard, and user profile
## should not see button-style “User Administration” links on _any_ user dashboards, pseud dashboards, or user profiles, including their own

column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as User A
# Ensure your preferences are set to allow co-creator invitations
## Hi, username! → My Preferences
## If it’s not checked, check “Allow others to invite me to be a co-creator.” 
## Press Update
# Log out
# Log in as User B
# Post a work with a co-creator
## Post → New Work
## Fill in required information
## Check “Add co-creators?”
## Fill in the name of User A
## Press Post
# Log out
# Log in as User A
# Approve the co-creator request you received from User B in Step 5e
## Hi, username! → My Dashboard → Co-Creator Requests
## Check the “Selected?” checkbox for the relevant request
## Press Accept
# Add another chapter to the work you just accepted the co-creator request for
## Access the work (you can use the link in the success message)
## Follow the Add Chapter link
## For “Current co-creators,” check the name of User B
## Fill in some text
## Press Post
# Log out
# Log in as a policy_and_abuse or superadmin
# Go to the user administration page for User A either by going directly to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/users/USERNAME|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/users/USERNAME] or by
## Manage Users → Find Users
## Enter User A in the Name field
## For Search settings, check Exact Match Only
## Press Find
## Follow the Details link
# Ban the user
## Choose “Suspend permanently (ban user)”
## Write something in the Notes field
## Press Update
# Log out
# Log in as User A
# Access the multichapter work you share with user B
# Try to follow the Edit or Edit Chapter links on your work because you want to orphan the work, delete the work or chapter, or remove yourself as a work or chapter co-creator

h1. What happens

You are redirected to your dash with an error message telling you you cannot add or edit content.

For a chapter, you can currently delete it by going directly to the deletion confirmation page: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/000/chapters/000/confirm_delete|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/000/chapters/000/confirm_delete]

You can also currently orphan a work by going directly to the orphan confirmation page: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/orphans/new?work_id=000|https://test.archiveofourown.org/orphans/new?work_id=000]. 

h1. What should happen

You should be able to access the edit page for your work and then:

* follow the Delete Work link to delete your work
* follow the Orphan Work link to orphan your work
* if the work is co-created, follow the Remove Me As Co-Creator link to remove yourself from the work

Or for your chapter, you should be able to access the edit page and then:

* follow the Delete Chapter link to delete your chapter
* if the chapter is co-created, follow the Remove Me As Chapter Co-Creator link to remove yourself from the chapter

You should get the error message about adding or editing content if you attempt to:

* Post or Preview changes to your work or chapter 
* Add Chapter
* Manage Chapters

[Where a work creator would have an Edit Chapter link|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/f7cd4fc80c1482e12d216422759b3eee670b45fb/app/views/chapters/_chapter.html.erb#L16-L18] above chapter titles in both Entire Work and Chapter-by-Chapter modes, authorized admins should have a Delete Chapter link. It should have the same teal bottom border as the [other admin options|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/views/admin/_admin_options.html.erb] (e.g., Delete Work).

Deleting a chapter should be [logged in Admin Activities|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/f7cd4fc80c1482e12d216422759b3eee670b45fb/app/controllers/admin/user_creations_controller.rb#L53]. The Target should be the chapter, and the Summary, accessible by following the link in the Date column, should include info like: {{#<Chapter id: 3571050, content: [FILTERED], position: 2, work_id: 1677716, created_at: \"2023-06-15 05:25:49.000000000 +0000\", updated_at: \"2023-06-15 05:25:49.000000000 +0000\", posted: true, title: \"\", notes: \"\", summary: \"\", word_count: 3, hidden_by_admin: false, published_at: \"2023-06-15\", endnotes: \"\", content_sanitizer_version: [FILTERED], notes_sanitizer_version: 3, summary_sanitizer_version: 3, endnotes_sanitizer_version: 3>}} (NB: This is a test chapter from my dev enviornment, not someone else's real data.)

An email should be sent to each creator of the work (not chapter). The email should contain HTML and txt attachments of the chapter, including the title, summary, and beginning and end notes, as well as the chapter text.

{quote}[AO3] A chapter of your work has been deleted by an admin

Dear [fancy style]username[/fancy style],

[fancy style]Chapter #: Chapter Title[/fancy] of your work [link]Work Title[/link] was deleted from the Archive by a site admin.

If it's possible this chapter of your work violated the Archive's Terms of Service, please [link]contact our Policy & Abuse team[/link].

column1: Include user_role and comment_type in data sent to Akismet
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
We don’t include {{comment_type: "contact-form"}} in the support ticket data we send to the spam checker, which means it gets mixed in with comment data.

Let’s add it to the [akismet_attributes|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/754e816d0e1730d51dada5c6650cdc4db00717f2/app/models/feedback.rb#L25-L34] for support tickets, like we have it [in abuse reports|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/754e816d0e1730d51dada5c6650cdc4db00717f2/app/models/abuse_report.rb#L30].

redsummernight also suggested adding a {{comment_type}} to the comments we check. Let’s use {{comment}} for admin post comments (because Akismet assumes {{comment}} means “blog post comment,” and an admin post is pretty similar to a blog post) and {{fanwork-comment}} for comments on works.

The Akismet team also wouldn’t mind having {{user_role}} data:

* works should have {{user_role: "user"}}
* comments should have {{user_role: "guest"}} 
* abuse and support tickets should have {{user_role: "guest"}} for guest and {{user_role: "user-with-nonmatching-email"}} for logged-in users with emails that don't match their account emails.

*Testing*

Make sure you can submit both support and abuse ticket as a guest and a logged-in user with an email that doesn’t match the one associated with your account, post a work, and leave comments on both works and admin posts as a guest.

column1: Error 500 for long CSS entries in skin editor
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
*Steps to reproduce* 

# Log in
# Go to the skin editor, creating a site or work skin. 
# Enter CSS in the CSS field that is more than 65 000 characters
# Enter a name
# Submit the form
# Get an Error 500

*What should happen*

* I should be redirected to the page with an error message saying that the CSS is too long. 
* It would be helpful to have JavaScript validation to stop the user from hitting beyond 60 000 characters (This is to account for created spaces from sanitization)

*Notes from AD&T*

* There actually is a a limit to how many characters skins can have in the code (500k, or ArchiveConfig.CONTENT_MAX) that should give an error when your skin hits that length... but I guess the 500 error is probably happening because the CSS sanitizer just can't handle something that long?
* We'll need a buffer between the displayed limit and the real limit, because the sanitizer can add spaces (maybe make the displayed limit 60k and the real one 65k?) so if you're taking them out to make room because you're almost at the limit... yeah, it's just going to add them back and you'll hit the limit anyway
* We might need a news post or something to make sure people whose skins are too long (i.e., because the sanitizer didn't always error at this specific length, or because they're in the no man's land between the new limit we set to keep people from running into the 500 error and the number that actually causes the 500 error) don't lose part of their skin the next time they try to save
* The ideal fix would be to find the cause of the 500 error, keep the ArchiveConfig.CONTENT_MAX limit instead of lowering it, and add a display counter (with a buffer, like we do works, so actually CONTENT_MAX: 510000 and CONTENT_MAX_DISPLAYED: 500000)

*Deploy notes*

column1: "Log In" link in header doesn't have required ARIA role
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The  {{p}} with the Log In link has an ARIA role of {{menu}}. This role requires that its children have the role {{menuitem}}, so screen readers know how to interpret the structure of the HTML. ([https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.1/#menu|https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.1/#menu|smart-link] )

However, the link that is the direct child of the paragraph doesn’t have any roles.

Suggested solution: add the role {{menuitem}} to the Log In link.

How to test:

* Manually: use a screen reader to visit the Archive while not logged in. Check that the Log In menu is announced correctly.
* Automatically: I use the axe tools plugin (free). Install the plugin, open Developer Tools, use axe tools to scan the page for issues. There should be no issue affecting the login link element.

column1: The list of media on the homepage doesn't have required ARIA role
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Visit the home page while logged out, or logged in if you don’t have any favorite tags, so you get the list of media under the “Find your favorites” heading.

Scan the page with an automated accessibility tool like axe DevTools.

axe DevTools reports a “critical” issue, which is that the list with the role {{menu}} doesn’t have required children.

Elements with the role {{menu}} must have direct children with the role {{menuitem}}. (Or a few other roles like {{menuitemcheckbox}}, but I’m only giving the one relevant to this menu.)

The {{li}} elements don’t have a role.

However, Sarken rightly pointed out that the list shouldn’t be a menu in the first place, but a navigation.

Let’s change it into a navigation - but if we just replace the role on the {{ul}}, we’ll have a similar ARIA role mismatch issue, where it will complain that the {{li}}s don’t have an appropriate parent.

The solution seems to be to have a container {{div}} around the {{ul}}, and apply the navigation role to the container. The {{ul}} and its children shouldn’t have a role declaration.

How to test:

* with a screenreader, presumably that the navigation is announced properly and it makes sense
* with an a11y tool checker, that it doesn’t report any brokenness

Other concerns:

* does this change impact any site skins?

*Deploy notes*

Has CSS changes.

# In the Characters field, enter a tag in both English and Hebrew, e.g., {{עופר שכטר - Character}}

In Chrome, Safari, and Edge, the Hebrew part of the character tag displays to the left of the relationship tag, while the English part displays to the right of it. (This issue does not occur in Firefox 114.)

Let’s delete the patch, since it’s no longer necessary. No manual QA required.

column1: Remove the fetch_admin_settings hook, and change code that uses @admin_settings to use AdminSetting.current instead
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The {{fetch_admin_settings}} hook is [skipped|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ba94c04580de2bac4c7a932e33a11fad4de7e06d/app/controllers/application_controller.rb#L523-L528] for JS and JSON requests. However, occasionally there are JS or JSON requests for pages that don’t have a JS or JSON view, like the homepage. This results in an error where the views are expecting the admin {{@admin_settings}} variable to set, when it’s not. This produces a 500 error.

This can be addressed by switching over to using {{AdminSetting.current}} instead of {{@admin_settings}} everywhere. This won’t actually prevent the mismatches, in cases where e.g. a JS action should be returning an error instead of redirecting to an HTML version of the homepage, but it’s nice to reduce 500 errors.

Note that, in cases where {{@admin_settings}} is accessed multiple times in quick succession, this won’t result in multiple memcached reads, because Rails' {{MemCacheStore}} maintains a [local cache|https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveSupport/Cache/Strategy/LocalCache.html] when performing a single request.

We need to update sanitize due to a vulnerability:

{quote}[CVE-2023-36823|https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f5ww-cq3m-q3g7]: Fixed an HTML+CSS sanitization bypass that could allow XSS (cross-site scripting). This issue affects Sanitize versions 3.0.0 through 6.0.1.

When using Sanitize's relaxed config or a custom config that allows {{<style>}} elements and one or more CSS at-rules, carefully crafted input could be used to sneak arbitrary HTML through Sanitize.

See the following security advisory for additional details: [GHSA-f5ww-cq3m-q3g7|https://github.com/rgrove/sanitize/security/advisories/GHSA-f5ww-cq3m-q3g7]{quote}

ticking instant has started [a branch|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/compare/master...tickinginstant:otwarchive:noodling-admin-user-search-past] and notes that, if she is unavailable when we’re ready, the coder who claims this issue is welcome to use as much or little as they like. h1. Deploy

Workers need to be restarted first. Then, this ticket has an associated rake task (only run this once!)

{noformat}rake search:index_admin_users{noformat}

h1. Find Users

{{https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/users}}

!find_users.png|width=100%,alt="Find users form, altered to include the new 'Include past usernames and emails' checkbox and remove 'Exact match only'"!

The new search will perform exact matches by default, but allow wildcard queries with {{*}}, the way you can do, e.g., when searching by Author/Artist in Work Search. 

The “Exact match only” checkbox will be removed from “Search settings.”

We’d also like to include past usernames and emails in the indexed document. We can do this by reading from audits.

Note that [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6483|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6483|smart-link] nominally blocks this, but it is not necessary to wait for 6483 to be completed. Instead, it can be fixed by doing part of that issue: adding {{BCrypt::Password}} to {{config.active_record.yaml_column_permitted_classes}}.

To prevent confusion and unexpected results, searching past usernames and emails will be optional, enabled using a new “Include past usernames and emails” checkbox under “Search settings.”

h1. User Administration

{{https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/users/USERNAME}}

!user_information.png|width=100%,alt="User Information section including 'Past usernames' and 'Past email'"!



Past emails and usernames will be shown in comma-separated lists in the User Information section of User Administration pages.

Past usernames are already available in the User History table, but including them at the top will make them easier to find at a glance.

column1: Define the translate_string function using % instead of I18n.translate
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Currently, the {{translate_string}} function is defined as follows:

{code:ruby}    def translate_string(str, **options)
      translate(str, **options.merge(default: str))
    end{code}

But it would be simpler (and probably faster) to define it as {{str % options}} instead, so that the i18n-related gems don’t end up having to go through the normal process of looking up the translation key and discovering that it doesn’t exist before doing the desired formatting.

column1: Enable Admins to Mark Canonical Tags So They Appear in the Filtering Autocomplete but NOT the Work Form Autocomplete
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
While some metatags are useful for filtering in tag search, their usefulness is limited specifically because their appearance in the work form autocomplete causes an increase in ambiguity issues. As such, we were wondering whether it would be possible to create a field on the tag edit page which allowed tag wrangling admins to mark a tag so it would not appear in the work form autocomplete whilst still appearing in the filtering autocomplete? 

(I understand folks would still be able to tag for it there as folks can tag for any ol' tag there, but removing it from the autocomplete database for the work form specifically would keep it from being chosen just because it happened to pop up.)
column149: 07/Aug/23 4:11 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;Claiming this so no one works on it until it’s been discussed.
column150:

*  would be more feasible if we used Elasticsearch for autocomplete
* but we use Redis
* so our current less-than-ideal ideas are
** duplicate the tag autocomplete data, which comes with the obvious downsides of duplicating data
** use the tag autocomplete score as a hack
*** score them low so they are less likely to appear in the autocomplete
*** give them a specific score and exclude tags with that score when doing the lookup on the posting form

# Log in and ensure you have inbox comments enabled
## Hi, username! > My Preferences

# Post a work with moderated comments
## Post > New Work

## Post

# Go back to the browser or window where you are logged in as the work creator and refresh the page

## Press Approve
# Check your inbox

column30:
[/user_mailer/_work_info.text.erb|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/views/user_mailer/_work_info.text.erb], [/user_mailer/_work_info.html.erb|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/views/user_mailer/_work_info.html.erb], and the helpers they use to determine things like whether the gift email should say “Fandoms: Fandom A and Fandom B” or “Fandom: Fandom A” use the work’s tag associations rather than tag strings, which creates more work for the database.

We’d like to use the strings here so the database doesn’t keel over when we start using the work_info partials in subscription emails (AO3-4309). 

And because the pull request for [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4309|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4309|smart-link] is a big one, we’d like to do this as a separate pull request so the _reviewers_ don’t keel over.

*Testing*

Assuming you have access to someone’s email, since you need to check the email notification:

* Give someone a gift work tagged with one fandom, character, rating, freeform, warning, and relationship, and ensure the label text for the tag type is singular (i.e., “Character:” rather than “Characters:”) and, in the HTML email, bold and red. The fandom should also be linked in the HTML email.
* Give someone a gift work tagged with more than one fandom, character, rating, freeform, warning, and relationship, and ensure the label text for the tag type is plural (i.e., “Relationships:” rather than “Relationship:”) and, in the HTML email, bold and red. The fandoms should also be linked and written as “Fandom A, Fandom B, and Fandom C” or “Fandom A and Fandom B” in the HTML email.
** [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6533|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6533] has instructions for adding multiple ratings to a work

column1: Give admins options when hiding works
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. *Overview* This issue is the first in a series of updates designed to streamline the Policy & Abuse team's processes, link admin records with Zoho tickets, declutter the user admin page, and remove access to user account status options from admin roles that don't need them. To lay the groundwork for these updates, a separate "Policy & Abuse: Action Users" form should be created that allows PAC admins to take action against a user's account and hide any works that need to be hidden simultaneously. This is complicated by three factors:  # Users may have multiple works that need to be hidden; 10+ is not unusual, and some users may need dozens hidden # Some of the works may have co-creators, who may also have additional violating works separate from the first creator # When there are multiple users being actioned, those users may have differing histories and so receive differing penalties  To accommodate this, a two-page action process is needed to allow the actioning of multiple works and users at once: # The "Policy & Abuse: Mass Action Setup" page (henceforth in this issue referred to as just the "Mass Action Setup" page), which is a form where the admin enters a list of works to be hidden and/or a list of account names that they are actioning # The "Policy & Abuse: Action Users" page (henceforth in this issue referred to as just the "Action Users" page), which is a form (created by the input into the Mass Action Setup form) where the admin specifies the individual actions applied to each account, the individual reasons for each user to be actioned, and confirms the list of all works to be hidden. The accounts displayed on this form are determined by what was entered on the Mass Action Setup form.  The Mass Action Setup form should be accessible from the admin navigation bar, as a new option on the "Manage Users" menu. This navigation option, the Mass Action Setup page, and the Action Users page should only be accessible to admins with the {{policy_and_abuse}} or {{superadmin}} roles.  h1. Mass Action Setup page Example mockup of the Mass Action Setup page:  !AD_4nXc9ReZWhz7eFCDSUxhUNXW-z7WUTncbtgjLGy5UommfTo1s9HyoVU70Wk7uey8dFI2eXtxFw9CBnmGyGPIqSBqlFj_OnaHCE6C0iys-YYQ0GRKp-HSWD08E1LhlcSy3iDL4-YcvxQ_key=XPh-Ir_561mY6U5syTSOv5wb|width=875,height=661! The Mass Action Setup form should have two entry fields:  # Works to hide: allows the admin to enter the work URLs for those works to be hidden, as a text list separated by line breaks. Locating the work ID on each line should key off of {{/works/00000}}, where 00000 is the work ID. Lines may include extraneous other text on the same line (such as whitespace, title or author), which should be ignored –  the important info is the work ID. E.g.: [+https://archiveofourown.org/works/1234567+|https://archiveofourown.org/works/1234567] [+https://archiveofourown.org/works/9876543/+|https://archiveofourown.org/works/9876543/]  "Example work title", located at [+https://archiveofourown.org/works/1234567+ |https://archiveofourown.org/works/1234567/] "Example work title", located at [+https://archiveofourown.org/works/1234567/chapters/987654321/+|https://archiveofourown.org/works/1234567/chapters/987654321/]  # Users to action: allows the admin to enter usernames of users to action, as a text list separated by line breaks. Whitespace on either side of an entered username should be ignored. When the admin clicks the "Proceed to Action Users form" button, the form should:  # Validate works:  #* For each line, locate the work ID on the line, ignoring any irrelevant text #* Ignore any empty lines  #* Verify that each work in the "Works to hide" field is an existing work or draft on AO3  #* Check that each work is not already hidden #* Remove any duplicate entries #* If there is an invalid URL, the submission should fail and an error message should be provided stating that there is an invalid work entry and what it is # Validate additional users:  #* For each line, remove any whitespace around the username  #* Ignore any empty lines #* Verify that each username listed is a user on AO3 #* If there is an invalid username, the submission should fail and an error message should be provided stating that there is an invalid username and what it is # Generate a list of "users to action", consisting of:  #* Each user who is a creator on one or more of the works in the validated "Works to Hide" list (excluding the orphan_account), AND #* Any accounts listed in the validated "Users without works to hide" list, even if they're not a creator on one of the listed works  # Remove any duplicate entries from the "users to action" list (whether from being listed twice in the "Additional users" list, or appearing in both the "works to hide" and "additional users" lists, etc)  # Remove the orphan_account from the "users to action" list, if present # Create the "Action Users" form with the validated "Works to hide" list as the works list, and a user subsection for each user on the "user to action" list  If both the "Works to hide" and "Users to action" fields are blank, then the submission should fail with an error message saying that at least one valid work or user must be listed to proceed.  Please consider- In future issues, this tool may be expanded from hiding works only to also being able to hide series and bookmarks. However, for now the scope is works only.  Rough HTML for the Mass Action Setup page for ease of reference; please note that labels and inputs are not properly associated here: {noformat}

Policy & Abuse: Mass Action Setup

All works and users being actioned must belong to the same ticket.

Works to hide

List the full URLs of all works you wish to hide, separated by line breaks.

Users to action

List the current usernames (not pseuds) of users you wish to action, separated by line breaks. You don't need to list the creators of the works you are hiding, as they will be included automatically.

{noformat} h1. Action Users page An example of the page when multiple works, one of which has multiple creators, have been added to the form to be hidden: !AD_4nXccxSthK24iH1-z-szQ7kDx-IaLo6SrsIfVyEhpZIXuS2LnJX1rnOj-szP5aeCbXYgCIeHp2tErkmd5lYqaSkmbXfW4wPMyNGq2YWSv56yagWoCAAmdc5D5CpSznNIXk_7pKyQa_key=XPh-Ir_561mY6U5syTSOv5wb|width=952,height=1207! On this page the admin can perform a variety of actions: # Enter the ID of a ticket with the initial complaint to confirm hiding the work(s) or taking action against the account(s), the same way admins enter ticket IDs to confirm profile edits # For each account, record a note, warning, or suspension on the user's account, along with a reason.  The Ticket ID (of the original complaint), action (for each user), and reason (for each user) are required fields. If any of these is empty, then it should not be possible to submit the form with the "Preview emails" or "Take action and hide work(s)" buttons; instead, attempting to do so should fail and a red error message should pop up beside each unfilled field reminding the admin that it is a required field. The Ticket ID should be validated upon form submission (by either the "Preview emails" button or the "Take action and hide work(s)" button), in the same manner that ticket IDs are validated for profile edits. If it fails, then the submission should fail and an error message should appear at the top of the form, using the same set of error messages as for failed ticket IDs for profile edits. Each work on the "Work(s) to be hidden" list should display on its own line as: {quote}*TITLE* by UserA, UserB, UserC{quote} where *TITLE* is a link to the work. Creators should be listed with usernames only, not in the "pseud (username)" format. No method is provided (in this stage) to add or remove a work from the form; if that is necessary the admin would need to start over with the Mass Action Setup form. The order of the works listed should match to the order the works were entered on the Mass Action Setup page. If the orphan_account is listed as a creator on the work then they should be listed in this byline, even though they should not have their own user subsection below on the form.  If all of the works to be hidden are orphaned, then only the Hide Works section will display and there will be no User sections below it. Each user subsection should be titled "User: Username (userID)" where the username is a link leading to that user's admin page (that is, [+https://archiveofourown.org/admin/users/username+|https://archiveofourown.org/admin/users/username]).  The "Action on User" options should be present with the same logic that the current User Admin page has for "Warnings and Suspensions": * If a user is temporarily suspended, then the option to temporarily suspend becomes "Lift temporary suspension, effective immediately." * If a user is permanently suspended, then the option to suspend the user permanently becomes "Lift permanent suspension, effective immediately." and the option to temporarily suspend them is disabled * If a user is first temporarily suspended and then permanently suspended, then it should be possible to lift either suspension state without affecting the other  * Unlike the current User Admin page, there should _not_ be a spamban option Unlike the "Notes" box on the User Admin page, the "Reason for actioning user" should be a text input, one line high, not a textarea.  Form validation upon submitting via either the "Preview emails" or "Take action and hide work(s)" buttons should include:  * Re-validating the works list:  ** If a work URL is no longer for a valid work or draft (because it has been deleted or expired in the time since the list was generated), then the submission should fail with an error message identifying that "Work 000 does not exist" (where 000 is the work ID). The admin will need to manually return to the Mass Action Setup page to change the work list – they should not be automatically redirected from the Action Users page. ** If a work URL is for a work that is already hidden, then the submission should fail with an error message identifying that "Work 000 is already hidden". The admin will need to return to the Mass Action Setup page to change the work list. * Re-validating the users list:  ** If a user has deleted their account, then the submission should fail with an error message that "User ID USERID no longer exists". The admin will need to return to the Mass Action Setup page to recreate the users list.  ** If a user has changed their username, then the submission should fail with an error message that "User OLDNAME (USERID) has updated their username to NEWNAME. The form has been updated." The user subsection for that user should update and change the username to match the new name. All of the information the admin has entered on the Action Users form should be retained on the updated form. ** Because users can rename or delete their accounts between the submission of the Mass Action Setup form and the Action Users form, the Action Users form's setup should track users by (and validation should occur based on) their userID, not their username or a pseud. The "Preview emails" page should validate the form information and then provide a single-page preview with the works list at the top (formatted in the same way it is on the Action Users form), and then the actions, reasons, and emails for each user.  This is a "dumb" previews page only – there should not be any way to edit anything from here; the user only has the option to submit. However, if the admin back-buttons in their browser then they should be taken back to the filled-out Action Users form, and once there they should be able to edit if needed and then resubmit, rather than starting over entirely from the beginning.  Each user subsection on the Preview Emails page should be titled the same way it is on the Action Users form, as "User: Username (userID)". The username should be a hyperlink to the user's admin page.  Example:  {quote}*User:* [+*Testy*+|https://archiveofourown.org/admin/users/testy] *(6477)* 30-day suspension NFW (discord ad) [Email preview]{quote} The email preview should be for the body of the email only. It should not include any header information, subject line, to/from, etc.  The descriptions for each type of action available on the form should be:  Noted Warned X-day suspension Temporary suspension lifted Permanent suspension Permanent suspension lifted At the bottom of the preview page, there should be the option to return to the Action Users page to edit, or to "Take action and hide work(s)". When the emails are generated, they will include the list of works specific to that user. For example, if the "Works being hidden" list is as follows:  {quote}*TITLE1* by UserA *TITLE2* by UserA, UserB{quote} then UserA's email notification will list both TITLE1 and TITLE2, but UserB's email notification will only list TITLE2.  The order of the works listed in the email should match to the order the works were entered on the Mass Action Setup page. If a user does not have any works to be hidden, then they will not receive an email. They should still have a section on the preview page, which should contain a note saying they will not receive an email. For example:  {quote}*User:* [+*Testy*+|https://archiveofourown.org/admin/users/testy] *(6477)* 30-day suspension NFW (discord ad), user orphaned No email {quote} If all of the works to be hidden are orphaned, then there should be no emails or user sections on the Preview Emails page, but it should still display the works list. All of the validations performed if the "Take action and hide work(s)" button was used on the "Action Users" page should also be performed if "Take action and hide work(s)" is used from the Preview Emails page. If the validations fail, then the admin should be returned to the "Action Users" form, with the form still filled-out, and with appropriate error messages displaying to indicate what failed. Successfully submitting with the "Take action and hide work(s)" button (whether from the Preview Emails page or directly from the Action Users form) will:  # apply the appropriate action(s) to the user account(s),  # record the note(s), warning(s), and suspension(s) in the user history, # hide the work(s),  # log the admin activities,  # send the appropriate email(s), and # take the admin to the Mass Action Setup page, with the form cleared, and a blue success banner at the top saying "Policy & Abuse enforcement action successfully taken". If the process fails midway, then it should not proceed with the remaining actions. Instead, it should go to the Action Users page (with all of the fields still filled out) and put up an error banner at the top stating that the process failed midway. The admin will then need to investigate to see what failed before trying again.  If the admin closes the Mass Action Setup form, the Action Users form, or the Preview Emails page without submitting (e.g. by closing the tab), then it should act the same as if there was a "Cancel" button on these pages – nothing should be changed on any user accounts or works, nothing logged, and the data entered should be discarded. Future updates in this series of issues will allow PAC to use the Action Users page to update the works to hide list, specify different types of pre-generated emails, as well as send custom messages (similar to comment notification emails). Please ensure that the design for this issue will not cause difficulties for this future expansion.  Rough HTML for the Action Users page for ease of reference; please note that labels and inputs are not properly associated here: {noformat}

Policy & Abuse: Action Users

* Required information

Ticket ID
Ticket ID*

This is the main ticket with the original complaint.

Hide Works

Work(s) to be hidden:

This is a nonfanwork, by UserA

This is also a nonfanwork, by UserA, UserB

User: UserA (3216541)

Action on UserA*
Action on UserA
Reason for actioning UserA*

User: UserB (3216542)

{noformat} h1. *'Hide Work' button* There should be no changes to the current "Hide Work" button behavior present on works (that will be covered in a future issue). h1. *User Admin Page* There should be no changes to the current options on user admin pages (that will be covered in a future issue).  The date and activity (note, warning, or suspension) should be logged in the User History table. When the Action Users form is used to apply a note, warning, or suspension, the information in the "Details" field should be updated to contain:  * The ticket number of the initial complaint ("Ticket ID"), linked to the Zoho ticket * The admin account name * The "reason for action" provided for that user Example details field:  {quote}[+#123456+|http://zohoticketurlhere] (admin-Testy): NFW, user deleted {quote} h1. *Admin Activity Log* The date, admin, activity, and target should be logged for each work as usual. The summary should contain the ticket number of the initial complaint, linked to the Zoho ticket (in the same way that profile edits link to the Zoho ticket). h1. *Emails* If a user is having any works hidden, then they should receive the same email that is sent when the "Hide Work" button is pressed: {{admin_hidden_work_notification}}. Note: this mailer first needs to be updated to allow hiding multiple works at once, see [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6970|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6970|smart-link] h1. *Testing* * Some users have several dozen works that are in violation. The number of works that would be most useful to test for large numbers of hidden works should be determined and tested * Test behavior when the orphan_account is one of the creators as well as the sole creator * If all works listed are orphaned, should still be able to mass-hide the works * Test behavior when users delete works or accounts mid-process * Test behavior when users publish draft works mid-process  * Test behavior when users change a work title or delete a chapter mid-process * Test behavior when users rename their accounts mid-process * Test behavior when the same account is listed twice as the creator of the work (due to it appearing under multiple pseuds) * Test behavior when users on the same form are receiving different kinds of penalties  * Test behavior when users on the same form have different numbers of works, including a user with no works

column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as an admin with the {{open_doors}} or {{support}} role
# Manage Users > Find Users
# Enter some search criteria in the fields, e.g., fill in “Name” with “testy”
# Press “Find”

h1. What happens

In the results table, you can check the “Archivist” and “Opendoors” checkboxes for a user (if you are an {{open_doors}} admin) or none (if you are a {{support}} admin), but you cannot check the “No Resets” box.

column1: Optimize the database query for the series count in the user sidebar
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Currently, there are a couple of problems with [the series count in the user sidebar|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/0f30207d6dfe9050d38398522339f1a0d754c58c/app/helpers/users_helper.rb#L82-L100]:

# It calls {{length}} to compute the number of series. This results in all series owned by that user being loaded, which can take a long time for users like the {{orphan_account}}. The reason it does this is because the {{exclude_anonymous}} scope is rather complex, with a join on the works table and a group, so calling {{count}} returns a hash instead of a number. But you can call {{count.size}} instead of {{length}} to get the true number.
# The scope that it uses, {{for_pseuds(user.pseuds)}}, means that the SQL query includes a list of all of the user’s pseud IDs. This is fine for most users, but not great for {{orphan_account}}, with its 10,000+ pseuds. It would probably be better to do a join on the pseuds table.

Let’s try to fix this, so that viewing {{orphan_account}}’s various pages is a little easier on the database.

We are sending out 1 invitations per day.” This should be pluralized correctly using Rails i18n so it says, “There is currently 1 person on the waiting list” or “There are currently 2 people on the waiting list.”

column1: Switch to reviewdog for running rubocop
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Hound, our current tool, is several versions of rubocop out-of-date, and also does not support custom cops (which would be useful for catching common issues like needing to use {{departure}} for large tables). We already use reviewdog for running ERB lint, so let’s use that for running rubocop as well.

Here’s a draft of what the new Github action workflow could look like:

{code:yaml}  rubocop:
    name: Rubocop
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Set up Ruby and run bundle install
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
        with:
          bundler-cache: true

      - name: rubocop
        uses: reviewdog/action-rubocop@e70b014b8062c447d6b515ee0209f834ea93e696
        with:
          use_bundler: true
          reporter: github-pr-check
          rubocop_version: gemfile
          rubocop_extensions: rubocop-rails:gemfile rubocop-rspec:gemfile{code}

h1. Testing Instructions

After this is merged, update an existing PR (or create a new one). Ideally this would be one that has known Rubocop violations, but that shouldn’t be required.

h1. Post-Merge Actions

A senior AD&T member will need to do the following once this is merged:

# -Go into the Hound console and disable/remove the otwarchive project. This will avoid duplicate checks, and errors when we upgrade rubocop or introduce custom cops.- (This won’t be done until we migrate JS linting away also.)
# Authorize the {{reviewdog/action-rubocop@e70b014b8062c447d6b515ee0209f834ea93e696}} action via the Github repo’s settings. (Refer to the linked issue for details.)

column1: Allow users to resend invitations
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30: h1. Description Users frequently submit support requests because they have accidentally deleted or not received their invitations. Therefore, we’d like to allow users to resend their invitations without submitting a support ticket. (In the case of missing emails, it’s fairly likely the resent email will continue to be eaten by spam filters, but it’s possible some will get through.) To prevent spam, there should be a configurable limit on how soon you can resend an invitation ({{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}). It should start off at 24 hours. Resending an invitation should not alter the invitation’s {{sent_at}}, because we sometimes need this information. It should be tracked separately as {{resent_at}}. This information should be available to admins on pages where the [invitation partial|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/views/invitations/_invitation.html.erb] is used, e.g., {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/invitations/###}}, where it can be added below the existing “Sent at” info as “Last resent at.” Users can currently check the status of their invitations by entering their email address on [https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status|https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status]. We’d like to add the resend option to this page. *If the user checks the status of their invitation less than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is initially sent*, the resend option should not be present. The text should say: {quote}Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there. If it has been more than [{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}] hours since you should have received your invitation, but you have not received it after checking your spam folder, you can visit this page to resend the invitation.{quote} *If the user checks the status of their invitation more than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is initially sent*, the resend option should be present. The text should say: {quote}Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there. Because your invitation was sent more than 24 hours ago, you can have your invitation resent. [button reading: Resend Invitation]{quote} *If the user checks the status of their invitation less than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is resent*, the resend option should not be present. The text should say: {quote}Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date] and resent on [resent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there. If it has been more than [{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}] hours since you should have received your invitation, but you have not received it after checking your spam folder, you can visit this page to resend the invitation.{quote} *If the user checks the status of their invitation more than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is resent*, the resend option should be present, and there should be a suggestion to contact Support. The text should say: {quote}Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date] and resent on [resent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there. Because your invitation was resent more than 24 hours ago, you can have your invitation resent again, or you may want to contact Support. [button reading: Resend Invitation]{quote} h1. Notes If you could fix it so the “Invitation status for email@example.com” heading is an {{h3}} when loaded on [https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status|https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status], that would be appreciated! (It should remain an {{h2}} when you have JavaScript disabled and it takes you to a separate page.) The problem seems to be the invitation has no {{sent_at}} date -- and we have a bunch with that problem on staging (I didn’t check production, but we can assume it’s a problem there as well):

{noformat}Invitation.unredeemed.from_queue.where("sent_at IS NULL").size

So. That’s fun, because that’s like 8 years of invitations that might be affected.

I don’t particularly want to write a version of each message that’s unique to invitations without sent_at data. So I think our options are

# give a “no results” response if there’s an invitation without a sent_at date
# or, if the sent_at date is nil for the found invitation, substitute the created_at or updated_at date,
# or make a rake task to find any invitations from_queue: true with nil sent_at dates, and set sent_at date to the created_at or updated_at date

But if Option 2 is a pain – and I think it might be, because I think we use the sent_at in the backend, not just the displayed text -- maybe we could sort of split the difference and go with an Option 4: limit the search to invitations created in the last year?

column1: Upgrade to Rails 7
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Let’s upgrade to Rails 7! (It feels like we just did a Rails upgrade 😆 ). From the release notes, some significant changes are:

* {{ActionView::Helpers::UrlHelper#button_to}} has been changed to use {{PATCH}} by default when passed an already-persisted object
* [Spring|https://github.com/rails/spring] is off by default
* Sprockets is now an _optional_ dependency (so if we need it, the gem needs to be specified explicitly in the Gemfile)
* Applications can now only run in {{zeitwerk}} mode (this should be fine since we switched as part of the Rails 6 upgrade)
* {{config.autoloader=}} has been deleted
* {{ActiveSupport::Dependencies}} private API has been deleted
* Autoloading during initialization is now an error, in contrast to being a deprecation warning in Rails 6.1
* {{ActionDispatch::Request#content_type}} now returns Content-Type header as it is.
* Key generator digest class changing to use SHA256
* Digest class for ActiveSupport::Digest changing to SHA256
* There is a new ActiveSupport::Cache serialization format
* Active Storage video preview image generation (requires ffmpeg v3.4+)
* Active Storage default variant processor changed to :vips

Of the above, the autoloading change definitely needs action before the upgrade. And as part of the upgrade, we should add code to convert legacy SHA1 things to SHA256 (there is an example in the upgrade guide). Requirements to upgrade, in broad strokes, are described in [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#upgrading-from-rails-6-1-to-rails-7-0|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#upgrading-from-rails-6-1-to-rails-7-0|smart-link] .

We also get some new features, which are described in [https://rubyonrails.org/2021/12/15/Rails-7-fulfilling-a-vision|https://rubyonrails.org/2021/12/15/Rails-7-fulfilling-a-vision|smart-link] .

column1: Avoid autoloading constants deprecation warning
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
In Rails 6, autoloading constants during initialization outside configuration blocks is deprecated and logs a warning at application boot. This will become an error in Rails 7 ([https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#autoloading-during-initialization|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#autoloading-during-initialization|smart-link] ), so we need to fix the warning before we can upgrade.

We currently have quite a few:

Some may be grouped together, so not a lot of changes may be necessary. Unfortunately, the warning is not very helpful, so adding {{pp caller_locations}} might be a good idea to track things down.

* When the application starts, no messages of {{DEPRECATION WARNING: Initialization autoloaded the constant}}appear in the log

The creatorship notification data used in our creatorship mailer previews (accessible via [https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers|https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers]) currently assumes the creatorship you’re being notified about is for a work:

{noformat}  def creatorship_notification_data
    first_creator = create(:user, login: "JayceHexmaster")
    second_creator = create(:user, login: "viktor_the_machine")
    work = create(:work, authors: [first_creator.default_pseud, second_creator.default_pseud])
    second_creatorship = Creatorship.find_by(creation: work, pseud: second_creator.default_pseud)
    [second_creatorship, first_creator]
  end{noformat}

Pages on narrow screens (eg, iPhone), if not refreshed, appear correctly in landscape mode. Only some pages are affect on both narrow and wide screen layouts.

* My Bookmarks (bottom “Sort & Filter” button on top of “Sort by” dropdown menu)

column150:
28/Sep/23 4:59 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;The problem seems to be heavily related to use of {{clear}}

* On the new work form, the problem isn’t the co-creators field (or the pseuds field, if you have multiple pseuds), but the notes field, which has moved out of its usual position at the bottom on the field set. Disabling {{clear: right}} for {{.notes}}? Fixes it.
* For Edit My Profile, disabling {{clear: right}} on {{.dashboard .landmark}} fixes the position of the Update button, but causes the form to shift down. Disabling {{clear: left}} on {{ul#skiplinks, .landmark, .landmark a, .index .heading.landmark}} brings the form back up to the expected position.
* On Change My Email, Edit Pseud, and Change My Password, disabling {{clear: right}} on {{.dashboard .landmark}} once again fixes the position of the button. However, the forms still overlap with the navigation buttons above them. Disabling {{clear: right}} on {{form}} then fixes that… however, toggling (i.e., disabling and then re-enabling) other things also fixes it. 🙄 
* On Change My User Name, disabling {{clear: right}} on {{.dashboard .landmark}} once again fixes the position of the button.
* The bookmarks page is a smidge more complicated, because disabling {{clear: right}} on {{.dashboard .landmark}} shifts everything down and that can’t be fixed with simply modifying the clear on {{form}}. However, just setting {{clear: both}} on the {{dt.landmark}} for the second submit button fixes the button position without breaking the rest of the page.

So with that last one in mind, I went back and revisited the other places where we have problems – all {{dt}} elements inside {{form}} elements with {{clear: right}}. 

Putting {{clear: both}} on all of them fixed the button position in every case.

For the Notes field, the {{dd}} required a {{clear: none}} in addition to the {{dt}} change. 

The forms that overlap the navigation also required clear: none on the {{form}}.

I don’t know if this is the fix, since it might have negative impact in other browsers (I haven’t tried yet), but it’s a direction to explore.

ETA: [Draft of a fix|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/compare/master...sarken:otwarchive:AO3-6616?expand=1]. It doesn’t look like it has any ill-effects in Firefox, but I want to play around with it a bit and clean it up.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Create a collection if you don’t already have one:
## Browse > Collections > New Collection
## Enter required information, making a note of the title and name you use
## Press Submit to create the collection
# Add a bookmark to your collection
## Navigate to a work, any work, e.g., the first one on Browse > Works
## Use the Bookmark button to open the bookmark form at the bottom of the work
## In “Add to collections,” start entering the title of the collection you created in the last step, and choose it from the autocomplete when it appears
## Press Create to create the bookmark
# Locate the bookmark on your Manage Collection Items page
## Hi, username! > My Collections (if it’s not there because it’s your first collection and the menu’s caching hasn’t updated, go to My Dashboard and choose Collections from the sidebar instead)
## Follow the Manage Collection Items button-style link
## Follow the Approved button-style link
## Locate the bookmark you created – it’ll have the title “Bookmark of [Title of Work You Bookmarked]”
## Press the corresponding “Details” button to reveal the blurb

h1. What happens

The Edit, Delete, Add To Collection, and Share options are there, and the Edit button doesn’t even work.

h1. What should happen

If you check a work blurb on this page, you’ll see it doesn’t have the equivalent owner navigation (Edit, Edit Tags, and Add Chapter). Ergo, the bookmark owner navigation shouldn’t be there either.

h1. Notes

This is also true if you’re looking at an item you own on the collection’s Manage Items page ( {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/COLLECTION_NAME/items?status=approved}})

column1: Kindle EPUB Table of Contents sometimes greyed out
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Find and access a multi-chapter work
# Download the EPUB
# Send it to your Kindle device via email (it’s unclear if this issue occurs on the app)
# Open it

h1. What happens

The built-in ToC only shows the preface and a greyed out Table of Contents, but not the actual list of chapters.

h1. What should happen

The built-in ToC should work!

h1. Notes

Some folks suggested that downloading the mobi and converting it to EPUB with Zamzar works just fine, so I took a look at the resulting file and did some thinking out loud in a Slack channel with Support chairs: 

----

The file from that site that reportedly works: {{<meta content="calibre (4.13.0)" name="dtb:generator"/>}}

The file from us: {{<meta name="dtb:generator" content="calibre (5.12.0)"/>}}

So if we're optimistic, _maybe_ it's a bug with our version. If we're pessimistic, newer versions of Calibre might just produce incompatible tables of content

I'm comparing the guts of the two files and the most notable differences to me are -- actually, let me back up and give some background. EPUBs are basically containers. Each chapter is a separate file inside the container, and you have a file for the TOC, and any images and stysheets and stuff. They're not special files, really -- the image is a JPG or whatever, the stylesheets are CSS, etc.

Now, the two big things I'm noticing are Zamzar's EPUB, converted from our MOBI files using calibre 4.13, uses .html extensions for the chapters, and the chapter names are like {{index_split_001.html}}.

_But_ the EPUB file straight from the Archive has .xhtml chapters, and the chapter names match the download file name. So my chapters are {{The Devils Right There_split_001.xhtml}} .

I wonder if Kindle chokes when it encounters the encoded spaces in the TOC

{noformat}    <navPoint id="uR7o4lGb4J2CSJToHLQAhNF" playOrder="2">
      <navLabel>
        <text>truth is like blood underneath your fingernails</text>
      </navLabel>
      <content src="The%20Devils%20Right%20There_split_002.xhtml"/>
    </navPoint>{noformat}

We could test that theory by having someone with a Kindle download the epub of a multichapter work with a one-word title and see if it worked

Looking a little more and the manifest seems to use actual spaces, e.g., {{<item id="html4" href="The Devils Right There_split_029.xhtml" media-type="application/xhtml+xml"/>}}, while the TOC uses the encoded {{%20}}, so I'm increasingly willing to bet that's the issue

----

Brian tested my theory and confirmed: epubs with one-word titles work, while those with multi-word titles produce the broken ToC.

So we should be able to fix this by stripping spaces from the file names.

However! That makes them hard to read, especially when each word doesn’t start with a capital letter and result in lovely camel casing. So let’s replace the spaces with underscores instead, since we know it can handle them as well.

h1. Testing instructions

Please try downloading EPUBs of works with and without spaces in their titles and making sure they work when sent to Kindle! 

It wouldn’t hurt to try the Kindle app as well.

With any device, and in any download format, please also try downloading works with:

* titles in non-Latin scripts, and confirming they are transliterated and the words are separated with underscores in the filename (note that we do not have control over _how_ they are transliterated)
* titles containing only emoji, and confirming the filename is {{Work_##.extension}}, where {{##}} represents the work's ID
* titles that are only 1-2 characters long (e.g., {{Me}}), and confirming the filename has {{_Work_##}} added to it (e.g., {{Me_Work_##}}).

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a tag wrangler (e.g., testy)
# Create a new tag with a Chinese ({{，}} ) or Japanese ({{、}}) comma
## Browse > Tags > New Tag
## In the Name field, enter a tag name that contains one of the commas 
### Both {{Tag With 、Japanese Comma}} and {{Tag With ，Chinese Comma}} have been created on staging
## Select a Category, e.g., Additional Tag
## Check the Canonical checkbox
## Press Create Tag
# Try to use the tag in an autocomplete field
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required fields
## In the appropriate tag field, enter the name of the tag you created in Step 2, or choose it from the autocomplete
## Press Post

h1. What happens

The tag is split at the comma. 

For example, I entered both  {{Tag With 、Japanese Comma}} and {{Tag With ，  Chinese Comma}} when creating [this work|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1083964], but the actual tags on the work are [Tag With|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Tag%20With/works], [Japanese Comma|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Japanese%20Comma/works], and [Chinese Comma|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Chinese%20Comma/works] instead of the expected [Tag With 、Japanese Comma|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Tag%20With%20%E3%80%81Japanese%20Comma/edit] and [Tag With ，Chinese Comma|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Tag%20With%20%EF%BC%8CChinese%20Comma/edit].

h1. What should happen

The Chinese and Japanese commas should be added to the [list of invalid characters for tag names|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/d87652399df73fa5e3b829b0089529501a381538/app/models/tag.rb#L170-L172], and attempting to create a tag with one of the characters should result in an error message.

* remove the commas
* if the tag can’t be saved because the comma-less version already exists, remove the comma and append “ - AO3-6626” to the end of the tag name so it can be found and dealt with by a wrangling admin

column150:
26/Nov/23 4:16 AM;712020:b4b9a112-a7d4-4093-b9df-a77ca8b0c4e8;[~accountid:557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0] The {{_otw_session}} cookie does expire after two weeks, after which browsers delete the cookie. But now that I think about it, Rails updates the session cookie on every page load, since the previous URL is stored in the session for redirect purposes. This means the session is extended by two weeks on every visit.

Rails does not expire sessions by default, so it is possible users who frequent the site never have to sign in. The fact that session cookies are valid forever is bad for security, but that is another conversation altogether…

They should be able to:

* banners: list all banners, create, edit, delete
* admin posts: create, edit, delete
* admin post comments: delete, freeze, mark as spam, and hide on admin posts (note: all admins can freeze and hide admin post comments regardless of role)
