column30:
As the first step in experimenting with speculative loading, only next chapters will be loaded when the browser is idle. This will prevent works being unexpectedly added to a user’s reading history.

*Testing Instructions*

* Using Google Chrome
** Open a multi-chapter work and make sure you can browse to each individual chapter in order.
*** After clicking the “next chapter” link, open the browser’s DevTools console and type the following: {{performance.getEntriesByType("navigation")[0].deliveryType}}. The result should be {{'navigational-prefetch'}}.
** Open a multi-chapter work and make sure you can browse to each individual chapter out of order.
** Open a single chapter work and make sure everything looks normal.
** Check reading history to make sure nothing unexpected was added there.
* Using another browser (i.e. Safari or Firefox)
** Open a multi-chapter work and make sure you can browse to each individual chapter, both in order and out of order.
** Open a single chapter work and make sure everything looks normal.
** Check reading history to make sure nothing unexpected was added there.

Questions:

* Should I add tests of some sort? I’m not sure what would be appropriate here, especially since it’s browser-specific.
* I’m using [document rules|https://chromestatus.com/feature/5112150536749056], which are only available in Chrome 121+ (currently Chrome Dev/Canary; Beta 2023-12-06; Stable 2024-01-23). We can get this working in earlier Chrome versions using various strategies:
** Get an origin trial token and put a <meta http-equiv=”origin-trial”> in the head, or use a HTTP header. This can be a bit annoying since then localhost:3000 would have different behavior than [archiveofourown.org|http://archiveofourown.org] or its subdomains. Or we could get one token for [archiveofourown.org|http://archiveofourown.org] and one for localhost:3000, and then use some configuration setup to manage which one is deployed.
** Use [list rules|https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Speculation_Rules_API], where we list specific URLs instead of using the “.next.chapter a” CSS selector. This is probably simpler, but I could use a hint on how to output the URL of the next chapter. (Without using link_to.)



Also note: because of a [Chrome DevTools bug|https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=1501720] I just discovered, the DevTools incorrectly says the prefetch is not being used. However, it is. I am working on getting that bug fixed ASAP.

column1: Usernames that have numbers aren't searched correctly
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
We use Elasticsearch’s simple analyzer in the bookmark index’s [bookmarker field|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/bba3552e90254ea003cd8e67191a0c207fc1ea40/app/models/search/bookmark_indexer.rb#L46-L49] and [+creators field+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/bba3552e90254ea003cd8e67191a0c207fc1ea40/app/models/search/bookmark_indexer.rb#L36-L39], which means searching for bookmarks by bookmarkers or creators whose usernames or pseuds contain numbers produces either:

* no results if the username/pseud only contains numbers, or
* unwanted results if two users have names or pseuds that differ only by numbers (e.g., if you have users named testy2 and testy5, results for testy5 will appear when searching for testy2)

To reproduce:

* create an account with a username that's all numbers
* bookmark something
* go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search|https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search], enter the whole numerical username in either "Any field on bookmark" or "Bookmarker," press Search Bookmarks
* notice there are no results

Another way to reproduce:

* go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search|https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search]
* enter “testy2” in “Bookmarker” and press Search Bookmarks
* notice you’ll get results for testy5 and other testy accounts

This was discovered by a user in zoho ticket #653212

*Deploy notes*

We may need to give users a warning before reindexing things.

column1: Work search throws error when sorting by certain columns
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Elasticsearch is very flexible with regards to filtering and sorting of search results, so it allows sorting by any field in the index. However, the pretty-printing logic that maps e.g. {{created_at}} to {{date posted}} causes an internal error if the specified {{sort_column}} does not have a pretty name. For example, sorting by work ID is not currently possible: [https://archiveofourown.org/works/search?work_search%5Bsort_column%5D=id|https://archiveofourown.org/works/search?work_search%5Bsort_column%5D=id]

!search_error.png|thumbnail!

*Testing*

The following tasks should be carried out to ensure that the fix works as expected and does not break the current pretty-printing:

* Navigate to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/search?work_search[sort_column]=id&work_search[sort_direction]=asc|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/search?work_search%5Bsort_column%5D=id&work_search%5Bsort_direction%5D=asc] and verify that works are sorted by their ID in ascending order
* Navigate to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/search?work_search[sort_column]=expected_number_of_chapters&work_search[sort_direction]=desc|http://test.archiveofourown.org/works/search?work_search%5Bsort_column%5D=expected_number_of_chapters&work_search%5Bsort_direction%5D=desc] and verify that works are sorted by their expected chapter count in descending order
* Navigate to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/search?work_search[sort_column]=created_at|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/search?work_search%5Bsort_column%5D=created_at] and verify that pretty printing of {{created_at}} → {{date posted}} still works

column30:
I noticed some errors when running departure migrations for the latest release. At first, they seemed to be related to to the {{--alter-foreign-keys-method=auto}} flag:

{noformat}Caused by:
Departure::Error: No foreign keys reference `otwarchive_test`.`invitations`; ignoring --alter-foreign-keys-method.
Slave set to watch has changed
  Was: test-ao3-secondary-va02
  Now: test-ao3-secondary-uk02
Slave set to watch has changed
  Was: test-ao3-secondary-uk02
  Now: 
	(in cleanup) 2023-12-03T18:21:58 Error copying rows from `otwarchive_test`.`invitations` to `otwarchive_test`.`_invitations_new`: Use of uninitialized value in string eq at /usr/bin/pt-online-schema-change line 4321.{noformat}

However, [~accountid:557058:e4a3ada3-097a-4936-af08-46ecac880066] tracked it down to replica checking. It should be OK for higher replica lag, since we don’t read critical information from them AFAIK, we can just ignore replica lag. Per [https://forums.percona.com/t/skip-check-slave-lag-is-not-working-for-pt-online-schema-change/22060|https://forums.percona.com/t/skip-check-slave-lag-is-not-working-for-pt-online-schema-change/22060|smart-link] , it seems we can add {{--recursion-method=none}} to [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6c3041970f9bb9825847afa79f61e2e56f0fc506/config/config.yml#L540|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6c3041970f9bb9825847afa79f61e2e56f0fc506/config/config.yml#L540].

*Testing*

As an admin, create a migration file (on {{test-app16}}) like

{code:ruby}class BrianTest < ActiveRecord::Migration[6.1]
  uses_departure! if Rails.env.staging? || Rails.env.production?

  def change
    add_column :invitations, :brian_test, :datetime
  end
end{code}

and run {{bundle exec rake db:migrate:up VERSION=XXXXXXX}} (then the same thing but with {{down}} to clean up).

column1: Next chapter speculation rules not always present when wanted (or missing when unwanted)
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

{color:#ff5630}+*NOTE FOR TESTING:*+{color}{color:#ff5630} {color}{color:#ff5630}*The position of the speculation rules has changed! It’s under div#feedback.*{color}

# Log in
# Make sure your preferences are set to chapter-by-chapter mode
## Hi, username! > My Preferences
## Uncheck “Show the whole work by default” if it’s checked
## Press “Update” to save
## Do not, under any circumstances, ask me why this is necessary or if I’m sure it is
# Post a *three-chapter* work following these *very specific* *steps*, because deviating from these steps might cause exciting new variations of the bug (see also Step 2d)
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required information only
## Press “Post”
## Follow the “Add Chapter” link to add a new chapter
## Fill in required information only
## Press “Post”
## Repeat Steps 3d-3f to add a third chapter
## Touch nothing! Nothing! Just stay there on the page showing you Chapter 3!
# Navigate to Chapter 2 and confirm it contains speculation rules
## Use the “Previous Chapter” link at the top of the page to navigate from Chapter 3 to Chapter 2
## Use your browser developer tools to inspect the page or view the page source
## Use your preferred method to make sure the source includes {{<script type="speculationrules">}}  – it’s toward the bottom of {{div#chapters}}, which is inside {{div#workskin}}
## Once again, touch nothing after you have done the previous step! Just stay there on the page showing you Chapter 2
# Access the work in Entire Work mode and observe the presence and absence of speculation rules for various chapters
## Use the “Entire Work” link at the top of the page to access the work in full work mode
## Use your browser developer tools to inspect the page or view the page source
## In an ideal world, neither Chapter 1 nor Chapter 2 would have {{<script type="speculationrules">}}, because there is no next chapter page to prefetch – everything is already on the page you’re accessing. _However_, it’s extremely likely you will be able to locate {{<script type="speculationrules">}} inside {{div#chapter-2}}. 
## Again, follow no links! Just proceed to the next bit!
# Navigate to Chapter 1 and observe whether it has speculation rules
## Use the “Chapter by Chapter” link at the top of the page to access the work in chapter-by-chapter mode, which will put you on Chapter 1
## Use your browser developer tools to inspect the page or view the page source
## In an ideal world, {{div#chapters}} _should_ have {{<script type="speculationrules">}}, but it likely doesn’t!

If you want, you can then use Next Chapter to see if Chapter 2 has speculation rules (it probably does) and Previous Chapter to go back to Chapter 1 and see if it has speculation rules (it probably doesn’t).

h1. Notes

* I was able to reproduce this consistently on production and staging, but I was doing it pretty quickly. On production, when I refreshed my work in Entire Work mode after a while, none of the chapters had speculation rules, which is the desired result! But weird that they vanished. 
* I hesitate to mention this, but when I was doing this and simultaneously checking the cache from the console, I uh… couldn’t find Chapter 1 or Chapter 2 in the cache. (Chapter 3 was there immediately after posting it, which makes sense. It also makes sense that Chapters 1 & 2 would’ve gotten deleted from the cache after posting Chapter 3. But I couldn’t find them in the cache even after accessing them again. It’s possible I wasn’t reloading something I should’ve been.)

Regardless! The point is! We should never see speculation rules in Entire Work mode, but if we’re dealing with a 3-chapter work, I should always see them on Chapter 1 & 2 in Chapter-by-Chapter mode. 

This smells like caching, because both {{works/show.html.erb}} and {{chapters/show.html.erb}} use {{chapters/_chapters.html.erb}}, which has a ginormous cache block containing the chapter content and speculation rules:

[https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c2354df0800637c1e9a0ddd9a3651cc59a17597a/app/views/works/show.html.erb#L34-L47|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c2354df0800637c1e9a0ddd9a3651cc59a17597a/app/views/works/show.html.erb#L34-L47]

[https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c2354df0800637c1e9a0ddd9a3651cc59a17597a/app/views/chapters/show.html.erb#L24-L26|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c2354df0800637c1e9a0ddd9a3651cc59a17597a/app/views/chapters/show.html.erb#L24-L26]

[https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c2354df0800637c1e9a0ddd9a3651cc59a17597a/app/views/chapters/_chapter.html.erb#L20-L97|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c2354df0800637c1e9a0ddd9a3651cc59a17597a/app/views/chapters/_chapter.html.erb#L20-L97]

The speculation rules are only included in {{chapters/_chapters.html.erb}} if {{@next_chapter}} is set, and _that_ is only set for {{chapters/show.html.erb}}, not {{works/show.html.erb}}. 

[https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c2354df0800637c1e9a0ddd9a3651cc59a17597a/app/views/chapters/_chapter.html.erb#L82-L93|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c2354df0800637c1e9a0ddd9a3651cc59a17597a/app/views/chapters/_chapter.html.erb#L82-L93]

[https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c2354df0800637c1e9a0ddd9a3651cc59a17597a/app/controllers/chapters_controller.rb#L29-L52|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c2354df0800637c1e9a0ddd9a3651cc59a17597a/app/controllers/chapters_controller.rb#L29-L52]

So it seems like sometimes we're writing speculation rules to the cache and sometimes we're not, depending on whether a chapter was first accessed from {{works/show.html.erb}} or {{chapters/show.html.erb}}. 🙃

column1: PDF files containing Japanese characters are very large
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Post a work that only uses characters in the Latin alphabet (Aa-Zz)
# Download the work in PDF format
# Edit the work to include Japanese characters either in the actual content or the metadata, e.g., add a fandom tag like “ハートキャッチプリキュア! | Heartcatch Precure!”
# Download the updated work in PDF format
# Compare the size of the two files

h1. What happens

The second PDF is enormous because it includes a font that’s about 8 megabytes in size (WenQuanYi Zen Hei) in order to display the Japanese. 

It’s very likely this problem also occurs with Chinese and Korean, since WenQuanYi Zen Hei contains Chinese, Japanese, and Korean and is probably used in PDFs for all three languages.

h1. What should happen

The two PDFs should be much closer in size.

We can use Calibre’s {{--subset-embedded-fonts}} option for PDFs to only include the necessary characters.

h1. Testing notes

* Make sure to use a new work for this so you’re not getting a cached download file.
* Please test a second time using different characters – we want to be sure the second file contains the new characters.

19/Feb/24 1:09 PM;557058:48d6a38e-168b-4aa7-a58d-a1853a844295;I’ve continue to poke at this, and it looks like Calibre 6.13 – the version available to Debian Bookworm (the version we will be upgrading our servers to) – fixes the issue, or at least makes a sizeable (hah) dent in the PDF size when CJK characters are included.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. *Steps to reproduce*

Since [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5627|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5627|smart-link] is fixed, it’s no longer possible to reproduce this without console access.

# Log in as User A
# Post a work 
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required fields
## Press Post
# Add a draft chapter
## Follow Add Chapter link on work
## Fill in required fields
## Press Preview
# From the console, delete the first posted chapter
# Log out
# Log in as User B
# Set your preferences to show works in chapter by chapter mode
## Hi, username! > My Preferences
## Under Display, uncheck “Show the whole work by default.”
## Press Update
# Go to User A’s works page ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/UserA/works}}) and follow the link to the work you posted earlier

h1. What happens

You get stuck in a redirect loop and likely encounter an error from your browser. 

However, if you either change your preferences to enable “Show the whole work by default” or go directly to the full work URL ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/####?view_full_work=true}}), you see the work meta/header, title, and byline, with a blank space where the work text would normally be.

h1. What should happen

Rather than get stuck in a redirect loop, you should see the work header/meta, title, and byline, with a blank space where the work text would normally be. 

The way to accomplish this _might_ be to redirect to the work URL with the {{view_full_work}} parameters rather than attempting to show something at the chapter URL ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/####/chapters/####}}). 

If we went that route, the redirect would need to only apply to people who are not an admin and not a creator (or invited creator) of the work. It would also need to apply _only_ if the chapter belonged to a posted work. (The behavior for attempting to access a draft chapter on a draft work should not change.)

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a user
# Create a collection
## Browse > Collections > New Collection
## Fill in required information
## Press “Submit”
# Join a collection
## Browse > Collections
## In the filters, choose “No” under “Closed”
## And choose “Yes” under “Moderated”
## Press “Sort and Filter”
## Use the “Join” button on the first collection that appears in the list and which you do not own/are not a moderator of
# Log out
# Log in as an admin with the superadmin or policy_and_abuse role
# Ban the user from Step 1 for spam
## Manage Users > Find Users
## In “Name,” enter the user’s name
## Check “Exact match only” for “Search settings”
## Press “Find”
## Follow the appropriate “Details” link in the results table
## Under “Record Warnings, Suspensions, or Notes,” choose “Spammer: ban and delete all creations”
## Fill in some text under “Notes”
## Press “Update”

h1. What happens

On the Delete Spammer Creations page, the yellow banner says something like, “Are you sure you want to *_delete_* all the works and comments created by this user, along with their 0 bookmarks, 0 series, and 2 collections? This *cannot be undone*.”

Wait. *2* collections? But if I look at the user’s dashboard or collections page, they only have one!

Yeeeeah. Here’s what I said to PAC:

{quote}The [spam ban actions define a user's collections as @user.collections|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e211c6bb9ad792e344aacb629020c3bc92576b0a/app/controllers/admin/admin_users_controller.rb#L131-L150], but all that does is get you [a list of collections the user is a participant in|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e211c6bb9ad792e344aacb629020c3bc92576b0a/app/models/user.rb#L97-L98]. What it should do is get a list of collections the user is an owner or maintainer of, which would be [@user.maintained_collections|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e211c6bb9ad792e344aacb629020c3bc92576b0a/app/models/user.rb#L101], or maybe even [sole-owned collections, like when you're deleting your account|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e211c6bb9ad792e344aacb629020c3bc92576b0a/app/controllers/users_controller.rb#L180].{quote}

h1. What should happen

It should only count and delete collections the user is the sole owner of.

h1. Testing notes

In addition to Steps 1-3, you should also make a second collection and add a co-owner before testing the spam ban. To do so:

#  While logged in as the user from Step 1, repeat Step 2 to create a second collection you own
# Access the collection
# From the collection’s Dashboard, follow the “Membership” link under the collection title
# Under “Add new members,” enter the name of another user
# Press “Submit”
# Choose “Owner” from the select/dropdown menu that corresponds with the user you just added
# Press “Update” to save

column1: Reduce load on mysql from searching for imported works.
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The fallback query in [Work.find_by_url_uncached|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/9ce7f82a0e0eaca675a7899222b805eed421b57c/app/models/work.rb#L383] resorts to a LIKE with a leading {{%}} which means that the entire {{works}} table will be scanned for non-matching queries. 

Some external links to previously imported urls are hitting this and periodically tying up MariaDB with unnecessarily slow queries (additionally compounded by a bug for urls that don’t start with {{www}})

The following changes therefore need to be made:

* modify {{with_www}} and {{no_www}} to preserve the protocol
* add {{with_http}} to change the protocol from HTTPS to HTTP
* add {{with_https}} to change the protocol from HTTP to HTTPS
* change {{Work.where(imported_from_url: [url.minimal, url.no_www, url.with_www, url.encoded, url.decoded]).first}} to now include {{url.with_http}} and {{url.with_https}}
* remove {{Work.where("imported_from_url LIKE ?", "%#{url.minimal_no_http}%")}}

column1: Languages page caching
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Going to [https://archiveofourown.org/languages|https://archiveofourown.org/languages|smart-link]  is _painfully_ slow, especially when logged in. We should cache it for everybody (including logged in users) since the counts definitely don’t need to be real-time, and even adding new languages doesn’t need to be reflected there instantaneously. Let’s try caching for 1 day to begin with.

Another improvement we can make is to use [https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActionView/Helpers/NumberHelper.html#method-i-number_to_human|https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActionView/Helpers/NumberHelper.html#method-i-number_to_human|smart-link]  to display the values, which will better indicate (at least for larger counts) that the numbers are now effectively approximations.

*Testing*

Go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/languages|https://test.archiveofourown.org/languages] and check the counts there. Most languages in stage will be unaffected, but 

* numbers bigger than 999 should now have delimiters (i.e. “1,000” versus “1000”) and 
* the largest numbers should have similar rounding to the homepage (i.e., “863,300” instead of “863,301”)

Next, try posting a work *and a restricted work* (in a smaller language that has a precise number) and return to the languages page. The counts should _not_ update. When you come back in 24 hours, then they should have updated. *Check the count for a registered user is updated by 2 but the guest count is only updated by 1.*

The page heading should also say “Work Languages” now instead of “The Archive supports these languages.”

column1: Allow certain admins access to an index of orphaned works by a given original creator
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Post a few works you don’t mind orphaning
## Post > New
## Fill in required information
## Press “Post”
## Repeat as desired (Note: When testing, we’ll want to put some of the works in anonymous and unrevealed collections, plus have an admin hide one of the works.)
# Orphan the works you posted in Step 2
## Hi, username! > My Works > Edit Works
## Check the checkboxes for the works you want to orphan
## Press the “Orphan” button
## Press “Yes, I’m sure” to confirm
# Log out
# Log in as an admin with the superadmin, legal, or policy_and_abuse role
# Access one of the works you orphaned in Step 3

h1. What happens

In the meta box at the top of the work, it will say “Original Creator ID: 123 (username)".  (Note: If the user is deleted, the text that appears is only the ID.) 

Refer to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5521|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5521|smart-link] for more details on Original Creator IDs.

h1. What should happen

In the meta box, the text “123 (username)” should link the username to the user’s admin page ({{/admin/users/username}}). The user ID should be a link to {{/work_original_creators/123}}, and that page should use an {{<ol>}} to list the blurbs for all works orphaned by that user, including anonymous, unrevealed, and hidden works. 

The unrevealed blurb should not by the mystery work placeholder, but rather the full blurb, allowing the admin to actually access the work.

Blurbs should tell you when the original creator orphaned the work, e.g. “Orphaned at: [date time],” similar to the way your History page shows you when you last visited the work.

The page heading should be “Orphaned Works by 123 (username)” and the browser page title can be the same. If the user still exists, the text “123 (username)” in the heading should link the ID number to the user admin page ({{/admin/users/username}}) and the username to the user's works page ({{/users/username/works}}). 

The list should be paginated, as any other work listing would be. 

There should not be filters or a sidebar.

Like the data on the orphaned works themselves, the page should only be accessible to admins with the superadmin, legal, or policy_and_abuse role.

Going to {{/work_original_creators/123}} should give a 404 if there’s no data in the {{work_original_creators}} table for the given ID.

column1: Switch our imageset partially to SVG
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
We want to switch many of the pixel images used on the Archive to SVG. And then as a next step we want to create variations of these in our skins, namely reversi. But they should also be skinnable by users for their own skins. This goal dictates a specific way this needs to be implemented:

# it needs to be inline SVG
# with css classes for individual parts
# copied from SVG file to inline in a way that ensures no duplicate IDs either on the SVG itself or the elements inside the SVG (blurb icons are rendered many times in a works listing, for example)
# i18n-able aria-titles and/or other text (so not part of the source SVG file, but added while inlining)
# We need to allow some SVG-specific attributes in our CSS parser. A full list needs to be compiled, but {{fill}} and {{stroke}} are needed for certain.

Not part of this switch to SVG are the user icons (default, anon, guest, etc). Everything else can be switched to SVG but it's not necessary to switch all of them at once. The high priority and the main reason for this switch is the work blurb icons. The kudos icon is also used in emails, where we want to keep using the pixel version. So this specific one will have both a SVG version and a pixel version.

The look of our icons creates some complications. It's possible to create gradients and drop shadows in SVG, but these are defined in a {{defs}} block at the start of the file and are then used by elements by referencing their IDs. That means the same drop-shadow would be inlined for every icon on the page. So we have to ensure that each one gets a unique ID. The same is the case for the gradients. These two things have different possible solutions.

h2. Gradients

This is the easy one. Since we want these icons to be CSS-stylable anyway, we will get rid of the gradients in the graphic, render the SVG with a flat color background and then add the gradient via CSS.

One thing to note here is that you can't set a CSS background for SVG elements, only {{fill}} works. So the way to do this is to set {{fill: none;}} on the element (in the CSS) and then set the background gradient on the SVG element itself (in the CSS).

If somebody comes up with a reason for why we don't want to do it that way, the other possible solutions are the same as for the shadows.

h2. Shadows

We can't go the CSS-only route here, since the {{box-shadow}} CSS attribute has no effect on SVG elements, and would also render a rectangle box, instead of following the shape of the element. And while the {{drop-shadow}} CSS filter works, it can't help us, since we need inline shadows.

# The radical approach is to get rid of the shadows. Web design has changed a lot in the ~15 years since the work blurbs were added, maybe we use this project as a reason to give the blurb icons a new look.
# Least favorite option, only if everything else doesn't work out: We accept the bloat in the HTML file and add the shadow every time, our SVG renderer has to consider this and apply unique IDs to the shadow definitions when creating the inline SVG.
# We use {{use}} to build our icons. This means we have one big inline SVG element at the top of every page (visually hidden). This SVG contains all individual elements that we use on the site. The actual SVG icons that are visible on the page then are made up of {{use}} elements that reference the components from the sprite SVG at the top of the page.
## This is basically the imageset solution we have now, except SVG
## This would mean we don't have to deal with duplicate IDs
## No bloat, because even aside from the shadow and gradient issues, we wouldn't have to render the "Gen" (for example) icon N times either, only ever once.
## Here is a guide on how to do this from 2014: [https://24ways.org/2014/an-overview-of-svg-sprite-creation-techniques/|https://24ways.org/2014/an-overview-of-svg-sprite-creation-techniques/|smart-link]  with one very important change though: shadow DOM has come a long way in the last ten years and now it _is_ possible to reference these elements in CSS, so they are skinnable for us. The solution noted in the article, to externally reference the SVGs, however, _isn't_ suitable for us, since SVG hasn't come that far and filters (aka what we use to create the shadows in SVG) aren't externally referencable ([Open bug on Chromium|https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=109212).]). This was the big stumbling block when we first worked on this, so it's really great that we have a viable solution now.
## browser support: [https://caniuse.com/mdn-svg_elements_use|https://caniuse.com/mdn-svg_elements_use|smart-link] 

h2. TL;DR, the individual steps that need to be done:

* Rebuild the pixel icons in SVG, this is mostly done, but needs to be adjusted to work with whatever solution that inlines it into the HTML.
* In case of the sprite solution:
** Make a partial with an SVG element that is visually hidden (width 0, height 0, etc) but not display: none (this differs from the article I linked above but is needed for the {{defs}} block to work).
** Define a single {{defs}} block at the top for all the gradients (if we use them) and the shadow, etc.
** Make a {{symbol}} for every icon with its own viewBox.
** Add the partial to all necessary layout files.
* In case of the "bloat" solution:
** add the SVGs as individual files to our Rails project
** Write a view helper (or whatever would be best suited for this task) that takes a path to an SVG, plus additional options we might need (string to use to build unique IDs, any text, etc), reads and copies the contents of that file and outputs the inlined SVG markup. Obviously should only work for files in our own project, can't pass external URLs. Take a look at [https://github.com/jamesmartin/inline_svg|https://github.com/jamesmartin/inline_svg|smart-link]  to see if there is a way for us to use it. Right now, to display the icons 1:1 the answer is no. Because 1. can't set IDs for elements inside the SVG, 2. we use neither sprocket nor webpack (and webpacker is deprecated). But forking it or using parts of the code might speed this task up.
* Change CSS parser to allow {{fill}} and {{stroke}} and other attributes TBD.
* Change HTML and CSS for every place the pixel version of an icon is currently used and redo it with the SVG version.
* This can be a next step in a separate issue: Redo the imageset to only contain the remaining pixel graphics. Update all instances where the imageset is used to the new x and y positions of the remaining graphics.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
* Admins with the {{policy_and_abuse}} or {{superadmin}} roles should be able to access a user’s Change Username page ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/username/change_username}}) by
** following the “Change Username” link on {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/username/edit}}
** following the “Change My Username” link on {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/username/preferences}} if [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6542|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6542|smart-link] has been completed
** following a new “Rename” link on {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/users/username}} , located between “Activate” and “Manage Roles” 
* For these admins, the Change My Username page should look and behave differently from the user version:
** The page heading should be “Change Username”
** The yellow caution box should not appear
** Where the page says, “If that is not what you want, you can create a new Pseud instead,” it should instead say, “Change the name of this user to a generic name in the format user + their account ID.”
** Where the existing navigation is, there should instead be a button-style navigation link to “Manage User,” which should point to {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/users/username}}
** The “New username” field should be disabled and prefilled with “user123,” where “123” is the user’s ID
*** There should be backend validation to ensure the prefilled username is not altered
*** The footnote associated with this field should say, “This username cannot be edited. If you need to change it to a different name, contact your chair.”
** In place of the “Password” field, there should be a "Ticket ID" field that is used to validate the ticket exists in the ticket tracker, a la [AO3-6156|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6156].
*** If [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6587|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6587|smart-link] is not completed, the field should have a footnote that says, “Numbers only.”
** Assuming validations pass, submitting the form should rename the user and log it in the User History as "Old Username: whatever, New Username: whaterever, Changed by: admin-whoever, Ticket ID: #123"
*** Ideally, this would rename the user even if it had not been 7 days since their last rename
* Other admins attempting to access {{/users/username/change_username}} should redirected

h1. Notes

If [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6717|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6717|smart-link] is implemented first, admins should be able to change the usernames of banned or suspended users.

h1. Additional testing

We set up multiple pages for future i18n. For these pages, we need to check that there is no exposed HTML in the text (e.g. a visible {{<strong>}} tag) or missing translations. Furthermore, any instances of “username” should be written without a space, so “Username”, not “User name” etc.

# Log in as an admin
# Invitations > Invite New Users. Check that this page looks fine as described above.
# Fill a username in the “Track invitations” section and search. Check that this results page looks fine as described above.
# Log in as a user
# For a gift exchange that you moderate or own, go to the sign-ups page (e.g. {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/aardvark_gift_exchange/signups}} when signed in as testy). Check that this page looks fine as described above and that the buttons to expand and close the offers and requests work.
# My Dashboard > Invitations > Manage Invitations. Check that this page looks fine as described above.

# Log out
# Go to {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/password/new}}. Check that this page looks fine as described above.

This is the bulk of the upgrade! Refer to [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#upgrading-from-rails-6-1-to-rails-7-0|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#upgrading-from-rails-6-1-to-rails-7-0|smart-link] for details about this. We definitely need to include the cookie rotator.

*Testing*

There are a number of changes, so I’ve pulled the list of deprecated features so we can double check them. Also of note, we can now opt in to native (not Ruby) memory management for libxml2 for improved speed performance but with the potential for issues that come with C memory management.

h3. Deprecated

* Passing a {{Nokogiri::XML::Node}} as the first parameter to {{CDATA.new}} is deprecated and will generate a warning. This parameter should be a kind of {{Nokogiri::XML::Document}}. This will become an error in a future version of Nokogiri.
* Passing a {{Nokogiri::XML::Node}} as the first parameter to {{Schema.from_document}} is deprecated and will generate a warning. This parameter should be a kind of {{Nokogiri::XML::Document}}. This will become an error in a future version of Nokogiri.
* Passing a {{Nokogiri::XML::Node}} as the second parameter to {{Text.new}} is deprecated and will generate a warning. This parameter should be a kind of {{Nokogiri::XML::Document}}. This will become an error in a future version of Nokogiri.
* [CRuby] Calling a custom XPath function without the {{nokogiri}} namespace is deprecated and will generate a warning. Support for non-namespaced functions will be removed in a future version of Nokogiri. (Note that JRuby has never supported non-namespaced custom XPath functions.)

h3. Removed

* Removed {{Nokogiri::HTML5.get}} which was deprecated in v1.12.0. [[#2278|https://github.com/sparklemotion/nokogiri/pull/2278]] ([@flavorjones|https://github.com/flavorjones])
* Removed the CSS-to-XPath utility modules {{XPathVisitorAlwaysUseBuiltins}} and {{XPathVisitorOptimallyUseBuiltins}}, which were deprecated in v1.13.0 in favor of {{XPathVisitor}} constructor args. * Removed {{XML::Reader#attribute_nodes}} which was deprecated in v1.13.8 in favor of {{#attribute_hash}}. [[#2598|https://github.com/sparklemotion/nokogiri/issues/2598], [#2599|https://github.com/sparklemotion/nokogiri/pull/2599]] ([@flavorjones|https://github.com/flavorjones])

column1: Remove session cookie migration logic
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
I wrote a piece of code to migrate session cookies from encrypted to signed format as part of [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6629|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6629|smart-link]. This was done to ensure users would not be logged out.

[https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/4e56a347944a6fb831414d9cccdfc866ddfacce5/app/controllers/application_controller.rb#L99-L108|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/4e56a347944a6fb831414d9cccdfc866ddfacce5/app/controllers/application_controller.rb#L99-L108]

The AO3 session cookie has an expiry of two weeks, after which browsers delete the cookie automatically. Each page load causes AO3 to issue a new session cookie, so a user who visits at least once every two weeks can stay signed in indefinitely.

Here’s how removing the migration logic will (not) impact users:

* Users who visited the site since the upgrade have already had their session cookie migrated to the new format. Removing the migration logic will not impact these users.
* Users who have not visited since the upgrade will have to sign in again on their next visit regardless, since their browser will have already deleted the session cookie (change was made more than two weeks ago). Removing the migration logic should have no impact here either.
** Users who selected “remember me” at sign in have another cookie named {{remember_user_token}}. This cookie has a longer expiry, but the format of this cookie did not change, so it does not depend on the migration logic and will still work.
* The impact to bots depends on how they’re written.
** Bots with a proper cookie jar will stay signed in, since their session cookie will have been migrated automatically if they made a request since the change was deployed. Standard HTTP libraries usually have cookie jars.
** Bots with a hard-coded session cookie will be logged out. The session cookie itself does not have an expiry date (it’s only enforced by the browser), so it is possible some developers have done this.

The function has a slight impact on server load since it runs on every request. There’s also little reason to keep unused logic in the codebase. Those are the main reasons for removing it.

column30: h1. Steps to reproduce # Log in as an admin with one of the following roles: {{superadmin board communications support}} # Banners > New Banner # Fill in required fields # Check “Active” # Press “Create banner” # Log out # As both a logged in and logged out user, navigate to the × for making the banner go away while using a screen reader h1. Deploy notes Skins need to be recached.

We would like to take two steps to make it less likely for users to accidentally delete their History.

# Change the wording on the “Clear History” button to say “Clear Entire History” instead.
# Remove the confirmation pop-up and make the user go through an entire confirmation page.

h1. Notes

The confirmation page should be modeled after the other deletion confirmation pages (e.g., [this one for bookmarks|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/68dff8e5164b3b14b3b4b574a63b379d44ab2f57/app/views/bookmarks/confirm_delete.html.erb]), but it might be best to call it {{confirm_clear}} rather than {{confirm_delete}}, since the [prepareDeleteLinks function|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/68dff8e5164b3b14b3b4b574a63b379d44ab2f57/public/javascripts/application.js#L402-L417] will convert any confirmation pages to confirmation pop-ups when JavaScript is enabled.

{quote}h2 heading: Clear Entire History

Text: Are you sure you want to *_clear_* your entire history? This *cannot be undone*.

column1: Parts of header navigation inaccessible to screen readers
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
# Log in on an iOS device (ideally 17.3.1)
# Use VoiceOver to access the navigation in the site header

A user reports that the items in the “Hi, username!” menu are read only as “menu item” instead of the text, e.g. My Dashboard.

The ARIA roles {{menu}} and {{menuitem}} are not meant to be used for navigation. Instead, they are meant to be used for application-style menus and menu items, like in the Rich Text Editor.

So let’s fix some of the accessibility issues in the header. That means:

* The {{menu}} and {{menuitem}} roles should be removed.
* The {{<div>}} around the header should now be a {{<header>}} element instead.
** This gives the section the {{banner}} role, which might seem weird if you’re not used to screen readers, but it's the normal behavior. (Refer to mdn’s [ARIA: banner role|https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Roles/banner_role] and [header element|https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/header] documentation for more info.)
* The navigation lists should now be wrapped inside {{<nav>}} elements, with {{aria-label}} attributes to distinguish the user nav (the one containing "Hi, name!" and so on) from the site nav and the admin nav.
** The names should not include the word “navigation,” because screen readers will say “navigation” shortly thereafter due to the presence of the nav element. (More [info on screen reader behavior with aria-labels on nav elements|https://russmaxdesign.github.io/accessible-forms/landmarks-nav04.html].) 
* The search form in the site navigation was missing the {{search}} role. The role appears to have better support than the {{<search>}} element, so we want to use that, and we should give it an {{aria-label}} because it appears on all pages, including those with other search fields (although I don’t think any of them have the {{search}} role yet.)

column1: Automatically return unwrangleable tags with no fandom to unwrangled bin
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Overview

Wranglers can mark tags as unwrangleable without attaching a fandom tag which leads to these tags becoming lost and no longer easily accessible. Right now, we (sometimes) run manual updates to get the tags back. To reduce manual work, we’d like to create a Resque job to do this for us. Once every week for now should be fine.

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a user with wrangling privileges
# Access your wrangling page: Hi, username! > Tag Wrangling
# Mark a tag as unwrangleable without assigning it a fandom
## If you have tags in your unwrangled bins…
### Access one of the unwrangled bins by clicking on the tag count
### Follow the Edit link for one of the tags
### Check “Unwrangleable”
### Do not fill in the “Fandoms” field
### Press “Save changes”
## If you don’t have tags in your unwrangled bins…
### Access one of your unfilterable bins by clicking on the tag count
### Follow the Edit link for one of the tags
### Check “Unwrangleable”
### In the Fandoms listbox, check the boxes for all of the fandoms to select them for removal
### Press “Save changes”

h1. *Testing*

Follow the steps to reproduce. After the configured time, the job will run and the tag should be returned to the unwrangled bins for all of its suggested fandoms.

The first time the task is run, you may end up with a lot of tags in your unwrangled bins, not just the tags you personally marked unwrangleable. This is expected, since it will be returning any existing fandom-less, unwrangleable tags to the bins as well.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The GitHub action workflow for running the linters (Rubocop, ERB Lint) with Reviewdog currently installs all gems with bundler.

As of version [2.3.19|https://github.com/rubygems/rubygems/blob/master/bundler/CHANGELOG.md#2319-july-27-2022], bundler supports installing just a single group of gems with the {{BUNDLE_ONLY}} environment variable. The linters are already in their own group in the Gemfile after [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6069|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6069|smart-link] , so let’s make use of that option.

Installing less gems should hopefully speed up the workflows.

h1. Testing Instructions

After this is merged, update an existing PR (or create a new one). Ideally this would be one that has known Rubocop or ERB Lint violations, but that shouldn’t be required. Make sure that the reviewdog workflows run and don’t error out (and detect violations if any were added).

column1: Allow certain admins to choose FAQ categories for inclusion in main navigation
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Once [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6698|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6698|smart-link] is implemented, admins with the docs or superadmin role should be allowed to choose FAQs for inclusion in the main navigation.

* “FAQ” should be removed from the “About” menu
* An “FAQ” menu should be added after “About,” and when JavaScript is disabled, clicking it should link to {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/faq}} 
* The first item in the “FAQ” menu should be “All FAQ Categories”
* Admins with the docs or superadmin roles should be able to choose up to X FAQ categories to appear in the menu, where X represents a configurable number (we can set it to 10)
* The admins should be able to set the text used to represent the category in the FAQ menu, but if none is provided, it should fall back to using the category name
* The menu should be cached

When an authorized admin goes to a category’s edit page (e.g., {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/faq/category_name/edit?language_id=en}}), the topmost fieldset should contain

* a checkbox for including the category in the menu, labeled “Included in FAQ dropdown menu” and with the explanatory paragraph “If this box is checked, the category will be included in the FAQs dropdown menu in the main navigation. Up to [configured value] categories can be included.”
* a text field labeled “Display name for FAQ dropdown menu,” with the explanatory paragraph, “Alternate name for dropdown menu; if left blank, uses category name.”

The paragraphs can be plain paragraphs without classes, as on tag edit pages, rather than footnotes.

These fields should be disabled for support or translation admins. (There should be a backend check, not just front end disabling.)

If the maximum number of categories have already been selected for the FAQ dropdown menu, the admin should get an error when attempting to save their changes.

column1: Some tests don't run due to a rake task calling exit
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The {{search:index_tags}} rake calls {{exit}} [here|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/99bb7437c931a244ac3dc1855840c70294999280/lib/tasks/search.rake#L23] and there is a test that triggers this call in[ spec/lib/tasks/search_tasks.rake_spec.rb|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/99bb7437c931a244ac3dc1855840c70294999280/spec/lib/tasks/search_tasks.rake_spec.rb#L78-L81]. The {{exit}} call causes RSpec to exit the program, so tests after this rake test are not run. Furthermore, if any test fails before the rake test, the failure is not reported back to GitHub Actions, which we noticed in a [workflow run|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/actions/runs/8509027006/job/23303756586#step:12:1593] that should have failed due to a failing i18n test.

The SystemExit exception [should be rescued in the test|https://github.com/rspec/rspec-core/issues/2508#issuecomment-541593284] so that RSpec does not stop.

column1: Enhance the Redis initializers to allow sentinel
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Right now, if the one Redis instance the Archive points to goes down, the whole application is inaccessible. Failing over requires updating (either manually or via Ansible) the config to point at a new Redis server – if one is even available. We can use Redis replication along with [https://redis.io/docs/management/sentinel|https://redis.io/docs/management/sentinel|smart-link] to enable automatic failovers.

The following initializers will need to be updated:

* [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/17b131fa4df492ec7576e7642e4d4844797766e8/config/initializers/gem-plugin_config/redis.rb|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/17b131fa4df492ec7576e7642e4d4844797766e8/config/initializers/gem-plugin_config/redis.rb|smart-link] 
* [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/59fa3bb71e4376dd1f61a521e338681f7d6a0716/config/initializers/gem-plugin_config/resque.rb|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/59fa3bb71e4376dd1f61a521e338681f7d6a0716/config/initializers/gem-plugin_config/resque.rb|smart-link] 

Updating them must maintain backwards compatibility with the existing string-based configuration.

*Testing:*

There are quite a few things that use Redis (kudos, scheduled tasks, etc.) but either they all break with this or none of them do. Test that things like giving kudos and receiving emails (like for new comments or kudos) still work as normal.

Actually testing failover will be done separately by systems.

Admins with these roles:

* should see the “Inbox (#)” link on user dashboards
* should be able to follow the link to access that page
* should be able to use the inbox filters to filter comments
* should *not* be able to approve or delete comments, or mark them as read (but they can still see the buttons, and it’s okay if the Select All/Select None/Select buttons still work)

Admins with other roles should be redirected to the homepage with an error saying, "Sorry, only an authorized admin can access the page you were trying to reach."

column1: Add a "Delete All Subscriptions" option to Subscriptions page
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Sometimes for various reasons users want to stop getting any subscription emails, or want to clear out all their subscriptions and start fresh.  However, currently you can only unsubscribe from works/creators/series one item at a time.  This can be tedious and even prohibitive if you have a lot of subscriptions.  

We’d like to add a button at the top right of the “My Subscriptions” page ([https://archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/subscriptions|https://archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/subscriptions]), to the right of the existing buttons, that reads “Delete All Subscriptions”.  Clicking on it should generate a confirmation prompt (like the one in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6688|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6688|smart-link] History) that asks the user to confirm their choice.

Once confirmed, the button would then delete all of the users' existing subscriptions to works, creators, and/or series.

h1. Notes

The confirmation page should be modeled after the other deletion confirmation pages (e.g., [this one for bookmarks|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/68dff8e5164b3b14b3b4b574a63b379d44ab2f57/app/views/bookmarks/confirm_delete.html.erb]), but it might be best to call it confirm_delete_all rather than {{confirm_delete}}, since the [prepareDeleteLinks function|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/68dff8e5164b3b14b3b4b574a63b379d44ab2f57/public/javascripts/application.js#L402-L417] will convert any confirmation pages to confirmation pop-ups when JavaScript is enabled.

column1: Allow users to resend invitations, this time with index
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30: h1. Description Users frequently submit support requests because they have accidentally deleted or not received their invitations. Therefore, we’d like to allow users to resend their invitations without submitting a support ticket. (In the case of missing emails, it’s fairly likely the resent email will continue to be eaten by spam filters, but it’s possible some will get through.) To prevent spam, there should be a configurable limit on how soon you can resend an invitation ({{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}). It should start off at 24 hours. Resending an invitation should not alter the invitation’s {{sent_at}}, because we sometimes need this information. It should be tracked separately as {{resent_at}}. This information should be available to admins on pages where the [invitation partial|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/views/invitations/_invitation.html.erb] is used, e.g., {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/invitations/###}}, where it can be added below the existing “Sent at” info as “Last resent at.” Users can currently check the status of their invitations by entering their email address on [https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status|https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status]. We’d like to add the resend option to this page. *If the user checks the status of their invitation less than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is initially sent*, the resend option should not be present. The text should say: {quote}Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there. If it has been more than [{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}] hours since you should have received your invitation, but you have not received it after checking your spam folder, you can visit this page to resend the invitation.{quote} *If the user checks the status of their invitation more than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is initially sent*, the resend option should be present. The text should say: {quote}Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there. Because your invitation was sent more than 24 hours ago, you can have your invitation resent. [button reading: Resend Invitation]{quote} *If the user checks the status of their invitation less than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is resent*, the resend option should not be present. The text should say: {quote}Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date] and resent on [resent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there. If it has been more than [{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}] hours since you should have received your invitation, but you have not received it after checking your spam folder, you can visit this page to resend the invitation.{quote} *If the user checks the status of their invitation more than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is resent*, the resend option should be present, and there should be a suggestion to contact Support. The text should say: {quote}Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date] and resent on [resent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there. Because your invitation was resent more than 24 hours ago, you can have your invitation resent again, or you may want to contact Support. [button reading: Resend Invitation]{quote} h1. Notes If you could fix it so the “Invitation status for email@example.com” heading is an {{h3}} when loaded on [https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status|https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status], that would be appreciated! (It should remain an {{h2}} when you have JavaScript disabled and it takes you to a separate page.) Example: !javascript_resend.png|width=83%,alt="The Invitation Request Status page with the invitation status loaded below the email field using JavaScript."! !no_javascript_resend.png|width=83%,alt="The separate Invitation Status page for users who have JavaScript disabled."! This was deployed in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6609|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6609|smart-link] and reverted with [this pull request|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4710] due to the performance issues described in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6666|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6666|smart-link]. We can probably revert the revert to get the code back, and then add the necessary indexes. Regarding what to index, Brian notes: {quote}It looks like we don't even have an index on {{invitee_email}} (at least according to the [latest schema dump|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/bd57a26224017d4b871fb70a9787d7fe3c29d249/db/schema.rb#L377]) which is quite surprising to me. Adding those 2 indexes sounds like a reasonable approach to me, we can try running an {{EXPLAIN}} on staging before the deploy to make sure the DB is doing the right things with them{quote} And Bilka notes: {quote}I tried locally running the explain for the current table/index situation, it was very unhelpful. I think an index on {{redeemed_at}} by itself might not make much sense, because all the queries are looking for (not) null, not a specific value. {{invitee_email}} would be a very good target, agreed with Brian there.{quote} h1. Testing # Make sure the invitation queue is on: ## Log in as a superadmin ## Go to “Settings” ## Check “Account creation enabled,” “Account creation requires invitation,” and “Invite from queue enabled” ## Press “Update” ## Stay logged in as admin so you can send invitations without waiting for the automated task # In a different browser or an incognito/private window, add yourself to the queue: ## Make sure you are logged out ## Go to the homepage ## Follow “Get Invited!” ## Under “Request an invitation,” fill in “Email” with an address that a) you have access to and b) is not already being used by an account ## Press “Add me to the list” # Back in the browser or window from Step 1, send invitations to everyone in the queue: ## Invitations > Invite New Users ## Under “Send invite codes to people in our [invitations queue|http://localhost:3000/invite_requests],” note how many people are in the queue ## Enter that number where it says “Number of people to invite” ## Press “Invite from queue” # In the browser or window from Step 2, check the status of your invitation request and ensure the process matches the details in this issue; i.e., ## there is no resend button in the first 24 hours after the invitation is sent ## 24 hours after the invitation is sent, the status page changes and you can resend the invitation ## once you have resent the invitation, and the status page updates again ## an admin can see the “Last resent at” date on the invitation page ## 24 hours after you’ve resent the invitation, the status page changes again ## if you resend the invitation again, an admin sees the new date under “Last resent at” h1. column1: Allow comment moderation on news posts
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
We’d like to have comment moderation for news posts, just like comment moderation for works.

# Log in as an admin who can create news posts (board, board_assistants_team, communications, support, translation, superadmin)
# Admin Posts > Post AO3 News

There should be a check box for “Enable comment moderation” above the section for “Who can comment on this news post” 

Checking this box and pressing post should create a news post with a comment section. 

The comment form should have a blue notice on it that says, “Comments on this news post are moderated. Your comment will not appear until it has been approved.”

# Log out of your admin account
# Access the news post
# Leave a comment (or two or three)

You should get a success message that says, "Your comment was received! It will appear publicly after it has been approved."

# Log in as an admin with any role, because for the initial roll out we’re treating this like hiding comments on admin posts (which any admin can do)
# Access the news post

There should be a link at the top of the news post that says, “Unreviewed Comments (#)” near “Delete Post.”  

Following the link will take you to a page with the heading “Unreviewed Comments on [News Post Title].” 

The page should say under the heading, “Please note that comments cannot be unapproved once you have approved them. After you delete any comments you do not wish to appear on the news post, you can approve all that remain.”

You should be able to approve the comment by using either:

*  the “Approve” button on the comment, which will take you back to the Unreviewed Comments page and give you the success message, “Comment approved,” or
* the “Approve All Unreviewed Comments” button, which will take you to the admin post with the success message, “All moderated comments approved.”

The approved comments should appear on the news post (please allow for possible delay due to caching). 

If there are no unreviewed comments, the “Unreviewed Comments (#)” link will go away.

Some other things you can test, if you’d like:

# using other buttons on the unreviewed comments, e.g., hiding, deleting, or spamming a comment – there’s no new behavior here, but if there are existing bugs, it wouldn’t hurt to log them
# combining the moderated comment functionality with limiting who can comment on the news post to no one or logged-in users only – again, this can already be done on works and there’s no new behavior here, but if there are existing bugs, it wouldn’t hurt to log them
# on a *work* with moderated comments enabled, an admin should not be able to approve comments (AO3-5977 exists for getting rid of the big “Approve All Unreviewed Comments” button)

# Follow the Edit link

We’d like to extend [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6564|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6564|smart-link] to all comments and comment emails.

h1. Testing

You can test with comments on works or tags (to comment on a tag, you’ll need to be logged in as a tag wrangler, e.g., testy). 

*Because you’ll need to check emails and inboxes*, it’s easiest to use works created by another account you own, or tags wrangled by another account you own.

# *Before anything else*, go to your preferences (Hi, username! > My Preferences) and make sure you have the following settings
## “Turn off emails about comments” should be *unchecked* 
## “Turn off messages to your inbox about comments” should be *unchecked*
## “Turn off copies of your own comments” should be *unchecked*
# *Before this is deployed to staging*, leave a comment containing an image. Bookmark this comment or otherwise remember where it is (if you have emailed copies of your own comments enabled as instructed above, that’s a good way to find it).

column1: Synned Relationship Tags Not Carrying Over Fandoms + Character Tags to Newly Created Canonicals
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Since about July of 2023, we've had an issue where tags were significantly delayed in carrying over parents and children when synned. This issue seemed to begin to occur with increasing regularity from about :30 past the hour until about :50 past the hour whenever the archive was moderately to extremely busy. It was an inconvenience, but it didn’t directly impact our workflow beyond being a little annoying. This issue impacts all tags, but is most noticable and impactful in the creation of relationship tags.

Recently this issue has gotten significantly worse, to the point where it is occuring more and more frequently outside of that time frame and tags which would normally transfer to the canonical during synning are not transferring at all if they are not left attached to the syn until they have done so (which, can take a long, long time depending on how bad the delay currently is). 

For example, if I attach character tags *Alastor* and *Angel Dust* to a relationship tag and then use that tag to create the canonical for *Alastor & Angel Dust (Hazbin Hotel)*, the fandom and the character tags would not immediately transfer to the new canonical. If I leave them on the syn, eventually they will transfer over, typically after the delay window has passed, but if I remove them at any point prior to them transferring, it will never add them at all and those tags will instead need to be added manually. 

Delays relating to tags being assigned to fandoms and works from synned tags to be aggregated into the works on the canonical tag have also significantly increased. 

Additionally, if the character tags are removed prior to fandom & character tags transfering to the syn, though the syn is still assigned to the fandom, the fandom will never transfer to the canonical. It will only eventually transfer _if_ the character tags are still attached when the delay has resolved.

This is all having a significant impact on workflow.


*To Reproduce Issue:*

# Create a work
# Assign a fandom to this work and create a new relationship tag and add it to this work
# Publish work
# Go to unwrangled bin of the fandom assigned to the work and find the newly created relationship tag
# Assign character tags to the relationship tag
# Wait until between :31-:49 past the hour. While this error occurs other times, it occurs most frequently within this time frame
# Use this relationship to create a canonical tag via the Synonym of field on the tag edit page
# Click through to the canonical tag’s edit page
# Refresh and observe whether the fandom + character tags are added to the canonical tag
## If they have not been added you can check whether they will be added as designed (i.e. regardless of whether the syn has the character tags attached when the delay resolves) by taking the following steps:
### Remove the character tags from the synned relationship tag
### Navigate back to the canonical tag edit page
### Refresh and wait to see if the character and fandom tags show up on the canonical tag
### If functioning properly, the fandom & character tags should be showing up eventually on the canonical whether the character tags are currently attached to a syn or not
## If they have not been added, you can verify that they will be added if the character tags are left attached to the synned tag by taking the following steps: 
### Remain on the canonical edit page
### Refresh periodically until character & fandom tags show up on the canonical tag (typically this happens when the delay resolves, usually between :50-:00 of the hour

column1: Update i18n-tasks and use the new default_i18n_subject matcher

Right now, we have to use a magic {{i18n-tasks-use}} comment to get the i18n-tasks gem to recognize the locale used by email subjects translated with the {{default_i18n_subject}} method, e.g. [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c2354df0800637c1e9a0ddd9a3651cc59a17597a/app/mailers/user_mailer.rb#L219-L220|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c2354df0800637c1e9a0ddd9a3651cc59a17597a/app/mailers/user_mailer.rb#L219-L220|smart-link] . That's inconvenient, so let's update to [i18n-tasks version 1.0.14|https://github.com/glebm/i18n-tasks/blob/main/CHANGES.md#v1014], which adds an optional matcher that can detect this automatically. Together with the upgrade we should remove all existing magic comments for mailer subject locales.

The matcher needs to be enabled in the i18n-tasks configuration file. Let’s take the opportunity to also use the [simplified configuration syntax|https://github.com/glebm/i18n-tasks/blob/9e765a40308ecd9674453d70a9177d74a2596c61/templates/config/i18n-tasks.yml#L99-L101] for the RailsModelMatcher, so we don’t need to manually require it.

Due to a change in the i18n gem that led to a crash in i18n-tasks, i18n also needs to be upgraded to at least [version 1.14.5|https://github.com/ruby-i18n/i18n/releases/tag/v1.14.5], which contains [the fix|https://github.com/ruby-i18n/i18n/pull/688] for that.

column1: Separate languages used for works from other uses of languages
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h2. Overview of changes

The {{languages}} table currently serves multiple purposes:

* allow users to identify the language their works are in
* allow admins to 
** identify which languages we can provide support or abuse assistance in
** identify languages of FAQs and admin posts
** associate languages with locales

Using one table to serve user-facing and admin-facing purposes sometimes creates problems, as the needs of these two groups can be conflicting.

Ergo, we’d like to separate the admin-based uses and the user-based uses. 

# Create a new table called {{locale_languages}} that is a duplicate of the existing language table in terms of both structure _and_ existing data. The goal here is to keep everything associated with the language it is currently associated with.
# Update the code for FAQs, admin posts, locales, and the support and abuse forms to use {{locale_languages}}.
# Add admin pages for listing, creating, and editing locale languages, approximately matching the existing pages for work languages, but ideally replacing any use of “Language” or “Work Language” with “Locale Language”:
## {{/locale_languages}} should list the locale languages. It should be accessible to {{translation}}, {{support}}, {{policy_and_abuse}}, and {{superadmin}} admins. There should be no public-facing version of this page.
## {{/locale_languages/new}} should be accessible to {{translation}} and {{superadmin}} admins.
## {{/locale_languages/edit}} should be accessible to {{translation}}, {{support}}, {{policy_and_abuse}}, and {{superadmin}} admins.
### {{translation}} and {{superadmin}} admins should be able to edit any field.
### {{support}} admins should only be able to edit the “Support available” checkbox.
### {{policy_and_abuse}} admins should only be able to edit the “Abuse support available” checkbox.
# Remove the “Support available” and “Abuse support available” checkboxes (and associated code) from {{/languages/new}} and {{/languages/whatever/edit}}. (You can leave the columns in the database for the time being; we will probably rename the table to {{work_languages}} for clarity and we can drop them in that migration.)
# Allow work languages to be created and edited only by admins with the {{support}} or {{superadmin}} role.

Note: The existing Languages page isn’t linked in the admin navigation. We can cope with this also being true for Locale Languages for now, although ideally we will probably want a menu that contains Locales, Work Languages, and Locale Languages.

h1. Deploy notes

TBD.

h1. Testing

h3. Before & after the deploy

We’ll need to compare some things *before and after* the deploy:

# check the list of languages on the support and abuse forms before the deploy, and ensure they are the same after we deploy
# choose a few Languages from the Languages filter on {{/admin_posts}} and ensure the same posts are listed for it before and after we deploy
# choose a few Languages from the Languages filter on {{/faqs}} and ensure the same FAQ categories and questions/answers are listed for it before and after we deploy
# log in as a {{superadmin}} or {{translation}} admin, go to the Locales page, and follow the Edit link for a few locales to ensure their associated Language is the same before and after we deploy

h3. After the deploy

*Note:* Just to be very safe here, let’s {color:#ff5630}+*not*+{color} edit any existing languages, locales, etc – add a new one first and then edit.

*After* the deploy, log in as a {{translation}} or {{superadmin}} and:

# test the pages in Item 3 of the “Overview of changes” section
#  test the pages in Item 4 of the “Overview of changes” section
# create a new locale language
# create a new locale using a new locale language 
# post a new translation of an admin post and make sure
## it shows up when filtering admin posts for the correct Language
## the original post shows the correct language in its list of available translations
# post a new translation of an FAQ and make sure
## it shows up when filtering FAQs for the correct Language
# create a new locale language and ensure it is included on the {{/support}} page when you check “Support available” and on the {{/abuse_reports/new}} page when you check “Abuse support available”

column1: Option to ban a user and delete all their creations deletes other users' replies to spammer's comments and causes 500 errors
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

h2. For deleting other users' replies:

# Log in as a user whose creations you don’t mind deleting
# Comment on a work and keep the URL for your comment handy
# Comment again
# Log out
# Log in as a different user
# Reply to the comment from Step 2 and keep the URL for this reply handy 
# Log out
# Log in as an admin with the superadmin or policy_and_abuse role
# Ban the user from Step 1 for spam
## Manage Users > Find Users
## In “Name,” enter the user’s name
## Check “Exact match only” for “Search settings”
## Press “Find”
## Follow the appropriate “Details” link in the results table
## Under “Record Warnings, Suspensions, or Notes,” choose “Spammer: ban and delete all creations”
## Fill in some text under “Notes”
## Press “Update”
# Attempt to access the reply from Step 6

h2. For causing a 500 error:

# Log in as a user whose creations you don’t mind deleting
# Comment on a work
# Reply to your comment, still using the same account
# Log out
# Repeat Steps 8 & 9 from “For deleting other users' replies”

h1. What happens

A 404 error in the case of “For deleting other users' replies”. That is, the reply gets deleted as well, even though it’s not by the spammer.

In the case of “For causing a 500 error,” a 500 error.

h1. What should happen

With “For deleting other users' replies,” the reply should still exist, or at the very least, you should be warned that it will delete replies.

In “For causing a 500 error,” there should not be an error.

h1. Notes

[destroy_user_creations|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/71d6d4d1d92abf4fceca72c782eee5576133fb2c/app/controllers/admin/admin_users_controller.rb#L140-L150] uses destroy on all creations, but comments aren’t supposed to be destroyed that way. They should be removed using [destroy_or_mark_deleted|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/71d6d4d1d92abf4fceca72c782eee5576133fb2c/lib/acts_as_commentable/comment_methods.rb#L24-L33]. This resolves both issues.

This is easiest to observe on production.

# Search > Works

But to reproduce it:

# Log in

## Post  > New Work
## Fill in required fields
## Press Post
# Post a new work with just one canonical relationship tag
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required fields
## Fill in Relationships with a canonical relationship tag

## Post > New Work

## Press Post
# Search > Works
# In “Any field,” enter {{otp: true}} without quotation marks
# For “Sort by,” choose “Date Posted”
# Press “Search”

h1. What happens

On production, the results contain:

* works with no relationship, posted as late as May 17 (the time of this issue’s creation)
** specs indicate this is *not* desired behavior, and [works with no relationship should be otp: false|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/47cc03880769f4256456598e94eed99a8d6e0faf/spec/models/work_spec.rb#L272-L276]
* works with one relationship, posted on May 12 or earlier (possibly related: May 12 is when we deployed Rails 7)

It’s worth noting that existing zero-relationship works are getting otp: true set when they are reindexed for other reasons. We’re going to have to reindex all the things if works can retroactively have their otp field set incorrectly. 😭 

h1. What should happen

It should contain any works with only one relationship (or multiple variations of the same canonical relationship).

h1. Notes

If you use database access to check a work that should show up but doesn’t, you’ll see:

*  {{Work.find(000).otp}} returns {{true}} as expected
* but {{$elasticsearch.get(index: WorkIndexer.index_name, id: '000')}} includes {{"otp"=>false}}

I used the Work Search for simplicity, but this is also observable by entering {{otp: true}} in the “Search within results” field on a tag page.

h1. Deploy notes

This will require us to reindex works.
