column1: Custom cop for calling html_safe on translated strings
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Let’s add another custom Rubocop cop for a common nitpick: Uses of {{t().html_safe}}.

[html_safe|https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/String.html#method-i-html_safe] does _not_ escape HTML in strings, instead it marks strings as safe so they are inserted into the HTML with no escaping. This is often used if there is some HTML in the translation, such as links. However, due to the lack of escaping, {{html_safe}} should not be called on potentially unsafe user-generated text, like interpolation variables in translations.

The {{t()}} method provides another way to [use translations with HTML|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/i18n.html#using-safe-html-translations]: Keys ending with {{_html}} or {{.html}} are considered html safe so they can contain HTML tags. But their interpolations are still escaped. Combined with using Rails helpers like [link_to|https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActionView/Helpers/UrlHelper.html#method-i-link_to] and the [tag helpers|https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActionView/Helpers/TagHelper.html#method-i-tag] that automatically handle marking their output as html safe, interpolations and translations can still contain all needed HTML without any calls to {{html_safe}}.

So, let’s recommend using translations keys ending with {{_html}} or {{.html}} when code calls {{html_safe}} on the {{t()}} or {{translate()}} methods.

The [PR for AO3-6691|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4763] has an example of adding a custom cops and tests that may be helpful. Furthermore, here is some initial code for the custom cop from ticking instant, but it will need some adjustments:

{code:ruby}module CustomCops
  class TranslateHtmlSafe < RuboCop::Cop::Base
    MSG = 'Instead of calling t(key).html_safe in views, try renaming the key so that it ends in _html or .html, and remove the .html_safe call'.freeze

    def_node_matcher :html_safe_translate?, <<~PATTERN
      (send (send nil? :t ...) :html_safe)
    PATTERN

    # optimization: don't call `on_send` unless
    # the method name is in this list
    RESTRICT_ON_SEND = [:html_safe].freeze

    def on_send(node)
      return unless html_safe_translate?(node)

      add_offense(node)
    end
  end
end{code}



This cop will complain about the [commonly used greetings|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/47cc03880769f4256456598e94eed99a8d6e0faf/config/locales/mailers/en.yml#L72-L74] in the mailers, {{mailer.general.greeting.formal}} and {{mailer.general.greeting.informal.addressed}}. Let's rename these locale keys to {{mailer.general.greeting.formal_html}} and {{mailer.general.greeting.informal.addressed_html}} and remove the {{html_safe}} calls on their translations in the mailer view files.

*Testing*

No manual tests required, automated testing is sufficient.

h2. Works

## Leave this browser/window open

## Reload the page
## Follow the “Unreviewed Comment (1)” link at the top of the post
## Press “Approve” on the relevant comment
# In the browser/window where you are logged in as the other user, edit the comment to completely change the text and put it back in moderation
## Follow the “Edit” link
## Delete all of the comment text you’ve written and replace it with entirely different text
## Press “Update”

h1. What happens

h2. Admin posts

The admin mailing list and commenter all get notified when a comment is left (step 8b) and when it is edited (steps 8e and 10c). All of the emails say, “Comments on this work are moderated and will not appear until approved by the work creator.” 

h2. Works

The work creator gets notified when a comment is left (step 6b) and when it is edited (steps 6e and 8c). The emails for edited comments say, “Comments on this work are moderated and will not appear until approved by the work creator.”

h1. What should happen

h2. Admin posts

The emails to both the mailing list and the commenter should all say, “Comments on this news post are moderated and will not appear until approved.”

The emails to the admin mailing list should also include a link that says, “Review comments on [Admin Post Title].”

h2. Works

The emails the work creator gets about the edited comments should say, “Comments on this work are moderated and will not appear until you approve them.”

They should also include a link that says, “Review comments on [Work Title].”

(The behavior in the emails for new comments is already correct.)

h1. Testing notes

It would be a good idea to also make sure the text and link *aren’t* included in the emails when you

* make a very minor edit (e.g., a typo fix) to an approved comment, since this doesn’t put the comment back in moderation
* post and edit a comment on a work and news post without moderation

h1. Deploy notes

The Resque workers need to be restarted.

column1: Update index tasks to include warning
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The existing index tasks will delete, re-create, and then populate Elasticsearch indexes ([https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/f47e0f5f9f0988907483b0250c3facf18b8d877e/lib/tasks/search.rake#L13-L43|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/f47e0f5f9f0988907483b0250c3facf18b8d877e/lib/tasks/search.rake#L13-L43|smart-link] ). Realistically, this should only ever be done when we’re taking down time, to avoid a weird and inconsistent experience for end users.

To improve these tasks, we want to do a couple things:

# Update the {{index_*}} tasks to include a warning like we added in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6624|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6624|smart-link]. We can word it something like {{Running this task will result in search failures and inconsistent results. Is the Archive currently taking down time to avoid problems? Enter YES to continue}}
# Add {{reindex_*}} tasks, similar to [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/f47e0f5f9f0988907483b0250c3facf18b8d877e/lib/tasks/search.rake#L45-L56|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/f47e0f5f9f0988907483b0250c3facf18b8d877e/lib/tasks/search.rake#L45-L56|smart-link] for the remaining indexes (tags, pseuds, bookmarks). We can probably use the skip_delete ([https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/f47e0f5f9f0988907483b0250c3facf18b8d877e/app/models/search/indexer.rb#L115|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/f47e0f5f9f0988907483b0250c3facf18b8d877e/app/models/search/indexer.rb#L115|smart-link] ) keyword arg to avoid re-inventing the wheel.

*Testing*

On staging, we can try deleting the indexes and running the tasks to make sure an error occurs (since the indexes wouldn’t be created with the new task).

Doing the count query directly in the DB is more efficient. So for these queries it depends on the query - for count queries, those usually can’t be eliminated with includes and can be left as is and factored into the test with {{perform_linear_number_of_queries}}. I find that the query logs generated by the test are the best way to see the generated queries and their N+1 behaviour to then match up to what code is creating them and what to put into {{includes}}. I found that I needed a bunch of experience with the codebase before I could match up queries to code to tackle N+1 issues like this one. column1: Chapter bylines do not update when a co-creator changes their username or pseud
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
If a work has multiple co-creators, with different ones for different chapters, and one co-creator changes their username or pseud, the chapters do not update with the new one. 

*Steps to reproduce:*

+Example 1: A co-creator changes their username+

# Log in
# Post a work with multiple chapters
# Invite a co-creator to the work
# Log in as the other account and accept the invitation
# View the work on your dashboard
# View each individual chapter so you can see the “Chapter by…” byline
# Preferences > Change My User Name (you may want to switch accounts, depending on which one’s name you’d like to change)
# Fill in required information
# Press "Change User Name"
# Press "OK" to confirm the name change
# Return to your dash
# Click on the work
# Note that the chapter bylines still have your old name

+Example 2: A co-creator changes their pseud+

# Log in
# Hi, username! > My Preferences > Manage My Pseuds > New Pseud
# Fill in the "Name" field with a name for your pseud, e.g. Pseud To Change
# Press "Create"
# Post a work with multiple chapters and invite a co-creator
# Log in as the invited account and accept the invitation
# View the work on your dashboard
# View the individual chapters (they should show “Chapter by Pseud to change (yourname), cocreatorname”
# Preferences > Manage My Pseuds (you may want to switch accounts, depending on which one’s pseud you’d like to change)
# Under Pseud To Change, follow "Edit"
# Fill in "Name" with something different, e.g. Changed Pseud
# Press "Update"
# Visit the work again
# Note that the chapters still show your old pseud

*What should happen*

The chapter byline should be updated as soon as possible.

*Notes*

If a chapter was authored a pseud that doesn’t match your username, editing which pseud is attached to the work does not update the username in the chapter byline. If you post the work and then change your name so the chapters say “Chapter by pseud_A (old_name)” and then edit the work and change the pseud it’s attached to on the edit work form, it results in the byline pseud updating but not the username so the chapters say “Chapter by pseud_B (old_name)”

column1: Low Vision Default: On narrow screens, expanded navigation menus hide behind top-level options and overflow onto main content
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in on a smallish mobile device in portrait mode, or in a browser window narrowed to resemble mobile
# In the Customize section of the footer, choose the Low Vision Default Skin
# Once the skin is applied, select one of the items in the main navigation that usually has a dropdown menu in the default skin, e.g., “Hi, username!” or “Fandoms” 

h1. What happens

The expanded options are underneath the main options, making it hard to see and use them, and then they overflow the header and spill onto the main content, making _that_ difficult to see and use as well. Furthermore, you can’t tell which menu you have open because the selected item has a solid grey background that is almost indistinguishable from the grey gradient on the unselected items.

Note that if you’re on a device with a large screen, the menus function correctly. 

!Screenshot 2024-07-05 at 7.59.05 PM.png|width=665,height=771,alt="Broken mobile screenshot. 'Fandoms' is selected, prompting a vertical list of black buttons to appear under the top-level navigation items and on top of the main content area, albeit with some aspects of the main content (the icon and subnavigation) overlapping them."!



h1. What should happen

They expanded items should appear between the selected menu item and the next one. The selected menu item (e.g., “Hi, username!”) should take on a red background instead of a grey that is so difficult to distinguish from the button styles.

Basically, it should work the same on narrow screens as on big screens.



!Screenshot 2024-07-05 at 7.59.41 PM.png|width=1177,height=767,alt="Correctly functioning header navigation. The selected 'Hi, sarken2' option has a red background instead of a grey gradient that looks like a button. Below the 'Hi, sarken2' item, the My Dashboard, My Subscription, My Works, My Bookmarks, My Sign-ups, My Assignments, My History, My Preferences, and Tag Wrangling options are clearly visible, listed vertically with black backgrounds. After those options, the button-style top-level menu options (Post, Log Out, Fandoms, Browse, Search) resume."!

h1. Deploy notes

An admin with the superadmin role will need to copy the updated CSS into Low Vision Default _before_ merging (to ensure it gets recached on deploying):

# Log in as admin
# Skins > Approved Skins
# Locate Low Vision Default in the table and click the title to open the skin show page
# Follow the Edit link at the bottom to access the skin edit page
# Copy the entire contents of public/stylesheets/masters/low_vision_default/low_vision_default_site_screen_.css from the pull request
# Paste into the CSS field on the skin edit page
# Press Update to save
# Merge the pull request

h1. Testing

Then testers should check the behavior of Low Vision Default on multiple screen sizes and browsers. The correct colors for the navigation:

# Top-level items should be button-style with black border and dark text by default.
# Top-level items that are being hovered over with the mouse, have keyboard focus, or are the parent of an open dropdown menu, should have red backgrounds with light grey text and border.
# Dropdown menu items should have black background with -light grey- white text and border.
# Dropdown menu items that are being hovered over with the mouse or that have keyboard focus should have light grey backgrounds with dark grey/black text.

column1: Admin Roles: Restrict admin access to wrangling-related areas
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Overview

As part of the admin roles epic (AO3-5518), we need to restrict admin access to wrangling-related areas. 

These areas are spread across a number of controllers, but should be governed by one policy: {{WranglingPolicy}}. The affected controllers and pages (actions):

# {{TagWranglersController}}
## Wrangler pages, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers/testy|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers/testy] ({{show}})
## Wrangling assignments, i.e. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers] ({{index}}, {{create}}, {{destroy}})
## Wrangler activity report ({{report_csv}})
# {{TagWranglingsController}}
## Mass bins, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=fandoms|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=fandoms] ({{index}}, {{wrangle}})
## Wrangling Tools, i.e. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings] ({{index}})
# {{UnsortedTagsController}}
## Unsorted bin, i.e. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/unsorted_tags|https://test.archiveofourown.org/unsorted_tags] ({{index}}, {{mass_update}})
# {{TagsController}}
## Tag edit pages, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/edit|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/edit] ({{edit}}, {{update}})
## New tag page, i.e. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/new|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/new] ({{new}}, {{create}})
## Tag bins, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/wrangle?show=characters|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/wrangle?show=characters] ({{wrangle}}, {{mass_update}})
# {{WranglingGuidelinesController}}
## Manage wrangling guidelines, e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/wrangling_guidelines/manage|https://test.archiveofourown.org/wrangling_guidelines/manage] ({{manage}}, {{update_positions}})
## New wrangling guidelines, e.g., [+https://test.archiveofourown.org/wrangling_guidelines/new+|https://test.archiveofourown.org/wrangling_guidelines/new] ({{new}}, {{create}})
## Edit wrangling guidelines, e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/wrangling_guidelines/2/edit|https://test.archiveofourown.org/wrangling_guidelines/2/edit] ({{edit}}, {{update}})
## Delete wrangling guidelines ({{destroy}})

Admins with the {{tag_wrangling}} or {{superadmin}} roles should have access to all of these actions. 

Admins with the {{policy_and_abuse}} role should have read-only access to:

* the mass bins ({{TagWranglingsController#index}}, but not {{TagWranglingsController#wrangle}})
* unsorted bin ({{UnsortedTagsController#index}}, but not {{UnsortedTagsController#mass_update}})
* tag bins ({{TagsController#wrangle}}, but not {{TagsController#mass_update}})
* tag edit pages ({{TagsController#edit}}, but not {{TagsController#update}} )

To make coding, reviewing, and testing manageable, each controller will have a separate issue. 

The issues can be worked on in any order. 

The final pull request will need to hide the major navigational elements: 

* the “Tag Wrangling” item in the admin navigation from all admin roles except {{superadmin}}, {{policy_and_abuse}}, and {{tag_wrangling}} 
* the sidebar on [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/search|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/search] and [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/testing|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/testing] from all admin roles except {{superadmin}} and {{tag_wrangling}}

There should be a mailer preview for the {{batch_kudo_notification}} email.

The amount of guest and user kudos should be flexible and controlled with [url parameters|https://www.bigbinary.com/blog/rails-5-2-allows-passing-request-params-to-action-mailer-previews], e.g. {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/kudo_mailer/batch_kudo_notification?user_count=5&guest_count=10}}.

To make the previews' locale selector work, the {{I18n.with_locale}} block should be moved outside the mailer method, into [RedisMailQueue#deliver_kudos|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/93f8571483aa496265f8fa165edb52c4940fa478/app/models/redis_mail_queue.rb#L40]. There should be a cucumber test for sending a translated kudos email to a user.

This is also a good opportunity to update the locale keys used in the mail to the [current I18n standards|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Internationalization-%28i18n%29-Standards]. Particularly, the keys used in the HTML mail should end in {{.html}} and the {{html_safe}} calls should be removed. The keys used in the text mail should be updated to match.

*Testing*

All of the following previews should be valid mails with no translation errors and no exposed HTML, for both the HTML and text version. Selecting a locale from the dropdown that has translations for at least the footer (e.g. cs, hr, ja, ko, de, sv) should result in a translated footer, but other text may remain in English, depending on whether translations are available.

* No params: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/kudo_mailer/batch_kudo_notification|https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/kudo_mailer/batch_kudo_notification]
* One guest: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/kudo_mailer/batch_kudo_notification.html?user_count=0&guest_count=1|https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/kudo_mailer/batch_kudo_notification.html?user_count=0&guest_count=1]
* One user: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/kudo_mailer/batch_kudo_notification.html?user_count=1&guest_count=0|https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/kudo_mailer/batch_kudo_notification.html?user_count=1&guest_count=0]
* Three users, two guests: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/kudo_mailer/batch_kudo_notification.html?user_count=3&guest_count=2|https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/kudo_mailer/batch_kudo_notification.html?user_count=3&guest_count=2]

column1: claim_notification mail doesn't respect user's locale preference
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
# Log in as a user whose emails you have access to.
# Change that user's "Your locale" preference to a locale that has translations for {{claim_notification}}, e.g. German, Danish, Japanese, Russian or Czech.
# Log in with an account with archivist permissions (e.g. testy)
# Use the Import Work form to create a new work and specify the name and email of the user from step 1 in the “Archiving for others” section of the form, selecting the “Import for others” checkbox

*What happens*

The user you logged in as in step 1 receives an email in English.

*What should happen*

The user receives an email in the locale selected in step 2.

*Notes*

The {{claim_notification}} mail is only sent when importing for a user with an existing account. When importing for an email without an associated account, {{invitation_to_claim}} is sent instead. That means {{claim_notification}} can and should be localised according to the existing account's preferences.

However, (outside of tests and mailer previews) {{claim_notification}} is currently only ever called with an ExternalAuthor, never with a User. It should be the other way around: The mailer should only be called with the User and never with an ExternalAuthor. At the same time, the {{I18n.with_locale}} call should be moved from the UserMailer to the external author model where the mailer is called.

There should be a cucumber test for this scenario, it should reuse some of the testing steps added for [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6764|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6764|smart-link].

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
There should be a [mailer preview|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Internationalization-%28i18n%29-Standards#user-content-Mailer_previews] for the {{invite_increase_notification}} email.

The invite count should be flexible and controlled with a URL parameter.

To make the previews' locale selector work, the {{I18n.with_locale}} block should be moved outside the mailer method, to where {{deliver}}/{{deliver_later}} is called on the mailer. There should be a cucumber test for sending a translated {{invite_increase_notification}} email to a user to cover this change.

This is also a good opportunity to update the locale keys used in the mail to the [current I18n standards|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Internationalization-%28i18n%29-Standards]. Particularly, the keys used in the HTML mail (except for the greeting) should end in {{.html}} and the {{html_safe}} calls should be removed. The keys used in the text mail should be updated to match.

*Testing*

The preview at [https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/user_mailer/invite_increase_notification|https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/user_mailer/invite_increase_notification] and [https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/user_mailer/invite_increase_notification?total=7|https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/user_mailer/invite_increase_notification?total=7] should be valid mails with no translation errors and no exposed HTML, for both the HTML and text version. Selecting a locale from the dropdown that has translations for at least the footer (e.g. cs, hr, ja, ko, de, sv) should result in a translated footer, but other text may remain in English, depending on whether translations are available.

We had to do some larger changes to the email sending, so we’d also like to test that:

# Log in as a user whose emails you have access to
# Change that user's "Your locale" preference to a non-English locale
# Go to your dashboard and follow “Invitations”
# Follow “Request Invitations”
# Fill out the required fields and press “Send Request“
# Log in as an admin

column1: Create previews for internationalized mailers
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
To make testing the translated emails simpler and quicker for Translation, we’d like to have [mailer previews|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Developing-mailers#user-content-Mailer_previews] for all the emails that are internationalized and can have translated versions sent out by the archive. The previews should cover variants of the mailers that are relevant for translation, such as the different kinds of creations (series/chapters) that a creator can be added to for a co-creator notification.

The locale selector in the mailer previews should be functional. This means that {{I18n.with_locale}}  should be moved outside the mailer method, to where {{deliver}}/{{deliver_later}} is called on the mailer. We’d like to have Cucumber tests to make sure that this doesn’t break sending the translated emails.

Full details on the expected email variants will be provided in the individual issues.

Also note: This tag exists on production as a freeform.

And a third note, because why not: This seems to work in tag nominations as well, and it causes 500s when the mods review the tag set. 

An easy to describe way:

# Log in as an admin
# Go to the edit page for a tag, any tag, e.g. https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/A%20Test%20Tag/edit
# In the Name field, enter the [zero width space character|https://unicode-explorer.com/c/200B] (you can copy it from that webpage)

A slightly more confusing way:

# Log in
# Post > New Work
# Fill in the required fields
# Now, in the freeform field, enter the [zero width space character|https://unicode-explorer.com/c/200B] (you can copy it from that webpage) *but do not press the comma or enter or anything else*. Just put the character in the field and scroll away without making it pop up above the field
# Press Post

You are left with a tag with no name, like our friend {{/tags/%E2%80%8B/edit}} .

h1. What should happen

The tag should not be created/renamed.

These steps are different from [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6266|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6266|smart-link], so this is getting its own issue, especially since a whole bunch of us just spent a few hours digging into the issue because we didn’t see that one while looking for an issue related to tags. ## Log in, if you’re not already
## Browse > Tags > Tag Sets > New Tag Set

## Check “Currently taking nominations?”

## Press “Submit”

## Follow the “Nominate” link from the Tag Set’s page
## Enter any tags you like – I’m entering the fandom “Star Trek” and the character “Spock”
## Press “Submit”
# Now we’ll edit our nomination to reproduce the bug
## Follow the “Edit” link from your Nomination’s page
## Use the remove option (×) to remove one of the tags – I’m removing “Spock”
## Press “Submit”

The tag you removed is no longer in your nominations, but instead, it’s replaced with the blank space tag. 

You can see it on your nominations page and the tag set mods can see it when reviewing nominations. (Except for when it causes a 500. More on that in another issue!)

I’d love to put images here, but Jira doesn’t recognize any file type I try to upload.

I’m not sure if the autocomplete JavaScript is to blame or something else – please do update the Components if this turns out to be either just front end or just back end.

Please also ensure the Synonyms field autocomplete on a canonical tag’s edit page does not suggest the nameless tag when you press the spacebar. Note: Holding onto this issue while we finalize the text.

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a superadmin, policy_and_abuse, or support admin
# Go to Settings
# Check the boxes for the following settings:
##  “Account creation enabled”
## “Account creation requires invitation”
## “Invite from queue enabled (People can add themselves to the queue and invitations are sent out automatically)”
# Press Update to Save
# Return to the Settings page
# Enter 0 in “Number of people to invite from the queue at once” 
# Press Update to save

h1. What happens

You get an error telling you 

h4. Sorry! We couldn't save this admin setting because:

* Invite from queue number must be greater than 0. To *disable* invites, uncheck the appropriate setting.

Except doing that also disables people’s ability to _add_ themselves to the queue. You have to work around it by setting “How often (in days) should we invite people from the queue” to a high number (this field will accept 0, but 0 currently behaves the same as 1).

h1. What should happen

You should be able to set either “Number of people to invite from the queue at once” or “How often (in days) should we invite people from the queue” (or both of them) to 0 if you want to pause sending invitations while still allowing people to join the queue.

When either/both of these are set to 0:

# [https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests|https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests] should say: If you have already requested an invitation, you can [check your position on the waiting list|http://localhost:3000/invite_requests/status]. There are currently X people on the waiting list. We aren’t sending invitations right now, but they’ll be back soon. For now, you can still join the waiting list.”
# [http://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status|http://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status] should say: There are currently X people on the waiting list. We are not sending invitations, but you can still check your position on the waiting list.”
## Once you submit your email address, if your invitation has not been sent, the resulting text should say: You are currently number *X* on our waiting list! We aren’t sending invitations right now, but they’ll be back soon. When we start sending them again, this page will tell you when to expect yours.”

When [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6712|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6712|smart-link] is done, only the first paragraph provided for each scenario should appear, and it should not be possible to resend invitations. For ease of reference, the text that should appear:

# *If the user checks the status of their invitation less than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is initially sent*, the text should say: Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there.
# *If the user checks the status of their invitation more than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is initially sent*, the text should say: Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there.
# *If the user checks the status of their invitation less than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is resent*, the text should say: Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date] and resent on [resent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there.
# *If the user checks the status of their invitation more than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is resent*, the text should say: Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date] and resent on [resent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there.

h1. Notes

A problem for future us: if we _are_ sending invitations, the text says, “We are sending out 1 invitations per day” even when “How often (in days) should we invite people from the queue” is set to 2 or more days.

If you have a work that

* was written in a script that doesn’t use spaces to indicate words (for our purposes, those are {{CHARACTER_COUNT_SCRIPTS: ["Han", "Hiragana", "Katakana", "Thai"]}})
* *and* was posted before [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2046|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2046|smart-link]

*then* the word count for the work is still incorrect _unless_ the work creator has edited the work text since December 23, 2018.

To fix this once and for all, we want a version of the rake task in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2378|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2378|smart-link] that will run on *all works* created before December 25, 2018 (let’s give it a little buffer to allow for the possibility it may have taken some time for the original task to complete), regardless of language.

Word counts can be broken like so:

{noformat}chapter.update_column(:word_count, 9001)
work.update_column(:word_count, 9001){noformat}

Check the staging site to make sure the blurb and meta for the works now display the broken word counts.

Then run the task and check the blurbs and meta again to confirm that:

# the word count for the work created before December 25, 2018 is fixed
# the word count for the work created after December 25, 2018 is still broken

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Create a skin and apply to make it public
## Log in as a user
## Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins > Create Site Skin
## Fill in required fields
## Check “Apply to make public”
## Save
## Log out
# Approve the skin and add it to the chooser
## Log in as a superadmin
## Skins > Approval Queue
## Locate the skin from Step 1
## Check “Approve”
## Press “Update” to save
## Skins > Approved Skins
## Locate the skin from Step 1
## Check “Cache” and “Chooser”
## Press “Update” to save
# Unapprove the skin and remove it from the chooser
## Skins > Approved Skins
## Locate the skin from Step 1
## Check “Unapprove,” “Uncache,” and “Not in chooser”
## Press “Update” to save

h1. What happens

The skin is unapproved and uncached, but stays in the chooser in the footer.

(Bonus fun, the update message will list the skin name once for each of its attributes that you update. In this case, the skin gets unapproved and uncached, so it says “The following skins were updated: Skin Title, Skin Title”)

h1. What should happen

Skins should absolutely not be in the chooser if they are not approved for public use. 

Either you should get an error telling you to remove it from the chooser before you unapprove it, or unapproving a skin should also remove it from the chooser. 

(We _could_ make it so skins included in the chooser also have to be {{official: true}}, but it’s better to get the {{in_chooser}} column set to {{false}} so re-approving the skin in the future doesn’t put it right back into the chooser.)

h1. Notes

{{official}} is the name of the column controlled by approving/unapproving skins.

The database column {{in_chooser}} is not getting updated; it's not a simple case of caching.

Featuring/unfeaturing has the same bug: if you try to unapproved it and unfeature it at the same time, it only unapproves. The {{featured}} column remains set to {{true}}.

16/Dec/24 6:20 PM;557058:48d6a38e-168b-4aa7-a58d-a1853a844295;[~accountid:5c4fbe624c070827c2a1e3f1] per the examples at the top of [https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveModel/Dirty.html#method-i-changed-3F|https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveModel/Dirty.html#method-i-changed-3F|smart-link] , {{changed?}} always returns false after the object is persisted (either via {{save}} or {{update}}) – so it needs to be called before any {{update}} is done.

{{changed?}} detects if an object in memory is “dirty” – that is, there are changes that haven’t been saved to the database yet. That will be the case when the box is toggled “for real”, but in the case where someone manually changes the box (and it isn’t sent via {{params}}), {{changed?}} will be false and we know the object wasn’t really updated.

column1: "Automatically flagged as spam" email gets sent when hiding works manually
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When the “Automatically hide spam works” setting is turned off, works flagged as spam are marked “Akismet Reported As Spam: true”, but not hidden and no email is sent. If that work is later manually hidden by an admin using the “Hide Work” button, the user receives the “flagged as spam” email instead of the “hidden by admin” email. This is misleading because the spam email tells the user their work was “flagged by our automated system as spam and hidden until it can be reviewed by our Policy & Abuse team” when this is not the case.

The “hide work” button should only ever send the “hidden by admin” email regardless of whether the work was flagged by Akismet or not. The “flagged as spam” email should only be sent when the work is automatically hidden (when the setting is on) or when the admin uses the “Mark as spam” button (on the work or from the spam queue). 

h2.  Testing:

# Log in as a policy_and_abuse admin or superadmin
# Locate a work in the unreviewed spam queue
# Make sure you have access to the account’s email address 
# Use the “Hide work” button to hide the work as an admin
# Check that the email you receive is the “[AO3] Your work has been hidden by the Policy & Abuse team” email and not the “[AO3] Your work was hidden as spam” email

# Unhide the work
# Unspam the work (or find a different work that isn’t flagged as spam)
# Use the “Mark as spam” button to hide the work as spam
# Check that you receive the spam email this time

column1: Editing a canonical fandom tag that has been nominated in a tag set incorrectly marks the fandom nomination as not parented
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a tag wrangler
# Create a tag set
## Browse > Tags > Tag Sets > New Tag Set
## Fill in required information
## Check “Currently taking nominations?” to enable nominations and expose nomination settings
## Set the “Fandom nomination limit” to 5 (the number doesn’t matter)
## Press “Submit”
# Nominate a canonical fandom that have parent tags (i.e., belong to a media tag)
## Follow the “Nominate” link from your tag set page
## On the nominations form, enter the name of a canonical fandom in the first Fandom field
## Press “Submit”
## Leave this page open – we’ll come back to it in Step 5
# Edit the fandom tag you nominated in Step 3
## In a new tab or window, go to the edit page for the fandom tag you nominated in Step 3: {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/TAG%20NAME/edit}}
## Press “Save changes” – no need to actually make any changes
# Review the nominations
## Follow the “Back to [tag set title”] link from your tag nomination page (the page you’ll be on immediately after submitting your nominations)
## Follow “Review Nominations”

h1. What happens

The name of the nominated fandom will appear in regular (not bold) text, and the tool tip that appears when you hover over it will say, "This is a canonical tag but not associated with the specified fandom” (not “This is a canonical tag“).

Checking the {{TagNomination}} in the database will show {{parented: false}}, e.g.

{noformat}[#<FandomNomination:0x00007f06b77c89a8                                       
  id: 6996529,                                                               
  type: "FandomNomination",                                                  
  tag_set_nomination_id: 347002,                                             
  fandom_nomination_id: nil,                                                 
  tagname: "A Spy Among Friends (TV)",
  parent_tagname: nil,
  approved: false,
  rejected: false,
  created_at: Thu, 12 Sep 2024 05:10:52.000000000 UTC +00:00,
  updated_at: Thu, 12 Sep 2024 05:10:52.000000000 UTC +00:00,
  canonical: true,
  exists: true,
  parented: false,
  synonym: nil>] {noformat}

h1. What should happen

The name of the nominated fandom will appear in bold text, and the tool tip that appears when you hover over it will say, “This is a canonical tag.”

Checking the {{TagNomination}} in the database will show {{parented: true}}, e.g.

{noformat}#<FandomNomination:0x00007f06b6a169b8
 id: 6978493,          
 type: "FandomNomination",
 tag_set_nomination_id: 345844,
 fandom_nomination_id: nil,
 tagname: "Tom Swift (TV 2022)",
 parent_tagname: nil,  
 approved: false,      
 rejected: false,      
 created_at: Mon, 09 Sep 2024 17:27:25.000000000 UTC +00:00,
 updated_at: Mon, 09 Sep 2024 17:27:25.000000000 UTC +00:00,
 canonical: true,      
 exists: true,         
 parented: true,       
 synonym: nil> {noformat}

h1. Notes

*Note: Just leaving this here for posterity. We figured out how to reliably reproduce the bug.*

It _seems_ like the {{set_parented}} callback might not always be running. We recently (AO3-6783, deployed August 13, about a month ago) started skipping it {{if blank_tagname?}}, but as you can see from the examples, the tag name doesn’t appear to be blank, nor do the nominations appear to have been edited. (The tags also appear to have had their parents before the nominations were created. So it’s not a case of someone nominating the fandom before it had a media.) 

But the timing is suspicious, and I checked the code inside the {{set_parented}} callback, and confirmed it _should_ be running [the code|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/f607097eacad333ee18fc92d3578026802f801e0/app/models/tagset_models/tag_nomination.rb#L74-L78] that sets {{parented = true}}

{noformat}spy_nom = tag_set.tag_nominations.where(tagname: "A Spy Among Friends (TV)").first
tagname = "A Spy Among Friends (TV)"

(tag = Tag.find_by_name(tagname)) && !tag.parents.empty? && spy_nom.get_parent_tagname.blank? || tag.parents.collect(&:name).include?(spy_nom.
get_parent_tagname)
 => true {noformat}

Some random theories that turned out *not* to be correct:

* it only happens if the nominated {{tagname}} has parentheses
* it only happens if the tag has a different {{sortable_name}} than the nominated {{tagname}}
* it only happens if the tag has syns
* it matters how many times the tag is nominated (e.g., it only happens if there is 1 nomination or >1 nomination)

Only fandom tags appear to be affected.

column1: Update cookie rotator to force Rails 6 compatibility
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

The rationale to this is very similar to what the Mastodon folks describe in [https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/pull/26023|https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/pull/26023|smart-link] . Basically, the Rails upgrade config was a tad misleading and we weren’t prepared for the new cookie when the corresponding release went out. In this story, we need to change the existing cookie rotator to force everyone to be compatible with Rails 6.X instead (AKA use SHA1 cookies). Only once that is done can we safely deploy Rails 7.0 config defaults.

The deploy is much faster on staging, so it’s hard to replicate the issue we had in prod. But, we should have 2-5 testers logged in and actively browsing staging as the PR is merged (until the message appears in slack that the deploy is done). No forced log outs or similar should happen.

column1: When an email is blocked from guest comments, also block it from requesting invitations
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When an email is used for guest comments by other than its owner, and that person contacts us about the unwanted emails, currently we can block their email from receiving any further notifications about existing guest comments, and prevent it from being used for any future guest comments.  We would like to extend this to also prevent their email from being used to request invitations.

Refer to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4536|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4536|smart-link] for more information on the current function.

When an email is blocked, the invitation queue should be searched and the email removed from it if it is currently in the queue.

If someone tries to add a blocked email to the invitation queue, the email should not be added to the queue and they should receive this error message:

“Email has been blocked at the owner's request. That means it can't be used for invitations. Please check the address to make sure it's yours to use and contact AO3 Support if you have any questions.”

*Testing*

column1: Prevent invalid tags from being added to the autocomplete via tag sets

column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Create a tag set
## Browse > Tags > Tag Sets > New Tag Set
## Fill in required information
## Press “Submit”
# Attempt to manually add some invalid tags to the tag set
## Follow the “Edit” link on the tag set page
## Enter an invalid tag into the “Add Characters” field
### Invalid tags are longer than 100 characters or include a restricted character ({{, ^ * < > { } = ` \ %}})
## Press “Update”

h1. What happens

The tag will not actually be created, but that doesn’t stop it from appearing in the dropdown menu for signups for events using that tag set.

The invalid tag will not appear in the mod interface and cannot be removed by the mods, because it doesn’t really exist. Sarken found that tags get added to the autocomplete regardless of whether they are created:  ​[https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/7fb763ae18c05d58467a79b368c9fca3e3bd72ba/app/models/tagset_models/tag_set.rb#L122-L131|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/7fb763ae18c05d58467a79b368c9fca3e3bd72ba/app/models/tagset_models/tag_set.rb#L122-L131|smart-link]  

h1. What should happen

If someone attempts to add an invalid tag, it should not be added to the autocomplete, and an error should be given to the mod to say that “The following tags are invalid: [TAG NAME]  Please make sure that your tags are less than 100 characters long and do not contain any invalid characters.  Name of a tag cannot include the following restricted characters: , ^ * < > { } = ` \ %.

There should be text added to the tag set interface to inform mods about what isn’t allowed: 

* Please make sure that your tags are less than 100 characters long and do not contain any invalid characters.
* Name of a tag cannot include the following restricted characters: , ^ * < > { } = ` \ %

For bonus points, any existing too-long or invalid tags should be removed from the autocomplete.

Policy & Abuse and Legal would like to update the text of the DMCA Policy page [https://test.archiveofourown.org/dmca|https://test.archiveofourown.org/dmca] If possible, please also prepare the text for translation according to [our i18n Standards|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Internationalization-(i18n)-Standards]. {noformat}

DMCA Policy

The Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) establishes the procedure the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW) must follow when users of our sites, including the Archive of Our Own (AO3), reproduce copyrighted material without authorization. Specifically, 17 U.S.C. § 512 protects the OTW from potential liability when infringing content is present on our sites.

The OTW will respond promptly to notices of alleged copyright infringement that substantially comply with all legal requirements. However, we believe that transformative fanworks are legal, and we reserve the right to review the allegedly infringing content and independently determine whether it is infringing. If you have any questions about our DMCA Policy, please contact the OTW Legal committee.

Table of Contents

  1. My work was posted on AO3 without my permission. What can I do?
    • Filing a DMCA takedown notice
    • Requirements of a DMCA takedown notice
    • DMCA takedown process
  2. I was notified that my work was removed from AO3 due to a DMCA takedown notice. What can I do?
    • Filing a DMCA counternotice
    • Requirements of a DMCA counternotice
    • DMCA counter-notification process
  3. Repeat offenses

My work was posted on AO3 without my permission. What can I do?

If you encounter content on AO3 that you believe infringes on your copyright, you have the following options:

  • Submit an Abuse report: Abuse reports are evaluated by the Policy & Abuse committee for violations of the AO3 Terms of Service, and held to a very high standard of confidentiality. When submitting an Abuse report about copyright infringement, you must provide a link to the violating content on AO3 and clearly identify the original source in your report description. For more information, please refer to the Terms of Service FAQ.
  • File a DMCA takedown notice: DMCA takedown notices can only be filed by the copyright owner or someone legally authorized to act on their behalf. DMCA notices must be sent to the OTW's designated agent and comply with all legal requirements. DMCA notices are not subject to confidentiality. The OTW reserves the right to make public all DMCA notices that we receive, though some information may be redacted for privacy.

Please do not submit an Abuse report if you intend to file a DMCA notice. Submitting both an Abuse report and a DMCA notice about the same content may delay the processing of both requests.

Filing a DMCA takedown notice

To initiate a formal DMCA takedown request, contact the OTW's designated agent using the Legal committee's contact form, via email to legal@transformativeworks.org, or by mailing a letter to:

Organization for Transformative Works
228 Park Ave S #18156
New York, NY 10003-1502
Attention: Legal

Requirements of a DMCA takedown notice

column1: Include creator IDs in abuse reports of works
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When an abuse report is submitted for a work, it should include the user IDs of the work creators in the field {{cf_user_id}}:

* multiple IDs should be separated by a comma *and* listed in ascending numerical order
* a given ID should be listed only once, regardless of how many pseuds the user has on the work
* the IDs should be included even if the work is anonymous or unrevealed
* the IDs of users merely _invited_ to be co-creators should not be included
* include the IDs from WorkOriginalCreators, if available (i.e., if the work was orphaned or an approved co-creatorship was removed no more than 72 hours before the report is submitted)

If the work is an orphaned work, in addition to the above, it should also:

* replace orphan_account’s ID with the placeholder *orphanedwork* (it should come before any other user IDs)

If the work does not exist, the field should include the placeholder text: *deletedwork*

Please note that this should not be transmitted via a hidden field on the abuse report form, but rather handled in the controller/model as appropriate.

h2. Testing

Someone will need to submit reports for the following and PAC will need to verify the expected information is available and correct for:

# a work with one creator
# a work with multiple pseuds from one user, such as {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1070078}}, {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1068059}} or {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1071662}}
# an anonymous work
# an unrevealed work
# a work with a co-creator
# a work with an invited co-creator who hasn’t approved the invitation yet
# an orphaned work that was orphaned < 72 hours before the report was submitted (requires admin access to verify)
# an orphaned work that was orphaned > 72 hours before the report was submitted (requires admin access to verify)
# an orphaned work that has another non-orphan co-creator, such as {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1061393}} or {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1065483}}
# a work that doesn’t exist, such as {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/000}} or {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/777777777}}

column1: Rename the Underage warning tag
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
In order to clarify the tag's meaning, the Underage warning should be renamed to Underage Sex. This means first adding a suffix to the existing Underage Sex freeform tag (Tag Wrangling has approved this change).

h2. Renaming the tag

Renaming a tag -- typically done by wranglers in the context of changing diacritics or by admins in the context of suffix swaps -- is already set up to handle any cache expiration or reindexing via Resque.

# The existing tag [+"Underage Sex"+|https://archiveofourown.org/tags/Underage%20Sex] first needs to be renamed "Underage Sex - Freeform.".
# The "Underage" warning tag needs to be renamed "Underage Sex."

We will create rake tasks to handle these steps. While we know "Underage Sex" is a freeform on production, the task for renaming it should be able to handle it regardless of type (e.g., if it's a relationship tag, it should rename it to "Underage Sex - Relationship" instead).

h2. Code changes

These changes appear to relate to tests and new archives.

# The [+WARNING_CHAN_TAG_NAME config variable+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/config/config.yml#L227] needs to be changed from "Underage" to "Underage Sex."
# Tests need to be updated. After making the following changes, run the test suite and fix any failures.
## The [+warning created in the tag fixtures+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/test/fixtures/tags.yml#L5631-L5643] needs to be renamed Underage Sex.
## The [+warning created in the tag_seed.json file+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/script/gift_exchange/tag_seed.json#L79] needs to be renamed Underage Sex.
## The [+content used by the work import steps+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/features/step_definitions/work_import_steps.rb#L5] needs to use the new Underage Sex warning.
## The [+content used by the API helper tests+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/spec/controllers/api/api_helper.rb#L18] needs to use the new Underage Sex warning.

h2. Text changes

Text needs to be updated in several places.

# [+https://ao3.org/help/work-search-text-help.html+|https://ao3.org/help/work-search-text-help.html] ([+https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/public/help/work-search-text-help.html#L34-L35+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/public/help/work-search-text-help.html#L34])
## ""Character A/Character B" Underage Mature OR Explicit" should be ""Character A/Character B" "Underage Sex" (Mature OR Explicit)"
## "an Underage warning" should be "an Underage Sex warning"
# [+https://ao3.org/help/warning-help.html+|https://ao3.org/help/warning-help.html]
## "and Underage" should be "and Underage Sex" ([+https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/public/help/warning-help.html#L7+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/public/help/warning-help.html#L7])
## "Underage:" should be "Underage Sex:" ([+https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/public/help/warning-help.html#L53+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/public/help/warning-help.html#L53]) 
# [+https://ao3.org/first_login_help+|https://ao3.org/first_login_help]   ([+https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/app/views/home/first_login_help.html.erb#L125-L126+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/app/views/home/first_login_help.html.erb#L125-L126]) 
## "and "Underage"" should be "and "Underage Sex"" 

h2. Testing notes

In addition to ensuring the text changes mentioned above are present...

h3. *Before* the warning is renamed:

# Post a work using the Underage warning. Include the work in a series.
# Bookmark a work that has the Underage warning.
# Bookmark a series that has the Underage warning.
# Bookmark a work and add the Underage tag as a bookmarker's tag.
# Create a tag set using the Underage warning.
# Create a gift exchange that uses the tag set you made. It should be set to match on warnings.
# Get at least two people to sign up for the gift exchange and use Underage in their sign-ups. Leave sign-ups open.

h3. After the warning is renamed:

# Make sure the work posting form now says Underage Sex.
# Make sure the work you posted says Underage Sex in the blurb (the information shown in the search results) -- including the text shown when you hover over the warning symbol -- and work meta (the box at the top of the work itself).
# Make sure the series your work is in says Underage Sex in the blurb, including the text shown when you hover over the warning symbol.
# Make sure the work search form now says Underage Sex and returns the expected results. 
# Go to a page with work filters and make sure the filters now say Underage Sex and that choosing it returns the expected results.
# Go to the bookmark search form and use the autocomplete "Work tags" field to search for bookmarks of works (or series) tagged with Underage Sex. Make sure that the results are correct.
# Go back to the bookmark search form and use the autocomplete "Bookmarker's tags" field to search for bookmarks tagged with Underage Sex by the bookmarker. Make sure that the results are correct.
# Go to a page with bookmark filters (your bookmark page is probably easiest) and ensure the filters now say Underage Sex. Make sure that filtering for Underage Sex using the warnings section and the "Other bookmarker's tags to include" field return the expected results.
# Access your tag set and make sure it says Underage Sex, both on the list of tags shown to anyone accessing the tag set and on the edit page. (Note: It's possible there is a caching issue with the list of tags.)
# Access the sign-up you created for the gift exchange and make sure it says Underage Sex.
# Using another account that hasn't already signed up for the exchange, access the sign-up form and ensure that it says Underage Sex and that you can create a sign-up using the tag.
# Make sure matching for the gift exchange works as expected. 

h2. Deploy notes

The rake tasks should be run in the following order: 

* {{bundle exec rake After:add_suffix_to_underage_sex_tag }}
* {{bundle exec rake After:rename_underage_warning}}

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:

* a work ID and/or chapter ID

Make sure to test the following types of URLs:

* chapter IDs without work IDs
* other comment parameters such as ?add_comment_reply_id=###

column1: Set channel and record user agent for PAC and Support tickets
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When submitting a PAC ticket, the Zoho ticket channel (field: {{channel}}) should be set to “Abuse Form”.

When submitting a Support ticket, the Zoho ticket channel (field: {{channel}}) should be set to “Support Form”.

[https://desk.zoho.com/DeskAPIDocument#Tickets#Tickets_Createaticket|https://desk.zoho.com/DeskAPIDocument#Tickets#Tickets_Createaticket] 



Support has also requested that PAC tickets begin recording the User Agent (field: {{cf_user_agent}}) of the reporter, so that they have the information if someone submits their issue to PAC by mistake. column30:

This is also a good opportunity to update the locale keys used in the mail to the [current I18n standards|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Internationalization-%28i18n%29-Standards]. Unfortunately, the Hebrew is wonky 😞 the line with the title is back-to-front – יצירתך should be the first word from the *right*, not left, then the title and then the stuff on the right should be on the left side of the title. “נמחקה מהארכיון על ידי אדמינית” is in the right order internally, though. (x) 

There’s the same problem with the second line too: “אם יצירתך הייתה שייכת למיזם שיובא לארכיון על ידי Open Doors (דלתות פתוחות), ניתן [להפנות שאלות נוספות לצוות דלתות פתוחות|http://opendoors.transformativeworks.org/contact-open-doors/].” Within the phrases, the words are the correct order, but they should be swapped in terms of where they are in relation to the English “Open Doors”. (x) 

The third line with “[צרו קשר עם ועדת מדיניות ושימוש לרעה|http://test.archiveofourown.org/abuse_reports/new]” is fine. (/) 

For the last line, the words are in the correct order but the full stop should be on the opposite end of the line. TBH Hebrew speakers will understand the full stop problem because it happens constantly, but the swapped phrases need to be fixed.

column1: Front end issues aplenty when viewing tags in tag sets
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

We’re going to need to make two tag sets that will cover all of the possible display variations. The first steps to making either tag set are the same:

# Log in
# Browse > Tags > Tag Sets > New Tag Set
# Fill in a title
# Check “Visible tag list?” in case you need to look at it with a different account or show it to someone else

Note that for most of these steps, it doesn’t actually have to be a canonical tag, just one with the proper associations – so canonical is easier.

h2. Tag Set #1

Example: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/745|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/745] 

Most tag sets group fandoms under their media categories, but this one will cover a special case where fandoms are their own top-level sections. This happens when we extrapolate the fandoms from character and/or relationship tags rather than explicitly entering a fandom. If we have tags that don’t belong to any fandom at all, a “(No linked fandom - might need association)” section is added.

We’re also going to create an Additional Tags section with multiple sections inside it.

# Under Add Fandoms, *do not enter anything*. 
# Under Add Characters, enter 1 canonical character and 1 brand new character tag
# Under Add Additional Tags, enter at least 31 additional tags. You can paste this list: 
Action/Adventure, Alternate Universe, Alternate Universe - Battlestar Galactica Fusion, Alternate Universe - Canon, Alternate Universe - Canon Divergence, Alternate Universe - Gate is Broken, Alternate Universe - Gender Changes, Alternate Universe - Historical, Alternate Universe - Modern Setting, Alternate Universe - Pirate, Childhood, Episode: s07e16 Election Day Part I, Fluff, Fluff and Angst, Friends to Lovers, Friendship, Missing Scene, Pillow Talk, Pirates, Podfic, Podfic & Podficced Works, Podfic Available, Podfic Length: 0-10 Minutes, Podfic Length: 10-20 Minutes, Podfic Length: 20-30 Minutes, Podfic Length: 30-45 Minutes, Politics, Romance, Romantic Comedy, Science Fiction, Smut, Taco Bell
# Press Submit

h2. Tag Set #2

Example: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/751|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/751]

This tag set will have fandoms listed under media categories; rating, warning, and category sections, an unassociated characters and relationships section, and a small section of additional tags.

# Under Add Fandoms, enter some canonical fandoms from different media. It doesn’t have to be a lot, but make sure at least one medium has multiple fandoms, e.g. 3 TV Shows and 1 Video Game.
# Under Add Characters, enter 
## multiple canonical characters from some of the fandoms 
## no characters from other fandoms
## at least one character that doesn’t belong to a fandom you listed in Step 1
# Under Add Additional Tags, enter at least one additional tag (but fewer than 31)
# For the Categories, Ratings, and Warnings sections, press the “All” button on each one to select all the tags
# Press Submit

h2. Combined Tag Sets

Example: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/show_options?restriction=3103&tag_type=freeform|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/show_options?restriction=3103&tag_type=freeform]

There’s another page that uses the same view partials that we should test. You’ll need to make a challenge that uses your tag sets to see it.

# Log in
# Browse > Collections > New Collection
# Fill in required information
# For “Type of challenge, if any,” choose “Prompt Meme” (either option will work)
# Press Submit
# Make sure “Sign-up open?” is checked
# Under “Request Settings,” enter 1 in the Allowed field for each type (for ease)
# Under “Tag Options,” enter the names of both tag sets in “Tag Sets To Use”
# Press Submit
# Follow the “Prompt Form” link in the sidebar
# Follow the “List X Additional Tags” link

h1. What happens

In general,

*  the buttons on the listboxes are misaligned, both with the headings and with each other 
* in fact, they aren’t even buttons – they’re links with a lot of invalid custom attributes, and they should be made into buttons with HTML5 {{data-*}} attributes)
* the heading levels are quite wrong
* the tags should be listed vertically, rather than in comma-separated lists

h2. Tag Set #1

!Tag Set #1 - Broken.png|width=91.66666666666667%,alt="Tag Set Number One with the problems described below."!

The “Expand All” and “Contract All” buttons are in a serif font and they’re huge. They are pushed all the way to the right of the listbox, while other “Expand All” and “Contract All” buttons are next to the arrow buttons (refer to Tag Set #2).

h2. Tag Set #2

!Tag Set #2 - Broken.png|width=100%,alt="Tag Set Number 2 with the problems described below."!

The “Expand All” and “Contract All” buttons are misaligned with the arrow buttons. Above the listbox for “Unassociated Characters & Relationships” is an {{h4}} that says, “The following characters and relationships don't seem to be associated with any fandom in the tagset. You might need to add the fandom, or set up associations for them.” 

h2. Combined Tag Sets

!Combined Tag Sets - Broken.png|width=100%,alt="Combined Tag Sets with the problems described below."!

The “Expand All” and “Contract All” buttons are, again, comically large, positioned all the way to the right, and in a serif font. The headings for the nested listboxes are the same size as their parent because they’re all {{h3}}. (This is because it uses the same code as the other pages.) 

Additionally, the {{h2}} for the page is just “Additional Tag Options From:” and below it is an inline list of links with the tag set names.

h1. What should happen/Testing instructions

Please make sure the buttons work and don’t just look pretty! This fix will involve changing the JavaScript and some markup, so it’s possible for them to get broken.

Note that the arrows for shuffle and contract do not appear until a section is expanded. The shuffle buttons are there even if there’s only one item. 

Not strictly necessary, but for bonus testing points, you could also make tag sets like these on production and run the HTML for both the production and staging pages through the [W3C’s Markup Validation Service|https://validator.w3.org], which should show fewer issues with the new version of the pages.

h2. Tag Set #1

!Tag Set #1 - Fixed.png|width=100%,alt="Tag Set Number One with the improved buttons and headings described below."!

# Buttons and headings should be approximately vertically centered in their collapsed grey box.
# The “(No linked fandom - might need association) (1)” and “[Fandom Name] (1)” listboxes should be collapsed by default. Their arrow buttons for expanding, collapsing, and shuffling should have more padding than previously.

column1: Always display invitation search results in table format
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When searching for an invitation ([https://archiveofourown.org/admin/invitations|https://archiveofourown.org/admin/invitations] > Track Invitations) by email address, there are two possible results: 

# if multiple invitations were sent to that address, the results will be in table format; following the link in the Token column will show the details of that invitation ([https://archiveofourown.org/invitations/####|https://archiveofourown.org/invitations/####]) and the final column has the option to delete the invitation.
# if only one invite was ever sent to that address, the results page will show the details of that invitation, but there is no way to access the direct invitation link nor delete the invitation without re-running the search using a fuzzier partial match. 

h3. What should happen

In order to access the invitation and deletion links regardless of how many invitations were sent, the results of /admin/invitations/find?[parameter] should always be displayed in table format.

column1: Create recipient_notification mailer preview
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
There should be a [mailer preview|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Internationalization-%28i18n%29-Standards#user-content-Mailer_previews] for the {{recipient_notification}} email.

There should be two variants of the mailer preview, one for a regular gift work and one for a gift work in a collection. Furthermore, the word count, chapter count, series count and tag counts per tag type should be flexible and controlled with a URL parameter, meaning one parameter for all counts. For example when the parameter is 2, the word count should be 2, the work should be in 2 series, the work should have 2 fandom tags, 2 warnings, 2 characters and so on.

To make the previews' locale selector work, the {{I18n.with_locale}} block should be moved outside the mailer method, to where {{deliver}}/{{deliver_later}} is called on the mailer. There should be a cucumber test for sending a translated {{recipient_notification}} email to a user to cover this change.

This is also a good opportunity to update the locale keys used in the mail to the [current I18n standards|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Internationalization-%28i18n%29-Standards]. Particularly, the keys used in the HTML mail should end in {{.html}} and the {{html_safe}} calls should be removed. The keys used in the text mail should be updated to match.

*Testing*
The two preview variants should be valid mails with no translation errors and no exposed HTML, for both the HTML and text version. Selecting a locale from the dropdown that has translations for the mail (e.g. cs, hr, ja, ko, de, sv) should result in an at least partially translated mail.

column1: Remove unused pinch recipient code from challenge assignments
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Challenge assignments have code for a “pinch recipient”, who receives the assignment if the original requester dropped out. However, since [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/1580|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/1580|smart-link]  the {{pinch_request_signup}} cannot be set in the Archive interface. So we would like to remove this inaccessible and mostly unused code.

There should be a rake After task that migrates the data from {{pinch_request_signup}} to {{request_signup}} if {{pinch_request_signup}} is set and {{request_signup}} is unset.

This means {{belongs_to :pinch_request_signup}} in the model and the database column itself need to stay around for now. They will be removed later in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6851|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6851|smart-link] .

*Testing*

# Create a gift exchange.
# Sign up at least two participants.
# Run matching and send assignments.
# Log in as a participant and default on one of the assignments.
# As a moderator of the gift exchange, view the defaulted assignments.
# As a moderator of the gift exchange, view the open assignments.

The pages in steps 4, 5 and 6 should show the correct information. That means the page to default should show the correct assignment with the correct info, and the two moderator pages should only show the assignments for the selected category, each with the correct info.

*Deploy notes*

Run the rake task: {{bundle exec rake After:migrate_pinch_request_signup}}

}}) and text. Press “Search”. On the search results page, confirm that the HTML tags are removed from the text after “You searched for:“. Then press “Edit Your Search“. column1: Update Character Limit for Tags to 150 (ArchiveConfig.TAG_MAX)
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h2. Description

The current character limit length for tags in all categories is 100. We would like this to be adjusted to 150 for all categories. This change has been discussed with all relevant committees. The configuration value that would need to be adjusted is ({{ArchiveConfig.TAG_MAX}}). 

*Associated updates that will required are as follows:*
Text on work form ([https://archiveofourown.org/works/new|https://archiveofourown.org/works/new]) will need to be updated to:

Tags are comma separated, 150 characters per tag. Fandom, relationship, character, and additional tags must not add up to more than 75. Archive warning, category, and rating tags do not count toward this limit.

*Error messages for too long tag length will also need to be updated to 150:*

h4. Sorry! We couldn't save this XX because:

* Tag name 'NAME OF TAG' is too long -- try using less than 150 characters or using commas to separate your tags.

h4. 
In addition to the current character limit length being changed in the code and the error message and associated updates above, an update to the text here: [+https://archiveofourown.org/help/relationships-help.html+|https://archiveofourown.org/help/relationships-help.html] would need to be adjusted as well. We (Tag Wrangling) are currently consulting with Docs about this change.

*Steps to Reproduce (Tag Wrangler)*

# Log in as a user with the tag wrangler role
# Open Tag Wrangling sub menu > New Tag
# Create a tag with a tag length of 100-150 characters by typing something of these length in the Name field
# Mark the checkbox next to canonical
# Choose a category from Fandom, Character, Relationship, or Additional Tag
# Create tag
# A tag should successfully be created
# Can be repeated for each caegory
# Try to create a tag of 150+ in character length
# Should return error message: 
Sorry! We couldn't save this character because:

* Tag name 'NAME OF TAG' is too long -- try using less than 150 characters or using commas to separate your tags.

*Steps to Reproduce (Work Form)*

# Log in as a user
# Navigate to Post > New Work
# Create new work with tags in all fields that are 100-150 characters in length
# Work should be created with these tags
# Try to create a work with tags longer than 150+ in character length
# Should return message: 
Sorry! We couldn't save this work because:

* Tag name 'NAME OF TAG' is too long -- try using less than 150 characters or using commas to separate your tags.

h1. Deploy notes

There is a migration for this change:

column150: 21/Dec/24 9:26 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;Should the {{tagname}} column on the {{tag_nominations}} table also have a limit set to {{150}}, since the limit applies there as well?
column151:
22/Dec/24 3:04 AM;557058:baa5f297-c116-4036-bbf1-109f8a7e50a7;Both tag noms as well as tags use the varchar type for the column. Based on the [mysql docs on storage size|https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/storage-requirements.html#data-types-storage-reqs-strings], changing the limit from 255 to 150 does not affect the overhead of storing the length of the string: It’s 2 bytes in both cases because the db uses {{utf8mb4}} which means each character needs up to 4 bytes. So 150 chars would be 600 bytes, which already larger than the largest length that can be stored in one byte.

I found some info that runtime performance is impacted by the limit of the varchar type but it’s not much info: [https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1962310/importance-of-varchar-length-in-mysql-table/1962329#1962329|https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1962310/importance-of-varchar-length-in-mysql-table/1962329#1962329|smart-link], [https://mariadb.com/kb/en/varchar/#for-storage-engine-developers|https://mariadb.com/kb/en/varchar/#for-storage-engine-developers|smart-link] So we could potentially gain some performance by limiting the length of {{tagnames}} and then also {{parent_tagnames}} and {{synonym}} for nominations.

However, similar to the down migration for tag names, we’d need to be sure that we do not have more characters than the new limit in the columns. Considering this migration would be a risk (making the type smaller is always harder than making it larger), would have no impact on storage size and may only have a small impact on performance, I don’t think it is worth the hassle. If we want to do migrations to improve database performance, adding (unique) indexes for slow queries is lower risk and already proven to help a lot.

h3. Observed on:

* iPad Pro 10.5, 17.7.2 Safari (screenshot attached) and Chrome
* iPhone SE, bug appears in Safari (logged in and out), Chrome (logged out), Firefox Focus (logged out), all both in portrait and landscape orientations. Does not occur in Opera Mini. On wider displays (tablet), there is an extra gap between the Link and Brief Summary textboxes and their respective footnotes. 

On narrower displays (phone), the Link footnote (“Please ensure…”) appears _between_ the Brief Summary header and textbox. This interferes with readability and leads to some confusion, e.g. mobile users entering links into the Summary field.

{quote}sarken: It's related to the invisible span that's there to hold the error message. For some reason, that's started taking up space now.{quote}

The Link and Brief Summary footnotes should be immediately beneath the textboxes they are associated with.

Skins need to be recached.

column1: Adding Additional Filtering Options to "Wrangling Status" in Tag Search
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Tag Search ([https://archiveofourown.org/tags/search|https://archiveofourown.org/tags/search]) already allows for some filtering based on the current wrangling status of a tag and we would like this options further expanded to allow filtering of tags based on whether they have been merged (made synonymous) with other tags. What we are requesting specifically is the addition of an option which allows for filtering based on whether a tag is “synonymous” as well as an option which allows for filtering based on whether a tag is both “non-canonical” and “non-synonymous” as these options will allow wranglers to more effectiveness search for missed syns and new concepts to make canonical within their assigned fandoms and elsewhere.


----

This update will require adjustment to the text of the Wrangling status options on the Tag Search page. We have consulted with Docs and suggest this text be adjusted as follows:

Wrangling status:

* Canonical
* Non-canonical
* Synonymous
* Non-canonical and non-synonymous
* Any status

h1. Testing instructions

Note: The pull request includes an additional option not mentioned above – “Canonical or synonymous,” located between “Synonymous” and “Non-canonical and non-synonymous” on the form. 🎉

# Search for each tag by name (or all tags at once if they share one or more distinct words in their names)

# Any *synonymous* tag should appear only when selecting the following wrangling status options: "Non-canonical", "Synonymous", "Canonical or synonymous", "Any status"
