On the subject of ARIA, though, there are some other changes we should make once we’re sure pagy is going to work for us:

* take the {{role="navigation"}} off the list element and instead wrap the pagination in a {{nav}} element
* move the {{aria-label}} to the {{nav}} element
** Ideally, the {{aria-label}} would be {{aria-labeledby}} and point to the {{id}} attribute of the {{h4}} landmark, but each {{id}} needs to be unique on a page, and that would be difficult on pages with multiple pagination sections.
*** Note: We could probably get rid of the {{h4}} if we’re using {{aria-label}}, but I am 99% sure we’ll see layout issues because it also functions as a {{clear}}.
** Also ideally, the label would be different for each pagination section on a given page. Again, this would be an issue for pages with multiple pagination sections. 
* add an {{aria-label}} saying “Page #” to each of the links, and maybe “last page, Page #” to the final item as [the US Web Design System pagination component|https://designsystem.digital.gov/components/pagination/] does ([Wayback link to USWDS pagination component page|https://web.archive.org/web/20250202070608/https://designsystem.digital.gov/components/pagination/] just in case)

We should also remove the {{pagy}} class when we’re done. It might be useful now if we need to temporarily style the new pagination differently than the {{will_paginate}} version, but once we’re only using pagy, it will be superfluous – plus it violates our class naming rules.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Traffic grows enough that recently we’ve had issues where the application starved memcached of memory.

Adding [https://github.com/zombocom/rack-timeout|https://github.com/zombocom/rack-timeout] which aborts requests taking too long gives us a mitigation option.

{quote}Rack::Timeout is not a solution to the problem of long-running requests, it's a debug and remediation tool. App developers should track rack-timeout's data and address recurring instances of particular timeouts, for example by refactoring code so it runs faster or offsetting lengthy work to happen asynchronously.{quote}

The gem can be configured by setting {{RACK_TIMEOUT_SERVICE_TIMEOUT}} environment variable, so no extra code is required beyond adding the dependency.

column1: Add puma_worker_killer gem
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
To temporarily address performance issues with puma (while we are waiting on new hardware), we want to do rolling restarts of puma appservers. This can be accomplished with [https://github.com/zombocom/puma_worker_killer|https://github.com/zombocom/puma_worker_killer|smart-link] .

Configuring the gem, we want rolling restarts to happen every 2 days with a random splay of 0..720 minutes. These should be configurable via the ArchiveConfig using

* PUMA_ROLLING_RESTART_FREQUENCY = 2.days
* PUMA_ROLLING_RESTART_SPLAY = 720

Details about configuring the library [https://github.com/zombocom/puma_worker_killer?tab=readme-ov-file#configure|https://github.com/zombocom/puma_worker_killer?tab=readme-ov-file#configure|smart-link]

column1: Upgrade to Rails 7.1
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Rails 7 drops out of security support in April, so let's upgrade to Rails 7.1! From the release notes, some significant changes are:

* Generate Dockerfiles for new Rails applications
* Add ActiveRecord::Base.normalizes
* Add ActiveRecord::Base.generates_token_for
* Add perform_all_later to enqueue multiple jobs at once
* Composite primary keys
* Introduce adapter for Trilogy
* Add ActiveSupport::MessagePack
* Introducing config.autoload_lib and config.autoload_lib_once for Enhanced Autoloading
* Active Record API for general async queries
* Allow templates to set strict locals
* Add Rails.application.deprecators
* Support pattern matching for JSON response.parsed_body
* Extend response.parsed_body to parse HTML with Nokogiri
* Introduce ActionView::TestCase.register_parser

Requirements to upgrade, in broad strokes, are described in [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#upgrading-from-rails-7-0-to-rails-7-1|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#upgrading-from-rails-7-0-to-rails-7-1|smart-link] .  Furthermore, there are several config changes that can only be done after the initial upgrade.

We also get some new features, which are described in [https://rubyonrails.org/2023/10/5/Rails-7-1-0-has-been-released|https://rubyonrails.org/2023/10/5/Rails-7-1-0-has-been-released|smart-link] .

*Testing*

Nokogiri had a new version with some breaking changes, so we need to test importing:

* Confirm that posting and importing works with some formatting functions normally. You can compare to what was observed on [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6511|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6511|smart-link]  .
* Tips: For importing, you can use a text post from Tumblr with /mobile at the end of the URL, e.g., [https://sarking.tumblr.com/post/704571626519429120/curds-and-wheyface-i-think-a-fundamental-part/mobile|https://sarking.tumblr.com/post/704571626519429120/curds-and-wheyface-i-think-a-fundamental-part/mobile|smart-link]  . Note that a given URL can only be imported once, so if you use the URL here, it would be kind to delete the work when you’re done, which will let someone else use it.
* For posting, you can use the RTE to apply formatting or paste already formatted text (like the same Tumblr post).

Bookmark search had some issues as well, so we need to test that it functions normally when searching for bookmarkers:

* On [https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search|https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search], search for a Bookmarker, both by pseud and by username. The search should return only bookmarks bookmarked by that pseud/user.

The file where the session secret is set for Rails changed so we should do a smoke test to make sure it’s still getting read. See the deploy section for this.

*Deploy*

There are migrations and production config changes.

Ansible needs to be run to upgrade the version of {{rubygems}} installed. Example from staging:

{noformat}ANSIBLE_CONFIG=env/production/ansible.cfg ansible ao3app_staging --become-user ao3app -m shell -a "~/.rvm/bin/rvm rubygems 3.6.0" -u brianaustin -i env/production/inventory -kK --vault-password-file group_vars/vault_pass {noformat}

Migrations should be run pre-deploy. Because of a bug in Departure ([https://github.com/departurerb/departure/issues/110|https://github.com/departurerb/departure/issues/110|smart-link]), they need to run with [advisory locks disabled|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/configuring.html#configuring-a-mysql-or-mariadb-database].

column1: Reduce the amount of unclean disconnections from the Resque workers to the database
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
We can see a large number of closed database connections from Resque workers. MaxScale can not save us as they are not calling {{mysql_close()}}. It’s possible that Resque is not correctly wrapping jobs (with [the Rails Executor|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/threading_and_code_execution.html]), meaning Rails' connection pooling management does not happen.

We need to reduce the amount of connections to the database as the connection thundering is causing issues with database stability. This is likely more of an issue now than in the past because ActiveStorage uses more database connections (for example, [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6878|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6878|smart-link]).

column1: Upgrade to latest version of jQuery and jQuery UI
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
We're currently using jQuery 1.9.0 and jQuery UI 1.10.0, so we very badly need to update to the current versions. (Generally speaking, you don't need jQuery these days, but upgrading is much easier than finding replacement plugins and rewriting our existing code to use vanilla Javascript.)

Because there are [many breaking changes|https://jquery.com/upgrade-guide/3.0/] along the way, the usual course of action would be to use the [migrate plugin|https://github.com/jquery/jquery-migrate], which would require us to first update to jQuery 1.12 or 2.2, and then use the plugin to migrate to 3.x. 

Fortunately, we don't use a lot of complex jQuery, so it turns out we can skip that process and go right to 3.7.1. The main change is we need to replace the [Live Query plugin|https://plugins.jquery.com/livequery/] with a {{MutationObserver}} to keep autocomplete working.

ticking instant has a [branch that upgrades to 3.6.4|https://github.com/tickinginstant/otwarchive/tree/noodling-javascript-barebones]; sarken has a [branch that resolves that branch’s merge conflicts, removes the unrelated changes, and upgrades to 3.7.1|https://github.com/sarken/otwarchive/tree/jquery_update]. 

It will probably need updating again by the time we're ready for it.

column1: Use ActiveJob for asynchronous indexing
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The Rails Executor can [return acquired db connections to the pool|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/threading_and_code_execution.html#default-callbacks], and asynchronous jobs using Active Job or Action Mailer wrap code in an executor by default.

Sidekiq is one example of a queue backend that [wraps code in an executor|https://github.com/sidekiq/sidekiq/pull/3221], but it looks like Resque (as of 2.6) does not.

We will attempt to address [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6895|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6895|smart-link] by moving one of the more common jobs, [AsyncIndexer|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/671cdb9273be76984a14957bfe7e44f0c7bfd841/app/models/search/async_indexer.rb#L56], to Active Job.

column1: Extra spaces after colons in some mailers
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
As discovered in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6848?focusedCommentId=361893|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6848?focusedCommentId=361893|smart-link] , there are extra spaces after some of the colons in {{challenge_assignment_notification}}. column1: Remove PseudSweeper class and move callbacks to user and pseud models
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When a pseud or a user gets renamed, there are callbacks to update the autocomplete cache, not in the pseud or user models themselves, but in [a cache sweeper|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ec6c90fc44815a902e0bd738071292887b922b5a/app/sweepers/pseud_sweeper.rb]. While we never actually enabled the cache sweeper in [the Devise controller that creates users|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ec6c90fc44815a902e0bd738071292887b922b5a/app/controllers/users/registrations_controller.rb], it rarely if ever becomes a noticeable issue. From [~accountid:557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6]:

{quote}There’s something a little odd going on with the {{PseudSweeper}}. As I understand it, sweepers are only supposed to add callbacks in those controllers that [explicitly specify|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ec6c90fc44815a902e0bd738071292887b922b5a/app/controllers/pseuds_controller.rb#L2] {{cache_sweeper :pseud_sweeper}}. But a few days ago I noticed that there’s no line enabling the {{PseudSweeper}} for the {{Users::Registrations}} class, which is where users (and their initial pseud) are actually created. So in theory, no new user accounts will be added to the autocomplete.

In practice, it seems that there’s a bug in the way that the sweepers work: if the server has ever filled a request that involved the {{PseudSweeper}}, then all subsequent requests seem to have the {{PseudSweeper}} enabled as well, regardless of which controller is used. So because all of the unicorn workers have probably served at least one request for the {{PseudsController}} or the {{UsersController}}, that bug effectively cancels out the bug with {{PseudSweeper}} not being enabled for the {{Users::RegistrationsController}}.

But it still would be good to either move the autocomplete changes out of the sweeper and into the Pseud class, or add {{cache_sweeper :pseud_sweeper}} to the {{Users::RegistrationsController}}.{quote}

Let’s delete the sweeper and move the callbacks into the model classes. This way we can also remove the special code to run the cache sweeper in feature tests ([one|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ec6c90fc44815a902e0bd738071292887b922b5a/features/support/user.rb#L13-L15], [two|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ec6c90fc44815a902e0bd738071292887b922b5a/features/support/user.rb#L37]), since it’s not run by default.

# Change your user / pseud to an uncommon name. Make sure that the new name shows up in autocomplete when you type it into the “Name” field of [https://test.archiveofourown.org/people/search|https://test.archiveofourown.org/people/search].
# Change your user / pseud back to its original name. Make sure that the uncommon name no longer shows up in autocomplete.

column1: Custom error page for RackTimeout error
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30: When a page takes too long to respond, users are currently greeted with the generic 500 error page ([https://archiveofourown.org/500.html|https://archiveofourown.org/500.html|smart-link] ). That can be confusing, because it’s not quite what happened. Additionally, the underlying error shows up in Sentry, which is confusing for _us_, because we don’t actually need a fix for it (other than perhaps redesigning some things like downloads, but that’s a separate issue). Using the 503 error page as a template, we want to create a new page that says “The page was responding too slowly. Please try again after a few minutes. If you still get this error after a few tries, you can contact Support.” (with a link to the support form) We can use {{rescue_from}} (example [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/controllers/application_controller.rb#L5|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/controllers/application_controller.rb#L5|smart-link] ) to render that new page. The particular error to rescue is {{Rack::Timeout::RequestTimeoutException}}. *Testing* First, we need Systems to change [https://github.com/OTWSystems/ansible/blob/ac3993dabf5269e7e0d525834edc84a9d54d1dc0/roles/core/ao3_app_support/defaults/main.yml#L12|https://github.com/OTWSystems/ansible/blob/ac3993dabf5269e7e0d525834edc84a9d54d1dc0/roles/core/ao3_app_support/defaults/main.yml#L12] to a relatively small value. Once that is done, try downloading something that will take awhile (a work over 200k is a good bet). You should get the new error instead of a generic 500 error. A senior AD&T person (or someone from Systems) should also check Sentry to make sure the exception above is not recorded there either.

column1: Allow invite job to run every N hours
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
After a certain number of invites, it makes more sense to reduce the number we process from the queue but process the queue more often. We can already control the number via AdminSetting, but we need to make adjustments to let us schedule per N hours instead of N days.

# Update [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/775ed1341c628f91fb345e12b12e5f62e08810b8/app/models/admin_setting.rb#L59-L60|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/775ed1341c628f91fb345e12b12e5f62e08810b8/app/models/admin_setting.rb#L59-L60|smart-link]  to use {{Time.current}} instead of {{Date.today}}, and {{invite_from_queue_frequency.days}} to {{invite_from_queue_frequency.hours}}.
# Add a comment to[https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/775ed1341c628f91fb345e12b12e5f62e08810b8/config/config.yml#L83|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/775ed1341c628f91fb345e12b12e5f62e08810b8/config/config.yml#L83|smart-link]indicating that it is in hours, and change the value to 12 (run the job twice per day by default)
# Modify the schedule for [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/775ed1341c628f91fb345e12b12e5f62e08810b8/config/resque_schedule.yml#L83|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/775ed1341c628f91fb345e12b12e5f62e08810b8/config/resque_schedule.yml#L83|smart-link]  to run it every hour
# Update [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/775ed1341c628f91fb345e12b12e5f62e08810b8/app/models/invite_request.rb#L24|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/775ed1341c628f91fb345e12b12e5f62e08810b8/app/models/invite_request.rb#L24|smart-link] and [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/775ed1341c628f91fb345e12b12e5f62e08810b8/config/locales/views/en.yml#L338|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/775ed1341c628f91fb345e12b12e5f62e08810b8/config/locales/views/en.yml#L338|smart-link] to account for the above changes



h3. Testing

# Log in as an admin with the role {{superadmin}} ✅ 
# Follow the “Settings” link in the admin navigation ✅ 
# If the homepage does not have a “Get Invited!” link (this will be the case on staging), enable the invitation queue by checking all three of these settings: “Account creation enabled”, “Account creation requires invitation”, and “Invite from queue enabled (People can add themselves to the queue and invitations are sent out automatically)” ✅ 
# Fill in “How often (in hours) should we invite people from the queue” with “1” to send invitations every hour ✅ 
## Verify that the form label says _hours_ not _days_ ✅ 
# Fill in “Number of people to invite from the queue at once” with “1” to force multiple batches  ✅ 
# Press “Update” to save ✅ 
# Log out of your admin account ✅ 
# Go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests|https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests]
## Verify the text after the form says, “We are sending out 1 invitation every hour.”
# In the “Email” field, enter an email address that you have access to (you’ll need to check that you’ve received the email, so {{@example.com}} won’t work) _and_ that isn’t already being used by an account
# Press “Add me to the list”
# Repeat steps 8-10 so you’ll have 2 batches (no need to repeat 8a)
# Follow the “check your position on the waiting list” link in the text under the form
## Verify the text near the top of the page says, “We are sending out 1 invitation every hour.”
# Wait ~1 hour and ensure the first invitation email is received.
# Wait another ~1 hour and ensure the invitation email from the second batch is received.

After confirming invitations are sent as expected, please also:

# Log in as an admin with the role {{superadmin}}
# Follow the “Settings” link in the admin navigation
# Fill in “How often (in hours) should we invite people from the queue” with a number greater than 1 (you can use 2, 5, 72, etc)
# Fill in “Number of people to invite from the queue at once” with a number greater than 1
# Press “Update” to save
# Go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests|https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests] and verify the text now says, “We are sending out [number from step 4] invitations every [number from step 3] hours.”
# Go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status|https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status] and verify the text now says, “We are sending out [number from step 4] invitations every [number from step 3] hours.”

The frequency message on the “Invitation Requests” page should be internationalized like this:

{noformat}t(".sending", 
  queue_number: t(".invitations", count: invite_from_queue_number),
  queue_frequency: t(".hours", count: invite_from_queue_frequency.hours)
)

sending: We are sending out %{queue_number} every %{queue_frequency}.
invitations:
  one: %{count} invitation
  other: %{count} invitations
hours:
  one: hour
  other: %{count} hours{noformat}

From [~accountid:60315dca4b2b9e00695c2b40] and translators: since both counts are part of the object rather than the subject of the sentence, they won't change the verb conjugation, so this sentence construction should work.

h3. Deploy notes

The resque workers and scheduler need to be restarted.

*Shortly after deploy* (and after resque workers/scheduler have been restarted), set the invite from queue frequency to 12 hours and the number of people to invite from the queue at once to 3000 in the admin settings.

# Implementing a script to create backup codes on demand (in case we need to reset 2fa for a user).

Follow [https://github.com/devise-two-factor/devise-two-factor?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-started|https://github.com/devise-two-factor/devise-two-factor?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-started|smart-link] and [https://www.jamesridgway.co.uk/implementing-a-two-step-otp-u2f-login-workflow-with-rails-and-devise/|https://www.jamesridgway.co.uk/implementing-a-two-step-otp-u2f-login-workflow-with-rails-and-devise/|smart-link] to enable TOTP and backups codes for Admin users. We’ll want to provide secrets via environment variable.

h1. Implementation

h2. 2fa activation

There should be a link to set up two-step verification (the friendlier name we’ll use for 2fa) on the landing page:

!image-20260124-164357.png|width=444,alt="image-20260124-164357.png"!

The text also needs some updating.

{quote}*With great power comes great responsibility.*{quote}

should be removed. The existing log out reminder should be bold instead: 

{quote}*Please remember to log out before resuming your normal site activity!*{quote}

After this, we want a horizontal line to separate the introduction from a new “Account Settings” section. Within a box (like the meta on a work), should appear the admin’s roles, the two-step verification status, and a link to set up two-step verification with an authenticator app.

Clicking on the link should bring the admin to a page to confirm their password:

!image-20260124-164833.png|width=444,alt="image-20260124-164833.png"!

Entering the correct password should bring the admin the page with instructions on setting up two-step verification:

!image-20260124-164939.png|width=444,alt="image-20260124-164939.png"!

After entering the correct 6-digit code, the admin should be presented with the backup codes, for use in case they lose the device that has been set up for two-step verification. Once they acknowledge the backup codes, they should be returned to the admin landing page. Now, the 2fa status should be enabled, and there should be two links: 1) to disable 2fa and 2) to regenerate the backup codes.

h2. Logging in with 2fa

If an admin has 2fa enabled, after entering their username/password, they should be prompted for a 2fa code:

!image-20260124-165355.png|width=444,alt="image-20260124-165355.png"!

_Entering either the code or a backup code should work here_.

h2. Disabling 2fa

Following the link on the admin landing page should prompt the admin for their password. Once entered, 2fa should be disabled and the admin returned to the admin landing page (with a flash message to let them know 2fa was disabled). _Right now, we are not going to require a 2fa code here._

h2. Password Resets

We are not going to require a 2fa code to reset passwords for now. There is a follow-up ticket to do this later: [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7220|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7220|smart-link]

* The Dark Mode (staging only), Reversi and Low Vision Default skins need to be manually edited

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Create a collection
## Browse > Collections > New Collection
## Fill in the required fields
## Press “Submit”
# Go to its Subcollections page by following the “Subcollections” link in the collection dashboard

h1. What happens

There is an “Open Challenges” link, which takes you to the main Open Challenges page ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/list_challenges}}) 

h1. What should happen instead

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

h2. Variation 1: Assignment has not been completed

# Create an account you don’t mind deleting
## From the homepage, follow “Create Account” (If this option isn’t present, someone will need to log in as a superadmin, go to Settings, and make sure “Account creation enabled” is checked and “Account creation requires invitation” is unchecked.)
## Fill in the required information
## Submit
## Follow the activation link (If you’re on staging, it will be in your email; if you’re on dev, it will be in a blue notice banner on the confirmation page.)
# Create a collection with a gift exchange challenge
## Log in with a *different* account than the one you made in Step 1 (you don’t want to delete the collection owner account!)
## Browse > Collections > New Collection
## Fill in required information 
## Choose "Gift Exchange" for "Type of challenge, if any"
## Submit
## On the exchange settings form, check "Sign-up open?"
## Submit
# Sign up for the exchange as at least three different users, including the account from Step 1
## Follow the "Sign-up Form" link in the collection sidebar
## Since we accepted the default settings, we don't even need to fill anything in – just press "Submit"
# Run matching
## If you're not already logged in as the collection owner, log back in with that account
## On your collection's sidebar, follow  the "Challenge Settings" link
## Uncheck "Sign-up open?"
## Press "Update"
## From the sidebar, follow the "Matching" link
## Press "Generate Potential Matches"
## You'll get a pop-up warning you matches will be random; choose "OK"
## Wait briefly for matching to finish and refresh the page to see potential matches
#  Send assignments
## Press "Send Assignments"
## You'll get a pop-up telling you assignments will be sent; choose "OK"
# Delete the account from Step 1
## Log in with the account from Step 1
## Hi, name! > My Dashboard > Profile
## Press “Delete My Account”
## You’ll get a pop-up asking you if you’re sure; choose “OK”
# Check on the state of assignments for your exchange
## Log back in as the collection owner
## On your collection’s sidebar, follow the “Assignments” link
## Follow the “Open” link to view open assignments

h2. Variation 2: Assignment has been completed and work is deleted with account

Do the following in place of Variation 1’s Step 6: 

# Log in with the account you plan to delete
# Post a work that fulfills the assignment
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required information
## For “Does this fulfill a challenge assignment”, choose the relevant assignment
## Post
# Delete your account and the work
##  Hi, name! > My Dashboard > Profile
## Press “Delete My Account”
## You’ll get a pop-up asking you if you’re sure; choose “OK”
## Because you had a work, it will take you to a page asking what you want to do with your work. Choose "Delete completely"
## Submit

h2. Variation 3: Assignment has been completed and work is orphaned when account is deleted

Do the same as Variation 2, but for *Step 3d*, choose either "Leave my pseud but attach to the orphan account" or "Change my pseud to ‘orphan’ and attach to the orphan account."

h1. What happens vs what should happen

Note for the curious: The assignment where the deleted user was the _recipient_ will have vanished entirely from the Assignments page, but it will remain on the giver’s Assignments page as “[Collection name] for - None -”. The giver will still be able to access the assignment by following the “ - None - “ link, but instead of showing the request, the page will say, “No request! Contact challenge moderators for help.”

h2. Variation 1: Assignment has not been completed 

There is an assignment on the Open Assignments page that just says “for [recipient]” instead of “[giver] for [recipient].” That’s the one that belonged to the deleted user. 

The assignment should be marked defaulted and should appear on the “Defaulted” page. Instead of blank text, it should say “deleted user.” (Lowercase is [what we use for prompt meme claims|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/fd5046c72ca2b2f6874aaaf839bd54a5410e2677/app/models/challenge_claim.rb#L140-L142], so we might as well match.)

h2. Variation 2: Assignment has been completed and work is deleted with account

Same as Variation 1.

h2. Variation 3: Assignment has been completed and work is orphaned when account is deleted

The assignment is not on the Open Assignments page, but rather the completed assignments page. This is correct! However, where the giver/assignee’s name would normally appear (the {{<dt>}}), there is empty space. It should say “deleted user”.

(I do not know the version it was first found; this is from a ticket from June 2021)

It goes with zoho ticket #420322 . There is no specific incident referred to

Currently, the {{collection_notification}} is used to send the “Assignments sent” mail and the “Challenge default by UserA” mail. We would like to split it into two separate mailer methods and update their text. The mailers should be coded as [translatable|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Internationalization-%28i18n%29-Standards] and have [mailer previews|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Developing-mailers#user-content-Mailer_previews]. Their subjects should be defined with {{default_i18n_subject}} so that they are fully translatable, including a parameter for the collection title. The “Assignment default” email should not be sent if any of the users no longer exists. h3. [AO3][Collection Title] Assignments sent h4. HTML email The body should be approximately as follows: {noformat}

All assignments have now been sent out for your gift exchange <%= style_link(@collection.title, collection_url(@collection)) %>.

{noformat} h4. Plain-text email The body should be approximately as follows: {noformat}All assignments have now been sent out for your gift exchange "<%= @collection.title %>" (<%= collection_url(@collection) %>).{noformat} h3. [AO3][Collection Title] Assignment default by User1 h4. HTML email The body should be approximately as follows: {noformat}

<%= style_bold("User 1") %> has defaulted on their assignment for <%= style_bold("User 2") %> in your gift exchange <%= style_link(@collection.title, @collection_url(@collection) %>.

You can assign a pinch hitter on the <%= style_link("collection assignments page", collection_assignments_url(@collection)) %>.

column1: Spam check comments from new users
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Comments posted by logged in users are not currently checked for spam. 

We’d like to begin spam checking comments from new users on works and admin posts (but not tags).

When submitted to Akismet, these comments should have

* the {{user_role}} set to {{"user"}}, 
* the {{comment_author}} set to the user’s {{login}}, and 
* the {{comment_author_email}} set to the user’s {{email}}.

For now, there should *not* be a way for admins or users to mark individual comments by logged in users as spam. 

_However_, when an admin with the {{policy_and_abuse}} or {{superadmin}} role bans any user for spam, the user’s comments should be submitted to Akismet as spam before deletion. (Note that they should not be marked as spam in our database, partly for efficiency and partly due to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5002|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5002|smart-link].) This will help train Akismet to recognize logged-in comment spam.

Admins with the {{policy_and_abuse}} or {{superadmin}} role should be able to set the threshold for newness by going to the Settings page. 

The option should be in a new “Content” fieldset, along with the existing options for “Automatically hide spam works” and “Turn off guest comments across the site.” The option should be an input labeled “How old (in days) accounts should be before we stop checking comments for spam.” (Note that the attached mockup does not reflect the desired wording.) It should accept any integer. Entering 0 should disable spam checking of logged in comments, and the field should have a (properly ARIA-associated) footnote that says, “Enter 0 to turn off comment spam checks for all logged in users.” It should initially be set to 0.

h1. Testing

The tl;dr: We’re going to make an account with an email that should always trigger a positive (spam) response from the spam checker. Then we’re going to make sure its comments don’t get marked as spam if the spam check is off, and do get marked as spam (on works and admin posts) when spam checking is on. We’ll also make sure we can spam ban the user.

# Make sure we have a new account for testing since we’ll spamban it in step 9:
## follow the “Create an Account!” link on the homepage
## fill in the required information, making sure to use an email address you have access to, and press “Create Account”
## follow the “follow this link to activate your account” link in the activation email
# ✅ Shortly after this is deployed (ie, before anyone might try to update the admin settings) an admin with the {{policy_and_abuse}} or {{superadmin}} role should make sure the initial newness threshold is set correctly.
## log in
## go to Settings
## make sure “How old (in days) accounts should be before we stop checking comments for spam” is set to 0 (don’t change it – you’re just checking the initial value; if it’s not already 0, there’s a problem) 
# An admin with the {{tag_wrangling}} or {{superadmin}} role should make sure our test account is a tag wrangler and can therefore comment on tags:
## log in
## go to Manage Users > Find Users
## search for the user you created in step 1
## check the “Tag Wrangler” checkbox in the appropriate row of the results table and press “Update” to make sure the user has the wrangling role
# ✅  An admin with the {{superadmin}}, {{board}}, {{board_assistants_team}}, {{communications}}, {{support}}, or {{translation}} role should make an admin post to comment on:
## log in
## go to Admin Posts > Post AO3 News
## fill in required fields, make sure logged-in users will be able to comment, and post 
# Log in as the user from Step 1 and ensure the spam check is disabled by commenting just “viagra-test-123” (without the quotation marks) on a tag, an admin post, and a work without getting an error. (You can also try replying to a comment on a work or admin post. This shouldn’t error, either.)
# Using an account that is *not* the user from Step 1, reply to one or all of the comments left in Step 5. Make note of the work, admin post, or tag where you left these replies – we’re going to use these later to make sure we’re not affected by [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5002|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5002|smart-link].)
# An admin with the {{policy_and_abuse}} or {{superadmin}} role should make sure the spam check will run when the user from Step 1 posts a comment:
## log in
## go to Settings
## change “How old (in days) accounts should be before we stop checking comments for spam” to “10” and save
# Log in as the user from Step 1 and ensure the spam check is enabled and working by commenting “viagra-test-123” (without the quotation marks) on a tag, an admin post, and a work. 
## on the work and admin post, you should get an error that comment looks like spam
## you should not get an error on the tag
## if you try replying to a comment, it should error if the comment you’re replying to is on a work or admin post
# An admin with the {{policy_and_abuse}} or {{superadmin}} role should make sure the user can be spam banned and that [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5002|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5002|smart-link] doesn’t cause problems:
## log in
## go to Manage Users > Find Users
## search for the user from step 1
## follow the “Details” link in the corresponding row
## choose the “Spammer: ban and delete all creations” option, enter a note, and press “Update”
## press “Yes, Delete All Spammer Creations”
# Visit the items from Step 6 and make sure you can see the replies, and that there is a deleted comment placeholder above the replies.

* {{/faq}} (or {{/faq?language_id=en}}), {{/faq/new}} , and {{/faq/manage?language_id=en}} should have Archive FAQ, New FAQ Category, Reorder FAQs

column1: Update autocomplete to treat pipes (|) as delimiters
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
[~accountid:712020:bb568d1c-045f-4d41-b06d-825ace2cfa5b] noticed that adding pipes (without spaces in particular) to search messes with autocomplete results, as shown in the attached screenshot.

Additionally, folks have observed that adding more pipes (surrounded by other delimiter characters like spaces) can result in increased response times for the autocomplete popup, depending on how many pipes are in the inputted text. So “taylor hebert | skitter” takes longer than “taylor hebert skitter” or “taylor hebert|skitter”. Compared to requests without pipes, the response times are generally up from 3 times longer for fandoms, 5+ for characters and freeforms, 15+ for relationships, and 30+ for all-tag search, which is at least several seconds of delay and really noticeable.

We should be able to add the pipe character to the list of delimiters (characters used to split phrases) [here|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/82f4b30f3a0ba490207ce34edaef6bc97805ef5f/lib/autocomplete_source.rb#L243] to resolve these issues.

*Testing*

# Open the Post new work page, do the following in the “Relationship” field:
# Try inputting “|” (a single pipe) - the autocomplete should say “No suggestions found”
# Try inputting words only separated by a bar with no spaces, e.g. “Taylor|Skitter“ - it should result in some autocomplete suggestions
# Take a search query that has a pipe or multiple, e.g. a character tag like “Taylor Hebert | Skitter | Weaver“
## First try inputting it with the bars removed (“Taylor Hebert Skitter Weaver“), note how long it takes to show autocomplete suggestions (probably less than a second)
## Try inputting it with the bars present, it should take a similar time to search and not weirdly long. If “&;” shows up in the search results, you can ignore it, that’s [a different bug|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6348]
# Repeat step 4 for another different tag to make sure it’s consistent

column1: Manage Items page for collection may show unrelated work instead of bookmark
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
# Create an open, unmoderated collection
# Add a bookmark to it
# View the approved items on the Manage Items page for the collection: {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/items?status=approved}}

*What happens*

The page lists a completely different work.

*What should happen*

The page lists the bookmark that you added.

*Explanation*

The page is showing the work that has the id of the bookmark. As a result, this is difficult to reproduce on production and staging, where new bookmarks have much higher ids than new works and so it can be difficult to get the bookmark id to also be a valid work id. However, this can be tested with an automated test that sets the id of objects so that there is a valid work with the id of the bookmark.

This is a bug with {{includes}} that we can work around by changing the {{:include_for_works}} scope on CollectionItem to be {{{ includes(item: :pseuds) }}}.

*Testing*

No manual QA, automated tests only.

column1: Avoid unhiding admin-hidden works when un-spamming
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Right now, marking a work as not spam (ham) will un-hide the work. This is the correct behavior only if the work was automatically hidden for being spam, not if it was manually hidden by an admin. We want to make it so that admin-hidden works stay hidden even when marked as not spam (either individually or in bulk). 

In addition, if an admin hides and then later unhides a spam-flagged work, the work should be marked as not spam upon being unhidden (because the admin has presumably reviewed the work and confirmed it is no longer in violation of TOS).

This came up when discussing the email fix implemented in [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4947|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4947|smart-link] , so that may be a good start for inspiration.

h3. *Testing*

# As a PAC admin or superadmin, go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/settings|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/settings] and check the “Automatically hide spam works” box.
# As a user, post three works (A, B, C) that get flagged as spam (you can try setting the work body to akismet‑guaranteed‑spam per [https://akismet.com/support/getting-started/confirm/|https://akismet.com/support/getting-started/confirm/] ).
## You should receive an "Automatically flagged as spam" email for each work and all three works should be hidden from public view.
# As a PAC admin or superadmin, go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/settings|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/settings] and uncheck the “Automatically hide spam works” box.
# Repeat step 2. You should not receive any emails and all three works (D, E, F) should be visible to all users.
# As a PAC admin or superadmin, use the "Hide Work" button to admin-hide all six works.
# Go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/spam|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/spam] and check the "Not Spam" boxes for works A and D, then click "Update Works".
# Use the "Mark Not Spam" button to unspam works B and E.
# Use the "Unhide Work" button to unhide works C and F.

h3. Expected Results:

* After step 2, the user should receive an "Automatically flagged as spam" email for each work and works A-C should be hidden.
* After step 4, the user should not have received any new emails. All six works should be marked “Akismet Reported As Spam: true”, but only works A-C should be hidden.
* After step 5, the user should receive a "Your work has been hidden by the Policy & Abuse team" email for works D-F, but not works A-C (since those were already hidden as spam). All six works should be hidden and marked “Akismet Reported As Spam: true”.
* After step 8:
** All six works should be marked “Akismet Reported As Spam: false”.
** Works A, B, D, and E should be hidden (red-locked) and the buttons at the top should say "Unhide Work" and "Mark As Spam".
** Works C and F should not be hidden and the buttons at the top should say "Hide Work" and "Mark As Spam".

column1: Skip submitting marked-as-deleted comments to spam checker when banning a user for spam
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When an admin bans a user for spam, and the user has comments that have been marked as deleted (but were not actually deleted due to having replies), we should skip reporting the marked-as-deleted comments to the spam checker, since the comment’s original spam content is no longer available.

We’ll need automated tests to confirm the deleted comment isn’t reported, but we should still confirm spam bans work:

column1: No error message shown when clearing reading history fails

column1: Missing text in heading on new comment error page
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

Note: This is just one way to arrive at the page with the problem; you might be able to get there by triggering other errors.

# Log in
# Find a work to comment on, e.g. by going to Browse > Works and following links until you find a work with comments enabled
# Enter some text in the comment field
# Copy the text to your clipboard – you’re going to need to reenter it exactly the same way
# Press “Comment” to submit the comment
# Scroll back up to the comment box and paste in the text (note: to trigger the error we’re testing with, you have to be commenting on the exact same item; you can’t be replying to a comment or commenting on a different chapter)
# Press “Comment” to submit the comment
# Look at the error page

h1. What happens

The h2 says “New comment on” and ends there.

h1. What should happen

It should use either the title or name of the ultimate parent. So if you’re commenting on an admin post or work, or replying to a comment on an admin post or work, it should use the item’s title. If you’re commenting on a tag, or replying to a comment on a tag, it should use the tag name.

This heading text will also apply when accessing the new comment page without triggering an error, e.g. when going to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/comments/###/comments/new|https://test.archiveofourown.org/comments/###/comments/new] or [https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/###/comments/new|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/###/comments/new]. 

h1. Notes

The behavior I described in “What should happen” is different than the behavior the [current code|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/bab383a53b516f48112434bf48da47da73fefbe4/app/controllers/comments_controller.rb#L305-L319] tries to produce. However, it’s more in line with [the heading we use when accessing comment threads|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/bab383a53b516f48112434bf48da47da73fefbe4/app/views/comments/show.html.erb#L3].

column1: Incorrect error message when leaving duplicate comment
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a tag wrangler
# Go to the comment page for a tag, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/comments|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/comments] 
# Enter some text in the comment field
# Copy the text to your clipboard – you’re going to need to reenter it exactly the same way
# Press “Comment” to submit the comment
# Scroll back up to the comment box and paste in the text (note: to trigger the error we’re testing with, you have to be commenting on the exact same item; you can’t be replying to a comment or commenting on a different chapter)
# Press “Comment” to submit the comment
# Look at the error page

h1. What happens

The error message says, “This comment has already been left on this work. (It may not appear right away for performance reasons.)”

It would also give this same error if you did this on an admin post or when replying to a comment, since we use the same validation regardless of what the comment is on. 

h1. What should happen

We _could_ make it specify the correct item type, but it would be easier to make it say, “You’ve already left this comment here. (It may not appear right away for performance reasons.)” 

This is also more accurate. [The validation|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/bab383a53b516f48112434bf48da47da73fefbe4/app/models/comment.rb#L71-L75] isn’t checking if anyone left the same comment; it’s checking if _you_ left the comment. And it’s not even checking if you left it on the work, but on the specific item you’re commenting on, e.g., you can reply “Thank you!” to multiple comments on the same work, but you can’t reply “Thank you!” to the same comment twice.

h1. Testing

It’s not necessary to verify the error message on tags, works, admin posts, and comments, since they all use the same validation.

h1. Overview Admins with certain roles should be able to create and manage draft admin posts, similar to the way users can create draft works. This includes the ability to preview the admin post. It does not include automatic draft deletion. Users should not see any change to the way admin posts work. h2. Translations It should be possible to create drafts that are translations of either posted _or_ draft admin posts. Posting a draft should also post its draft translations.  Deleting a posted _or_ draft admin post with draft translations should delete the draft translations. h1. Database The {{admin_posts}} table will need two new columns: * a {{posted}} boolean column * a {{published_at}} datetime column h2. Existing Data Existing admin posts should have their {{posted}} column set to {{true}} and their {{published_at}} set to their {{created_at}} date. This is necessary to maintain the current behavior for published posts. h1. Roles (AdminPostPolicy) Admins with existing {{POSTING_ROLES}} ({{superadmin}}, {{board}}, {{board_assistants_team}}, {{communications}}, {{support}}, {{translation}}) should be able to create, edit, delete, and post drafts. Admins with {{DRAFTING_ROLES}} ({{policy_and_abuse}}) should be able to create, edit, and delete drafts, but not post them. h1. Public Pages The admin post index and show pages, as well as the news section on the homepage, should be updated to keep the current behavior: * The posts on the page and in the sidebar should only include admin posts where {{posted: true}}. They should be ordered by the {{published_at}} date. * The posts on the page and in the sidebar should be ordered by the {{published_at}} date. * The "Published" date for a post should use {{published_at}}, not {{created_at}}. * The list of translations for a post should only include posts where {{posted: true}}. * The "Preview Post" and "Next Post" links on individual posts should navigate according to the posts' {{published_at}}, not the posts' ID. h1. Admin Pages h2. Admin Navigation "Post AO3 News" should say "Draft AO3 News" for admins with {{DRAFTING_ROLES}}. "AO3 News" should continue to lead to the public index for admins without {{POSTING_ROLES}}. “AO3 News Drafts” should be added after “AO3 News” and it should link to the index of draft admin posts. It should be visible to any admin with a role listed in the {{AdminPostPolicy}} section. h2. Subnavigation The admin post pages share subnavigation, so these changes should apply across all pages. (If [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6940|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6940|smart-link] is done first, or if you’re not a {{superadmin}}, you may see slightly different subnavigation than in the mockups.) * "AO3 News" should continue to lead to the public index for admins without {{POSTING_ROLES}}. * "AO3 News Drafts" should be added between "AO3 News" and "Post AO3 News." It should be visible to any admin with a role listed in the {{AdminPostPolicy}} section. * Moving between "AO3 News" and "AO3 News Drafts" should not remember any language or tag filters you have currently selected. For example, if you have filtered for posts tagged "site changes," when you follow "AO3 News Drafts," you should see all drafts, not just those tagged "site changes." * "Post AO3 News" should say "Draft AO3 News" for admins with {{DRAFTING_ROLES}}. h2. Sidebar For simplicity, the sidebar should always link to the most recently published admin posts. h2. Index of Posted Admin Posts [+https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts+|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts] !news_drafts_posted_index.png|width=100%,alt="Admin index of published admin posts. It has the heading AO3 News and an AO3 News Drafts subnavigation item. The post information includes the published date as well as the create and updated dates."! * This page should continue to use the public index for admins without {{POSTING_ROLES}}. * The list of posts should only include admin posts where posted is true, including when filtering by language or tag. * The posts should be ordered by {{published_at}} date. * The date information for individual admin posts should be changed to "Published at YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC (Created at YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC and updated at YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC)." * Optional but appreciated changes: ** "(includes Release Notes)" should be removed from the page heading. ** The "Manage News Postings" heading should be converted into an invisible landmark with the {{landmark}} class. ** The browser page title should be "AO3 News | Archive of Our Own." h2. Index of Draft Admin Posts [+https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/drafts+|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/drafts] !news_drafts_draft_index.jpg|width=100%,alt="Admin index of draft admin posts. It has the heading AO3 News Drafts and the new AO3 News Drafts subnavigation, which is styled to indicate it is currently selected. The created and updated dates are shown for the posts. The posts have Show, Edit, Post Draft, and Delete Draft options."! * The page should have the heading "AO3 News Drafts" and the browser page title "AO3 News Drafts | Archive of Our Own." * The list of posts should only include admin posts where {{posted: false}}, including when filtering by language or tag. ** As with published posts, the list of draft posts should only include posts in the Archive’s default language (English) unless filtering by another language. * The posts should be ordered by {{created_at}} date. * The date information for individual admin posts should be listed as "Created at YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC and updated at YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC." * Each post should have the following actions: Show, Edit, Post Draft, Delete Draft. (Refer to the Overview section for information on how posting and deleting should behave.) ** "Post Draft" should only be available to admins with {{POSTING_ROLES}}, and only if the post is in the Archive's default language (English) or is a translation of a published post. ** "Delete Draft" should have a confirmation pop-up, like the "Delete" pop-up for published posts. h2. Show Admin Post [+https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/###+|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/###] !news_drafts_draft_show.png|width=100%,alt="A show page for a draft news post. The sidebar is present and the main content has a light grey background and dashed grey border. The heading is AO3 News Draft. The subnavigation refers to drafts, not posts. The translations and tags are listed but not the published date."! If the admin post is a draft: * The page heading should be "AO3 News Draft" instead of "AO3 News" and should link to the index of draft admin posts. The browser page title should be "Admin Post's Title (Draft) | Archive of Our Own." * The subnavigation  ** does not need to include previous and next links. (If it does, it should use "Previous Draft" and "Next Draft" and link to the appropriate drafts.) ** should say "Edit Draft" and "Delete Draft" instead of "Edit Post" and "Delete Post." ** should link "Back to AO3 News Drafts" instead of "Back to AO3 News Index" at the bottom. * The main content should be wrapped in a light grey box with a dashed outline, created by applying the {{draft}} class to the {{div}} that currently has the {{"news admin home"}} classes. * The “Published at” metadata item should not be included, since there is no published date. h2. New Admin Post [+https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/new+|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/new] * Admins with {{POSTING_ROLES}} should have "Save As Draft," "Preview," and "Post" options. * Admins with {{DRAFTING_ROLES}} should have "Save As Draft" and "Preview" option. * Optional: The browser page title should be "New AO3 News Post | Archive of Our Own." h2. Edit Admin Post [+https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/###/edit+|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/###/edit] Note: Previews for edits to published admin posts are optional. * Admins with {{DRAFTING_ROLES}} should only be able to access the edit page for drafts. * Admins with {{DRAFTING_ROLES}} should only have "Save As Draft" and "Preview" options. * Admins with {{POSTING_ROLES}} should have ** "Save As Draft," "Preview," and "Post" options on drafts. ** "Preview" and "Post" options on posted admin posts. h2. Admin Post Preview [+https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/###/preview+|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/###/preview] !news_drafts_preview.jpg|width=100%,alt="The preview page for an admin post draft. The heading is Preview and the minimal post content and metadata are wrapped in light grey. A fieldset after the preview includes options to Post, Save As Draft, Edit, and Cancel."! Note: Previews for edits to published admin posts are optional. * The page heading should be "Preview" and the browser page title should be "The Admin Post's Title (Preview) | Archive of Our Own." * The preview should just give a general impression of how the admin post content and metadata will look once it has been posted or updated: ** It should not include the sidebar, the header module at the top of the admin post, or the feedback section at the bottom of the admin post. ** It should include translations and tags. ** It should not include the published date. * The admin post content should be wrapped in a light grey box with a dashed outline. * After the admin post content, there should be a form with the following options: ** "Post," "Save As Draft," and "Edit" if the post is a draft and the admin has {{POSTING_ROLES}} ** "Post" and "Edit" if the post is published (only admins with {{POSTING_ROLES}} can edit and preview published admin posts) ** "Save As Draft" and "Edit" if the admin has {{DRAFTING_ROLES}} (admins with {{DRAFTING_ROLES}} can only edit and preview drafts) * The "Save As Draft" option should save the changes and take you to the show page for the draft. h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in to an account with works, series, and a non-default pseud
# Set your Preferences so you’ll see the adult content notice
## Hi, username! > My Preferences
## Uncheck “Show me adult content without checking”
## Press “Update”
# Choose “Reversi” from the footer to apply the Reversi skin
# Take a gander at the following pages:
## an adult content notice on a work (Note: Even with the preference we set, you might not see this. If you don’t, you either need to use your browser developer tools to delete the view_adult cookie or try in a private/incognito window.)
## the Change Username page: https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/change_username
## the Orphan Work page: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/orphans/new?work_id=###|https://test.archiveofourown.org/orphans/new?work_id=###] (Note: ### can be the ID of any work you own, and accessing the page won’t complete the orphan process, so your work is safe)
## the Orphan Series page: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/orphans/new?series_id=###|https://test.archiveofourown.org/orphans/new?series_id=###] (Note: ### can be the ID of any series you own, and accessing the page won’t complete the orphan process, so your series is safe)
## the Orphan Pseud page, which we’re going to have to access the long way:
### Make a non-default pseud if you don’t have one
#### Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Profile > Manage My Pseuds > New Pseud
#### Fill in a name
#### Press “Create”
### If your pseud doesn’t have a work, create one
#### Post > New Work
#### Fill in required fields
#### For “Creator/Pseud(s)”, choose the name of your non-default pseud
#### Press Post
### Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Pseuds > All Pseuds
### Follow the “Orphan Works” link for the non-default pseud with works (Note: Accessing the page won’t complete the orphan process, so your works are safe.)
## the Orphan All Works page: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/orphans/new|https://test.archiveofourown.org/orphans/new] (Note: Accessing the page won’t complete the orphan process, so your works are safe.)
## the page for confirmation the deletion of multiple works, which we have to access the long way:
### Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Edit Works
### Check the checkbox to select at least one work
### Press “Delete” (Note: Accessing this page won’t complete the deletion process, so your work is safe)
## the confirmation page for muting a user: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/sarken/muted/users/confirm_mute?muted_id=USERNAME|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/sarken/muted/users/confirm_mute?muted_id=testy] (Note: USERNAME can be any existing user other than you and who you don’t already have muted. Again, accessing this page won’t complete the muting process, so you can look at anyone.)

h1. What happens

In 4a-4g, which have the wrong classes, your eyeballs are assaulted by the default yellow caution styling of a yellow background with black text, which is way too much on Reversi, and doesn’t work with Reversi’s link colors.

In 4h, which is an example of a page with the right classes, the text and border are just white on a Reversi dark grey background, which conveys neutrality rather than caution. 

h1. What should happen

We’re just going to steal the style from the rewritten version: on everything from 4a-4h, the background should be Reversi’s normal dark grey background, but the text and border should be a kind of golden/brown/muted yellow that won’t make you flinch in the dark.

h1. Notes

This is Medium priority because PAC would appreciate it if we can fix this before we add a new caution notice to another page.

h1. Deploy notes

This involves changing a site skin, so an admin with the {{superadmin}} role will need to update Reversi either shortly before or after deploy:

# Log in as an admin with the {{superadmin}} role
# Skins > Approved Skins
# Follow the “Reversi” link in the table
# Follow the “Edit” link
# Copy and paste the CSS from GitHub into the CSS field
# Press “Update” to save

And then Systems will need to run the playbook for recaching skins.

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Choose either “Reversi” or “Snow Blue” from the “Customize” section in the footer
# Browse > Tags > Tag Sets > New Tag Set
# Enter a name in the “Title” field
# Check “Currently taking nominations?”
# Enter at least “1” for “Fandom”, “Character”, and “Additional Tags”
# Press “Submit”
# Follow the “Nominate” link
# Enter a fandom in the relevant field
# Enter a character in the relevant field
# Enter an additional tag in the relevant field
# Press “Submit”
# Follow “Back to Tag Set Title”
# Follow “Review Nominations”
# Hover over the “+” and “-” checkboxes

h1. What happens

In Reversi:

# The nominated tags are written in light text on a white background. You can’t read it.
# The checkboxes have red text and a light grey highlight on hover.

In Snow Blue:

# The checkboxes have red text on hover.

h1. What should happen

In Reversi:

# The nominations' background should be the same grey that you see behind the autocomplete field to the left.
# The checkboxes should have similar hover styling to the rest of the links and buttons.

In Snow Blue:

# The checkboxes should have blue text on hover.

h1. Notes

The hover state issue also affects the Review Associations page. To see it, you have to approve a nomination for a character who is not currently associated with their nominated fandom and then access the Review Associations page.

h1. Deploy notes

This involves changing a site skin, so an admin with the {{superadmin}} role will need to update Reversi and Snow Blue either shortly before or after deploy:

# Log in as an admin with the {{superadmin}} role
# Skins > Approved Skins
# Follow the “Reversi” link in the table
# Follow the “Edit” link
# Copy and paste the CSS from GitHub into the CSS field
# Press “Update” to save
# Repeat for Snow Blue

And then Systems will need to run the playbook for recaching skins.

column1: Line breaks in page title and description meta tag lead to awkward link previews on other sites
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

Paste a link from AO3, e.g. a news post, onto a site like Bluesky or Tumblr that generates automatic link previews.

h1. What happens

On some sites, the link preview has the page title broken across lines, e.g. the news post title will be on one line, the | character on the next, and then the site name after that. 

On other sites, it might have extra space between parts (Bitly is good at that), like {{Page Title           |          Archive of Our Own}}

Additionally, some sites display the content of the description meta tag, and break _that_ into two lines as well (as seen in the [bit.ly|http://bit.ly] screen shot below).

!Screenshot 2025-04-03 at 5.08.57 PM.png|width=535,height=166,alt="A link preview with the post title on one line, followed by I... on the second."!

h1. What should happen

It should be on one line that can be wrapped or truncated as needed by whoever is generating the link preview.

h1. Notes

This happens because it’s not stripping the line breaks from the page title or the description meta tag. If you view the page source (which is what you’ll have to do on staging to test this, since you won’t be able to link to it), you see they look like this:

{noformat}<meta name="description" content="An Archive of Our Own, a project of the
    Organization for Transformative Works" />

<title>
          
          Admin Posts
        |
        Archive of Our Own
    </title>{noformat}

(Note: I do mean page source. Depending on the browser, using the inspector may strip the line breaks and display it as, e.g., {{<title>Admin Posts | Archive of Our Own</title>}} unless you edit the node.)

That happens because the code in application.html.erb is like this:

{noformat}    <meta name="description" content="An Archive of Our Own, a project of the
    Organization for Transformative Works" />
    
    <title>
      <% if defined?(@page_title) %>
        <%= @page_title %>
      <% else %>
        <% if defined?(@page_subtitle) %>
          <%= @page_subtitle %>
        <% else %>
          <%= controller.action_name == "index" ? "" : process_title(controller.action_name) %>
          <%= controller.action_name == "index" ? process_title(controller.controller_name) : process_title(controller.controller_name.singularize) %>
        <% end %>
        |
        <%= ArchiveConfig.APP_NAME  %>
      <% end %>
    </title>{noformat}

The best fix would probably involve putting the page title logic in a {{browser_page_title}} helper.

h1. Testing notes

It would be a good idea to check that the browser page titles on the following pages display as usual in your browser:

* a work, logged in and out, ideally with and & or < in the title
* an admin post, ideally with an & or < in the title

column1: Optimize feature tests by creating works with FactoryBot instead new works page
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
A lot of feature tests need a work to post comments on, bookmark, edit or similar. Many times, that work has no requirements besides a specific title and author. Nonetheless it’s created with the {{I post a work}} step which requires a logged in user and then creates basic tags, visits the new works page, fills in all the fields and then posts the work. That’s a lot of steps when we can just create these works with {{FactoryBot.create}}.

Let’s switch over features files with a lot of simple {{I post a work steps}} within the {{Given}} section to the {{the work "title" by "author"}} step (which uses FactoryBot) and measure whether this speeds up the tests. There may also be some frequently used step definitions that can be switched to use FactoryBot to create the work.

This optimisation was previously blocked by [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6439|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6439|smart-link] : if {{User.current_user}} was set due to the previous request, it would mess up work creation with FactoryBot. 

h3. Testing

No manual QA, automated tests only.

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Create a new tag set that’s taking nominations and allows multiple fandoms and characters, and at least one additional tags
## Browse > Tags > Tag Sets > New Tag Set
## Fill in a title
## Check “Currently taking nominations?”
## In the “Nomination Limits” section, fill in 2 for each type of tag’s nomination limit (we don’t _need_ to allow relationships, but it won’t hurt)
## Submit
# Nominate at least two characters in two fandoms and at least one additional tag
## Follow the “Nominate” link
## For Fandom 1, enter a fandom and two characters, at least one of which should not be wrangled into that fandom if it exists on the site (e.g., nominate Luke Skywalker in Star Trek fandom)
## For Fandom 2, enter a fandom and any other tags you like
## For Additional Tag 1, enter an additional tag
## Submit
# Approve one fandom and one tag that needs to be associated with a fandom 
## Follow the “Review Nominations” link
## Select the “+” checkbox to approve Fandom 1 and the character in Fandom 1 that is not already wrangled into that fandom
## Submit

h1. What happens

On the Review Nominations page, the name of the fandom is an h3, which is the same heading level as the “Already Approved Fandoms” and “Fandoms (# left to review)” headings. The “Already Approved Fandoms,“Fandoms (# left to review),” and “Additional Tags (# left to review)” headings are also higher up in the grey area than the buttons for approving and rejecting.

If you follow the “Review Associations” link, you’ll see the “Approve Nominated Associations” h3 is similarly misaligned.

h1. What should happen

The names of the fandoms should be h4 headings, which will be a bit smaller. 

The headings should be a bit closer to being vertically centered in the grey area/with the buttons.

column1: 500 error on tag page if the ArchiveConfig.FANDOM_NO_TAG_NAME doesn't exist
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. What happens

If you attempt to access the tag cloud ({{/tags}} or {{/tags?show=random}}) when the tag named in {{ArchiveConfig.FANDOM_NO_TAG_NAME}} doesn’t exist, you’ll get a 500 error.

h1. What should happen

Instead of a 500 error, it would be better if the page loaded but did not display any tags.

Because this is unlikely to be something you see in reality, we can keep this simple: there’s no need to change any text or navigation on the page. We can cope with it saying “These are some tags…” and then showing nothing.

h1. Reproducing in dev

To see this in action, use your {{local.yml}} to set {{FANDOM_NO_TAG_NAME}} to a tag that doesn’t exist in your dev environment, restart your server, and try to go to [https://localhost:3000/tags|https://localhost:3000/tags]. You’ll get a 500 error:

{noformat}NoMethodError in TagsController#index
undefined method `children' for nil:NilClass
Extracted source (around line #35):
33 else 
34   no_fandom = Fandom.find_by_name(ArchiveConfig.FANDOM_NO_TAG_NAME)
35   @tags = no_fandom.children.by_type('Freeform').first_class.limit(ArchiveConfig.TAGS_IN_CLOUD){noformat}

You could also update this test added in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6963|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6963|smart-link] to remove the line that creates the tag:

{noformat}Scenario: An index page uses only the controller name in the default browser page title

  Given a fandom exists with name: "No Fandom", canonical: true
  When I go to the tags page
  Then I should see the page title "Tags | Example Archive"{noformat}

 With that line removed, the test will fail until this is fixed.

h1. Testing notes

If you wanted to reproduce this, you’d either:

* log in as an admin with the {{tag_wrangling}} or {{superadmin}} role, go to the edit page for the No Fandom tag ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/No%20Fandom/edit}}), and rename it to something else (please don’t do this; it will probably cause a cascade of issues)
* ask Systems to change the value of {{ArchiveConfig.FANDOM_NO_TAG_NAME}} to a tag that doesn’t exist or  isn’t a fandom

However, I’d say automated tests are enough for this.

column1: Email user when they change or reset their password
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30: h1. Steps to reproduce # Log in # Hi, username! > My Preferences > Change Password # Fill in the form # Press “Change Password” OR # While logged out, visit /users/password/new (you can click on Forgot password? under the login form) # Fill in the form # Click on the link in your email # Fill in the form  # Press “Change Password” h1. What should happen You should get an email telling you your password has been changed. The email should have the formal addressed greeting and the PAC footer. The date should be localized and include the timezone. In the HTML email, the username should be bold red (style_bold) and the links should be red (style_link). HTML: {code:none}[AO3] Your password has been changed Hi %{name}, The password for your AO3 account was changed on %{date}. If you made this change, you can log in with your new password or reset your password if you've forgotten it. If you experience technical issues, please contact Support. If you did not make this change, someone else may have access to your AO3 account. Please reset your password now or contact Policy & Abuse.{code} TXT: {code:none}[AO3] Your password has been changed Hi %{name}, The password for your AO3 account was changed on %{date}. If you made this change, you can log in with your new password (https://archiveofourown.org/users/login) or reset your password if you've forgotten it (https://archiveofourown.org/users/password/new). If you experience technical issues, please contact Support: https://archiveofourown.org/support. If you did not make this change, someone else may have access to your AO3 account. Please reset your password now (https://archiveofourown.org/users/password/new) or contact Policy & Abuse: https://archiveofourown.org/abuse_reports/new.{code} h1. Notes There is [a setting in the Devise config|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/5f5af39ee9950f9f996d75e5d7df2466fdbfadf7/config/initializers/devise.rb#L104C1-L105C53] that can be enabled to send this email. Devise has [instructions on implementing custom mailers|https://github.com/heartcombo/devise/wiki/How-To:-Use-custom-mailer]. We already have the [ArchiveDeviseMailer class|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/mailers/archive_devise_mailer.rb] to extend the Devise mailer. This email should only be sent if the user initiated the password change, since PAC emails users separately if the change was made by a database admin. Therefore, before this is deployed, a database admin should confirm that we can skip sending the notification when manually resetting passwords, by doing the following: {code:ruby}user = User.find_by(login: "username") user.skip_password_change_notification! user.update!(password: "newpassword"){code} If that works, we should update our internal instructions for manual password resets. If it doesn't, we need to investigate how to skip sending the email before this can be deployed.

The {{days_to_purge_unactivated}} admin setting is currently not used to set any value in the code. Let’s fix that and use it in the {{purge_unvalidated_users}} rake task to replace the hardcoded [two weeks|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/7da89d39ecc5aa70fb8281b54ab9dc6492ccae4a/lib/tasks/admin_tasks.rake#L19]. The setting should no longer default to {{ArchiveConfig.DAYS_TO_PURGE_UNACTIVATED}} in the model, but instead to {{2.weeks}}. Similarly, the spots that use the admin setting to [display a value to a user|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/437ad9a7fa1e95cac4322e65a94ff02ad6d9b3a8/app/views/users/confirmation.html.erb#L13-L15] should no longer default to {{ArchiveConfig.DAYS_TO_PURGE_UNACTIVATED}} .

{{DAYS_TO_PURGE_UNACTIVATED}} in config.yml (and the remaining spots where it is used) should be renamed to {{DAYS_TO_CONFIRM_EMAIL_CHANGE}} so that it describes what it actually does.

The hardcoded 14 days in [this error|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e8efaa641da2a6db70fa998cdabd8e55041aa421/app/controllers/users_controller.rb#L112] should be replaced by the admin setting.

h3. Testing

The cronjob that runs the {{purge_unvalidated_users}} task should run as normal.

column1: Spam check edited comments by new users and exclude comments on commenter's own work from spam check
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Similar to how we [put edited comments back into comment moderation|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/0a7fea21e1b22af418f9fab2c9b0f21094a997d5/app/models/comment.rb#L145-L155], we would like to resubmit significantly edited comments into the [spam checker for comments by new users|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6933].

This should reuse the [content_too_different?|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/0a7fea21e1b22af418f9fab2c9b0f21094a997d5/app/models/comment.rb#L309] method to check that the edit was significant. However, it should use a different limit than the comment moderation threshold, configurable in the {{ArchiveConfig}}.
