column1: Support form notices
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Background

Support would like to have quickly editable text on the /support page that Support admins can quickly change in reaction to changing site events, without having to close the Support form entirely. These will be called “notices”, although the share some characteristics with the site-wide banners functionality.

h1. Implementation

There are two pieces: displaying the notices to users, and giving admins the ability to manage the notices.

h2. User-Facing

Banners should be displayed, with a configurable existing class (notice, caution, error), right under the information about what languages we can provide support in.

!support_notice.png|width=325,alt="support_notice.png"!

If there is no banner marked active, the banner would not display a placeholder.

h2. Admin-Facing

A new table will need to be created to store these notices. It should be called {{support_notices}}, with the model being called {{SupportNotice}}. This can be structured the same as the [existing admin_banners table|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/7da89d39ecc5aa70fb8281b54ab9dc6492ccae4a/db/schema.rb#L67].

We need to create new routes:

# {{/admin/notices/support}} that points to an index of all Support notices, similar to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/banners|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/banners]
# {{/admin/notices/support/new}} for a form to create new notices. This can be modeled on [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/banners/new|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/banners/new], although the types should be Notice, Caution, Error. Notice should be the default.
# {{/admin/notices/support/:support_notice_id/edit}} to update the support notice. (This will also require the corresponding update route)
# A route to delete a notice

There needs to be a new item on the admin menu, next to banners, called “Support Notices”, which links to {{/admin/notices/support}}. This menu should only be visible to admins with the superadmin and support roles, and all of the new routes should display an error if an admin without one of those roles attempts to access them.

When an admin creates, updates, or deletes an support form notice, the action should be logged as an admin activity: the date, admin name, action (i.e., update support notice, create support notice, destroy support notice), and target (Support Notice ID) should be recorded, and the summary should contain the notice text (because notices can be deleted). For updates, the summary should contain the new notice text, not the old.

h1. Deploy notes

This has a migration {{rails db:migrate:up VERSION=20251215194643}} and needs a skin recache.

h1. Testing

# An admin with a superadmin or support role creates a notice for each of the types listed above and marks it active. Then, at least one guest and one registered user open the support form to make sure the notice is in the right place and styled properly.
# An admin with a superadmin or support role marks the notice(s) as inactive. Accessing the support form should not show any notice (it looks the same as on production AO3).
# An admin without the superadmin or support role logs in and makes sure there’s no “Notices” option in the menu.
# An admin with the superadmin or policy_and_abuse role should be able to find the logs of previous admin’s actions in the admin activities.

column1: Add suggested fandoms to a tag via checkbox
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a tag wrangler (you can use testy on staging)
# Post a work with at least two fandom tags and a new character, relationship, or additional tag (it doesn’t _have_ to be new, but it’s a tiny bit easier for these directions)
# From the meta of your newly posted work, follow the link to your new tag’s landing page
# Follow the Edit link

h1. What happens

There is a list of Suggested Fandoms that is just a comma-separated list of tags.

!suggested_fandoms_current.png|width=91.66666666666667%,alt="The current Suggested Fandoms area, which is a list of links to tags."!

h1. What should happen

The list of Suggested Fandoms should be a listbox full of checkboxes, like the list of fandoms on the tag, but it should say “Check to add” instead of “Check to remove” and there should not be an autocomplete section.

Since noncanonical fandoms cannot be added as parents, the checkbox would ideally be disabled for them, and the grey gradient area around the checkbox would be flat grey ({{#ccc}}) .

If that’s not possible, when you check a noncanonical fandom, you should experience a similar error to the one you get when entering a noncanonical fandom manually: you are taken to {{/tags/TAG%20NAME}}, which has an error that says, “Cannot add association to ‘FANDOM': Parent tag is not canonical.” Ideally, any fandoms that errored will be unchecked and you’ll only have to press “Save changes” to actually finish adding the valid canonical fandoms.

Other than that, the behavior should generally be the same: 

* the name of the fandom tag should be a link to its edit page, 
* adding a fandom should remove it from the Suggested Fandoms section, and
* the Suggested Fandoms section should not be present if there are no suggested fandoms. 

!suggested_fandoms_new.png|width=100%,alt="Suggested fandoms as a listbox containing checkboxes, with All and None buttons and instructions to check to add. The noncanonical fandom's checkbox is flat grey."!

## Fill in the comment form on the top of the page and press “Comment” to post the comment
# Log out
# Log in as WranglerB
# Make sure you’re set up to receive copies of your own comments via email
## Hi, username! > My Preferences
## Uncheck “Turn off copies of your own comments.”
## Press “Update” 
# Leave a comment on WranglerA’s fandom tag from Step 2
## Go to the tag comment page using the URL from Step 3c
## Fill in the comment form on the top of the page and press “Comment” to post the comment and send two emails: 
### “Comment you left on the tag [Tag Name]” to WranglerB (comment_sent_notification)
### “Comment on the tag [Tag Name]” to WranglerA (comment_notification)
## Use the “Edit” button to change your comment and trigger two emails:
### “Comment you left on the tag [Tag Name]” to WranglerB – this is the same comment_sent_notification email as in Step 7bi, so you won’t need to test anything in this step
### “Edited comment on the tag [Tag Name” to WranglerA (edited_comment_notification)
## Use the “Reply” button on WranglerA’s comment from Step 3 to leave a reply and trigger two more emails:
### “Reply you left to a comment on the tag [Tag Name]” to WranglerB (comment_reply_sent_notification)
### “Reply to your comment on the tag [Tag Name]” to WranglerA (comment_reply_notification)
## Use the “Edit” button to change your comment and trigger two emails
### “Reply you left to a comment on the tag [Tag Name]” to WranglerB – this is the same comment_reply_sent_notification email you got in Step 7di, so you don’t need to test it a second time
### “Edited reply to your comment on the tag [Tag Name]” to WranglerA (edited_comment_reply_notification)

h1. What happens 

At the top of each email is some text that includes the phrase “on the tag [Tag Name].”

It should say “on the [Tag Category] tag [Tag Name].”

In a total change of pace, please don’t i18n these emails as part of this. Let’s keep it straightforward to test/review.

h1. Testing notes

It would be a good idea to test multiple types of tags to make sure the category is correct.

No manual QA, automated tests should pass.

column1: Use CommentMailer when sending comment emails to admins
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
When we send comment notifications to the admin email address, we use {{AdminMailer.comment_notification}} and {{AdminMailer.edited_comment_notification}} and their corresponding templates. 

The templates are duplicates of the ones for {{CommentMailer}}.  

We’d like to consolidate the code for comment notifications and use {{CommentMailer}} and its templates instead.

h1. Testing

# Be subscribed to the mailing list that gets notifications of comments on admin posts
# Log in as an admin with one of the following roles: superadmin, board, board_assistants_team, communications, support, translation
# Admin Posts > Post AO3 News
# Fill in required fields
# Check “Enable comment moderation”
# Set “Who can comment on this news post” to “Registered users and guests can comment” (you can also use “Registered users only” – the important thing is registered users can comment and therefore edit their comments)
# Press “Post”
# Make note of the URL of the news post
# In another browser or an incognito/private window, log in
# Go to  the news post URL from step 7
# Fill in some comment text
# Press “Comment”
# Follow the “Edit” link
# Make some changes
# Press “Update” to save

After steps 11 and 14, the admin email address should get emails. 

The individual admin who posted the admin post should _not_ get any emails.

The email for step 11:

{quote}Subject: [AO3] Comment on Admin Post Title

username (Registered User) left the following comment on Admin Post Title:

Comment text.

Posted: 2025-05-14 06:23:57 UTC

Comments on this news post are moderated and will not appear until approved.

Review comments on Admin Post Title
Go to the thread starting from this comment
Read all comments on Admin Post Title{quote}

And step 14:

{quote}Subject: [AO3] Edited comment on Admin Post Title

username (Registered User) edited the following comment on Admin Post Title:

Edited comment text.

Posted: 2025-05-14 06:23:57 UTC
Last edited: 2025-05-14 06:24:11 UTC

Comments on this news post are moderated and will not appear until approved.

Review comments on Admin Post Title
Go to the thread starting from this comment
Read all comments on Admin Post Title{quote}

We just want to confirm that the email is still the same and we didn’t somehow completely eliminate the note about comment moderation. 

Optionally, if you’d like to go back to your browser window from step 8, you can edit the news post, uncheck “Enable comment moderation,” and repeat steps 8-14 to confirm that the “Comments on this news post are moderated…” text isn’t present in the emails for those comments.

h1. Deploy notes

The Resque workers need to be restarted.

column1: Permanently strip image embeds from comment notification emails
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Make sure images are allowed in work comments (we want to be sure images are never included in comment emails, not even if they’re allowed in the comments themselves)
## If [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6992|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6992|smart-link] is done:
### Log in as an admin with the {{policy_and_abuse}} or {{superadmin}} role
### Follow the “Settings” link in the admin navigation 
### In the “Content” section, for “Turn off images in comments on,” uncheck “Works and chapters”
### Press “Update”
### Log out of admin
## If [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6992|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6992|smart-link] isn’t done, you’ll need to ask Systems to make sure {{PARENTS_WITH_IMAGE_SAFETY_MODE}} doesn’t include {{Chapters}} ✅ 
# Log in as a user whose email you can access
# Post a work with comments for logged in users enabled
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required fields
## Set “Who can comment on this work” to “Only registered users can comment” or “Registered users and guests can comment”
## Press “Post”
## Make note of the URL
# Log out
# Log in as a different user whose email you can access
# Set your preferences to receive copies of your own comments
## Hi, username! > My Preferences
## Uncheck “Turn off copies of your own comments”
## Press “Update”
# Visit the work from Step 2
# Leave a comment with an embedded image (it doesn’t matter if you use a valid image URL)
# Edit the comment (you don’t have to edit the image HTML – any edit is fine)
# Log out
# Log in as a third user whose email you can access
# Set your preferences to receive copies of your own comments (refer to Step 5)
# Visit the work from Step 2
# Expand the work’s comment section by following the Comments link at the top of the work
# Reply to the comment with an embedded image (again, it doesn’t matter if you use a valid image URL)
# Edit your reply (you don’t have to edit the image HTML here either)

h1. What happens

* At Step 8
** the work creator receives comment_notification
** the original commenter receives comment_sent_notification
* At Step 9
** the work creator receives edited_comment_notification
* At Step 15
** the second commenter receives comment_reply_sent_notification
** the original commenter receives comment_reply_notification
* At Step 16
** the original commenter receives edited_comment_reply_notification

Each of these emails contains the embedded image (or a broken image placeholder if you didn’t use a working HTML).

h1. What should happen

The emails should only contain the HTML for the image, stripped of its angle brackets, e.g. {{img src="https://example.com/image.jpg" alt="A daisy" width="500" border="5px solid black"}}, as described in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6987|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6987|smart-link]. 

h1. Deploy notes

Mailer workers need to be restarted.

column1: Always set up skin chooser skins in Docker installs
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
For ease of development, skins that belong in the skin chooser should be set up on installation. 

We currently have a rake task called {{load_user_skins}}, which theoretically creates or updates skins in the database based on the files in {{/public/stylesheets/site/user_skins_to_load/}}. However, that directory is empty. It would be nice to repurpose that task to load the skins we actually do keep in the repo, which are the skins for the chooser.

However, instead of the original approach of putting information about the parents, media, and so on in the stylesheets and trying to parse it out with regular expressions, we'd like to move all of that information to the fixtures. Then the task can just be concerned with updating the skins' {{css}} fields to contain the CSS from the files.

This should not affect production behaviour.

h3. Testing Instructions 

For Docker/Gitpod installs, verify that the skin chooser is populated for users and admins. In addition, verify that the Basic Formatting work skin is available for users.

h1. Steps to reproduce

# On iOS 17.6.1 with the Safari browser, log in

## Press “Post”

# Leave a comment on the work you posted in Step 2
## Visit the URL from Step 2e
## Press “Comments” to jump to the comment section
## Fill in the comment form with some text
## Press “Comment”
# Back in your iOS Safari window from Step 2, reload the work (or go to the URL if you closed the tab)
# Follow the “Unreviewed Comments (1)” link

h1. What happens

The text on the Approve All Unreviewed Comments, Freeze Thread, and Approve links are bold.

h1. What should happen

The text should be a normal weight, not bold.

h1. Notes

This may or may not apply to iOS versions other than 17 and iOS browsers other than Safari.

As of [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5953|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5953|smart-link] this also affects Mark For Later, Mark as Read on works and other links that were changed to be buttons.

The user agent stylesheet helpfully sets {{font-weight: bold}} for {{input[type="submit"], input[type="submit"]:active, button[type="submit"], button[type="submit"]:active, button[type="menu"], button[type="menu"]:active}} so this probably happens in other places. 

Adding {{font-weight: 400}} to {{.actions a, .actions a:link, .action, .action:link, .actions button, .actions input, input[type="submit"], button, .current, .actions label}} should fix things.

column1: Invitation without an email can be searched and resent
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
Currently, the account invitation checker does not validate the email address and accepts an empty string. On production, this locates an existing invitation sent in 2011, which can be resent using the Resend Invitation feature. 

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Make sure invitations can be requested and the queue is sending invitations
## Log in as an admin with the role {{superadmin}} 
## Follow the “Settings” link in the admin navigation 
## If the homepage does not have a “Get Invited!” link (this will be the case on staging), enable the invitation queue by checking all three of these settings: “Account creation enabled”, “Account creation requires invitation”, and “Invite from queue enabled (People can add themselves to the queue and invitations are sent out automatically)” 
## Fill in “How often (in hours) should we invite people from the queue” with “1” to send invitations every hour
## Fill in “Number of people to invite from the queue at once” with your desired number
## Press “Update” to save 
## Log out of your admin account
# The broken data is not available on dev or staging, so you’ll have to break some with the help of a database admin
## Go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests|https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests]
## In the “Email” field, enter an email address that you have access to (to make it easier to see that it has been sent) and that isn’t already being used by an account
## Press “Add me to the list”
## Wait for the queue to send your your invitation
## Now get a database admin to change the invitation’s {{invitee_email}} to a blank string
### Tell them the email address you used so they can look it up with {{invite = Invitation.find_by(invitee_email: "email@example.com")}}, set {{invitee.invitee_email = ""}}, and save
# Once 24 hours have passed (this will allow resending), go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status|https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status] and press “Look me up” without entering anything in the search field
# Press “Resend invitation”

h1. What happens

After Step 3, you see

{quote}Invitation Status for

Your invitation was emailed to this address on [DATE]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there.

Because your invitation was sent more than 24 hours ago, you can have your invitation resent.{quote}

After Step 4, you get a success notice that says “Invitation resent to .”

h1. What should happen

We should add a validation on the email field so {{invitee.invitee_email = ""}} doesn’t work. 

We should also ensure that a [search without JS|https://archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/show?email=&commit=Look+me+up] displays an error from the backend.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
The old version of Reversi has a few problems:

* It’s disorganised
* It has more visual bugs compared to the default skin
* Updating it is annoying
* The name is confusing now that the rest of the web has standardised on terms like “dark mode”

Sarken has the code in [https://github.com/sarken/otwarchive/tree/rewrite_reversi|https://github.com/sarken/otwarchive/tree/rewrite_reversi|smart-link] , and since [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6232|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6232|smart-link] is done, we should be ready to PR it.

h1. Deploy Notes

* This will require logging in as AO3_ADT and creating three skins as described in the README, and then logging in as an admin with the superadmin role and approving the skins before actually deploying the Archive code. *UPDATE:* Three skeleton skins (i.e., skins with placeholder CSS and nothing else) were created on June 23, since we needed the skin IDs for the news post.
** It will be necessary for a database admin to rename the existing skin with the title “Dark Mode,” which belongs to a user. Then AO3_ADT can be used to rename the skin currently titled “Dark Mode (Rename Me).”

column30:
h1. Steps to reproduce

Note: The kudos button is just a handy example here; this problem can also be seen in other places where we have hidden inputs, like the inbox on the homepage.

# In Safari on MacOS on a device with a keyboard, ensure that you have “Press Tab to highlight each item on a webpage” enabled in the [Safari settings|https://dequeuniversity.com/mac/keyboard-access-mac]
# Access a work you don’t own
# Use the Tab key to navigate through the focusable elements to the Kudos button (faster version: scroll down to the comment field, click in it to put your focus there, and use Tab + Shift to navigate backwards)

h1. What happens

If you’ve used Tab, your keyboard focus will vanish for three presses between the button right before Kudos (probably Top or Next Chapter) and the Kudos button.

If you’re going backwards and using Tab + Shift, it will vanish for three presses after landing on the Kudos button but before moving to the button before it (which might be Next Chapter or Top).

h1. What should happen

You should never lose focus! It should go straight to the Kudos button.

h1. Notes

This happens because we accidentally override user agents' {{display: none;}} style on {{input[type="hidden"]}} when we do things like {{.actions input { bunch of styles including display: inline-block; }}}. 

While we usually avoid the {{!important}} keyword, in this case it would be appropriate to remove {{input[type="hidden"]}} from [this rule set in 07-interactions|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/900c8e833ced9a1b027fa0e5ab5701396e19eaab/public/stylesheets/site/2.0/07-interactions.css#L55-L62] and add {{input[type="hidden"] { display: none !important; }}}.

Skins need to be recached.

column1: ActiveStorage::FileNotFoundError for some icons uploaded pre-2025
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column30:
In [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5778|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5778|smart-link], we switched to ActiveStorage. However, for some reason, the backfill script (in {{after_tasks.rake}}) resulted in some DB records being created even when S3 uploads didn’t succeed (or just didn’t happen – why is unclear).

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Find a user or collection whose icon was uploaded around 2024 or earlier.
# Ask Systems (AD&T doesn’t have access to the S3 bucket yet) to delete the icon manually via the AWS console (don’t worry, they’ll know what to do roughly even if you don’t know what that means 🙂 )
# Load a page that should display the icon

Note: this impacts skins too, but previews for them are more annoying so feel free to skip them – the code should be exactly the same.

h2. What happens

The image is not shown, and an [error is recorded in Sentry|https://organization-for-transformativ.sentry.io/issues/6308530931/?project=4507488737820672&query=is%3Aunresolved&referrer=issue-stream&stream_index=4].

h2. What should happen

# The image is not shown on initial page load
# On subsequent reloads (or other page loads), the icon should now be shown again.

h1. Implementation Notes

This takes 2 parts: rescuing the exception, and re-backfilling the icon. (Cleaning up the active storage data doesn’t need to happen now, but if you want {{purge}} ing the icon like we do on delete should work.)

h2. Exception rescue

The easiest (and probably best) way to do this would be to create an exception handler in {{ApplicationController}} like [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/controllers/application_controller.rb#L28|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/controllers/application_controller.rb#L28|smart-link] .

There is another option, though, if that ends up being too much code for that file: implement a custom subclass of the ActiveStorage controllers [as described in the Rails docs|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_storage_overview.html#authenticated-controllers].

h2. Re-backfill

AD&T has a script to do this ad-hoc for a list of users. You’ll need to figure out a way to get the right objects to update though, since we can’t just rely on {{User.current_user}} (because collections are also a thing to consider). _Note from Brian:_ collections may be much less likely to display this issue due to how the backfill for them worked (it used simpler code) – in a  pinch, I suppose we can just assume it’s a user.

{code:ruby}usernames = %w[...]
User.where(login: usernames).each do |user|
  user.pseuds.each do |pseud|
    next unless pseud.icon_file_name
    image = pseud.icon_file_name
    ext = File.extname(image)
    image_original = "original#{ext}"

    icon_url = "https://s3.amazonaws.com/otw-ao3-icons/icons/#{pseud.id}/#{image_original}"
    old_icon = URI.parse(icon_url).open
    pseud.icon.attach(io: URI.parse(icon_url).open,
                      filename: image_original,
                      content_type: pseud.icon_content_type)

    puts "Sleeping to avoid DB issues"
    sleep 2
  end
end{code}

h1. Steps to reproduce

If you use the default site skin with JavaScript disabled on a small screen, you’ll see there’s a Filters link at the top of the page that will jump you down to the filters. Likewise, there’s a link in the filters to return to the top.

# Press “Update” to save

And then Systems will need to run the playbook for recaching skins.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins > Create Site Skin

h1. What happens

There is an option called “Apply to make public,” but if you click on the help link, it says you can’t apply to make skins public. (This is also true for work skins.)

h1. What should happen

This option should only be there for official users, not for admins or for users with no or other roles (e.g., tag wranglers). (Note: Generally, we like to keep the forms the same for admins and users, in case admins need to screenshot something. In this case, most users will _not_ see the “Apply to make public” checkbox, so including it would have the opposite effect. Additionally, including it provides no information for admins: if the skin author doesn’t check this box, the admin cannot access its edit page.)

The help link and associated file can be removed.

After this is deployed, we should remove all skins from the Approval Queue and Rejected Skins pages. We can do this with a rake task included in this issue.

h1. Testing

Note: It would be a good idea for an admin who can access Manage Users > Find Users to confirm that testy_official has the “official” role before testing.

{color:#bf2600}+*Before this is merged*+{color}{color:#bf2600}*, create a new skin and apply to make it public:*{color}

# Log in as a user *without* the “official” role (i.e., not testy_official)
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins > Create Site Skin
# Fill in required information, including a preview image, and check “Apply to make public”
# Press “Submit” to save the skin
# Leave a comment on this issue with the name of/a link to the skin to make sure an admin can find it

After this is merged, but *before* the task is run:

### Skins > Approved Skins

### Follow the “Edit” link at the bottom of the page
### Confirm “Apply to make public” isn’t present
## you can’t see the “Apply to make public” checkbox on a work skin

## Repeat 9d using a work skin

# As a user with the “official” role (i.e., testy_official), make sure you can still apply to make a site skin public, edit the skin, and undo applying to make it public.
## Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins > Create Site Skin

## Change something other than “Apply to make public”
## Press “Update”

column1: Redirect to the forgotten password page when requesting password reset fails

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Make sure you’re logged out
# Follow the “Forgot password?” link below the login fields
# Enter the username of a user with password resets disabled, such as {{testy4}} on Staging
# Press “Reset Password”

h1. What happens

You get a flash message and you are redirected to the homepage.

h1. What should happen

You should still get a flash message, but you should be redirected to the “Reset Password” page instead, so that you do not end up on the heavily cached homepage.

h1. Deploy notes

Systems should disable full page caching for logged out users on the “Reset Password” page ({{users/password/new}}). The redirect target change combined with disabling caching of the page should ensure that users aren’t accidentally getting served cached versions of the error message (which we suspect is occasionally happening with the password resets disabled error).

Update: It appears this page is already uncached in cloudflare/nginx, so nothing to change here.

h2. Testing

Manual testing is covered by the instructions in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7061|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7061|smart-link] .
